PREFACE TO THIS VOLUME.

THIS Third Volume of The Statutes of the Realm contains the Acts from the Beginning to the End of the Reign of King Hemy VIII. A.D. 1509-10. to A.D. 1545. (') printed from the Inrollment on the Rolls of Parliament in Chancery, when the Acts are found entered thereon : In default of such Inrollment, all Acts, which are contained in any former printed Collection of the Statutes, are here printed from the Original Bills or Acts preserved in the Parliament Office. (') In two Instances only, where the Inrollment and the Originals are both deficient, Recourse has been had to another authentic Source, and to the earliest Printed Collections. (*) In every Instance where an Act is not printed from the Inrollment on the Roll of Parliament, as specified at the Commencement of each Year, a Note is annexed referring to the Source from which it is printed.

From the First Year to the End of the Twenty-eighth Year, all the Acts, whether heretofore printed or not, which appear on the Inrollments of those Years, are now printed, such Acts as were not heretofore printed being distinguished by a smaller Type, in conformity with the Plan pursued through the Seventh and subsequent Years of King Henry VII. in the Second Volume of this Work.

In the Thirty-first Year, when the Distinction between Public and Private Acts is first specifically stated on the Inrollment, and in all the following Years, such Acts only are printed in this Volume as are so specified to be Public Acts, or as have been uniformly inserted in, or referred to, as such, in Sessional and other Printed Collections of Statutes. The Act now inserted as Chapter LI. of 32 Henry VIII. (4), enabling Kings of England to make Jointures on their Queens, is the only Exception to this Rule: that Act is printed, from the Inrollment in Chancery, as being decidedly distinct in its Character from all the other Acts of those Years not heretofore printed.

All Acts here printed from the Inrollment in Chancery, have been compared with the Original Acts in the Parliament Office, whenever any such still exist: Of the Acts passed in the Two Sessions, one holden in the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Years, (’) and the other in the Twenty-first Year, (‘) no Originals are preserved, nor are any Acts of those Sessions noticed, in the Calendars or Journals now existing, at the Parliament Office: Several of the Original Acts of other Sessions are also wanting there. It will be seen that Instances continually occur in which Amendments of the Inrollment are suggested from the Original Acts; and sometimes, though rarely, Errors in the Original Acts have been amended in the Inrollment (7) Where any manifest Error or Deficiency appears to exist both in the Inrollment and the Original, Recourse has been had to the Printed Copies, which, not unfrequently, substitute a corrected Reading in the place of an erroneous one: when that is not the Case, an Amendment is suggested by a Note. (')

1 For the Title of the only Act passed in the 38th Year, A.D. 1546-7, see the last Article in the Chronological Table immediately following this Preface, and the Note there.

* The first Act printed wholly from the Original, not being inrolled, is 32 Hen. VIII. c. 49. pa. 809.—In 5 Hen. VIII. c. 19. pa. 120. certain Letters Patent referred to in the Act are not iurolled: and in 7 Hen. VIII. c. 11. pn. 203. the Roll is mutilated, and ends abruptly. These two Utter Deficiencies are supplied from the Original Acts.

» See 37 Hen. VIII. c. 12. pa. 999. and c. 25. pa. 1019. 4 See pa. 824. of this Volume.

* See pa. 206 A seq. 6 See pa. 282 & scq.

» See 25 H. VIII. pa. 465. n. 6.-26 H. VIII. c. 3. pa. 496. n. 4.—c. 19. p. 518. n. I.

1 For material Amendments afforded by the Printed Copies, see 21 Hen. VIII. c. 3. pa. 284.

( iv )

All such Acts as are printed, either from the Inrollment where no Original Act exists, or from an Original Act which is not inrolled, have been compared with the Printed Copies, and the Variations noted; except in Cases where the Printed Copies are manifestly erroneous, or the Variations are wholly unimportant.

The Titles of the Acts as inrolled in Chancery, during the Period contained in this Volume, differ from those on the Original Acts; and in the Calendars in Chancery and in Parliament there are still further Differences: In the Chronological Table following, it has been thought sufficient to notice those Titles only which appear on the Inrollment artd on the Original Acts. The Title prefixed to each Chapter, in the Body of the Work, is that which is inserted in the Margin of the Roll at the Beginning of the Act, in all Oases where any such appears: Sometimes a List of the Acts is given at the Commencement of the Roll, with Titles differing from those in the Margin of the Entry of each Act; and sometimes, where a List is so given, no Titles are inserted in the Margin ; In this latter case, the Titles in the List are also prefixed to each Chapter as printed. Hie Titles of the Acts which are printed from the Originals are those which are generally indorsed on, but sometimes written at the Head of, such Original Acts.

Tables of the Titles of the Acts of each Session have been printed in the Modem Editions of the Statutes, distinguishing them into Public and Private Acts \ including in the first Description all such as have been printed in Sessional and other Collections of Statutes, and considering as Private Acts all such as have not beer so printed. These Tables have, on Examination, been found inaccurate in many Instances; as well in inserting the Titles of Acts under improper Years, as in inserting Titles not justified by any existing Acts, and omitting the Titles of some Acts actually passed. The ensuing Chronological Table refers to all the Acts of each Session, whether printed or not, which are either inrolled in Chanceiy or preserved among the Original Acts, or which, though not now so inrolled of preserved, yet are specifically stated in the Journal of the House of Lords to have received the Royal Assent. In this Table are inserted not only the number of the Chapters, but also the Numbers entered on the Inrollment of the several Acts 'in Chanceiy and upon the Original Acts in Parliament: In many instances the Original Acts are preserved in the Bundles, and referred to by the Calendars, of improper Years; and are referred to by this Table accordingly. The Chapters of the Acts, heretofore printed, are numbered according to the uniform Series in former printed Collections of the Statutes \ the Acts, now first printed, are numbered, in the Volume and the Table, in a Succession of Chapters, after the other Acts heretofore printed; and of all such Acts, in and after 31 Henry VIII. as are not so printed, the Titles are inserted in the Table in like Succession.

Two Engravings, one of the Commencement of the Roll in Chancery of 31 Henry VIH., and the other of the first Act entered .on thal Roll, are inserted at Pages 717 and 718 of this Volume.

London,

Is/ January 1817*

T.E. TOMLINS,

W. E. TAUNTON,

Sub-Commissioners.

STATUTES OF KING HENRY THE EIGHTH.

Anno Y HENRICI, VIII. A.D. 1509-10.

STATUTES MADE IN THE PARLIAMENT BEGUN TO BE HOLDEN AT WESTMINSTER, on Monday the twenty-first day of January,

In the FIRST Year of the Reign of K. HENRY VIII.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte for the repealinge of a Statut for Fyshinge in Island.

"VTTHER in tyme passed the King of Denmark made an ordinaunce that no Englisshman or other Straunger borne oute v Y of his Lande shulde repaire into eny parte of his realme or Dominions to gett Fysshe or other Schaundyse but oeniy to the Towne called Northbame ; At whiche tyme the King of noble memorie Henry the Syxte late King of this Realme beyng then in pfite Amytie wyth the seid King of Denmark and at his contempla£5n ordined & stablisshed by au&oritie of Parliament holden at Westm the viijth yere of his reigne, that noen of his Subgie&tf beyng Englisshmen shulde goo or repayre into eny of the Pardez Lordeshipps or Domynyons of the seid King of Denmark confry to his seid ordinaunce uppon payne of forfeyture of all his goodf moveable; by force of whiche Statute made in the seid ▼up yere divers of the Kyngf Subgie&f nott knowyng the seid Statute adventuryng & repairyng into Islande and other pdes of the Lordshipps & Domynyons of the seid King of Denmark for Fysshe and other Marchaundyse hathe ben grevouriy punysshed to ther great Losse & Hynderaunce, and contrary to good conscience considering that Fysshe and other Comodities of that Cuntre be muche behovefull and necessarie towarde the cden Weale of this Realme: Be it therfore ordeyned stablisshed and enacted by au&oritie of this $feent Parliament that the seid Acte made in the said viij* yere of the seid Kyng Henry the Syxte at his seid Parliament and all other a&es thereof made be fromehensforthe utterly voyde and of none effe&e repelled and annulled.

CHAPTER II.

An Acte concerning the making of Wollen Clothes.

"TTTHER in the Parliament holden at Westm the xxiij Day of January in the firste Yere of the Reigne of Richard the v v thyrd late in Dede and not in Right Kyng of Englonde, An Acte was made con&nyng the makyng & drapyng of Wollen Clothes; For as muche as the seid a&e is in suche forme that the clothyer doyng his true Diligence cannot observe the same w*owte meny tymes offendyng ayenste the seid a&e; in whiche be so strayt & greate penalties and forfriroures made against the seid Clothiers, So that they havyng no comforte, but that the aforesaid Acte shulde stonde sty lie goode and effectuall be lyke to leve the occupacbn of Cloth makyng whiche shulde be occasion of extreme Povtie and Idelnesse of greate nombre of the Kingf Subgie&f, wherof many greate inconvenientf shulde and may ensewe: Wherfore be it enacted by Au&oritie of this £feent Pliament that the Kyng our SouPaign Lorde nor eny other Psone or Pmoes shall take eny Avauntage or pfyte of eny Penalties or forfaytoures geven or lymytted by the seid Acte made the seid xxnj Day of January for eny clothe made or to be made afore the begynnyng of the nexte Parliament.

CHAPTER m.

An Acte concerning Receyvors.

XX7HER AS the Kyng oure Sou9aign Lorde entendythe that divers Revenues & Duetys deweand to be dewe to hys TV Highnes shalbe payde to his trusty §v*nt John Heyron his ge&all Receyvo' And to other Psones by his Highnesse hereafter in lyke office to be deputed and assigned as in the tyme of the late Kyng of faimus Memory Henry the vij1* hathe ben used. And for that that his Subgie&f may be truly and lawefully discharged of Paymentf made or to be made by them of e$y of the pWssis to the seid John Heyron or to oder Psones therto to be lymyted and appoynted in forme aforeseid; Be it therfore ordeyned enacted and establysshed by the Au&oritie of this psent Pliament that all Acquit*unces and Billes of Receyte heretofore made by the seid John Heyron, in the tyme of jthe seid late noble Kyng, and in the tyme of our SouPaign Lorde that nowe ys and hereafter to be made by the seid John Heyron, and all other the seid Psones by our seid Sou9aign Lorde to the seid Offices to be appoynted, and of e$y of them of eny his revenues or Duetys [what so ev*y *] they be, be a sufficient discharge to e$y suche Psone ayenst the Kyng our Sou^aign Lorde hys Heres and Successoures, Aswell in the Kyngf Eschequiour as in eny other of the Kingf Courtf wythowte eny other Warraunte tayle or pryvate Seale therof to be hadd opteyned or shewed. An Acte that Informations uppon Penall Statutf shalbe made within three Yeres.

WHER in tymes passed have ben made dyvers and meny A dies and Statutf Penalle for the whiche Penalties have ben geven actions and informations popular by Wrytte information or byll, and also enditementf made and taken uppon the same Statutes; The greate nombre of whiche Statutes penalle have nott ben putt in execucion tyll nowe of late ; By meane wherof meny and divers good and well disposed Psones ignoraunte of eny suche Statutes theyr heyres Sc executoures have ben putt to greate Losse of goodes vexatiOn & troble by accion information and enditementf for offenses surmysed to be doone confrye to the same Statutes meny Yeres after the Offenses wer surmysed to be doone ; Uppon whiche delatyng of so longe tyme muche Pjurye greate troble vexatiOn and meny [inconvenience1] insued to greate nombre of the Kingf Subgietf ; Wherfore be it enacted, by the Kyng our Sou^aigne Lorde and by the assente of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Coens in this £feent Pliament assembled and by the Au&oritie of the same, That all actiOnes informatics & indytementf frome hensforthe to be made hadde or taken by or for the Kyng our seid SouPaigne Lorde hys Heyres or Successoures, of & uppon eny suche penalle Statutes made or to be made, be hadde made & taken wythyn Thre Yere nexte immediately foloweyng after the seid Offence so made comytted or doone. CHAPTER XV.

An Acte concerning landf made in trust to Empson and Dudley.

WHER AS Richarde Empson late of London Knight and Edmunde Dudley late of London Squyer nowe [standyng5] and be atteynted of high treason after the course of the Comen Lawe, and they or one of them wer or be seased or [any of them6] Jountly wyth other were seased of dyvers Manners Landes and Tenementf and other Hereditamentf to the use of our Souvaigne Lorde the King or to the use of other the Kingf Subjects or in morgage or Coven*nte uppon payment or non payment and uppon divers other Coven*ntes: Be it therfore ordeyned and enacted by the au&oride of this psent Parliament, that e$y psone and psones to whos use the seid Richarde and Edmude or ether of them wer seased the xxtl day of Apryll laste paste or eny tyme sythen may entre into the same, wherof the seid Richard or Edmunde wer seased and make astate therof to other psones in Fee to there use as they myght have done yf the seid atteyndoure hadde never be hadde ne made aswell uppon the possession of our SouQaign Lorde the Kyng as of eny other psone: And that of all suche Manners, Landes, Tentf and other Hereditamentf, wherof the seid Richarde and Edmunde or ether of them were Joyntly seased wyth eny other psone or psones the seid xxu day or eny tyme sythe, the same jointe [Feoffere7] and ther Heyres and evy of them to stonde and be seased of the hoole to suche use and entente as the same Joynte Feoffey or Feoffeys wyth the same Richarde and Edmunde or [other*] of them wer seased the said xx*1 day or eny tyme sythen the seid atteyndours notwythstondyng. Provided alway that this a&e extende nott to eny Lordeshippes Manners Landes Teiitf Possessiones or Hereditaments that were of John Ratclyffe knyght late Lorde Fyzwater unto the whiche Robert Ratclyffe (9) nowe Lord Fyzwater Sone and Heyre of the seid John ys restored by an a&e of resdtudon made for hym in this pfeent Parliament; but that the seid Robert and his Heyres may have and enjoye all the same Lordeshippes Manners Landes Tenementf Possessiones & Hereditamentf accordyng to the 'seid a&e of restituf&n wyth the Pvysowes conteyned in the same, this Acte or eny other Acte made or to be made in this psent Parliament in eny wysse notwythstandyng; Ne that this Acte or eny thyng conteyned therm be in eny wysse hurtfull or (^judicial! to the seid Robt or hys Heyres of or in the jPimisses or eny of them.

Persons to whose uie Empion and Dudley were aeiied, or who were joint Feoffee* with them, may enter into and convey Laodt, See. notwithstanding their Attainder.

Proviso in favour of Lord Fitxwater.

CHAPTER m.

An Act concerning shooting in Longe Bowes.

TEE KYNG our Soveign Lord callyng to his most noble and gracious remembraunce that by the feate and excise of the Subgiettes of this his Realme in shotyng in long bowes there hath contynually growen and ben within the Mine grete nombre and multitude of good Archers which hath not oonly defended this Realme and the Subgiettes therof ayenst the cruell malice and daunger of theire owte ward enmys in tyme heretofore passed, but also with litell nombre and puyssaunce in regarde have done many notable aftes and discomfetures of warre ayenst the infidelis and other. And furthermore subdued and reduced dyPse and many regyons and Countrees to theire due obeysaunce to the grete honour fame and suertie of this Realme and Subje&f and to the terrible drede and fere of all straunge nacions any thyng to attempte or do to the hurte or damage of theym or any of them; and albeit that diPse gode and pfitable statutes in the cyme of his noble pgenitours and f?decessours kynges of this land for the mayntenaunce of Archery and longbowes heretofore have ben made, amongest wich the right famose Kyng of noble memory Henry the vij* Father to our said Soveign Lord by au&oritie of diPse pliamentis caused good and notable attis and statutes to be establisshed and made.

F)R ASMOCHE that the Kynge oure Sovaigne Lorde entendeth by the grace of God to send o9 the see a greate armye trustyng therby not only to pserve this his realme in his aundent fame and honoure but also to set in pfyte peace and fnquyllite his subgiettf of the same and the better to be disposed to §ve God; How be it many tymes by the inordynate covedsenes of Capiteynes reteyned with Princes afore this tyme gfeate parte of the nombre of Soudeours for whom such Capiteynes have endented with Princes at tyme of nede have lakked of theire nombre of Soudiours wherby great Jeopdy have ensued and irrecupable damages may ensue if remedy therfor be not seen and had. And that e$y Capteigne Petycapteyne and all other havyng under theyme retynue of Souldeour or Soldeours at the Kyngf Wagf shall uppon the payne afore sad pay to the retynue of Souldeour or Souldeours and evy of the same the Wagf ratably as is allowed unto theym by the Kyng oure Sovaigne Lorde or the Tresourer of his Warres without lessyng or withdrawyng of any parte therof. CHAPTER VI.

An Act against deceyptfull making of Wollen Cloth.

FOR the deceitfull drapyng and makyng of wollen clothes made and draped within this Realme, And also for mesuryng in sale of the same, Our SoPayn Lord the Kyng by thadvyse and assent of his Lordf spueil and tempell and the Comons in this j^sent parliament assembled and by au&orite of the same hath ordyned established and enacted dyPse ordyn*ncf and statutf for the trewe makyng and drapyng of suche wollen clothes and for mesuryng in sales the trewe content of the same in ma8 and forme folowyng; Fyrst That the Wollc whiche shalbe delyPed for or by the Clothier to any p6one or psones for brekyng kembyng cardyng or spynyng of the same the delyPe therof shalbe by even just and true poise and'weight of haberdepois sealid by auctorite not excedyng in weight after the rate of xij pounde Wolle seymed above oon quart* of a pound for the waste of the same wolle and in noon other maner; And that the breker or kember to delyp agayn to the seid Clothier the same Woll so broken and kempt and the carder and Spynner to delyP agayn to the same Clothier yeme of the same Woll by the same even just and true poise and weight the wast thereof excepted without any part therof concealyng or eny more oyle water or other thyng put therunto deceyvably upon payn to be sett upon the pillorie or the Cukkyngstole Man or Woman as the case shall requyre upon due prof of suche deceyte afore and by the discrecyon of the Maire Baily or other Hede Officer of Citie Burgh or Town where the deceyt shall appere, The same Maire Baily or Hede Officer callyng to hym such psones as shall seme to hym convenyent for the prof of suche deceyt. Item that the Wever whiche shall have the wevyng of eny wollen yeme to be webbed into cloth shall weve werk and put into the webbe for Cloth to be made therof asmoche and all the same yerne as the Clothier or eny psone for hym shall delyp to the same WeP with his usyd mark put to the same without changyng or eny pcell therof levyng out of the same webbe or that restore to the same Clothier the surpluis of the same yeme if eny be left not put into the same Webbe and without eny more oyle brene moistur dust sonde or other thyng deceyvably puttyng to or castyng to the same Webbe upon payne to be sett upon the pillorie by prof discredon and in mare as is aforeseyd. Item that no ma8 psone bye eny coloured Wolle or coloured wollen Yeme of eny Carder Spynner or WeP but onely in open Markett upon payn to be sett upon the pillorie in man! aforeseyd. Item that the Walker and Fuller shall truely walke fulle thikke and werke evy webbe of wollen yeme whiche he shall have to walke fulle thikke or werke without eny Flokkes or any other man! deceyt to be usyd in the same and shall not rowe nor werke any Clothe or Webbe with any Cardes on the right side nor of the wrong side upon payn to be sett upon the pillory in ma9 afore rehersed. Item that the Clothier nor other psone whatsoeP he be after the fest of Midsofi next cumyng shall not put eny cloth to sale which when it shalbe full wette shall shrynke more than oon yerd in all the lengtit and oon quar? of a yerd in the brede for the more pt therof \ and clothes callyd Narowes or Straites after the rate, upon payn to forfet for epy clothe otherwise put to sale iij s. iiij d. and besydf that to deducte of his price for the same to be rebated to the byer therof asmoche after the rate as the same clothe so otherwise put to sale beyng full wette shall shrynke more than a yerd of that it was in lengtit tyme of the same sale and as it shall beyng wette shall want of the brede of oon yerd and iij quarPs of a yerd. CHAPTER IX.

An Acte against disguysed psons and Wearing of Visours.

II.

And on Persons selling or keeping Visours.

FORASMOCHE as lately wythin this realme dyvers psones have disgysed and appareld theym, and covert theyr fayces with Vysours and other thyngf in suche manro that they sholde nott be knowen and divers of theym in a Companye togeder namyng them selfe Mummers have comyn to the dwellyng place of divers men of honor and other substanciall psones; and so depted unknowen; Wheruppon Murthres felonye Rape & oder greate hurtes & inconveniences have afore tyme growen and hereafter be lyke to come by the colour therof, yf the seid disordre shulde contynue not reformed: Wherfore be it ordeyned and enacted by the Kyng oure Sou\?aign Lorde, & by the Lordes spuall & temporall & the Comens in this psent pliament assembled and by the au&oride of the same, That yf eny p6one herafter dysgyse or apparell them wyth Vysoures or other wyse uppon theyr faces, and so disgysed or apparelde as Mommers or psones unknowen by reasone of theyr apparrell assocyate or accompanye theym to geder or aparte and attempte to entre or entre into the house of eny psone or psones, or assawte or affraye make uppon eny p6one in the Kingf hye waye, or in eny other place in forme aforeseid disgysed. That then the seid Mommers or disgysed p6ones and e9y of theym shalbe arreasted by eny of the Kingf liege people as Suspedes or Vacabundes and be comitted to the Kingf gaole, Ther to be imprisoned by the space of thre monthes wythowte bayle or maymprys, and then to make fyne to the Kyng by the discresdon of the Justices by whome they shalbe delyverd owte of prisone. And also it is ordined and enacted by the seid auctoride that yf eny psone or p6ones sell or kepe eny Vysoures or Vysoure in his house or in eny other place wythin this realme after the feaste of Easter nexte comyng and after this acte pelaymed. That the seid psone that kepyth the seid Vysoure or Vysoures shall forfeyte to the King oure Soupaigne Lorde for e9y Vysoure xx11 shillyngf; and ferther shall suffre imprisonament and make fyne after the discresdon of the Justices afore whome he ys therof convicted, by examyna£6n or by inquisic&n after the course of the comen lawe. And that the Justices of the Peace in their sessions, and Justices of gaole deliPey and all other the Kingf Justices have auctoride to enquere hiere & defmeyn all the fPmisses as well by examinaflfa as by inquisidon after the course of the Comen lawe. And this acte to endure to the nexte pliament.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte for the serching of Oyles within the Cytty of London.

PRAYEN yowre Highnesse the Comens in this psent pliament assembled, that where as dips ma8 of Oyles ben brought in to this realme as well into the Cide of London as to diPs oder places wythin this same realme whiche be daylye used & mynystred aswell for mannys sustynaunce and comforte as for necessaryes for drapyng of Wollen Clothes and for oder dyvers necessaries used for the weale of yowr Subgie&f, & for lake of goode oPsyght serche and correction of suche Oyles meny sympyle psones byers of the seid Oyles to selle afterwarde falsely and deceyvablye by craftye meanes doo myxe and alter the same Oyles frome their former nature and goodnesse to the greate loste jeopdye and daunger and deceyte of yowre Subgie&f; Wherfore be it by yor Highnesse by thadvyse & assent of yor Lordes spuall & temporall k of yor Comens in this ffeent pliament assembled and by au&oride of the same ordeyned enabled and establisshed That the Mayre of the Citie of London for the tyme beyng wyth the Maister and Wardens of the misterie or crafte of Talloughchaundelers of the same Cide for the tyme beyng shall fromehensforthe have foil power and audoride to serche all man8 of Oyles brought in to the seid Cide of London to be solde in whos handes so eP they be or shalbe founde; And that as often as the case shall requyre; And that the seid Mayre wyth the seid Maister & Wardens of the seid mys?ye or crafte of Talloughchaundelers for the tyme beyng shall truely serche and oPsee that the same Oyles to be putt to sale, be not myxte nor altered frome their ryght kyndes but that they be good and lawfoll as they ought to be. And be it further enacted by the seid auftoritie, that the Mayre in evy Citie Borough and Towne wythin this realme wher Mayre ys for the tyme beyng, or the GoPnoure or GoPnoures or Rulers of evy other Cide Borough and Towne corporate wythin this realme also for the tyme beyng, shall have wythin their Jurisdicc6n libde and Frauncheses evy of theym lyke au&oride and power to make and do lyke serche ordure direcdone correction punysshment and execucion of the same, of for & uppon all Oyles beyng defeSyfe or discey-vablye or falsely myxed and altered by eny psone or psones wythin theyr libties and Frauncheses in manner & forme as ys afore rehersed as the seid Mayre Maister and Wardens of the seid Cide of London by this psent Acte have or moughte have of for or uppon any Oyle solde or to be solde wythin the seid Cide of London.

PR ATEN the Comons in this psent pliament assembled, that for asmoch as the land of Bretayne and also the haven of Brest lyeth streight ayenst the South see costes of the Countie of Cornwall and that the Frenchemen or aunden enemyes and Bretaynes enemyes by reason of theire fysshyng upon the se costes knowe aswell evy haven and creke within the sayde Countie as evy landyng place in as large maner as any subgiett of or SoPrigne Lorde the Kyng dooth ; And that the said Countie is thre score and ten myle in lengfit and the substaunce therof right litle more than six myle in brede from the Southsee to the Northsee, by reason wherof they also knowe that grete multitude of people can not shortly resort to put theym of at theire landyng; And that in divs and many of the seyd landyng placf nother pile blokhouse ne Bulwork is made to greve or annoye theym at their landyng; Whiche consideracions unto or sayd enemyes grete audadte comfort and corage gyveth to arrive and land in the same parties, to the grete annoyance of or sayd Sovaigne Lordis subgiettf there and to the utterly undoyng of dyPs and many of theym oonles a remedie be the soner pvyded: Therfor be it enacted by the Kyng or Sovaign Lord his Lordes spuell and temporell and the Comons in this fPsent pliament assembled and by au&orite of the same that the Justices of the Peace and Shiref of the sayd Countie do ride and viewe all the sayd Southcost from Plymmouth Westward, to the Landes ende. De Subsidio Regi conceff.

To the King oure Sou9aign Lorde.

FIR ASMOCHE as it ys openly and notoryously knowen unto all psones of Cristes Religion, That Lewes the Frensche Kyng adversary unto owre moste drade Sovereigne and naturall liege Lorde Kyng Herry the viij111 and to this hys realme of Englande hathe moved and styred and dayly moveth Sc styreth by all the subtyle meanes to hys powre to sett and bryng scisme variaunce and asmoche as in hym lyeth studyeth the meane of contynuall errour to be had in the Churche of Cryste. Takyng of late uppon hym ageyn the wyll and mynde of oure holy Fader the Pope the hole Courte of Rome and holy Churche, to somon and call a Councell to be holden at the Citie of [ - - - 1 ] Wherunto emonge other of hys abhomynable presumpeion he letted not by playne declaracion of his seid malicious [- - - - «] to somon our holy Fader the Pope to have there appered in hys propre parsone, and in the same Councele psumptiously contrary to the lawes of Gode and all holy Churche pceded, And in the same towarde the further execucion of hys cruell malice, And to thentente to have the hole Rule & govemaunce of all holy Churche under hys domynyon and comaundement. And that the Scisme and erroures shulde in suche manner be shewen That yt shulde be right harde to be redressed or wythseid. And wythoute grounde cause or au&oritie in the same Councell caused to be decreed That our seid holy Fader shulde frome thens-forthe be sequestred of & fro all Jurisdiccion and admynystracion Papall wyth other greate terrible Decrees as by the same more at large dothe appere. And howe be it our seid holy Fader for the charetable reformacion of the seid Frensche Kyng willyng the helthe of the soule of the seid Frensche Kyng hathe for his seid psumpeons & diverse other his manifeste offences as ys be foreseid declared and publisshed the hole realme of Fraunce and all Terrytoryes under the dominyon & govemaunce of the seid Frensche Kyng to be enterdyted & so under that en?dic£on yet remayne. all manner of pennys beyng Silver & havynge the prente of the Coigne of this realme nott regardyng the quantitie greatnesse or

smalnes of the same penyes, Excepte onely peynes beryng lyke dyverse Rowles of Spurres betwyxte the barres of the Crosse.

And those penyes to be taken & have course oonlye for halpens.

Provyded alway that this Acte of graunte of a dyme & fyftene or eny other Acte made or to be made in this psent pliament in eny wyse extende nott ne be pjudiciall to eny College Halle, Hostell, or other places w‘in the Uni^siries of Oxforde and Cambrigge nor to the Colleges of oure blessed Lady of Eton & Wynchester College besyde Wynchester ne to eny Maners Lordeshyppes Landes Tenement? Possessions or Hereditament? what so e9 gyven appropreed amortesed or ptcynyng to eny of the seid Colleges, Halles, Hostelles, or places, but that they & e9y of theym by what soe9 name or names the seid Colleges, Halles, Hostelles, & Playces, or eny of theym be called be qwyte & discharched ayenste us for payment of the seid xv« and x« and of e9y parte & parcell of the same, The seid Acte or graunte or eny thyng therm conteyned in eny wyse notwythstondyng: Provyded alway that this Acte ne

CHAPTER VI.

An Acte that Surgeons be discharged of Constableshipe & other thinges.

SHE WITH unto your discrete wisedomes your humble oratours the Wardens and felisship of the crafte and misPye of Surgeons enfraunchesid in the Citie of London not passyng in nombre xij psones: That wher as they and their pdecessours from the tyme that noo mynde is to the cont'rie aswell in this noble Citie of London as in all other Cme* and Boroughes within this Realme or elhs wher, for the contynuall Qvice and attendaunce that they daily and nyghtly at all houres and tymes gyve to the Kinges liege People for the relefe of the same according to their science have ben exempte and discharged from all offices and besynes wherin they shuld use or bere any man! of armoure or wepyn, And with like privilege have ben entreatid as Herawdes of Armes aswell in batelles and feldes as other places ther for to stond unhamesed and unwapenned according to the lawe of armes, because they be psones that nev used feates of warre nor ought to use but onely the besynes and excise of their science to the helpe and comforth of the Kinges liege people in the tyme of their nede: And in the forsaid Citie of London from the tyme of their firste Incorporacion when they have ben many moo in nombre then they be nowe were ne9 called nor charged to be on queste watche nor other office wher by they shuld use or occupie any armor or defencible gere of Warre Wherthorugh they shuld be unredye and lettid to pra&ice their cure of men beyng in pell: Therfore for that they be so small nombre of the said felisshep of the crafte and Mis?ye of Surgeons in regarde of the grete multitude of pacientf that be and daily chaunce and infortune happenyth and cncresith in the forsaid Citie of London, And that many of the Kinges liege People sodenly wounded and hurte for defaute of helpe in tyme to theym to be shewid perisshe, And so di^se have done as evidendy is knowen, by occasion that your said Suppliauntes have ben compelled to attende upon such Constableship Watches and Juries as aforesaid ; Be it enacted and establisshed by the Kinge oure So\?aigne Lorde and the Lordes spuall and temporall and by the Comens in this P&ent Pliament assembled and by au&oritie of the same that fromhensforth your said suppliauntes be discharged and not chargeable of Constableshipp Watch and of alman! of office beryng any armour and also of all enquestes and juries within the Cide of London; And also that this Acte in all thynge do extende to all Barbours Surgeons admytted and approved to exccise the said MisPye of Surgeons according to the forme of the Statute lately made in that behalfe: So that they excede ne be at one tyme above the nombre of xij psons.

V.

The Commissioners shall name sufficient Persons to be the Collectors ; and deliver to them an Estreat containing the Names of the Officers, and the Sums of each Hundred, See,

The Collectors shall appoint Days and Places of Payment; and give Notice thereof.

On Non-payment by the Officers of the Sums comprised in the Estreats, the Collectors may levy same upon them by Distress and Sale.

The Commissioners by their Discretion may punish by Fine or Imprisonment any Disobedience or Resistance to this Act.

CHAPTER V.

Acte conc?nyng pulling downe of townes.

CHAPTER XII.

Acte that Norfolk Wolles be not caried oute of this Realme.

WHERE as moche people beyng in the Cide of Norwich and Countie of Norfolk have been well occupied by Wolles which have growen in the seid Countie of Norff as in spynnyng wevyng of Worsted sheryng therof dyeng and calendryng of the same, wherby greate comodi tie of Worstedf and Stamyngf have been well maynteyned within this Realme; And allthough the seid Wolles growyng in the seid Shire of Norff be noon Staple Wolles yet be there dy9se Straungers intendyng the distruccion of the seid Comoditie of Worsted makyng to be used in this Realme have now of late conveyed out of the same Countie of Norff by shippes in to the parties of Hohnd and Seland beyonde the See grete plentie of Wolles that hath growen in the seid Countie of Norff and upon the borders of the same of which lyke Wolles the said Worstedf and Stamyngf have been accustumed to be made within the seid Citie and Countie, which Wolles in noo wyse woll §ve to drape or make any wollen clothes but only §ve to thuse of making of the seid Worstedf, And of them as yet is seid the seid Straungers and Alyens intende to make Worstedf and Stamyngf in the seid parties beyond the See to the utter undoyng of the seid Citie and Countie and distruccion of the seid Comodities of Worsted if remedy be not therfore redely pvyded; Wherfore by the assent of the Kyng oure Sovaign Lord and his Lordf spuall and temporal! VI. Discharges of Arrears by Executors of this Ad.

VII.

Process from the Exchequer for Payment of such Arrears.

VIII. Release of Amerciaments on former Process.

IX.

Executors of this Act may take the Oaths from all Accountants; and make them due Allowances ;

and may imprison Accountants found in Arrear, or refusing to account, &c. as the Barons of the Exchequer might do.

Accounts shall be ingrossed and signed by Two Executors of this Act, and delivered into the Exchequer, and the Accountants thereupon acquitted,&c.

Accounts shall be so ingrossed within Half a Year after they are passed. Process shall be issued by the Barons at the Request of the Executors.

The King may appoint some of his Council to be Comptrollers of such Executors.

XXV.

The Chancellor, &c. shall determine on Doubts relative to this Ad.

XXVI.

Ad not to extend to Colledors of Subsidies, dec.

XXVII.

The King may by Privy Seal appoint Accounts to be taken before other Persons, or in the Exchequer.

VII. Persons shall be rated where they are dwelling;

or, if abroad, where last resident; at the highest Rate;

but not to be doubly charged, both for Lanas and Goods,

&c.

Anno 7° HENRI Cl, VIII. A.D. 1515

STATUTES MADE IN THE SESSION OF PARLIAMENT BEGUN TO BE HOLDEN at Westminster, by Prorogation, on Monday the Twelfth Day of November,

AND CONTINUED TO BE HOLDEN UNTIL THE TWENTY-SECOND DAY OF DECEMBER,

In THE SEVENTH Year of the Reign of K. HENRY, VIII.

Evils resulting from Decay of Towns, &c.

Towns, &c. decayed shall be re-edified, &c. withinOne Year.

All Tillage Lands turned to Pasture shall be restored again to Tillage.

Half the Value of Lands and Houses ncgle&ed shall be forfeited to the King or Lord of the Fee, until re-edified, when the Ownermay re-enter.

CHAPTER I.

Thacte advoidyng pullyng downe of Townes,

rpHE Kyng our Sovaigne Lord callyng to his most blessid remembraunce that where greate ynconvenyentf be and JL dayly encrease by desola£6n pollyng downe & destrucc6n of houses and townes wythin this realme and leyng to pasture londf which customably have bene manured & occupyed wyth tyllage and husbandry, wherby Idelnes doth encrease, for where in sdme oon towne CC psons men and women and childem and their auncestours oute of tyme of mynde were daylye occupied and lyved by sowyng of corne and greynes bredyng of catall and other encreace necessarye for manys sustenance, and now the seid psons and their pgenyes be mynysshed and decreasyd, wherby the husbandry which is the greatyst comodite of this realme for sustenance of man ys greatly decayed. Churches, destrued the Svyce of God wythdrawen, Chrysten people their buryed, nott prayed for, the Patrons and Curatf wronged. Cities Markett Townes brought to greate ruyne and decaie, Necessaries for mannys sustenance made scarce and dere, the people sore mynysshed in the realme, wherby the poure & defence therof ys febled and enpayrid, to the high dyspleasure of God and agenst his lawes and to the subPcyon of the edmon Weale of this realme and desolac&n of the same, yf substancyall and spedy remedy be nott therof pvyded; Wherfore the Kyng our Sovaigne Lord by thadvyse and assent of the Lordf Spuall & Temporall and the Comons in this psent parliament assembled and by thau&orite of the same, ordeynyth stablyssheth and ena&eth, that all suche townes, villages, borowes & hamlettf tythyng houses and other enhabitaebns in any paryshe or parysshes wythin this realme, wherof the more part the first daye of this psent parliament was or were used and occupied to tillage & husbandrye by the owner or owners therof for their synguler pfit availe & lucre wylfiilly syth the seid first daye be or hereafter shalbe suffred or caused to fall downe and decaye, wherby the husbondry of the seid townes vyllages boroughes hamlettf tythyng houses and other enhabitaebns & parysshes wythin this realme bene or hereafter shalbe decaied, & toumed frome the seid use and occupacyon of husbandry and tyllage into pasture, shalbe by the seid owner or owners their heires successours or assignes or other for theym, within oon yere next after suche wylfull decaie, reedified & made ageyn mete & convenyent for people to dwelle and enhabite in the same, and to have use and therin to exercyse husbondry and tyllage as att the seid fyrst day of this psent parliament or sythyn was there used occupied and hadde, after the raaner and usage of the countrey where the seid lond lyeth, att the costf and chargf of the same owner or owners their heires successours or assignes. And yf sythyn the seid first day of this psent parliament any landf, which att the same first day or sythyn were comonly used in tyllage, bene enclosed or frome hensforth shalbe enclosed and toumed only to pasture, wherby any house of husbondry wythin this Realme ys or shalbe hereafter decayed, that then all suche landf shalbe by the same owner or owners their heires successours or assignes or other for them, wythin oon yere nexte ensueng the same decaye, putt in tyllage and exercysed used and occupied in husbandry and tyllage, as they were the said first day of this psent parliament or any tyme sythen after the maner and usage of the countrey where suche land lyeth; And yf any pson or psons do confrye to the pmysses or any of them, that then ytt be leafull to the Kyng yf any suche landf or houses be holden of hym immediatlye after office or inquisicbn founden therof comPhendyng the same mater of recorde, or to the Lordf of the fees yf any suche landf or houses byn holden of theym immediatlie withoute office or inquisi£5n therof hadde, to receye yerely half the valewe of the yssues and pfittf of any such landf wherof the house or houses of husbandry be nott so mayntenyd and sustayned, and the same half dele of the yssues and pfitf to have hold and kepe to his or

CHAPTER II.

The maynten*nce of the Kingf Navye.

XX THERE in the parliament holden at Westm the [second1] [yere of the reyngne1] of the late Kyng Henry V v the vii* ytt was enadyd by the audorite of the parliament, for the maynten*nce of the [Navie of thys Realme of Englond’] and the marynours of the same, that noo maner of pson shuld bryng into this realme of Englond [Ierlonde Walys Calys or the4] marches thereof or into Berwyke any Wynes of the growyng of Guyon Gascoyne or [Woode callyd Tolowys Woode, but suche as shalbe3] conveyd adventuryd and brought in Shipp or in Schyppis wberof our seid Sovaign Lord or [sume of hys6] subjedes of this realme of Englond Ireland Walys Calys or Berwyke bene Owners Possessours and Pprietaries, and the Masters & Maryners of the same Schipp be Englysshe Ieryshe or Walyshe, or men of Berwyke Calys or marches of the same for the more partie, upon payn of fbrfeyture of the same wynes & Tolowys woode soo brought in cont'ry to the seid ade; And now of late dyvers psons aswell alienes as denezyns have opteyned of our Sovaign Lord the Kyng that now ys dyPse lycensys to bryng in wynes of the growyng of Gascoyn and Guyon & Tolowys woode, whych lycensys be to the grete hurt {Pjudyce & to the dekay of the seid Navye of this realme & the maryners of the same: Whbrfork be ytt enadid by the audorite of this fPsent parliament that all suche lycensys here before made, nott executed before the feast of Pentecost next comyng, shalbe for as moche as then shalbe nott executed before the seid feast from thensforth to be voyde and of none effed.

STATUTES MADE IN THE SESSION OF PARLIAMENT BEGUN TO BE HOLDEN

in the City of London, on Wednesday the Fifteenth Day of April,

In the FOURTEENTH Year of the Reign of K. HENRY, VIII.

AND AFTERWARDS PROROGUED, CONTINUED, AND ADJOURNED TO WESTMINSTER,

AND THERE HOLDEN

From Friday the last Day of July until Thursday the Thirteenth of August, In the FIFTEENTH Year of the Reign of the said King:

AND THEN ENDED AND DISSOLVED.

No Inhabitant of this Realm shall sell Broad White Woollen Cloths to Alien Merchants, upon Pain of 40s.

Proviso, that if any Subjcft on bringing such Cloths to Blackwell Hall, do not sell them mi Eight Days, he may sell them to Alien Merchants.

CHAPTER I.

Thacte con&iyng the conveying Pnsportyng and cariyng of Brode Whyte Wollen Clothes out of this Realme.

FOR ASMOCH as Marchaunt Strangers study eng and imagynyng the policies, wayes and meanys to set awarke the people inhabited in forren Countryes and Regions with and by the comodities of this Realme and to bryng the Kynges naturall Subject es from occupadon to idlenes. Do dayly convey t*nsporte and carie out of this Realme of Englond for their owne singuler lucre a great nombre of Brode Whyte Wollen Clothes to be coulored dyed and wrought in dyv*s and sondrie partes beyond the See to the great encrease comforte pfitte and advantage of the people inhabited in the said outwarde and forren regions, and to the utter ruyne decaye impoPysshyng and undoyng of a great nombre of the Kynges owne naturall Subjects; And for the effectuall furtheraunce of the said evyll ententes and purposes in the pmysses the said marchaunt straungers aswell by colour of enhaunsyng of pryce of the said Clothes for long dayes of payement as by fayr pmyses and subtyle adulacions, have heretofore gotten and regrated into their hondes an innumerable nombre of the said Clothes upon their credens amountyng to great somes of money ferre excedyng their own valours and substaunce, which somes of money many and oftyn tymes they have not payed accordyng to their apoyntmentes whereby the Makers of the said Clothes subtilly compassed by and with their layr and flateryng pmyses have susteyned importable losses to the great impov^ysshyng of this the Kynges owne Realme, and to the enrichyng of the Regions and Countries of foren Prynces: For remedy wherof be it enacted by the Kyng our Soveign Lorde and the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Commens in this psent parliament assembled and by auctorite of the same, that frome the feast of Saynt Michaell tharchaungell next comyng, no pson or psonnes inhabited withyn this Realme of what estate degre or condicion soe$ he be of, shall sell or delyv* or cause to be solde or delyPed withyn this Realme by contracte covenaunt bargeyn gifte or any of them or otherwyse, to any Schaunt or Schauntes straungers beyng borne in any of the parties beyond the See or ellf where oute of the Kynges Obeysauncc or to any of his or their Factours deputies or attoumeys straungers or Englishmen, to the use of the said Schaunt or Schauntes straungers, any ma8 of brode whyte Wollen Clothes made or hereafter to be made withyn this Realme of Englond upon payne to forfait xl s. for ev*y clothe solde or delyv^ed after the said feast of Seynt Michaell cont*rie to theffecte and fourme of this psent acte; the one halfe of eQy such forfeyture to be to thuse of our Soveign Lorde the Kyng, And the other halfe therof to be to the pson or psonnes other then the Offender, that wyll fyrst sue for the same by origynall of Dett Byll Playnt or Informacion in any of the Kynges Courtes after the usuall course of the Lawes and Customes of the Realme in which sute or acdon the Defendaunt or Defendauntes shall nat be admytted to wage ther Lawe, ne any essoyne lycence or pteccion shall be allowed. IN moste humbly wyse besechen Your Highnes your true and faithfoll Subjects and da^Jly Qvauntf the Six Clerkf of your High Courte of Chaun?ie j That where as of old tyme a custome hath be used in the said Courte that almaS of Clerkf and Ministres of the same Court wrytyng to the greate Seale shuld be unmaried except onely the Clerk of the Crowne so that aswell the Coursetours and other Clerkf as the Six Clerkf of the said Chaun?ie wer by the same cust5me restrayned frome manage whereby all those that confry to the same did marie wer noo longer suffred to write in the said Chaun&ie not onely to ther great hynderaunce losyng therby the benefyt of ther long studie and tedious labours and payne in youth taken in the said Court but also to the great decaye of the true course of the said Court. Provyded alwey that by any thyng in this Acte conteigned the Maister of the Rolles for the tyme beyng be not fpjudiced either in the gevyng and disposidon of the said Offices from tyme to tyme as hath bene heretofore accustomed the forfeyture of that Offices by reason of manage onely except And that the said Officers which nowe be and hereafter shalbe, do geve such attendaunce unto the said Maister of the Rolles for the tyme beyng as heretofore in the said Offices hath bene accustomed.

The Kynges Revenues.'

THE KYNGES pfeastir is that almaS Chambleyns Receyvours Baylyffes Fermours Occupiers and all other whatsoeP Accomptauntes and psonnes, chargeable to his Highnes to accompt of the Lordshippes honours londes tenementes and other hereditamentf possessions and revenues underwritten, that heretofore hath ben, nowe be and hereafter shalbe in the hondes and possession of our said Soveign Lorde, or of or for any prest lone frome the Kynges Highnes or other mater underwryten, shall accompt and atinswer yerely and fro tyme to tyme as the case shall requyre before the GeSall Surveyours of his londes, accordyng to the adfce of pliament whereunto this Cedule is annexed; and all the somes of Money comyng or growyng upon the accomptes and issues of the same to be payed yerely and fro tyme to tyme as they shalbe receyved and due, to the handes of the Tresaurer of the Kynges Chamber for the tyme beyng to thuse of his Highnes and in none otherwyse: And also the Kynges Highnes woll and comaundeth the Tresaurer and Barons of his Eschequyer that they ne award ne suffer to be awarded nor made oute of the said Eschequyer any pcesse or execucion, for any accompt or other thyng to be aunswered or made before them of any of the lordshippes possessions and other revenues or somes of money underwryten, nor for any Ma8s lordshippes londes tenementes or other pfittes aunswered or to be aunswered to the Kyng and comprised in accompt of any Receyvour of the said possessions underwrytten, though yt appere not to be parcell of the charge or receipt of the said Receyvour of any such londes or parte or parcell of the said enheritaunce wherof the same Receyvour is deputed Officer, unto such tyme as they have otherwise in comaunde-ment frome his Grace by writyng, but if it be desired and requyred of them by writyng of the said GeSall Surveyours for the tyme beyng or by the Writyng of oon of them; which pcesse so desired his Grace willeth and comaundeth to be made with all diligence.

npHE Kynges humble and lovyng subjedes in this |3sent parliament assembled callyng to remembraunce and consideryng that our JL Soveign Lorde the Kyng after his Royall Viage with puissant army into Fraunce, his vi&orious Warre there, and his triumphant retume thens, intendyng the further pursute of his noble enterprise aswell for the reducyng of Lewes the late Frenche Kyng from the scisme and division of Christendome unto the due obedience of the See Apostolyque, as the Realme of Fraunce to the obedience rule and go9nauncc of our said Soveign Lorde accordyng to his very just right and title, yet that notwithstandyng at the humble and instaunt sute of the said late French Kyng was content of his high goodness to take an honorable peace in such goodly wise as is thorowe all christen nacions right well knowen ; In which peace our seid Soveign Lorde of his blessyd disposicion had so great zele and good mynde fermely to stande and pse9e that his Grace nat onely upon the like sute of Fraunces nowe French Kyng renovelyd the peace, lege and amyte with hym after the discease of the said Kyng Lewes, But o9 that of his ferther g*cious zele and studie to the uni?sall quyet suertie savegarde weale and encrease of all Christendome to thende and intent that all Christen Nacions beyng in unyte rest and concorde among them self myght with one mynde holy con9t their strength and power ageynst the Infideles and enymyes of the christen faith, solicited peured obteigned and brought aboute an amyte, lege and peace betwene our Holy Father the Pope ThempeTOur and all Christen Prynces nat onely uni?sall but also duryng any of their lyves ppetuall; After which amyte, lege, and uni9sall peace in such wise concluded covenaunted and swome, the French Kyng nothyng regardyng his pmyse othe and covenaunt nor the comen harme that by his unjust and ungoodly breche was likely to ensue,and sith hath ensued among all Christen Regions, hath not oonly made Warre upon Thempour the Kynges dere Frende and Alye, but also where our said Sovaign Lorde the Kyng dy9s and sundrie wayes toke susteigned and endured great payne traveyle coste and charge not oonly to enftayne thamyte with the French Kyng for his owne parte, but also by good and honorable meanys to reconsyle hym ageyn to Thempours Majeste, The French Kyng agaynwarde not onely coude nat be enduced to any reasounable condicions of peace with Themperour, but also moost unkyndeley reaunswered our said Soveign Lordes kyndenes with manyfest injuries and wronges, nat lettyng to take his subje&es, arrest and raunsome them in tyme of peace both by See and Lande, nat oonly ageynst his lege and amyte but also cont*ry to his owne savecondu&e j And o9 that unjustly withdrewe and withhelde nat onely the Dower due to Mary the French Quene Dowagier of Fraunce the Kynges dere suster, which was ex^ssly covenaunted to be payed to her duryng her life to what place or countrie soe9 shee shulde dy?t aswell in Warre as in Peace, but also reteyned and refused to paye the yerely tribute and pencion that he had bounde hymself to paye to the Kynges Highnes and his heires under payne of fallyng in to the censures of the Church, into which by his unjust deteynyng he hath incurred > And with all this nat satisfied ageynst his othe and covenaunt sent the Duke of Albany into Scotland to take the go9naunce of that Realme and the yong Kyng into his hondes, to the open daunger and parill of lyfe of the Kynges dere Nephue and to pvoke the Scottes at that tyme desyrous of peace to reare Warre against this the Kynges

Thacte conSnyng the Kynges Honour of Beuleu.

F)RASMUCH as the Kyng our Soveign Lord hath lately caused a Palesse Roiall to be byelded and edified at his Manour of Newhall in his Countie of Essex at his great costes and charges to the which place his Highnes hath great pleasure to resorte for the helth comforte and preservacion of his moost roiall pson; In consideracion wherof his Grace intendith to annexe and unite to the same his Manours of Wrytle Boyton Haydon Hattefeld Bradok Bromshobury and Chepynge Ongor and the Hundredes of Ongor and Harlowe with ther appurtenaunces in his said Countie of Essex, which late came to the hondes of his Highnes by the atteynder and forfeyture of Edward late Duke of But: And to make his said Manour and Palais of Newhall and the said Manours and Hundredes so to the sayed Manour and Palais of Newhall annexed to be an Honour Roiall: And that his said Manour and Palais of Newhall shalbe the Chieff and Capitall place of the said Honour. CHAPTER XXI. Thactk of Au&orite.

TIE Kyng oure Sovaigne Lorde consideryng that dy9s and many psones wherof sume of thcym be deceased and sume of theym ben on life have ben atteynted of high treason for dy9s treasons by theym comitted and doon ayenst their iiaturall dutye of their allegeaunce, yet ne9theless the Kyngis Highnes of hys moost goodly and blessed mynde and of hys especiall grace enclyned to iScy and pitie consideryng the mentis and desertis of the seid offenders or such as shuld have ben their heires if the seid Atteyndours had not ben hadd, is agreed and contentid that it be enacted by his Highnes and the Lordes spuall and temporal! and the Comons in this psent parliament assembled and by thau&oritie of the same, That hys seid Highnes fromhensforth duryng hys life shall at hys pleasoure have full au&oritie and power by hys ires patentis under hys greate Seale to revise adnulle repele and avoyde the atteyndours of all and synguler parsones and e9y of theym as have ben atteynted of high treason by au&oritie of parliament or by the comon lawe at eny tyme fro the xxiju daye of Junye the first yere of the reigne of Kyng Richard the thirde or any tyme syn or any tyme duryng this psent parliament. And furthermore that the Kingis Grace by his seid ires patentis under his greate Seale have full au&oritie and power to enhable the seid psones so atteynted and e9y of theym and such as shuld have ben their heires if the seid Atteynders had not ben, in name blode pemynence and dignytie and to restore the same psons and e9y of theym to all such Castellis Manours Landes tends rends regions possessions and hereditamentis as at the tyme of the seid restitucion shall reste or be in the handes or possession of oure seid Sovaigne Lorde by reason of the seid Atteyndours or any of theym, as if the seid psones atteynted had not ben atteynted nor any such Atteynders had ne9 ben had or made; And that the seid ires patentis rehersyng the seid recall repell adnullacion and avoydaunce of the seid a&e or a&es of Atteynders or of the seid judgement or judgementis of Atteynders and the inhablementis of the seid psones or eny of theym that it shall pleas the Kyngis Highnes soo to enhable and the restitucion of the enheritaunce conteigned in any of oure seid Sovaigne Lorde the Kyngis ires patentis at eny tyme herafter to be made accordyng to theffe&e of this a&e shalbe as good effectuall and avaylable in the Lawe to e9y of the same psones to whome they shalbe made and to their heires and assignes after theffe&e tenour p'porte grauntis and wordis of the same, as if the same maters wordis tenours and prportis cooteigned in any of the seid ires patentis so made were fully ena&id established and au&orised by au&oritie of parliament.

CHAPTER I.

The Kynges Highnesse his geSall pdon.

THE KYNG oure Soveraigne Lorde, callyng to his blessed and moost gracious remembraunce the dayly and manyfolde daungers wherin his good and lovyng subje&es of this his realme of England doo and may incurre by thynges done ppretrated and comytted contrary to the Ordre of his Lawes, and havyng alway tender iye with mercy pyte and compassion toward his said Subjects, myndyng of his high goodnes and greate benignyte so always to ymparte the same unto them, as Justice beynge dayly administred all rigour be excluded, and the greate and benivolent myndes of the Kynges said Subjects largely and many tymes approved toward his Highnes by corespondence of gratitude reacquited; Cum of Refusal of Executors to ad in the Sale of Lands devised.

Where some of the Executors refuse, and others desire, to ad in Execution of a Will, Bargains and Sales of Lands, devised to be sold, shall be good if made by the ading Executors only.

CHAPTER VL

An Acts conSoinge the takinge of Mortuaries or demaundinge receivinge or clayminge of the same.

FOR AS MOCHE as questyon ambyguyte and doute is chaunced and rysen upon the ordre maner and fourme of demaundyng receyvyng and claymyng of Mortuaries otherwise called Corse presentes, as well for the greatnes and value of the same which as hath ben lately taken is thought over excessyve to the pore people and other persons of this realme, as also for that suche Mortuaries or Corse presentes have been demaunded and levyed for such as at the tyme of their deth have had no propart in any goodes or cattels, and many tymes for wayfaryng travelyng men in the places where they have fortuned to dye; To the entent that all dout contencyon and inctaynte herein may be removed, and as well the generalyte of the Kynges people therin remedyed, as also the Persons Vycars parysshe prestes curates and other havyng inPest in such Mortuaries and Corse presentes indyfferently provyded for: Be yt therfor enafled ordeyned and establisshed by the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons of this parliament assembled and by au&orite of the same, that from the fyrst day of Aprell in the yere of oure Lorde M VC xxx no Person Vycar, Curate nor Parisshe Prest ne any other spuall pson nor their Fermours baylyffif nor lesses shall take receyve or demaunde of any pson or psons within this Realme, for any person or persons dyeng within the same, any maner Mortuary or Corse present ne any some or sommes of money ne any other thing for the same more than is herafter mencyoned: Ne also shall convent or call any person or persons before any Judge Spuall for the Recovere of any such Mortuaries or Corse presentes or any other thyng for the same, more than is herafter mencyoned; upon payne to forfeyte for every tyme so demaundyng receyvyng takyng or conventyng or callyng any suche person or persons before any spuall Judge so moche in value as they shall take above the some lymytted by this Acte, And over that xl s. to the ptie greved contrary to this a&e ; for the whiche forfeyture the partie so greved contrary to this Acte shall have [and *] accion of det by writ by 11 playnt or informacion in any of the Kynges Courtes wherin no Wager of Lawe Esson nor Proteccyon shalbe alowed.

Fyrst it is ordeyned establisshed and enacted that no maner of Mortuary shalbe taken or demaunded of any pson what soo ever he be, which at the tyme of his deth hath in movable goodes under the value of x Marke. Also that no Mortuary shall be gyven asked or demaunded from hensforth of any maner person but only in such place where heretofore Mortuaries have ben used to be payed and gyven, and in those places non otherwise but after the rate and fourme hereafter mencioned; Ne that any person pay Mortuaryes in more places than one that is to saye, in the place of their moost dwellyng and habitacion and there but one Mortuary : Nor no Person Vicar Curate Parisshe Prest or other shall for any person dyeng or dede and beyng at the tyme of his deth of the value in moveable goodes of x Marke or more clerely above his dettes payed, and under the some of xxx ti. take for a Mortuary above thre shillynges and foure pence in the hole: And for a person dyeng or dede beyng at the tyme of his deth of the value of xxx ti. or above clerly above his dettes payed in movable goodes, and under the value of [ xxx ti. * ] ther shall no more be taken or demaunded for a Mortuary than yj s. viij d. in the hole; and for any person dyeng or ded beyng at the tyme of his deth of the value in movable goodes of xl ti. or above to any some what soo ever yt be clerely above his dettes payed, ther shall be no more taken paied or demaunded for a Mortuary than x s. in the hole.

Provyded alway that for no Woman beyng covert baron, nor chylde, ne for any person nat kepyng house any maner mortuary be payd; ne that any Person Vycar Curate Parysshe Preest or other aske demaunde or take for any such woman, chyld, or for any person nat kepyng house dyeng or ded, any maner thyng or money by waye of Mortuary; ne also for any wayfaryng man or other that dwelleth nat ne makyth resydence in that place where they shall happen to dey, but that the Mortuary of such wayfaryng persons be answerable, in places where Mortuaries be accustomed to be payed and in maner and fourme and after the rate before mencyoned and none other wise, in the place or places where suche wayfaryng persons at the tyme of ther deth had theyr moost habitacyon house k dwellyng places and no where els.

Provyded alway that it shalbe lefull to all maner of Persons Vycars Curates Parysshe Preestes and other spuall persons to take and receyve any maner some of money or other thyng which by any person dyeng shall fortune to be dysposed gyven or bequethed unto them or any of them, or to the high aulter of the Church; This Acte or any thyng therin mencyoned natwithstondyng.

CHAPTER VII.

An Acte for the punisshemente of suche §vauntf as shall withdrawe themselfes and go awaye with there Mas? or Mistres Caskettf and other Juells or Goodes comitted to them in truste to be kepte.

WHERE BEFORE this tyme dyvers aswell Noble Men as other the Kynges subje&es have upon confidence and trust delyvered to their servauntes their Caskettes and other jewels money goodes and catelles safely to kepe, to the use of theyr said Masters or Maystresses, and after suche delyvere the said Servauntes have withdrawen them self and gonne away from their said Maysters or Maistresses with the said kaskettes jewels, money, goodes and catelles or parte therof, to the entent to stele the same and defraude ther said masters or maystresses therof, and somtyme beyng with their said Masters or Maystresses have convW the said jewels money and other cattelies or parte theirof to their owne use; which mysbehavour so done was doughfull in the comon Lawe whether it were felony or nat, and by reason therof the forsaid servauntes have ben in great boldnes to comytte suche lyke Offences: Be it therfore enacted ordeyned and establisshed by the Kyng oure Soveraigne Lorde by the assent of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this present parliament assembled and by au&orite of the same *, That all and singuler such Servauntes to whome any such caskettes jewels money goodes or cattels by his or their said Maysters or Maystresses shall from hensforth so be delyvered to kepe, that if any such servaunt or §vauntes withdrawe hym or them from their said Masters and Maystresses and go awaye with the said caskettes jewels money goodes or other catelles or any parte therof, to the entent to stele the same, and defraude his or their said maysters or maystresses therof contrary to the trust and confidence to hym or them put by his or ther said maysters or maystresses, or els beyng in the servyce of his said master or maystres without assent or comaundement of his maysters or maystresses be imbesyll the same caskettes jewels money goodes or cattelies or any parte therof, or otherwise convert the same to his owne use with lyke purpose to stele yt, that yf the said caskettes jewels goodes money or catalles that any such Avaunt shall goo away with, or which he shall imbesell with purpose to stele yt as is aforsaid, be of the value of xl s. or above. That than the said false fraudelent and untrewe acte and demeanour frome hensforth shalbe demed and adjuged felony; and he or they so offendyng to be punysshed as other [ felons be punysshed for1 ] felonyes comytted by the course of the comon Lawe.

Provyded alwaye that this Acte or any thyng theirin conteyned shall nat in any wyse extende or be prejudicial! to any Apprentyce or Apprentices, nor to any person within the age of xviij yere, goyng away with his or their maysters goodes or jewels, or otherwise conPtyng the same unto his or their owne uses, duryng the tyme of their apprentyshode or beyng within the same age of xviij yeres: But that every apprentyce (1 ) apprentices such person or psons beyng within the said Age, doyng 6r offendyng contrary to this psent a&e, shalbe and stande in lyke case as they and every of them were before the makyng of this a&e. The same Acte to contynue and endure unto the next parliament.

CHAPTER XI.

An Acts for resdtuc&n to be made of the goodes of suche as shalbe robbed by Fellons.

BE YT enacted by this present Parliament, that yf any felon or felons herafter doo robbe or take away any money goodes or cattalles from any of the Kynges subjeSes, frome ther person or otherwise within this realme, and therof the said felon or felons be indyted and after arrayned of the same felony and founde gylty therof, or otherwise atteyted, by reason of evydence gyven by the partie so robbed or owner of the said money goodes or catalles, or by any other by their procurement, that then the partie so robbed or owner shalbe restored to his said money goode and cattels: and that as well the Justices of gaole delyvere as other Justices afore whom any such felon or felons shalbe founde gylty or otherwise atteynted by reason of Evydence gyven by the partie so robbed or owner or by any other by their pcurement, have power by this present Acte to awarde frome tyme to tyme wryttes of restitucion for the said money goodes and catels, in lyke maner as though any such felon or felons were atteynted at the sute of the partie in appele.

Restitution shall be made to the Owner of stolen Goods where the Felon is convided on the Evidence of such Owner, &c.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte for the Lynnen Drapers in London.

IN moost humble wyse sheweth unto the Eynges Highnes and to the Lordes Spuall and Tempo rail and the Comons in this present Parliament assembled, The Lynnen Drapers inhabytauntes within the Cyte of London, usyng to sell lynnen clothe called Dowlas and Lokeram of the c5modites wrought and made in Brytayne in the partes beyonde the See; That where by all the tyme wherof mynde of Man ys nat to the cont*ry in the tyme of the Eynges moost noble pgenytours, all suche marchantes as well Englysshe as Straungers, as at any tyme brought or conveyed the said Dowlas and Lokeram into thys Realme of Englande, brought and conveyed the same in peces or halfe peces, every hole pece of Dowlas conteynyng in length fyve score els of assyse accoptyng to every elle one ynche of Assyse, and in bredth one yarde of Assyse, and every halfe pece L. elles in length and one yarde [of1] bredth of lyke assyse. And all the hole pece and half pece of one goodnes in makyng; and aswell every pece of lokeram to be of lyke length as the hole pece of Dowlas [ and every halfe peace of lokeram to be of lyke lengthe as the halfe peace of Dowlas,*] and every such hole pece and half pece to be in bredth a hole yard lackyng a Nayle of a Yarde, and every pece and half pece to be in lyke goodnes by all the length of the same pece; which whan yt was so used was to the greate profyte of all the Eynges Subjects: And now of late within the space of xx or xxx yeres passed dyvers persons for ther owne singuler lucres have brought all the said Dowlas and Lokeram in halfe peces, which halfe pece lacketh in every suche one halfe pece of the due length foure or fyve elles and some more and some lesse, besyde the bredth of Assyse and accustomed, to the great and extreme hurt of the Eynges pore subje&es occupyers byers and sellers of the same : It may therfore please Your Highnes with the (3 ) Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Comons in this ^sent Parliament assembled and by the au&orite of the same, to ena&e and establysshe, that no person or persons Englysshe nor Straunger Denyzen or Alyen from or after the feest of Seynt Michell the Archaungell next comyng, shall brynge [and4 ] convey or cause to be conveyed or brought by any maner of meanes into this realme of England, any of the said Lynnen cloth called Dowlas and Lokerams, but only in hole peces or halfe peces of the full lengthes bredes goodnes and in Assyses as is beforsaid, and as heretofore in olde tymes hath ben accustomed and used, under payne of forfeyture of the same Dowlas and Lokeram soo to be brought or conveyed into this realme nat conteynyng the full length bredth goodnes (J) assyse, or the value therof: The one halfe to the Eyng our Soveraigne Lorde, and the other halfe of the said forfeyture to hym or them that shall take or sease the same or sue for the same by acdon informadon byll or otherwyse. In which acdons sutes or informadon no Wager of Lawe nor Esson shalbe admytted.

"TXTHERE afore this tyme dyvers persons have made leases of their Manours Landes Tefftes and other V T hereditamentes, somtyme by their Indentures and somtyme without writynges, to other persons for terme of yeres, takyng of them greate fynes for the incommes of the same leases, and after the same Leassours ther Heires or Assignes have caused and suffred recoverees to be had against them in the Court of our Soveraigne Lorde the Kyng, and in other Lordes Courtes, upon fayned and untrewe tytles, by crafte or covyn to put the said Termers firome ther said termes, and after suche recoverees had, the same [ Recoverees1 ] by reason of such recoverees and judgementes have entred into the same Maners Landes Tenementes and other Hereditamentes so to ferme Ietten and therof have expulsed the said fermers contrary to their said leasses covenauntes and agrementes: And by cause yt was doubted to some persons whether the said termers myght falsyfye such recoverees or nat. That all such termers shall and may falcyfie for his terme onely suche recoverees as well heretofore had as herafter to be had in such wyse and fburme as tenaunt of a fireholde shall and may doo by the course of the comon Lawe, where suche tenaunt of freholde was neyther prevy nor perte to the same recoveree: And that the same [ termes3 ] ther Executours and Assignes natwithstandyng such Recoverees so had, shall reteyne holde and enjoye their said Termes accordyng to their said Lesses ageynst all such [ Recoveres1 ] their heyres and assignes, as they shulde or myght have done agaynste the said Lessours yf such Recovery had nat be had ne suffred; and that the same [ Recoverer ’] ther heires and assygnes after such recovery so had, shall have lyke remedy against the said [Termes3] their Executours and Assignes, by avowry or accyon of det for the rentes and servyces reserved upon the same lesses, beyng due after the same [recoverers4] and also lyke accions against them for waste done, after the same [recoverers4] so had, in lyke maner and fourme as the said lessours shuld or myght have had yf the same [ recoverers4 ] had never be had.

And also be it further enacted by the au&orite aforsaid that no maner of statute of the Staple, Statute Marchaunt nor execution by elegit, be hereafter avoyded or in any wyse made frustrate by meanes of any such fayned recoverye; but that all persons havyng any Landes Tenementes or other Hereditamentes in execution, or beyng intytled to have execution of any Maners Landes or Tenementes by any suche meanes, shall have by force [by5 ] this Statute lyke rcmedye to avoyde and falsefy the said [ recoverers4 ] as before is ordeyned and provyded for the Lesse for terme of yeres.

CHAPTER XVL

An Acte ratefyinge a Decree made in the Sterre Chamber con&ninge Straungs Handicraftfmen intiitinge

the Realme of Englonde.

PRAYEN the Comons in this jPsent parliament assembled, that where in the [xv*116] daye of February in the xx yere of the raigne of oure nowe mooste gracyous Soveraigne Lorde Kyng Henry the viij, by our said Soveraigne Lorde the Kyng, his moost honorable Counsell in his Sterre Chambre at Westih, for the comon welth of his naturall Subjects borne within this his Realme, by great and deliberate advyse yt was demed adjuged and decreed, That no straunger artificer borne out of our said Soverayne Lorde his obeysaunce inhabytyng within any Cytie, Borough or any other place within this his Realme of England firome hensforth shuld kepe in his or their house or houses any maner of straungers servauntes borne out of hys obeysaunce but only two servauntes straungers and no mo at one tyme: And also all and singuler straungers, that than were or after the makyng of the said Decree shulde be made denysen, that at the tyme or after the makyng therof wolde inhabyte within the Cytie of London subbarbes or within two myles compas of the same, and kepe or wolde kepe houses or occupye their craft, shulde be contributaries to and with our said Soveraigne Lorde his Subjects Artifycers within the said Cyte of London, payeng beryng or susteynyng such charges as herafter shalbe expressed, that is to say; That all other strangers artyfyeers denysens or no deny sens of every handycraft or mystery, inhabytyng aswell within the Cytie of London as in any other Cyte Towne Boroughe or Village within this Realme, shulde pay here and susteyne all suche and lyke charges as our said Soverayne Lorde his Subjects of lyke craft and mystery do always use to pay ; And if any of them refused or denyed the same or any parte therof, than he or they so denyeng or refusyng so to do shulde nat any longer occupy any handy craft, upon the paynes damages and [parels7] specified, aswell in the a&es and statutes made in the xiiij & xv yeres of the raigne of oure now Soverayne Lorde, as in one estatute made in the fyrst yere of the reygne of Kyng Richard the Thred : And the same strangers denyses or no denysens housholders whiche wold remayne and abyde within our said Soveraigne Lorde his Realme, shulde upon lawful 1 warnyng to them gyven by the Mayster and Wardens of dyvers and sondry mysteries mencyoned and specyfyed in the said Deere within the said Cyties and Townes, psent themself in the Comon Halle or metyng place of the said craftes, and there to receyve and take their othe and be swome upon the Holy Evangelyst before the Mayster and Wardeyns of their said craft, to be faythfull and trewe to the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde and his heires Kynges of England and to be obedyent to hym and them and his and their Lawes :

Be yt furthermore enacted by the au&orite above said, that the Acte made in the parliament begon at London the xv day of Apryll in the xiiij yere of the reigne of oure Soveraigne Lorde the Kyng that nowe is, and frome London adjoined to Westm the last day of July in the xv yere of the reigne of our said Soveraigne Lorde, concemyng straungers artificers for takyng of apprentyces journeymen and covenaunt servauntes, and every article and pvyiyons conteyned in the same Acte, shall be frome hensforth put in due execucyon (3) to the trewe entent meanyng and purporte of the same, as well within the Cyte of London as in all other Cydes Boroughes and Townes Corporate within this Realme, and the same to endure ppetually: any thyng conteyned in the said a&e or decree to the contrary natwithstandyng.

Provyded always that no artificer alyaunt or strauger borne out of the Kynges obeysaunce, beyng a housholder or inhabytyng within any of the Uni^sities of Oxford and Cambridge, or within (4) seyntwary of Seynt Martin le Graunt within the Cyte of London, shall from hensforth have or reteyne in their servyce journeymen or apprentices beyng aliauntes or estraungers borne, above the nombre of x persons at one tyme, upon payne of the penalty conteyned in the said Acte made in the said xiiij and xv. yere of our said Soveraigne Lorde j The Provysyons conteyned or specyfyed in the 6ame Act natwithstandyng.
