WHERE of late our trewe and faythfull Subjects Artificers and Handycraftesmen borne under our obeysaunce inhabytyng within our Cytie of London and the Subbarbes of the same, exibited unto us a lamentable byll of complaynt conteynyng that nat withstandyng many good and necessary statutes and A&es of Parliament have ben edyfyed ordeyned and made, and especiall one in the fyrst yere of Kyng Rychard the thred, And the other beyng made in the (6) yere of the reigne of our derest father of noble memory Henry the vij late Kyng of this oure realme and in the xiiij and xv yere of oure reigne, concemyng the straungers artyficers and Handycraftesmen borne out of our obeysaunce usyng and exercysyng handycraftes within this our Realme of England, as well for the restraynyng of the excessyve nombre and unresonable behavour of the same straungers artificers borne out of our obeysaunce, whiche (7) contynuall resorte and repayre in to this oure said Realme dayly encreased, to the great detryment of our owne naturall Subjects Artificers of the same handycraftes and mysteries and of other sondry inconvenyences, by occasion that dyvers of the said Subjects for lacke of occupacion fall unto ydlenes, as also for the reformacion of sondry dysceytes and falshodes pra&ysed by the said straungers artyficers in ther said handycraftes to the greate damage and losse of us and of all our said natural Subjects, The said straungers artificers nothyng ponderyng or dredyng the said statutes ne the penalties in the same conteyned and expressed, cease nat cdtemptuously aswell to abuse the said statutes as moost parte entyerly to enfrynge and breke the same and to accumulate frome tyme to tyme more offences and enormytees, aswell agayne our Prerogatyve as to the detryment of the comon welth of this our Realme and our lovyng Subjects of the same, for whan any serche shalbe made in every handycrafte within any Cytie Towne or Borough Corporate within our said Realme by our

And also the great scarcyte of groyne and vytell at this f?sent tyme throughout this our Realme to be the more enforced and caused by reason of great multitude and contynuall recours of the said straungers handycraftesmen whiche consume a great porcion of come and vytall growen and bred within this our realme. And that as well all and every of the said Housholders straugers aforsaid as all other straungers artificers made or to be made denyzens that shalbe housholders and inhabyte and occupie any crafte within our said Cytie subbarbes or two myles compas of the same, as long as they shall remayne and abyde within the said Cytie subarbes and two myle compas of the same, beyng resonablie requyred and warned by the Wardens and other persons govemours in any Citie Towne or Borough corporat of their said craftes within any of our said Cyties or Townes Corpora! or by any of them for the tyme beyng or by their laufull deputies or deputye, shall go with the said Wardens or other Govemours there as no Wardens be, to make serche accordyng to the above remembred A&es of Parliament made in the xiiij and xv yere of our reigne; whiche yf they refuse to do and that proved before the Chauncellor of England or before the Mayre of London and (') other Cyties before the Chefe persons of the said Cyties or Townes for the tyme beyng, that than the said housholders or housholder so offendyng denyeng or refusyng the same, shall no lenger the same his Occupadon exercyse or use within this our Realme upon payne parell and daunger expressed in the afore remembred a&es and statutes. And that the same straungers artificers denyzens or nat denyzens housholders which will remayne and abyde within our said realme, shall upon laufull notyce (*) them gyven by the Mayster and Wardeyns of their crafte or one of them, personally present themselves in the Comon Hall or metyng place of ther said craftes within our said Cyties and Townes there as they be inhabytyng, and than and there every of them to receyve and take ther othes and be swome upon the Holy Evangelyst before the Master and Wardeyns of their said crafte and mystery within our said Cyties and Townes Corporate, to be faithfull and trew to us and our heyres Kynges of England, and to be obedyent to us and them and our and their Lawes and to all A&es Ordynaunces and Decrees made and confirmed by us and our Councell or by our Councell, and dewely and trewely at all tymes whan they shall be appoynted by the Wardeyns of their felyshippe crafte or mysterye for the tyme beyng or their deputies, to make serche with them accordyng to the purport tenure or effe&e of an Estatute and Acte of Parliament made in the xiiij and xv yere of our reigne, and have wamyng and monycyon therof by the said Wardeyns or any of them or any other their sufficient deputye or deputies in that behalfe to them made and gyven. And that they shalbe redy to go with the said Wardeyns to make the same serche ; And that they shal nat gyve notyce to any straunger of the said serche untyll they with the said Wardeyns come togyther to make the said serche; and that they shall well indefferentely and trewly behave them in the same, set all affection favoure malice and drede of any creature and all fraude and desceyte a parte. So helpe them God and all Sayntes and by the Holy Evangelyst; and their Othe so receyved in forme aforesaid the said straungers shall pay for their admyssion accordyng as our said Subjects have alway used to pay.

It is also further decreed That no straunger artificer or handycraftesman borne out of oure obeysaunce nat beyng denysyn, whiche at the day of the makyng of this Decree is nat a Housholder within this our Realme or kepeth any shoppe or shoppes within the said Cytie and subarbes or any other Cytie Towne or Borough within this oure realme, shall from that day forward set up or kepe any house or shoppe or chamber within our Cytie of London, subarbes or parisshes before rehersed, or within any other Cytie Towne Borough or Village within this our realme wherin he shall exercyse and pra&yse any handycrafte or mysterye, upon payne to encurre and ren in suche penalties as be conteyned in the Statutes before this tyme made and enacted: And that non of the said straungers artificers or handycraftemen borne out of our obeysaunce aswell denysens as other shall assemble in any company felyship congregacyon or conventycle but only in the Comon Hall of their craftes with our Subjects whiche be of the Company of their said crafte or craftes, at such tyine as they shall be commaunded and warned by the Mayster and Wardeyns of the said crafte or craftes, and at none other place and tyme or in any other maner upon payne afore exjpssed.

Provyded alwey that this decre and every parte therof con§nyng the crafte and mysterie of cordewayners shall extende as well to them that worke olde stuffe as newe within our Cytie of London, the subarbes of the same or in any other Cytie Towne Boroughe or Village within this Realme of England.

CHAPTER XVIIL

An Acte for the Towne of Newe Castell upon Tyne con?ninge the shippinge of fichaundize and unshippinge

therof within the libties of the saide Towne.

Limits of the Port of Newcastle upon Tyne; from Sparhawke to Hedwynstremes ;

Ships laden and unladen at divers Places in prejudice of the aid Port ;

HUMBLY shewen to your Highnes your trewe and faythfull Subjects the Mayre Burgeyses and Comynaltie of your Towne of Newcastell upon Tyne ; that where your Grace and your moost Noble Pgenytours Kynges of England tyme out of mynde have ben seased of the said Towne and of the Portes and Haven of the Ryver of Tyne therunto belongyng, and of all [the1] grownde with water covered within the said Ryver of Tyne, from one place in the mouth of the said Ryver called the Sparhawke, to one other place in the same Ryver called Hedwynstremes, in their demeane as of fee in right of their Crowne of England, and as parcell of the same; and duryng all the said tyme all maner of person or persons as well free men as straungers and denyzens applyeng or comyng into the said Porte Haven and Ryver from any parties of beyonde the See or of this realme of England, with Shippes or other Vessels charged or loden with any maner of wares or n?chandyses, or shippyng chargyng or lodyng any shippes or vessels with any kynde of fichandyses to be conveyed out of this said porte & haven to any partes of this realme of England or els where out of this said realme, have always duryng all the said tyme used to charge and dyscharge lode and unlode their said Goodes Wares and Marchaundyses at the said Towne of Newcastell and no where els within the said Porte & Haven, and there have always payd to your said Highnes and your said mooste Noble Progenytours all customes subsedyes tolles and other thynges due for the same amountyng yerely to the somme of fyve hundred poundes and above, wherof your Noble progenytours your Highnes and your Assignes have ben hytherto duely and truely answeryd and payed, as in your Escheker more ample and at large doth appere: The which your Towne of Newcastell is as well in tyme of warres as of peas the chefe key relyef and defence of all the parties of this [ours] realme theirunto adjoynyng; and by reason of the said liberties and fraunchesses your said Towne hath ben (3 ) this tyme well replenysshed and mayntened, in so moche as the inhabytauntes of your said Towne of late dayes have ben able to serve Your Highnes in your Warres with foure hundred Maryners or mo apte and able persons for that purpose; tyll no we of late that dyvers great personages as well Spuall as Temporall havyng landes adjoynyng to the said Porte and Ryver betwene the said Towne of Newcastell and the See, apte and easy for chargyng and dyschargyng of shyppes and iftchaundyses, have charged and dyscharged lodyd and unlodyd dyvers shyppes and Marchandyses within the said porte and Haven at the said Places nat payeng therfore any customes or other dutyes to your Highnes ; By meane whereof your said Towne is lykely to cum to utter decay and ruyne, and the inhabytauntes of the same to refuse and relynquysshe the said Towne and to repayre and resorte to the said places, to the greate dysheryson of your Highnes and mynysment of your customes subsedyes and duties and pfytes customably payed at

CHAPTER XIX.

An Acte conSninge Avouries.

WHERE as well the Noble Men of thys realme as dyvers other persons, by fines recovereys grauntes and secrete feoffementes and leases made by their Tenauntes to persons unknowen of the Landes and Tenementes holden of them, have ben put from the knowlege of their tenauntes upon whome they shulde by ordre of the Lawe make theyr Avowryes for their rentes customes and 9vyces, to their great losses and hynderaunces; Be yt therefore enacted establysshed and ordeyned by audorite of this f?sent parliament, that where soever any maner landes tenementes or other heredytamentes be holden of any maner person or persons by rentes customes or 9vyces, that yf the Lorde of whome any suche Maner landes tenementes or heredytamentes be so holden, dystrayn upon the same Maners Lands or Tenementes for any suche rentes customes or servyces and replevyne therof be sued, that the Lorde of whome the same londes tenementes or heredytamentes (3) so holden may avowe or his Baylyffe or servaunt make C.onysaunce or jusdfye for takyng of the said dystresses upon the same landes teiites or hereditamentes so holden, as in landes or tenementes within his [See4] or Seygnorye, alegyng in the said avowrye conysaunce and justificacyon the same Maners Landes and Tenementes to be holden of hym, without namyng of any person 8teyn to be Tenauntes of the same, and without makyng any avowrie justificacion or conysaunce upon any person certeyne; and lykewyse the Lorde Bayly or Servaunt to make avowrye justificacione or conysaunce in lyke maner and forme upon every wrytt sued of seconde delyveraunce.

CHAPTER XX.

An Acte that the jPsidente of the Kynges Counsaile shalbe associate with the Chauncellor and Treasourer of

Englonde and the Keper of the Kinges Privie Seale.

XXTHERE at a Parliament holden at Westmynster in the thyrde yere of the raigne of our late moost dred V v Soveraigne Lord Kyng Henry the vij, for as moche as by the unlawfull mayntenaunces gyvyng of lyvereys signes tokens and retaynders by endentures promyses othes wrytynges or otherwyse enbraceryes of hys subje&es, untrewe demeanyng of Sheryffes in makyng of Panels, and other untrewe retomes, by takyng of money by Juryes, and great ryottes and unlawfull assembles, the polecy and good [ruler *] of this realme was alinoste subdued: And for the punysshement of these inconvenyences by the accasyon of the {Pmysses nothyng or lytell myght be founde by enquyry, Wherby the lawes of the landes in execucyon myght take lytell effeSe, whiche was to thencrease of murders robyryes pjuries and unsuerties of all men lyvyng and losses of their landes and goodes, to the great dyspleasure of Almyghty God : For reformacyon of which fPmysses it was ordeyned and enadted by audlorite of the said parlyament amongest other thynges, That the Chaunceller and Tresorer of England for the tyme beynge and the Keper of the Kynges Pryve seale or two of them callyng to them a Bysshop and a Temporall Lorde of the Kynges moost honorable Councell and the two chefe Justices of the Kynges Benche and the Comon Place of the tyme beyng, or other two Justices in their absence, upon Byll or Informacyon put to the said Chaunceller for the Kyng or any other against any person for any mysbehavynge afore rehersed, shuld have au&oritie to call before them by Wrytt or by Pryve Seale the said mysdoers, and they and other by their discression by whome the trowthe myght be knowen to examyn, and such as they shulde fynde defedfyve to punysshe them after their demerytes after the forme and effedte of Statutes therof made, in lyke maner and forme as they shulde and ought to be punysshed yf they were therof convy&ed after the due order of the lawe, as by the same statute among other thynges now playnly doth appere : Neverthelesse in the same good and pfytable estatute the jPsydent of the Kynges moost honorable councell for the tyme beyng attendyng upon his most noble and ryall person ys omytted, and nat named in the said former statutes made in the thred yere of the reigne of Kyng Henry the vij to be one of the said persons that shulde have audlorite to call before them suche mysdoers so offendyng the Kynges Lawes in any of the pmysses as is before rehersed. Be yt therfore nowe by the auttorite of this [Psent parliament ordeyned and enadted, that from hensforth the Chaunceller Tresorer of England and the fPsedent of the Kynges moost honorable Councell attendyng upon his mooste honorable person for the tyme beyng, and the keper of the Kynges Pryve Seale or two of them, callynge unto them one Bysshop and one Temporall Lorde of the Kynges moost honorable Councell and the two Chefe Justices of the Kynges Benche and the Comon Place for the tyme beyng, or other two of the Kynges Justices in their absence, upon any Bill or Informacyon hereafter to be put in, the Chaunceller of England, Treasorer, Presydent of the Kynges seyd moost honorable Councell or Keper of the Kynges Pryve Seale for the tyme beyng, for any mysbehavyng before rehersed, from hensforth have full power and au&orite to call before them by Wrytt [of3] Pryve Seale suche mysdoers and them and other by their discression by whome the trouthe may be knowen to examyn, and suche as they shall fynde defeftyve to punysshe them after their demerytes after the forme and effe&e of the said former Estatute and of all other Estatutes therof tofore made and nat repelled nor expyred, in lyke maner and forme as they shulde and ought to be punysshed yf they were therof convy&ed after the due ordre in the Kynges Lawes.

And also be yt enacted by au&orite of this fPsent parliament that the said Presydent of the Kynges sayd moost honorable Counsell for the tyme beyng, yf he be than presente, may be at all tymes hereafter assocyate with the Chaunceller Tresourer of England and Keper of the Kynges Pryve Seale for the tyme beyng, aswell at the namyng of Sheryffes and settynges of Pryces of Wynes, as at all other A&es lymytted and appoynted by any statute to be done by the said Chaunceller and Tresourer or Keper of the Kynges Pryve Seale for the tyme beyng : any Acte Statute or Use heretofore made or used to the contrary natwithstandyng.

And moreover it was enacted that all Clothes of Worstedes Sayes and Stamyns made within any of the said Townes of Lynne and Great Yememouth or subarbes of the same or any of them, and marked with suche markes as sholde be lymytted to the [markers of! ] the said Wardeyns of the said Towne in maner and fourme as is above said, and [vyewed4] and sealed by any of the Wardeynes of the said Townes of Lynne and Yernemouth in forme remembred by force and vertue of the sayd ade, myght be lawfully put to sale by the owners and makers of the same without any other [ makyng5 ] or sealyng upon the same Clothes or upon any of them to be had or made (6) of or upon any of the said Clotheys for lacke of any other seales or markes ; any thyng conteyned in the said vij yere of Kyng Edwarde the fourth to the contrary natwithstandyng. And over this it was enabled that every craftes man of the said mysterye and occupacyon of Worsted makyng, dwellyng within any of the said Townes of Lynne and Yememouth and subarbes of the same, at theire owne free wylles and lyberties frome thensforth for ever myght have and take apprentyce or apprentyces beyng male of the age of [xviij7] yeres and upwarde and beyng the Kynges naturall subjedes for terme of seven yeres and nat under, so that none of them excede the nombre of two at ones to leme use and exercysc the said crafte within eyther of the said two Townes of Lynne and Great Yernemouth and subarbes of the same; all be yt the Father of the said Apprentice or Apprentices myght nat expende in Landes or Tenementes to the yerely value of xx. s. any Ade or Ordynaunce to the contrarie made or to be made natwithstandyng. Provyded alwey that the same Ade nor any thyng therin conteyned shall nat in any wyse be hurtfull or pjudycyall to the Mayre of Norwiche or to his Successour or to the Wardeyns of the said Cytie or Countie or to their successours in any poynt artycle power or audorite other than for wevyng serchyng and sealyng [of workes to the maker8 ] of Worstedes Sayes and Stamyns made or to be made onely within the said Townes of Lynne and Yermouth or subarbes of the same or to any of them, and for lymyttyng of markes to the [marker9] of Worstedes Sayes and Stamyns onely inhabyted in eyther of the said Townes and Suburbes thereof and takyng of Apprentyces in fourme above remembred ; But that the said Mayre of the said Cytie of Norwiche and Wardeyns of the same Cytie and Countie and every of them, myght have and use all other poyntes articles powers and audorities conteyned and specyfyed in the above remembred Ade made in the said seventh yere of Kyng Edwarde the iiij aswell for the searche sealyng correction and reformation of the said Wardeyns newly to be elede by the vertu of the same Ade and every of them, accordyng and after suche forme as they myght do or use any of the said Wardeyns of the said Cytie or Countye by force of the said ade made in the said vij yere of Kyng Edwarde the fourth as all and every other enqueryes corrections serches seasynges and reformacyons to be had for the trewe makyng of Worstedes Sayes Stamyns in and upon any person or persons as well within the said Townes of Lynne and Yermouth as without, without trouble let or vexacyon of any of the inhabytauntes of the said Towne, in as large and ample wyse as they myght have donne before the makyng of the said Ade ; any thyng conteyned in the same Acte to the cont*ry natwithstandyng. CHAPTER I.

An Acte ayenst Reg*tours & Gatherers of Wulles.

WHERE at a Parliament holden at Westfii in the w]* yere of the reign of the moste vi&orious Prince of famous memorie Kyng Henry the vij* most dere father unto the Kynges Highnes our Soveigne Lord for thencreaae and maigntenaunce of Drapery and makyng of Wollen Clothes within this realme. It was establysshed and enacted that no matt psone by hym selfc or by any other shuld bye or bargayne, from the firste day of Marche which was in the yere of our Lord God M CCCC lxxxix, any Wolles [than*] unshome of the growyng of Barkeshire, Oxfordeshire Glocetourshire Herefordeshire Shropshire Worcettershire Essex Wylteshire So&ettshire Dorsetshire Hampeshire Hartfordshire Cambrigeshire Norff Suffolke Kent Surrey or Sussex or of any of them, before the Feaste of thassumpeyon of oure Lady then nexte ensuyng, or by or bargayne any Wolles or take pmyse of bargayne of any Wolles that shuld growe in any of the said Shires in any yere or yeres to come after the said feaste of thassumpeyon of our Lady, any tyme before the same feaste of thassumpeyon of oure Lady that shuld be next after the sheryng of the same wolle or wolles, but only suche poones as of the said Wolles shuld make or do to be made yerae or clothe within this Realme, upon payne of forfeiture of the doble value of all the said Wolles bought or to be bargeyned or taken by pmyse of bargayne cont*rie to the said Ordenance: Nor that any March*unte Straunger by hymself or by any other pson in any yere [ than1 ] to come shulde bye any Wolles before the feaste of the Purificacyon of our Lady next after the clippynge or sherynge of the same, upon lyke payne of forfayture, the one halfe of suche forfayture to be to the Kynges use, and the other halfe to hym that wold sue the parde that shuld breke the said ordenaunce. And that any psone that wolde sue in that parte shuld have an accyon of dette of the said forfayture and suche proces in the same accyon shulde be had as is in an accyon of dette at the comen lawe or after the custome of the Citie, Borough or Towne where it shulde happen to be sued; and that no essoin ne pte&ion shuld be alowed for the defendant in that acdon, nor that the defendant therin shulde be admytted to wage his Lawe: And furthermore ic was ordeyned by the same acte that no maS psone beynge sworne to be a Wolle packer, in any wyse after the said first day of Marche, shuld bye or bargayne any ma8 of Wolle for any suche Marchaunt Straunger within this realme upon payne of forfeiture of the same Wolle so bought bargayned or gathered to the use of any suche Marchaunt straunger, as by the same aSe is pleynly declared. The whiche good Statute and ASe was made only to indure for the rme of x yeres [ than * ] nexte ensuyng, which terme is nowe longe tyme paste and expired; Sithen the expiradon wherof there hath ben and dayly be many broggers regratours and gatherours of Wolles within the said Sheris, aswell to the use of Straungers, as the Kynges Englysshe Subjects, whiche drape not the same Wolles within this Realme; which broggers and gatherours prevent so the Clothe makers in the pvysion of the said Wolles and put yerely suche prises to the same, that the Clothmakers by whome many of the Kyngf Subje&f of this realme have be commenly set a worke can not drape ne be able for lacke of Wolles at resonable pryses to drape suche multitude of Wollen Clothes as they have be accustomed in tymes paste; by reason whereof many of the Kynges Subje&f whiche lyved by drapery, for lacke of worke be brought to idelnes and dayly incurre and fall to roberyes and other inconvenyences: For repormacion wherof it may please the Kynges Highnes by thassent of the Lords Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons in this pfeent parliament assembled and by au&oride of the same, to establisshe and ena&e. That the said Estatute made in the said iiij* yere of the reign of the said late Kyng be revyved in evy article

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte for poysonyng.

THE Kynges royall majestie callyng to hys moste blessed remembraunce that the makyng of good and holsome lawes and due execution of the same agaynste the offendours therof is the only cause that good obedyence and order hath ben pserved in this Realme, and his Highnes havyng moste tender zeale to the same emonge other thynges consyderyng that mannes lyfe above all thynges is chyefly to be favoured, and voluntary murders moste highly to be detested and abhorred, and specyally of all kyndes of murders poysonynge, which in this Realme hytherto our Lorde be thanked hath ben moste rare and seldome comytted or pra&ysed ; and nowe in the tyme of this psente parliament, that is to saye, in the xviijt,‘ daye of Februarye in the xxij. yere of his moste vi&orious reygn, one Richarde Roose late of Rouchester in the Countie of Kente coke, otherwyse called Richard Coke, of his moste wyked and dampnable dysposicyon dyd caste a cteyne venym or poyson into a vessell replenysshed with yeste or barme stondyng in the Kechyn of the RevWle Father in God John Bysshopp of Rochester at his place in Lamehyth Marsshe, wyth whych Yeste or Barme and other thynges convenyent porrage or gruell was forthwyth made for his famylye there beyng, wherby nat only the nombre of xvij psons of his said famylie whych dyd eate of that porrage were mortally enfe&ed and poysoned and one of them that is to say, Benett Curwen gentylman therof ys decessed, but also Cteyne pore people which resorted to the sayde Bysshops place and were there charytably fedde wyth the remayne of the saide porrage and other vytayles, were in lyke wyse infe&ed, and one pore Woman of them that is to saye, Alyce Tryppytt wydowe is also therof nowe deceassed: Our sayde Sov^eign Lorde the Kynge of hys blessed disposicion inwardly abhorryng all such abhomynable offences because that in man! no psone can lyve in suertye out of daunger of death by that meane yf practyse therof shulde not be exchued, hath ordeyned and enacted by au&oryrie of thys psente parlyament that the sayde poysonyng be adjuged and demed as high treason, And that the sayde Richarde [ Rose for the sayd murder and poysonynge of the sayde two psones as is aforsayde by auctorite of thys psente parlyament shall stande and be attaynted of highe treason: And by cause that detestable offence nowe newly practysed and comytted requyreth condigne punysshemente for the same; It is ordeyned and enacted by au&oride of this psente parliament that the said Richarde Roose shalbe therfore boyled to deathe withoute havynge any advauntage of his clargie. And that from hensforth evy wylfull murder of any psone or psones by any whatsoeP psone or psones herafter to be edmytted and done by meane or waye of poysonynyng shalbe reputed demed and juged in the lawe to be highe treson ; And that all and e9y psone or psones which hereafter shalbe laufully indyted or appeled and attaynted or condempned by order of the Lawe of suche treson for any ma8 poysonyng of any psone shall not be admytted to the benefyte of hys or theyre clargye, but shalbe imedyatly after suche atteynder or condempnacion edmytted to execucion of deth by boylynge for the same. And that the Justycf of peace in evy shire eyrie or towne corporate wythin this Realme where Justices of Peace bene, shall have full power and au&oryrie in their Sessions to inquyre from tyme to tyme aswell of suche traytorous murderers and murders, as of the counterfaytynge of Coyne of any outewarde Realme, suffered to ronne and goo wythin this Realme by the Kynges assente, and to make pcesse therapon by Capias onely; And that the Justices of Assise in ev*y Shire of Englonde shall have power and au&oritie to here and de?myne in theyre Sessyons aswell such tresons edmytted and done by waye of poysonynge as the counterfeatyng of any such coyne suffered to ronne wythin thys Realme by the Kynges assente as ys aforesayd.

And furthermore it is enacted by au&oritie of thys psent parliament that all landes & tentf and other heredytamentf of any psone and psones which hereafter shalbe condempned or atteynted of any treson for poysonyng. as is aforesaide, shall eschete remayne and be to the lordes of the fees, as by the lawes of this Realme landes and tentf of felons or murderers atteynted have heretofore excheted; this Psente Acte of Treson or any thynge therein conteyned nat withstondyng.

CHAPTER X.

An Actb con&iyng Egypsyans.

FOR AS MOUCH as afore this tyme dy$se and many outlandysshe People callynge themselfes Egyptians usyng no crafte nor fai&e of marchaundyse have comen into this Realme, and gone from Shire to Shire and Place to Place in greate company and used greate subtyll and crafty meanes to deceyve the people, beryng them in hande, that they by Palmestre coulde telle menne and womens fortunes, and so many tymes by crafte and subtyltie have deceyved the people of theyr money, and also hath comytted many and haynous felonyes and robberies to the greate hurte and deceyte of the people that they have comyn amonge: Be it therfore, by the Kynge our Soveign Lorde the Lordes Spirituall and Temporall and by the C5mons in thys psente parliament assembled, and by the au&orytie of the same, ordeyned establysshed and enacted that from hensforth no suche peones be suffred to come within this the Kynges Realme, And yf they do [than1 ] they and evy of them so doynge shall forfayte to the Kynge our Soveign Lorde all theyr goodes and catalls and then to be edmaunded to avoyde the Realme wythin xv. dayes next after the comaundement upon payne of imprisonament: And it shalbe laufull to e9y Sheryff Justice of Peace and Eschetour to sease to the use of our Soveign Lorde his Heyres and Successours all suche Goodes as they or any of them shall have, and therof to accompte to our said Soveign Lord in his Exchequer ; and yf it shall happen any suche Straunger hereafter to edmytte wythin this Realme any murder robbery or any other felonye and therof be indicted and arayned, and to plede not giltie or any other plee triable by the edntrie, that then thenqueste that shall passe betwene the Kyng and any suche parde shall be all together of Englysshemen, albeit that the parde so indicted pray [ mediatem2 ] lingue according to the Statute of Anno viij Henrici vj or of any other Statute therof made.

Provydbd alwaye that the Egyptians nowe beynge in thys Realme have monycyon to departe within xyj dayes after prodamacyon of thys estatute amonge them shalbe made, upon payne of imprisonament and fbrfeyture of theyr goodes and catells, and yf they then so departe that then they shall not forfayte theyr goodes nor any parte therof; thys psente Estatute not wythstondyng.

(3 ) Provyded alwaye that evy suche psone or psons which canne pve by ij credable psones before the same partie that seaseth suche money goodes or catalls of the same Egyptians, that any parte of the same goodes money or catalls were craftely or felonously taken or stolne from hym, shalbe incontynent restored unto the same goodes money or catalls wherof he maketh suche pve before the same parde that so seaseth the same money goodes or catalles upon payne to forfayte to the same partie that make such prove the double value of the same by accyon of Dette Bill, or otherwyse in any of the Kynges Courtes to be sued, upon which accyon and sute he shall not be admytted to wage hys Lawe, nor any ptecdon or essoyne to be alowed; any thyng in the acte to the cont*ry not wythstondyng.

Provyded alwayes and be it farther enacted that yf any Justice of Peace, Sheryff or Eschetour which by au&orytie of this Acte have power to take or sease any goodes or catels of any Egyptians, at any tyme hereafter do sease or take the goodes or cattels of any suche Egyptians, that then e£*y such Justice Sheryff or Eschetour doyng the same shall have kepe and retayne to his owen use the moyte of all suche goodes so by hym seased, and of the other moytie so by hym seased or taken shall make answere and accompte to the Kyng in his Escheker accordyng to the tenour of this psent acte; any thynge in the same Acte conteyned to the cont"ry herof notwithstondyng *, and that uoon any accounte hereafter to be made for the said other moytie of the same goodes, the accountant shall paye no man of fees or other charges for his accounte or discharge to be hadd in the Kynges Eschequer nor els where.

CHAPTER XIII.

An Acte conSnyng Bakers, Bruers, Surgeos & Scryveners.

¥ Jk THERE dyvers Estatutes penall hertofore have been made ageyn straungers artyfycers for excysyng of hand V V craftes wythin this Realme & for kepyng of houses, apprentyses k servauntf estraungers as by the sayde sePall Estatutes more playnly ys rehersed: Sythen the makyng wherof, bere bruers and bakers whiche bene comon vitaylers and also surgens and scryveners beyng straung?s inhabyted and dweliyng wythin this realme hathe bene putte to trouble and great vexadon by occasion of informations brought ageyne them upon the sayde Estatutf supposyng that Straungers usyng bakyng, bruyng, surgerye or wrytyng shulde be hand craftesmen, upon the whiche information greate doubtes and ambiguytes have rysen, whether straungers usyng any of the sayde mysteryes or sdences shulde be understande suche handcraftesmen as were entended by any the sayde Estatutes: For playne declaradon wherof [hit is*] enacted by the Kyng oure Sov^dgn Lorde and the Lordes Squall and Temporall and the Comons in this present parliament assembled andby aufloryty of the same, that no pson nor psones srraungers beyng a comon baker, bruer, surgeon or scryvenour shalbe enterpret or expounded hande craftesmen in for or by reason of usyng any of the sayde mysteryes or scyens of bakyng bruyng, surgery or wrytyng. And that all informations sutes acdons and pcesse had taken or herafter to be taken upon eny of the sayde Estatutes agayn any suche straunger or straungers beyng bakers, bruers, surgeons or scryveners shall be by au&oryte of this psent acte voyde and of none effecte.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte con&iyng Abjuratyons into Seyntuaryes.

Erik from abjured fT^HE KYNG oure Soveign Lorde considering that many of his Subjedfcf hertofore for theyre offencf and merytes JL have bene putte to execution of dethe by the Lawes of this Realme, & many other comyttyng lyke offencf for tuydon of theire lyves have fledde and resorted to Churches & other halowed places wythin this realme, and there beyng have abjured the realme before the Kyngf Coroners of the same, dyvers of whiche men so abjuryng have bene knowen to be very expert Maryners, and many other have bene sene to be very able and apte men for the Warres and for defence of this realme, so that by the one meane and the other the strength and power of this realme ys gretely mynyshed; and dyvers of the sayde psones whiche heretofore have abjured this realme, beyng by reason of theyre abjurations in outwarde realmes and contreys have not onely peured many men of the same to the eSEcyse and pra&yse of Archery and have instru&ed them in the feate and knowlege therof, to the greate encrease and fortifyeasions of the same outwarde realmes and contreys, but also the same abjured psones have disclosed theyre knowleges of the Comodytes k Secretes of this realme to no little damage and pjudyce of the same: The Kyngf Highnes therfore dayly studyeng and dyvysyng to provyde for the safegarde of this his realme and of his subje&f albeyt they be transgressours of his lawes, so that the incomodyties ensuyng upon suche abjurations to be pserved to the best effe&e as farre as shall please God to gyve them grace, hath ordeyned & enacted by authoryte of this hys psent parliament,

II.

Sanctuary-Men committing new Offence shall lose all Benefit of Sanctuary.

And yf any pson or psons whiche shalbe endyted of any petye treason murder or felony or of any accessary to any suche offence happen herafter to be taken out of any Seyntuary for the same by auftoryte of this Estatute & upon his or theire arraynement plede Seyntuary accordyng to the order of the Lawe, [ Than' ] yt ys enabled by the autihoryte aforsayde that aswell the Kyngf Attourney as e9y other pson for the Kyng shall be admytted to obje&e and allege that the pson so arayned afore the doyng of the offence or offencf wherof he [than1 ] ys arrayned, dyd take pryvylege of Seyntuary in the same Sentuary wherof he allegeth hym to be taken out, or in any other place pryvyleged wythin this realme upon any abjuration or for any [other1 ] pety treason murder or felony than wherof he ys arayned, and that he there had and enyoyed privylege of Seyntuary for the same & that he so havyng ones pryvylege of Seyntuary in the same, dyd cdmyt the offence of pety treason murder or felony wherof he than ys arrayned, or that he wente out of the sayde Sentuary & comytted the same offence wherof he is endyted and arrayned, and pray that suche pson so arrayned may be excluded of restitution to the Sentuary by hym demaunded; And in case the said pice & objection so alleged be denyed by the pson so arrayned, [Than *] it is further enacted by the au&oryte aforsaide that it shalbe forthwyth tried afore the same Justices where suche pson is so arrayned, & by the same Jurours of the same Countie that shall trie the pety treason murder or felony wherof he is arrayned wythout further delaye, in what so ever Countie or Counties Place or Places of this realme the same other takyng of Seyntuary shalbe alleged or objefted to be done or had. CHAPTER XVI.

An Acte con&iyng the pdon graunted to the Kyngf Temporall Subge&f for the Premunyre.

THE KYNG our Soveign Lorde havyng alway most tender zeale favour & affeccion unto his most lovynge Temporall & Lay Subye&f of this his Realme of Englonde & of Wales, Cales & Marches of the same & inwarly remembryng the manyfolde greate offencf transgressions & contemptf ppefted comytted & done by dyvers & many of his sayde Temporall & Laye Subjeftf ayenst his Highnes his Corowne regally & jurysdi&ion royall cont‘ry to the Statutf of provysions provisours & pmunyre, by reason wherof they so offendyng have incurred into the daungers & penalites of the same Statutf in suche wyse that yf his Highnes wolde attempte or pursue those his sayde Temporall & Laye Subject f by the proces & course of his lawes they shulde therby not onely forfayte & lose their londf tehtf goodes & catalles but also they shulde be out of his g*ciouse ptec£6n; His Royall Majestye moved wyth most tender pyte love & compassion & not myndyng to use & extende all & singuler his penall lawes upon his Subje&f but as consideration shall move his Grace, so in parte or in hole to remyt & mytygate the rygour of the same, Of his mere motion & of his hye benygnyte specyall grace pitie & liberalyte hath geven & graunted & by au&horyte of this psent parliament gyveth & graunteth to all & synguler his Temporall & Laye Subje&f & Temporall bodies polytyke & corporated & to ery of them his most gratious geSall & free pardon of & for all & all maner offencf transgressions & contemptf comytted perpetrated or done ayenst the sayd Statutes of provysours, provisions & pmunyre or any of them before the thirtyeth day of Marche in the xxijtl yere of his most noble reign, & all forfaytures penalties judgementes execufftns & peynes for the sayde offencf transgressions & contemptf & eVy of them.

And furthermore be yt enacted by the authoryte of this psent parliament that all and singuler processes, sutf, prosecutions & ympeticions in any wyse herafter to be awarded or made ageynst any of his sayde Temporall Subje&f or against any of the saide Temporall bodies polytyke & corporated for or upon any of the sayde offencf transgressions or contemptf cdmytted or done before the sayd xxx day of Marche shalbe utPly voyde & of none effe&e.

CHAPTER IVm.

An Acte conSnyng the Kyngs Household.

■VY WHEREAS at a Parliament holden at Westfh the xx* day of Januarij in the first yere of the rcigne of our Sovaigne Lord T V the Kynge that now is, for the spedy and true payment from then to be made to his lovyng Subjects of and for thcxpensis of hit moat honorable houshold, It was enacted ordeyned and establisshed by our saide Sovaigne Lord with the advyse and assent of his Lordis SpirituaU and Temporall and his Comons in the said pliament assembled, that iij M1. viij C. j H. xij s. j d. ob. of the Colle&ourt of the Subsidie of iij s. of the Tonn and xij d. of the pounde in his porte of London, that then were or therafter shuld be9 with other sdmes in the saide Acte specified and expressid to the hole sdme of xixM1. iij C. iiij** xiiij ti. xvj s. iijd. ob. shuldbe from thensforthe yerely taken receyved and applied towardis the paymentis and contentyngis of thexpenses of the Kynges said most honourable houahold, And therfor yerely assignemends to be made by the Tresaurer of Englond in due and sufficient forme at the Receipt of the Kyngis Eschequier unto the Cofferer of the Kyngis most honorable housholde for the tyme beynge, of the Resceivo’s Fennours Occupiers Customers Colle&ours and other psons chargeable of the Maners Londis and Tenementis Custumes Subsidies and other thyngis in the said Acte specified and expressid; which said sdmes of Money hare not byne sithen the said Acte soo spedily levyed and paid as at the makyng of the said Acte it was thought they shuld hare bene, soo that for defaute of payment of the said sdmes to the handis of the Cofferer of the Kyngis said honourable houshold many of the Kyngis lovyng Subjects have not byne so redilie and spedily contentid for suche thyngis as apperteyned to and for the expensis of the same houshold as at the makyng of the said Acte it was pposid shuld have byne: In Consideracion wherof the Kyng out Sovaigne Lorde by the advyse and assent of his Lordis SpirituaU and Temporall and of his Comondis in his pliament assymbled begon and holdon at London the xv day of Aprell in the xiiij01 yere of his most noble reign, and afterward to Westffi the xxxjtlk day of Julij then next followyng proroged and adjoined and then ther holden, by thau&orite of the same did utterly repell adnull and evoyde the said Acte made in the said first yere of his said most noble reigne to be of no force nor effe&e j And it was declared by the same a&e that the Kyngis Highnes by the advyse of his honourable Counsell wold otherwise pvyde for more plener and spedy payment to be made to his lovyng Subjects for suche thyngis as shuld appertayne to and for thexpenses of his said most honorable houshold. CHAPTER XIX.

An Acte eon&iyng die assuraunce of c?ten Londf to the Heyres of Syr William Fyloll.

THTUMBLY shewen unto your Highnes the Maire, Bailliffis and Burgeisses of your Towne of Southampton whiche hold of your XJL Grace the same Towne in fee ferme yeldyng yerly unto your Grace your Heires and Successours two hundred poundis, as by the [ grauntis • ] by letters patentis therof made by your most noble pgenytour Kyng Henry the thurde too the pdecessours of your said Oratours by the name of Burgeses of your Towne of Southampton and by your Grace confermyd dothe appere, over and above forty markis of encrece charged uppon your said Oratours yerly in your Court of Eschequyre by the names of Men of Southampton, for the pardonyng and remysyng of a trespas don by the Burgeses of your said Towne in the tyme of your noble pgenytour Kyng Edward the firste as by the Recordis of your said Eschequyre also dothe appere; And also your said Oratours besides the pmissis be at many greate and yerly chargis for daily defence and savegarde of your said Towne as well ayenst the See as otherwise, and for die repacions and fortificacions of the Wallis Towns Towrettis Bulwarkis and Banckis, and for the kepyng of the Watch is and Wardis ther and other Chargis contynually ayenst the See. And your said Oratours have no mafl of Rent pfett ne Succoure for payment and sustentacion of the pmissis but onely petie Custume of Marchaundise which of old tyme was accustumed too be levyed of the goodis of Strangiers repayryng thither in Carreckis of Jeane laden with Jeane Woade; and in Gallies of Flourence and Venyse laden with Spicis, and nowe by the tyme of many yeres past sithen that Tolowes Woade hath ben usually brought into this Real me, and that the Kyng of Portyngale toke the trate of spicis from the Venyzians at Calacowte, fewe or noo suche Carreckis Galeis ne other Shippis have repayred unto your said Towne with Woade or Spicies nor be lyke too repayre hereafter \ and also the trate of other nlchaundises by reason of the Warns betwene your Grace and owtward Pryncis hath ben longe tyme withdrawne frome your said Towne, soo that your said Oratours have byn forsid to pay of ther ppre goodis within fewe yeris past many greate somes of money more then they could raise and levye of the said Petie Custume * And yet they stonde and be indetted for the said fee ferme in other great sdmes of money as well unto your Grace as unto other, havyng pcellis of the same fee ferine by the grauntis of your Highnes and of your noble pgenytours, and your said Oratours know not how too levye the same *, and for doubte and feare therof many psons that wer lyke too have growne to great substaunce have departed and forsakyn your said Towne and moo be in p'pose and mynde shortly too departe from the same, too the desolac5n of your said Towne excepte your most gracious favour helpe and succoure be iScifully unto them shewid for their relieffe in this their extreme necessite, havyng no other succour aide ne helpe but only of your Highnes. In considekacion wherof it may pleas your Highnes most gracious Soveigne Lorde with the assent of the Lordis Spirituall and Temporall and the Comons in this psent parliament assembled and by audiorite of the same; for the pservacion supportacion and mayntaynyng of your said Towne, of your most habundaunt grace and benyvolence too geve and graunte the said yerly s6me of xl. m*rckys unto the said Maire Bailliffis and Burgeses and too their Successours for e?more, and soo utterly for e? too release and extyndte the same yerly some of forty nrtrekis by what soo e9 name or namys your said Oratours be incorporated named or callid, or for what soe? cause or consideracion the said some of forty m*rckis of yerly encreace of the said fee ferme is and hath byn demaunded levyed or takyn of your said Oratours and of their pdecessours, be it for the said pardon and remysaion made by the said Kyng Edward the firste for the said trespas or otherwise: And that it may pleas your Highnes by the said au&orite of this psent pliamente too ordeyn establishe and ena&e, that the said Maire Baylliffis and Burgeses and their Successours, And also the Shirefie of the said Towne and his Successours for the tyme beyng, and all other men and inhabit*untis of the same, be and shalbe from the feaste of Saynt Michell the Archaungell in the xxiju yere of your most noble raigne remysed releassed and clerly acquyted and dischargid ayenst your Highnes, your heires and successours Kyngis of this Realme for ever of the payment of the forsaid yerly some of xl. m*rckis and evy parte therof; And that all suche right title invest enherit*unce and demaunde as your Highnes hath or any of your pgenytours have had in the same or in any parte or parcell therof; be and shalbe frome the said feaste clerly extyn&ed and defmyned for e9.

If Persons not privileged ship Wines to evade Prisage, it shall be paid.

Portage Wines may be shipped Prisage-free.

(1) Provyded alway that if any pson or psons not beyng discharged of paying of prisage, do shippe in any one vyage or vyntage at any tyme herafter any Wynes too the nombre of x Tonnes or above in dy9s Shippis or dy9s bottomes, with the Wynes of any of the said Burgeses or of any of their successours, too thentent too deceyve the Kyngis Grace of his prisage; the Kyng ne9thelesse shalbe satisfied and paid of his said prisage of the Wynes of all and e9y suche pson and psons not pryvylaged, which soo shall 6hippe their Wynes in se9all Shippis as is affbrsaid, in lyke mafl and forme as if all the same Wynes had ben shipped all in one Shippe or uppon one bottome, any thyng in this Acte too the contmry notwithstondyng*, and that it shalbe lefull too the Maister and Marynours of e9y suche Shippe or Vessell wherin they shall hereafter sayle, too shippe and lade their portage wynes and bryng theym into this Realme frely and too their most pfette withoute yeldyng therfore any prisage like as hath byn usid by suche Masters and Marianours in tymes paste.

STATUTES MADE IN THE SESSION OF PARLIAMENT,

HOLDEN BY PROROGATION AT WESTMINSTER, ON THE FIFTEENTH Day OF JANUARY,

In the TWENTY-THIRD Year of the Reign of K. HENRY, VIII.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte that no pson commyttyng Pety Treason Murder or Felony shalbe admytted to his Clergye under

Subdeacon.

WHERE at a parlyament holden at Westm in the thyrde yere of Kyng Edward the fyrst, the same Kyng moved the Prelates of the Realme, and theym enjoyned upon theyr feyth that they owed to hym, that in no wyse they shuld delyver those Clerkes whiche were indyted for felonye wythout due purgacyon, so that the sayd Kyng shulde have no nede to putt other remedye in that behalf: And that notwythstondyng after [the'] monycyon dyvers and many Clerkf convyde were accustomably dely^ed and suffredd to make theyr purgacyons, to the greate corage of evyll doers; by occasyon wherof afterward at another parlyament holden at Westmynster in the iiijth yere of Kyng Henry the fourth upon the complaynte of the Comons, the same Kyng Henry the iiijth then advertysed the Prelates of the Realme of the pmysses entendyng than to have pvyded remedy by audorytie of the sayd parlyament as apperteyned to his prerogatyve royall for the conservacyon of the peace of the Crowne ; At whiche tyme the Archebisshopp of Canterbery for hym selff and all other Bisshopps of his pvynce [ than * ] openly pmysed to the same Kyng Henry the iiijth, that yf any pson from thensfonhe were convyde of any treason whiche touched not the Kyng nor his royall Majestye, and suche as were notoryously knowen and reputed for thevys and for suche cause delyv^ed to any Ordenary as a Clerke convyde, that the Ordenarye to whome suche pson or psons were delyv^ed shuld safely kepe them after the effede of a consdtucyon pvyncyall to be made by the sayd Archebysshopp and Bysshopps, after the effede of the Letters of Symon [than *] afore that tyme Archebisshopp of Can?bury, bearyng date the xij kalendes of Marche the yere of our Lord God a M. CCC. L. and that no suche traytoure nor felon shuld make his purgacyon agayne the sayd constytucyon ; whiche constytucyon the sayd Archebysshopp [than *] pmysed to delyver to the same Kyng before his nexte parlyament, to thentent that yf yt shulde seme to the same Kyng that the same constytucyon were not suffycyent remedy for the pmysses, that [than*] the sayd Kyng myght pvyde suche remedye as shulde apptayne in that behalf: Sythen whiche tyme the same constytucyon was never notefyed ne shewed by the Prelates of this realme, but contynually sythen that tyme manyfest thevys and murderers indyted and founde gyltye of theyr mysdedes by good and substancyall inquestes upon [ payne 5 ] and profeable evydence before the Kyngf Justices, and afterward by the usagf of the cdmon lawes of the londe delyved to the Ordenaryes as Clerkes convyde be spedyly and hastely delyved and sett at large by the mynysters of the sayd ordenaries for corrupcyon and lucre; or ells because the ordenaryes enclaymyng suche offenders by the lifetyes of the Churche, wyll in no wyse take the charges in save kepyng of them, but lytyll regardyng the tryall and conviccyon of the sayd offenders by the due and playne course of the comon lawes of the londe, do suffer them to make theyr purgacyons by suche as nothyng knowe of theyr mysdedes, and by suche fraude adnull and make voyde all the good and provable tryall that ys used agayne suche Offenders by the Kynges lawes, to the greate disclaunder of suche as pursue suche mysdoers and to the pnycyous example encreace and corage of suche offenders, yf the Kyngf Highnes by his audoryte royall putt not spedy remedy in the pmysses as apperteyneth: Be it therefore enacted by the Kyng oure soPeign Lorde and the Lordf spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent parlyament assembled and by audoryte of the same. That no pson nor psons, whiche hereafter shall happen to be founde gyltye after the lawes of this londe for any maner of pety treason, or for any wylfall murder of malyce ppensed, or for robbyng of any Churches Chapells or other holy places, or for robbyng of any pson or psons in theyr dwellyng howses or dwellyng place, the owner or dweller in the same house

Provyded alway that this Acte extende not to gyve any benefyte to any suche pson or psons whiche after their confessyon or jugement geven agayn them of or for felony or murder or after they be outlawed for any suche cause, be admytted to theyr Clergye and delyped to the Ordenarye for the samej but that they and evy of them shall remayne in the custody of the Ordenaryes wythout makyng purgacyon, upon suche perill and in suche maner and fourme as yt was used by the Cdmen lawe before the makyng of this present a&e. This Acte or any thyng therin conteyned notwythstondyng.

And that evy suche jugement shalbe executed accordyngly, and that every Ordenarye so sendyng any suche Convi&e dysgraded into the Kyngf Benche, shalbe discharged ageyn the Kyng oure Soveign Lorde his heyrcs and successours of or for any further custody or kepyng of the same convi&e. This Acte to continewe unto the last daye of the next Parliament.

CHAPTER III.

An Acte concnynge pjurie & punysshement of untreue vdictes.

THE KING our Soveraygne Lorde, of his moste goodly and gracious disposicion calling to his remembrance howe that pjurie in this londe is in manyfolde causes by unreasonable meanes [detestably*] used, to the disheritaunce and greate damage of many and greate numbre of his Subjedtes well disposed, and to the mooste high displeasour of Almyghtie God, the good Statutes ayenst all officers havyng retorne of Writtes and their deputies making panellf pardally for rewardes to them geven against unlawfull mayntenours embrasours and Jurours and ayenst Jurours untruely yevyng their verdide notwithstanding; For reformation wherof, and for asmoche as the late noble Kinge Henry the vij pvided remedye for the same by a Statute made in the xj yere of his reigne, which Statute is nowe expired: Be it therfore nowe enacted by the King our SoPaygne Lorde and the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comens in this Psent pliament assembled and by audoride of the same, that uppon ev*y untrue verdide hereafter geven betwixte parde and parde in any suite playnt or demaunde before any Jusdces or Juges of Recorde, where the thinge in demand and $dide therupon gyven extendeth to the value of fourde pounde and con?neth not the jeopdie of manys liffe, the parde greved by the same verdytt shall have a writte of Atteint ageynst epy psonne hereafter so gevyng an untrue 9dide and evy of theym and agayst the ptie which shall have judgement upon the same verdide; And that in the same Atteynt there shalbe awarded against the pede Jurie the parde and the graunde June, somons resomons and distresse infinite, whiche graunde Jurie shalbe of like nombre as the graunde Jurie is nowe in Atteynt, and epy of theym that shall passe in the same shall have londes and tenementes to the value of xx markes by the yere of freeholde out of the auncient demesne j And uppon the distresse whiche shalbe delyvered of recorde uppon the same open pclamation to be made in the Courte there, the distresse shalbe awarded more xv. daies afore the retome of the same distresse; And e$y such distresse shalbe made upon the lande of ev*y of the said graunde Jurie as in other distresse is and hath ben used: And if the said Partie defendaunt or the petite Jurors or any of theym appere not upon the distresse, than the graunde Jurie to be taken ageynst them and e9y of them that shall so make defaulte: And if any of the said petit Jurie appere, than the partie complaynant in that behalve shall assigne the falce serement of the firste verdicte untruely gyven; wherunto they of the petie Jurie shall have none aunswere, if they be the same psonnes and the writte pcesse retorne and assignement good and lawfull, excepte that the demaundante or playndfe in the same Atteynt hath afore ben nonsuite or discontinued his suite of Atteynt taken for the same, or hath for the same verdide in a writte of Atteynt had judgement ageynst the said pede Jurie, but only that they made true serement; whiche issue shall be tried by xxiiij of the said graunde Jurie; and the parde shall plede that they gave true verdide or any other mat? whiche shall be a sufficient barr of the said Atteynt, and that plee notwithstanding the graunde Jurie to be taken without delaye to enquier whether the firste Jurie gave true verdide or noo; And if they fynde that the said pedte Jurie gave an untrue verdide, than e9y of the said pedte Jurie to forfait xx ii. wherof the oon halff shalbe to the King our SoPayngne Lorde and the other halff to the parde that sueth : And o9 that, that e9y of the said petite Jurie shall seQally make fyne and ransdme by the discretion of the Jusdces before whome the said falce serement shalbe founde, after thir severall offences defautes and sufficientie of e&y of the said pedte Jurie; And after that, that those of the said pedte Jurie so atteynted shall never after be in any credence nor thir Othe accepted in any Courte: And if suche plee as the parde pleadeth which is a barr of the said Atteynt be founde or demed ageynst hym that so pledeth, than the parde that so sueth shall have jugement to be restored to that he lost with his reasonable costes and damages.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte that no Breuers of Bere or Ale shall make their barrels kylderkyns nor firkyns within them;

and howmoche the same barrels &c. shall conteyne.

WHERE the Ale bruers and bere bruers of this Realme of England have used and dayly do use, for thir owne singuler lucre pfitte and gayne, to make in their owne houses theyr barrels kylderkyns and firkyns of moche lasse quandde contente rate and [assisse4 ] than they ought to be, to the greate hurte p^judice and damage of the Kinges liege people and cont*ry to dy9s a&es statutes auncient lawes and customes hertofore made had and used, and to the distrucdon of the pore crafte or mysterie of Cowpers: For reformacion wherof be it enacted by the King our Sovaigne for ^JeW*hj01 bTt ^orde Lordes Spuall and temporall and the Comons in this p'sent parliament assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that noo bere bruer nor ale bruer that shall brue to sale bere or ale shall fromehensforth occupie by hym selff nor by any other to his use in his house nor elswhere the misterie or crafte of Cowpers, nor make any barells kilderkyns fyrkyns or other vessels by hymselff nor by his or theyr owne §v*untes, wherby they shall putt theyr bere or ale to sale; but that all such barrells kilderkins and other vessels of Wood, wherwith they shall putt thir bere or ale to sale, shall from hensforth be made and marked accordingly as hereafter shalbe ex passed by the comon artificers of Cowpers exScised and pra&ised in the said occupation; upon payne to forfeite and pay for evy suche barrell kilderkyn firkyn or other vessell hereafter to be made contrarie to the tenour of this a&e, thre shillinges and foure pence.

An Acte conSnynge before whome Recognisaunces of Dettes shalbe made & the fo'ine of the obligation.

FOR ASMOCHE as the Maiers of the Stapull, in divers places of this Realme where any Stapull is kepte, in the psence of the Constables of the same Stapull before this tyme hathe and myght lawfully take recognisaunce or knowlege for dettes onely conc?nyng and touching the iSchaundise of the same Stapull, betwixte fichaunt and fichaunt of the same Stapull, according to divers lawdable estatutes and pvisions before this tyme had ordeyned and made ; Which Maiers and Constables many and sondrie tymes syns the making of the same Estatute have taken divers recognisaunces and knowleges of divers of the Kinges Subjectes for dettes, surmising the same knowlege or recognisaunce to be made for suertie of payment of sommes of Money for suche wares as were or ben bought in the same Stapull, where of trouth the same recognisaunce did not in anywise touche or conc?ne the iSchandise of the same, ne also the parties that is to say, the Cognisor ne the Cognisee that did knowlege and take the same recognisaunces were i2chauntes of the same Stapull; Which recognisances and knowleges takyn in forme aforesaid are not only clere contrarie to the true meanyng and intent of the same formar estatutes, but also therby diverse greate and sondrie inconveniences damages and deceytes doth dailie rise and growe to diverse of the Subjectes of our Sovaigne Lorde the Kyng, by reason of the mysusing of the same : And Forasmoche as the Kingez Highnesse of his moost high wisedome pceyveth the mysusyng and execucion of the same to be contrarie to the forme of the said formar estatutes, Therfore his pleasour is, that some trewe lawfull and reasonable bonde for suertie of payment of the dettes of his Subjectf shalbe made and devised by trewe and juste meanes which in it selffe may and shall purporte right and equitie and also consonaunt to reason: In consideracion wherof by thassent of the Kinges Highnes his Lordes spuall and temporall and his Commons in this psent parliament assembled and by the auctoritie of the same it is enacted ordeyned and establisshed, that frome the firste day of Aprill nexte comyng, the chieffe Justice of the Kinges Benche and the chieff Justice of the c5mon Place which nowe be or at any tyme herafter shalbe and e9y of them by hymselff, and in thir absence out of the Terme the Maier of the Stapull of Westmynster and the Recorder of the Citie of London for the tyme beyng, joyntly togethers by his or thir discrecion, shall have full power and auctoritie to take recognisaunces or knowleges of eQy of the Kinges Subjectes for the payment of dettes according to suche forme as hereafter ensueth : NovW univ^si p psentes me A. CHAPTER Vn.

An Acte that the Statutes made for the maynten*nce of the Navie of this Realme shall stonde in Rill strenght;

& howe Gascoyne and Frenche Wyne shall be brought in, and the same and other Wynes solde.

WHERE for the mayntenaunce and good continuaunce of the Navie of this Realme of England it was ordeyned and enacted by a Statute made in the v. yere of the reygne of the ryght noble King Richard the seconde, that none of the Kinges liege people shuld shipp fichaundise in any other shipp than in an Englisshe shipp upon peyne of forfeiture of the said marchaundise so shipped: And after that by another Statute made in the vj yere of the said noble Kyng it was enacted that for defaulte of Englisshe Shippes e$y man myght shipp their marchaundise in Straungers Shipps: And after that at a parliament holden at Westffi in the iiij yere of the late noble Kinge of famous memorye Kinge Henry the vij it was ordeyned and enacted that no psonne shuld carie or bring any Wynes of Gascoyne or Guyon, or Toloos Ode into Englande Wales Ireland Calice or the fiches therof or Berwik, but all onely in shippes of Englande Wales Ireland Calece or the fiches therof or Barwike; and that the Maistcr and Mariners of the same shippes for the moost parte of them shuld be of the same Countres; upon payne of forfeiture of the said Wyne and Ode as by the said good estatutes more at large is ex passed: And notwithstanding the said good estatutes yet neverthelesse the Navye of this Realme and the multitude of the Shippes of the same which tofore this tyme hath ben not onely a greate defence and suertie to this Realme of Englande in tyme of Warre, but also a high edmodide to all the Subjects of the same for t*nsporting and conveyance of Schauntdises in and frome this Realme, is nowe nivelously decaied and [ appeyred,1 ] and by occasion therof a greate multitude of the Kinges liege people which were Masters and Mariners of Shippes and by the exScise therof they theyr Wifes and Children had their livingf be nowe mynysshed and impovWhed; in suche wise that within fewe yeres there shalbe fewe Englisshe men that shalbe experte in the Sees, to the greate perrill of this Realme and decaye of the people of the same, if remedie be not pvided in this behalve: In Consideracion wherof the Kinges moost Roiall Majesde of his moost excellent goodnes havyng tender respede to the reformadon of the pmisses is contented and pleased, that it be enacted by his Highnes and the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this pfeent parliament assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that the said estatutes and e9y thing in them conteyned shall stonde in their full strenght force and effecte, so that frome hensforth no psone shall attempte to do contrarie to the tenours of any of the said estatutes upon the peynes conteyned in the same.

And It is further enacted by auctoritie aforesaid that no maner of pson or psonnes shall discharge and laye on Lond out of any Shipp or Shippes or other Vessell or Vesselles any Wynes of Gascoyne or Guyon or any maner of Frenche Wynes at any haven porte creke or other place within this Realme of England Ireland Wales or the Marches of the same at any tyme herafter betwene the feastes of Saint Michell tharchaungell and the purificacion of our Ladie ; upon payne of forfaiture of the said Wynes so brought in and discharged and leyed on Londe at any tyme herafter betwene the said feastes contrarie to this Acte; the one halffe of which forfeyture to be to the Kinge our Sov^aigne Lorde and the other halff therof to suche of the Kinges Subjectes as shall sease or sue for the same by accion of detynue or dette after the rate of the value thereof, by originall writte bill plaint or information in any of the Kinges Courtes, in which accions and suytes the defendaunte shall not be admitted to wage his lawe nor any pteccion or essoyne shalbe allowed.

And It is further enacted by auctoritie aforesaid that no psone after the feaste of the purificacion of oure Ladie whiche shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God M1 Dxxxij shall sell by retaile any of the said Wynes above viij d. the galon, that is to save a peny the pynte, two pence the quartee four pence the pottell, and eight pence the galon ; upon payne of forfaiture for evy pynt to be sold above the said price, iiij d. and for evy quarte solde above the said price, viij d. and for every potell so solde above the said price, xij d. and for e9y galon so sold above the said price afore limited, two shillinges ; and that no Malmeseis Romeneis Sakkes nor other swete Wynes after the saide feaste shalbe retailed above xijd. the galon vj d. the pottell, three pence the quarte, and id. ot> the pynt, upon payne to losse and forfeite iijs. iiij d. for e9y galon, xx d. for evy potell, xij d. for eVy quarte, and vj d. for evy pynt, that shalbe sold contrarie to this Acte.

Provyded Alwaye that the Lorde Chauncellour Lorde Treasourer Lorde President of the Kinges most honorable Counsaill Lorde privie Seale and the two Chiffe Justices of eyther Benche or v. iiij. or iij. of them shall have power and auctoritie by thir discrecions to sett the prices of all kynde of Wynes ; that is to saye, of the prices of the butt tonne pype hoggeshed poncheon teers barrell or rondlett whan it shalbe sold in grosse; (1) so that they or thre of theym cause the prices by them sette to be written and open pdamadon therof to be made in the Kinges Courte of Chauncerie openly in the terme tyme or els in the Citie Borowe or Towne where any suche Wynes shalbe sold in grosse (3); any thing conteyned in this Acte to the contrarie hereof notwithstanding.

And It is further enacted that if any psone or psones after suche prices be sette and putt in writing by the said Lorde Chauncellor Lorde Treasaurer Lorde President of the Kinges moste honorable Counseill Lorde privie Seale and the two Chieff Justices or by v. iiij. or iij of theym, and pdamadon therof had as is aforesaid do sell any Wynes in grosse (4) by any fraude or covyn contrarie to the said prices so sett and pclaymed, that [ than s ] ev*y offendor in that behalve shall losse and forfaite for e9y vessell by them solde in grosse contrarie to the said prices xl s. CHAPTER XVL

An Acte that no Englissh man shall sell exchaunge or dely9 to be conveid into Scotland, any Hors Gelding

or Maere without the Kinges licence.

In cate of any Interdict, fec. by the Pope, divine Service shall continue.

And if that uppon the foresaid reasonable amycable and charitable wayes and meanys by the Kynges Highnes to be experimented moved and compounded or otherwise approved, it shall and may appere or be seen unto his Grace that this Realme shalbe contynuallye burdonned and charged with this and suche other intollerable exactions and demaundys as heretofore it hath ben; And that theruppon for contynuaunce of the same, our sad Holy Father the Poope or any of his Successours or the Courte of Rome will or doo or cause to be doon at any tyme hereafter so as is above rehersyd, unjustlie uncharitably and unreasonablye vexe inquyet molest trouble or greve our seid Sovaign Lorde his heyres or Successours Kynges of England or any of his or their spirituall or lay subje&es or this his Realme, by excomunica£6n excomengement interdicc&n or by any other pcesse censures copulsories wayes or meanes; Be yt enacted by the Au&oritie aforesaid, that the Kynges Highnes his heyres and successours Kynges of Englond and all his spuall and lay subjects of the same, without any scripull of consciens shall and may laufully to the Honour of Almyghty God, the encrease and contynuaunce of vertue and good example within this Realme, the said censures excomunicac&ns interdictions compulsories or any of theym notwithstonding, mynister or cause to be mynistered thoroughout this seid Realme and all other the Domynions and Territories belonging or apperteyning thereunto, All and all maner Sacramentys Sacramentallys Seremonies or other Devyne §vice of Holye Churche or eny other thing or thinges necessarie for the helthe of the Soule of mankynde as they heretofore at any tyme or tymes have been vertuously used or accustumed to do within the same; And that no maner suche censures excomunicatiOns interdiccons or any other proces or compulsories shalbe by any of the prelates or other spuall Fathers of this Region ne by any of their mynisters or substitutes, be at any tyme or tymes hereafter publisshed executed nor devulged nor suffered to be publisshed executed or devulgyd in any maner of wise.

CHAPTER XXIV.

An Acte con&nyng an Exchaung of 2ten Londz betwene the Kyngz Highnes & the Provost of Eton.

BECAUSE that yt is notified and declared to this the Kynges moste honourable Courte of Parlyamente, that accordyng to the mutuall condiscente and agremente heretofore had and concluded betwene the Kyngf Highnes on the oon partie, and Roger Lupton Provoste of the College of our blessyd Lady of Eton and the same College on the other parte, that our said Sovaign Lord the Kyngia Highnes ys seasid yn his demesne as of fee by the feofemente of the said Provoste and College, of and yn the Scite and Circuyte of the Howse or Hospitall of Sayn&e James yn the felde and Jtayn other londis tenementis and hereditamentis, as by a Deade or Charter of that Feoffmente made by the same Pvoste and College evydentely appereth \ And that the same Provoste and College at this psente tyme ben seased yn theyre demesne as of fee to thuse of theym and of theyre successors for ever, of the gyfte and g*unte of our said Sovaign Lorde the Kyng to theyme made by his ires patentis, for and yn recompence and satisfaccion of the said Hospitall and other the pmysses specified yn the saide dede or Charter made by the saide Provoste and College, of and yn the Manour of Baudewyns besides Dartford yn the Countie of Kente and certayn other landes tenements and hereditamentis specified yn the Kyngis said ires patentis therof made by the Kyngis Highnes to the saide Provoste and College; The teanures of whiche saide Deade or Charter made by the saide Provoste and College and of the said ires patentis made by our said Sovaign Lorde the Kyng evydently hereafter ensue and followe yn e9y worde, and worde by worde as they bee made fourmed and t*nsa&id betwene the said parties.

STATUTES MADE IN THE SES8ION OF PARLIAMENT,

HOLDEN BY PROROGATION AT WESTMINSTER, ON THE FOURTH DAY OF FEBRUARY,

In the TWENTY-FOURTH Year of the Reign of K. HENRY, VIII.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte con?nyng trewe tannyng and coryeng of Lether.

FOR ASMUCHE as great multitude of Hydes and tanned Lether is untruely insufficiently & deceyvably tanned coried & wrought within this Realme and moche more excedyng in the prices than have ben at any tyme heretofore, by reason [wherof the Kynges poore Subjects be greatly hyndred & decayde & fewe of them can go or ride drie either in shoes or bootes, nor have any good or strong horse hameis of Lether, ne any enduryng sadells, maales, or boudgettes, ne any other thynges made of tanned lether to ther great damage losse & hynder\mce: And notwithstondyng dyvers good Statutes have ben made for the true coryeng & tannyng of Lether & searche of the same, yet nePthelesse the Tanners dayly sell ther Lether in ther owne dwellyng howses or in ther secrete places & houses out of the comon fayres or markettes, by reason wherof the same Lether is unserched & for the moost parte wrought in the necessaries amonge the Kynges poore Subjects to there great damage: For reformation wherof be it enacted by the Kyng our Sov^aign Lorde & the Lordes spuall & Temporall and the Comens in this pfeent Parlyamente assembled and by auGoritie of the same, That all & synguler Estatutes heretofore made conSnyng the Tanners Coriours & Cordeweyners & ev*y of them ther mysteries & occupacbns, and the mysteries & occupacbns of evy of them stondyng in force & not repelled nor expired, shalbe & stonde in ther full strength force & effeGe accordyng to the tenours & purportes of the same.

And to thentente that due & playne serche may be had of tanned Lether before it be put to sale, Be it enacted that no p6one nor psones from the Feaste of Saynt Michaell the Archaungell whicbe shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God M1. CCCCC. xxxiij. shall put any tanned Lether to sale within the Citie of London, nor within three myles compasse of the same, unlest it be brought into open Markette at Leaden Hall in London or ells in any the faires holden within the said Citie or ells where without the said Citie within the said thre myles compasse & there be serched & marked by suche that have the serche therof as hathe ben accustomed, upon payne to forfaite the value of ev*y hide or parcell of Lether tanned and sold after the said Feast cont*ry to this AGe; Nor that any psone or psones upon like payne put any tanned Lether to sale, out of the said Markette of Leaden Hall & out of the feires kepte within the said Citie & thre myles compasse therof in any other place or places of this Realme, but only in open fayres or markettf holden & kepte within any pte of this Realme; the one half of suche forfayture if it be within the Citie of London or within thre myles compasse therof, to be to the Kyng our Sovaign Lorde, and thother half therof to the Wardens of the Felowshipp of the Cordeweyners within the same Citie or to the Wardens of the Felowshipp of the Saddelers, Girdelers, Coriers, or any other of the Kynges Subjects in the said Citie, that is to saye; to suche of the said Wardens or Kynges Subjects that shall firste sue for the same, by acc&n of Dette Bill Pleynte or InformaCon in any of the Kynges Courtes, in whiche Sute no essoyne pteccion, ne wager of La we shalbe admytted : And if the said forfayture happen to be out of the said Citie & out of the said thre myles compasse, [than * ] the one moytie of suche penaltie to be to the Kyng our Sovaign Lord, and thother moytie therof to the Maires Sheriffes Bailliffes of Cities Boroughes & Townes corporate and Lordes of Letes within whose jurisdiedon or auGoritie any suche forfayture shall happen to be recoded by like acdon & sute, and after like maner as is above saide. And for lacke of so doyng, that then it shalbe lefull for any of the Kynges Subjects to have power & auGoritie in the suyng therfore.

PRAYEN the Comons in this psente Parlyamente assembled. That where dy9s psones within this Realme of Englond, as well Alyens as other usynge the Mysterie or Crafte of Dyers, now of late have used & exercised a false sleyghtie & deceyvable waye in dyeng withe Brasell & suche other like subtilytes first invented & founde by Alyens borne oute of this Realme of Englond, to the great hurte & sclaunder of Wollen Cloths died within the said Realme, whiche in tymes past have in all outwarde pries ben noted to have hadde the moost substanciall colored Wollen Clothes of all Realmes cristened; That it may therfor be enacted & establysshed by the Kyng our Sovaign Lorde, the Lordes Spuall & Temporall & the C5mons in this psente Parlyament assembled & by the au&oritie of the same.
