CHAPTER III.

An Acte for Fleshe to be sold by weight.

COMPLAYNETH to your moost excellent Highnes your poore Subjects of this yor Realme, that where all ma9 of Vytailies before this tyme hathe ben sold to your said Subjects at prices convenient, so that all your Subjects Sc in especiall the poore psones myght withe there crafte or bodilie labour bye sufficient for the necesside Sc sustenta£6n of them there Wyffes Sc Childem; But nowe gaciouse Lorde all vitaile Sc in especiall beoffe mutton porke Sc veale whiche is the cdmon fedyng of the meane & poore psones arr so solde at so excessyve price that your said nedye Subjects can not gayne withe ther labour & salarie sufficient to pay for there convenyent vitaile & sustynance; For reformacion wherof it may please Your Highnes, that it may be enacted by your Grace Sc the Lordes Spuall & Temporall Sc the Comons in this Psente Parliamente assembled & by audoritie of the same, that e9y psone, whiche shall sell by hym self, or any other, the Carcases of Beoffes Porke Mutton or Veale or any parte or parcell therof after the first day of Auguste nowe nexte ensuyng shall sell the same by laufull weighte called Haberdepayes & no otherwise ; the said Flesshe to be cut out in reasonable peces, according to the requeste of the byer in like fescion as before this tyme hathe ben used, without fraude or covyn. And that e9y psone, which by hymself or ony other shall sell any Flesshe of the said Carcases, shall have withe hym where he shall make sale of the said flesshe sufficient Beame Scales Sc Weyghtes sealed called Haberdepayes for true §vyng of the byers.

And furthermore, be it enacted by audoririe aforesaid, that after that day no psone nor psones take nor cause to be taken, for any pounde weight of flesshe of the carcases of Beoffe or Porke by hym or them to be solde above the price of one halfpeny, nor for any pounde weight of Flesshe of the carcases of mutton or veale above the price of one halfpeny & half ferthyng without deceyte or covyn, upon peyne to forfeite for e9y pound not solde [be1] weight or above the said price lymyted Sc for evy defaute done cont*ry to the true meanyng of this ade iij s. iiij d. the one moide therof to be to the Kyng our Sovaign Lorde & thother moytie to the partie that wyll sue for the same by byll, pleynte or informacion, in whiche Sute none Essoen, Wager of Lawe, nor ptection shalbe allowed : Provyded alway that the heedys neckes inwardes purtynances legges nor fete shall not be counted no parte of the carcases afore said, but suche to be solde for a lower price.

And furthermore be it enacted by audoritie aforesaid, that the Lorde Chauncellour Lorde Tresourer Lorde Pryvye Seale & Presidente of the Kynges moost honorable Counsell Sc the twoo chicffe Justices of either Benche or v. iiij. or iij. of them, shall have full power Sc audoritie by there discrecions, at all tymes hereafter for causes convenyent to mynysshe & abate the prices above rehersed but in no wise to enhaunce the same. And that all Justices of Assises in there circuyte Sc all Justices of Peace or two of them at the leaste within ther lymyttes, and all Mayers Bailliffes & other heed officers of evy Cide Borough & Towne corporate. Aldermen Sheriffes eleded Stewardes of Frauncheses the Maiers Bailiffes eleded Sc Jurates of the Portes, Sc all other psones havyng laufull audoritie before the makeng of this psente Ade, to sette price of Flesshe & ev*y of them in there lymyttes, shall have full power Sr audoririe to sette a lower price of suche Flesshe as is above remembred, & to enquere of suche offenders & to awarde like pees ageynst them & sette like fynes as they may do in psentmentes or inditementes of riotte or trespas tried before them.

Provyded alwayes, that no Calf above thage of eight wekys olde, be accompted for veale, but for beoffe and so to be solde, as is afore rehersed. Provyded alwayes, that where the Carcases of any beoffes, muttons, veale & porke within any partes or countres of this Realme be ut?ed Sc solde better chepe or after lasse prices than in this psente Ade is lymyted, that this Ade or any thyng therin conteyned shall not extend to any suche Countie or Place, but that they shall Sc may sell at like Prices & after suche rate as they dyd Sc used before the makyng of this Ade, upon peyne as is afore rehersed, any thyng in the same conteyned notwithstondyng. CHAPTER IV.

An Acte conSnyng sowing of Flaxe and Hempe.

TIE KINGES Highnes, callyng to his moost blissed remembrance the great nombre of ydell people daily encreasing thoroughout this his Realme, supposeth that one greate cause therof is by the contynuall bringyng into the same the greate nombre of Wares and Schaundise made and brought oute and firome the parties of beyonde the See into this his Realme, redy wrought by manuell occupacion; amongest the which Wares, one kynde of fichaundise in iftvelous greate quantide which is Lynnyn Cloth of dyvs sortes made in dyPs Countries beyonde the See is daily conveid into this Realme, which greate quantide of Lynnyn Clothes so brought is consumed and spente within the same; By reason wherof not only the said straunge Countres, where the seid Lynnen Clothe is made by the policie and industrie of makyng and ventyng therof are greately enriched and a Svelous greate nombre of theyr peple men women and children sett on worke and occupadon and kepte frome idelnes to the greate fortheraunce and advauncement of thdr comen Welthe, but also contrarie wise the inhitauntez and subje&es of this Realme, for Lake of like polide and industrie aboute the inventing pra&isyng and puttyng in ex?cise like occupadon beyng compelled to bye all or the moost parte of the said Lynnen Clothe contynually spent and consumed within this Realme amountyng to inestymable somes of Money in other regions and countreis; And also the people of this Realme, as well Men as Women which shuld and myght be sette on worke by exccisyng of like policie and craftes of spynnyng, weavyng and makyng of Lynnen Clothe lyve nowe in ydelnes and odositie, to the high displeasoure of Almyghtie God, greate dymynucion of the Kinges people and extreme ruyne decay and ympo^ysshement of this Realme ; For Reformacion wherof the Kinges Roiall Magestie, intendyng like a moost Ptuous Prince to pvide remedye in the pmisses nothing so moche coveytyng as the encreace of the Comenwelth of this his Realme with also the 9tuous exc?cise of his moost loving subje&es and people, and to avoyde that moste abhomynable vice of ydelnes oute of this Realme, hath by the advise and assente of his Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Commons in this pkent parliament assembled, and by au&oritie of the same, ordeyned and enaded, that all ma8 psones of what degree, estate or condicion they be of, havyng in their occupadon [threscore *] acres of arrable londe or pasture, or threscore acres of arrable Lande and pasture beynge apte for tillage, shall yerely for e9 after the feaste of Saynte Michell tharchaungell nexte comyng at their ppre costes and charges, till and sowe, or cause to be tilled and sowen in seasonable tyme oone roods that is to say, the iiijtb parte of one Acre of the Londe beyng in their occupacion as is afforesaid with lynseade otherwise called flaxe seade or hempe seade, or with bothe, the saide Roode to be sowen in one place together or in sePall places at their pleasoure; and so frome the said feaste yerely shall till and sowe or cause to be tilled and sowen one roode for evy [threscore'] Acres which he or they shall happen to have in occupadon as is aforesaid, without any fraude or covyne; upon peyne to forfaite iij s. iiij d. for e9y [thre score *] Acres which any psone or psones shall have in occupacion as is aforesaid, and not till and sowe or cause to be tilled and sowen oone roode according to this a&e in maS and forme afore rehersed.

An Acte that the Appeles in suche Cases as have ben used to be pursued to the See of Rome shall not be from

hensforth had ne used but wythin this Realme.

TT THERE by dyvers sundrie olde autendke histories and cronicles it is manifestly declared and exPssed that this V V Realme of Englond is an Impire, and so hath ben accepted in the worlde, gowned by oon Supine heede and King having the Dignide and Roiall Estate of the Imperiall Crowne of the same, unto whome a Body polidke compa&e of all sortes and degrees of people, devided in tenues and by names of Spualtie and Temporalde, ben bounden and owen to here nexte to God a naturall and humble obedience *, he beyng also institute and fumysshed by the goodnes and sufferaunce of Almyghtie God with plenarie hoole and intiere power Pemynence auftoritie progatyve and jurisdiction to rendre and yelde Justice and finall de?mynacion to all raa8 of folke reseauntes or Subjects within this his realme, in all causes maters debates and contencions happenyng to occurr insurge or begyne within the limittes therof without restraynt or pvocacion to any foreyn Princes or Potentates of the World: The Body Spuall wherof having power whan any cause of the Lawe devine happened to come in question or of spuall lemyng, [than *] it was declared interprete and shewed by that parte of the said bodye politike called the Spualtie nowe beyng usually called the Englishe Churche, which alwaies hath ben reputed and also founde of that sorte that bothe for knowlege integritie and sufficiencie of nombre it hath ben alwaies thought and is also at this houre sufficiente and mete of it selffe, without the intermedlyng of any exterior psonne or psonnes, to declare and detmyne all suche dubtes and to administre all suche offices and dueties as to their romes spuall doth apperteyne; For the due admynystracion wherof and to kepe them frome corrupcion and synystre affection the Kinges moost noble pgenitours, and the antecessours of the Nobles of this Realme, have sufficiently endowed the said Churche both with honour and possessions: And the Lawes Temporall for triall of pprietie of Landes and Goodes, and for the conservacion of the people of this Realme in unitie and peace without ravyn or spoilt, was and yet is administred adjudged and executed by sondry Judges and Administers of the other parte of the said body politike called the Temporaltie, and bothe their auctoritifes and jurisdictions do conjoyne together in the due administradon of Justice the one to helpe the other: And where as the Kinge his mooste noble pgenitours and the Nobilitie and Comons of this said Realme at dyvers and sondry parliamentes as well in the tyme of King Edwarde the firste, Edwarde the thirde, Richard the seconde, Henry the fourth, and other noble Kinges of this Realme made sondrye ordenaunces lawes statutes and pvisions for the entier and [suerconservacion of the progatyves libties and Pemynences of the said Imperiall Crowne of this Realme, and of the jurisdictions spuall and temporall of the same, to kepe it frome the anoyaunce aswell of the See of Rome as fromme the auctoritie of other foreyne potentates attemptyng die diminudon or violacion therof as often and frome tyme to tyme as any suche annoyaunce or attempte myght be knowen or espied: And notwithstanding the said good estatutes and ordynaunces made in the tyme of the Kyngf most noble pgenytours in Pservacyon of the auctoritie and progatyff of the said Imperyall Crowne as is aforesayd, yet nePtheles sythen the makyng of the sayd good statutes and ordenauncf dyvers and sondry inconveniences and

CHAPTER Xm.

An Acts for Reformacyon of Excesse in Apparayle.

WHERE before this tyme dyvers lawes ordyn*nces and statutes have ben with greate delibadon and advyse jpvided established and devised, for the necessarie refPssing avoydyng and expelling of the inordynate excesse dailye more and more used in the sumptuous and costly araye and apparell accustomahlye wome in this Realrae, wherof hath ensued and dailie do chaunce suche sondrie high and notable inconveniences as be to the greate manifest and notorious detryment of the comon Weale, the subv^cion of good and polidke ordre in knowelege and distinedon of people according to their estates ^emynences dignities and degrees, and to the utter impoPysshement and undoyng of many inexpert and light psones inclyned to pride moder of all vices; which good Lawes notwithstanding, the oulteragious excesse therin is rather frome tyme to tyme increased than diminysshed, eyther by the occadon of the pverse and frowarde maners and usage of people, or for that errours and abuses ones rooted and taken into longe custome be not facilie and at ones without some moderacion for a tyme relinquisshed and reformed: In consideradon wherof and for a reasonable order and remedye like to be observed pfourmed and contynuallye kepte, It is by the Kmgea Highnes the Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Commons in this jpsent pliament assembled and by auctoride of the same enacted established and ordeyned in matt and forme followyng ; Firste that no psone or psones of whate estate dignitie degree or condicion so ev* they be, frome the feast of the Purification of our Lady which shall be in the yere of our Lorde M1 D xxxiij use or were in any matt thdr apparell or uppon their Horse Mule or other beaste any silke of the Collour of Purpure, ne any Clothe of Golde of Tissue, but onely the Kinge, the Quene, the Kinges Moder, the Kinges Children, the Kinges firethem, and Systers and the Kinges Uncles and Auntes; CHAPTER I.

An Acte con&iyng Grasiers and Bouchers.

WHEREAS diverse and sondry Adys and Statutes have lately byn made and established within this Realme for pservacbn of the comon welthe of the same, amongis whiche the Ade for sellyng of beoffe mutton veale and porke by weyghte ys so necessarie for the pserva£6n of the povertie of the same that it may in nowyse be forborne, and for asmoche as sufficient audoritie ys not gyven by the seid ade to the Justices of the Pease maires baillyffes shyreffes and other officers rehersed in the same ade for to punyshe offenders and suche other as wyll not sell by weyghte accordyng to the force of the seid ade, And the Bouchers and other offenders pceyvyng the same not dredyng the vioiacion of the seid ade nor the punyshementys conteyned in the same ade, have wylfully and [obstinaly1] contempned and offended the seid ade and wolle in no wyse sell after the same, to the highe displeasure of the Kyngis Hyghnes in contempte of hys seid lawes and to the detrymente of the c5mon welthe of this Realme: Be it therfore further enadid by audoritie of this psent parliament that from the xx*1 day of Februarie in the yere of oure Lorde God M1. D. xxxiij11 it shalbe lawfull to all and e9y maires shireffes constables baylyffes and other govemours of Cities Boroughes and Market townes, aswell within libties as without, to whome any compleynt shall be made of or [apon*] any boucher hys wyf servantes or other his mynystres refusyng to sell the seid victuals by true and lawfull weyght accordyng to the tenour of the seid ade heretofore made, not only to comytt e9y suche Boucher and suche other offenders to warde, there to remayne withoute bayle or maynepryse unrill suche tyme as they and e9y of theym shall have payde all the forfetris and penalties comprised in the seid former ade, but also e9y of the seid maires and other officers aforseid and theire Deputies shall ymmediatly sell and utter or cause to be solde and ut?ed for redy money by true weyghte all suche viduals so refused to be retayled and solde by true and lawfull weyght accordyng to the effede of the seid former Ade, delyvering allways the monay therof comyng unto the owners of the same viduals; whiche owners shalbe utterly and for ever excluded to have any accion suyte or demaunde ayenst any suche maire or other officers or theire Deputies for sellyng or utteryng of the seid viduals by true and lawfull weyght in forme aforseid or for any other cause or thyng con?nyng the same, except only for the money receyved for the same viduals yf it be not [ apon1 ] reasonable request therof to be made payde or restorede without deleye.

And to the yntent that the Bouchers from tyme to tyme may be the more redie and able to utter and sell the seid viduals by true and lawfull weyght, It is further ordeyned establysshed and enadid by the audoririe aforsed that evy owner grader fermour breder drover and brogger of this Realme. which after the seid day shall have any beoffes muttons veales or porkes fatte and kepte to be sowlde for mans mete, shall at all tymes when soo ever any Boucher or Bouchers or other psone or p6ones shall resorte to theym to bye the same to be kylled or retayled ageyne by lawfull weighte, shall make sale of theire seid catallis, to ev*y suche Bocher or Bochers as [well by1] the same to be retayled by lawfull weight as is aforseid, at suche resonable pryse or prices so as the seid Bochers or others always may retayle the same agayne by lawfull weight as is aforeseid accordyng to the effede of the seid former ade made for the sellyng of fleshe by weight, The seid Bochers alwayes paying for the same catall redy money in hande or at suche dayes as the owner of the seid catall may be agreed withall; And yf the seid owners grasiers fermours breders drovers and broggers or any of theym at any tyme or tymes after the seid xxtl day of Februarij shall refuse to sette any suche

CHAPTER V.

An Acte for callendrynge of Worstedes.

XX7TIERE AS at the parliament holden at Westraynster the xxiij. day of Januarye in the v. yere of our Soverayne v v Lordys reigne the Kyng that nowe is, there was an acte and one estatute made pvided and establisshed for the advoydyng of deceytes and falsnes in worstedes, aswell by reason of drye callendryng therof with gummes oyles and presses as also by weete callendryng by psons havyng no connyng in orderyng of the same, which ade was made to endure but only to the parlyament then next folowing; And for as moche as it is evydently knowen that the same ade and estatute aforseid is verye good and necessarie for the comen welthe of this Realme, wherfor the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde by the advyse and consent of hys Lordis Spuall and tempo rail and the comons of this present parliament assembled and by the audoride of the same, hath ordyned enacted and establisshed that the seid ade and estatute made in the v. yere of hys most noble reigne aforsed, and evy thyng therin conteyned shall from the feast of Seynt Michell the archangell [nex1 ] comyng contynue and be good and effectuall in every poynte and ardcle of the same for ever.

And furthermore be it enacted and establysshed by the audoride aforseid, for the comen welthe of the Citie of Norwiche and maynten*nce supportadon and upholdyng of the howses tenemends and habitadons of the same, that noo maner peon usyng the crafte or mysPie of dying of worstedes stamyns or sayes or of any of theytn, nother by theymselves or any §v*nt fadour Depude or any other by hys edmaundement or assignement, from the feast of Christmas now next ensuyng, shall use to calender any worstedes stamens or sayes or any other comodities made of worstede yarne duryng all suche tyme as the same psone shall use the mystery or crafte of dying aforseid, uppon payn to forfett for e&y pece so dyed and calendred by colour coven or fraude cont*ry to the true meanyng and entent of this prent ade xl s. and to be devyded in thre egall pries, the one parte therof to the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde and one other parte to the maire for the tyme being and the thride parte to hym or theym that wyll sue for the same by byll accion of dette playnt informadon or otherwyse in any of the Kingf courtes wherin none essoen delaye or pteccion shalbe allowed.

CHAPTER VI.

An Acte for the punysshement of the vice of Buggerie.

CHAPTER VH.

An Acte against kyllyng of yonge spaune or frye of Yeles & Salmon.

FIR AS MOCHE as great hurte and dayly inconvenyence have and do ensue unto all the Kynges subie&es of this Realme by the gredie appetites and insaciable desire which sondrie of theym occupying Fysshing have used, by takyng kyllynge and destroyng the yonge spaune frie or brode of Yeles and Salmon aswell in sake ryvers as in fresshe ryvers Lakes plashes fennes and marshes in many parties of this Realme, to the no lyttyll hynderaunce and derogation of the comen weale of the same, as also in kyllyng of Salmons when they be unsesonable and not holsome for manna body called comenly kypper salmons: It is therefore enacted by the kyng our Sovaigne Lorde the Lordes spuall and temporall and the cSmons in this Psent parliament assembled and by the au&oritie of the same, that from the fyrst day of Februarye next comyng unto the last day of July then next ensuyng, and soo yerely from thensforth duryng the space of tenne yeres, no maner of pson or psones, of what estate degree or condidon so ever they be, with any maner of nette wele or with any devyse or engyne made of heare canvas or with any other cawtell, shall wyllyngly psume to take any Frye spawne or brode of yeles called yele fares or Ell vares, in any ryvers or waters sake or fresshe within this realme of Englond or Wales or in the marches of the same: And over thys that duryng the seid tene yeres no maner of psone or psones frome the furst day of May which shalbe in the yere of our Lorde God M1. And furthermore the seid Thomas Golde for the accomplisshment of hys sed moste traytrous intent hath of late byn a mesynger frome the seid Elizabeth, sithen she was in ward in the towre of London for the seid most false and traytrous offences by her and her seid complyces comyttid and done, he then being at libertie by hys message hath comforted dyvers others to stonde styffely by her revelacions that they were of God, notwithstondyng that she had confessed all her seid falshed before dyverse of the Kynges Counseylers, and that they were manyfestly proved founde and tryed most false and untrue; which thynge he dyd only to reyse and put sedicion and murmur in the people ayenst the Kynges Highnes hys Crowne and Dignytye Ryall: and one Thomas Abell clerke being of the confederacie aforseid and takyng suche firme and constante credyte to the seid false and feyned revelacions and myracles of the seid Nunne, not only caused to be prynted and sett forth in this Realme dyvers bokys ayenst the seid devorse and sepacion to the disclander of our seid Soveraigne Lorde, but also anymated the seid Lady Katharyne obstynatly to psist in hir wylfull opynyon against the same devorse and seperacion, and after the seid devorse lawfully had, to usurpe and take upon her stylle to be Qilene, and paired dyverse wrytyngys to be made by her by the name of Quene; and also peured and abetted the servauntf of the seid Lady Katharyne ayenst the Kyngf expresse comaundement and pclamacion to name calle accept and repute the seid Lady Katharyne for Quene of thys Realme, to the intent to make a cornyn dyvysyon and rebellyon in this Realme to the [to the4 3 great perell and daunger of our seid Soveraigne Lorde,

CHAPTER XIII.

An Acti conSayng Fermes & Shepe,

FOR ASMOCHE as dyvers and sundry [persones3] of the Kynges Subjects of this Realme, to whome God of hys Eriiof the Excess goodnes hath disposed greate plentie & abundaunce of movable substance, nowe of late within fewe yeres have dayly studyed pra&ised and invented ways and meanes how they myght accumulate and gather together into few of Tillage; handes aswell great multitude of fermes as greate plentie of catall and in espedall shepe, puttyng suche londf as they can gett to pasture and not to tyllage, wherby they have not only pulled downe churches and townes and inhansed the olde ratis of the rentis of the possessions of this Realme, or els brought it to suche excessyve fynes that no poure man is able to medell with it, but also have raysed and enhaunsed the prises of all maner of come catall woll pygges geese hennes chekyns egges and suche other almoste doble above the prices which hath byn accustomed, by reason wherof a mervaylous multitude and nombre of the people of this Realme be not able to pvyde meate drynke and clothes necessary for theym selfes theire wyfes and childern, but be so discoraged with myserye and povertie that they fell dayly to thefte robberye and other inconvenience, or pitifully dye for hunger and colde ; And as it is thought by the Kytiges most humble and lovyng subje&f that one of the gretest occasions that moveth and provoketh those gredy and covetous people so to accumulate and kepe in theire handes suche greate porcions and parties of the groundes and landis of this Realme frome the occupying of the poure husbondmen, and so to use it in pasture and not in tyllage, is only the greate pfette that comyth of shepe which now be c5myn to a few psons handes of this Realme in respecte of the holle nomber of the Kynges Subjectes, that some have xxiiij thousand s5me xx thousande some x thousand some vj thousande some v thousand and some more and some lesse, by the which a good shepe for vytall that was accustomed to be solde for ij s. iiij d. or iij s. at the moste, is now solde for vj s. or v s. or iiij s. at the leaste. And a stone of clothyng wolle that in s5me shire of this Realme was accustomed to be sold for xviij d. or xx d. is nowe solde for iiij s. or iij s. iiij d.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte for punysshement of Heresye.

IN moste humble wyse lamentablye [shewen1 ] unto your Highnes your most humble lovyng and obedyent subjedes the comons of this your Realme; That where the Clergie of the same in the secounde yere of Kyng Henry the iiij** one of your most noble pgenitours uppon theire suggestyon, dyd impetrate & opteyne by audoritie of parliament holden in the seid seconde yere, that it shulde be lefoll for evy ordynarye to convent areste and imprison any person or persons whom they thought defamed or suspede of Heresie; and theym to kepe in theire [persons1] tyll they were purged therof or abjured or comytted to [ley*] power; to be burned after the dePmynacion of the holy Churche and canonicall sandions ; as in an ade made at the parlyament holden in the seid secounde yere of Kyng Henry the iiij* emonges other thynges more at large doth appere; For asmoche as the seid ade doth not in any parte therof declare any certeyne cases of Heresye contrary to the determynacion of holye scripture or the canonicall sandions therm expressed, wherby your most lovyng and obedyent subjects mought be lemed to eschewe the daungers and paynes in the seid ade comprised, and to abhorre and deteste that foule and [destable4] cryme of heresie; And also by cause those wordes canonycall sandions and suche other lyke conteyned in the seid ade are soo generall, that unneth the most expert and best lemed men of this your Realme diligently lying in wayte uppon hym selff can eschewe and avoyd the penaltie and daunger of the same ade and canonycall sanctions yf he shulde be examyned upon suche capcious intxogatoryes as is and hath byn accustomed to be mynystred by the Ordynaries of this Realme in cases where they wyll suspede any pson or psones of heresye : And over this for asmoche as it stondeth not with the right order of justice nor good equytie that any pson shuld be convyde and put to the losse of hys lyfe good name or goodes onles it were by due accusacion and wytnes, or by presentment [verdyd5] confession or pees of outlarye; and also by the lawes of your Realme for treasons comyttid to the perell of your most Ryall Majestie, uppon whose suertie dependith the hole welth of this Realme, noo person can ne may be putto deth but by presentment verdid confession or proces of outlarye as is afore seid; wherfore it is not resonable that any Ordynarye by any suspeccion conceyved of hys owne fantasie without due accusacion or presentment shuld put any subjede of this Realme in the mfamye and slaunder of heresie to the perell of lyf losse of name and goodes; And that also there be many heresyes and paynes and punyshementes for heresyes declared and ordyned in and by the seid canonycall sanctions and by the lawes and ordynaunces made by the Popes or Bisshops of Rome and by theire audorities, for holdyng doing preachyng or spekyng of thynges cont*ry to the seid canonycall sandions lawes and ordynances which be but humayne being mere repugnaunte and contrarious to the prerogatyve of your ymperyall Crowne regal jurisdiccion lawes statutes and ordyn*nces of this your Realme; By reason wherof your people of the same for observyng maynteynyng defendyng and due executyng of your seid lawes statutes and prerogatyve royall by audoritie of that ade made in theseid seconde yere of Kyng Henry the fourth may be brought into slaunder of heresye to theire greate infamye and daunger and perell of theire lyves: In consideracion wherof it may please your Highnes by the assent of your Lordes Spirituall and temporall and the comyns in this present parliament [assembled6] and by audoritie of the same to adnulle abrogate frustrate and make voyde theseid ade made in the seid secounde yere of Kyng Henry the iiij,h and ev*y thynge therin conteyned.

And Nevertheles for asmoche as the mooste foule and detestable cryme of heresye shuld not here after growe and [incrace7] but utterly be abhorred detested and eradycate, ne that any heretikes shuld be favored but that they shuld have condigne and sufficient punyshment, and for the represse of herytykes and suche erronyous opynyons in tyme cdmyng; Be it establysshed ordeyned and enacted by the audoritie of this presente parliamente that the statute made in the fyfthe yere of your noble pgenitour Kyng Richarde the seconde, and the statute made in the seconde yere of Kyng Henry the v,h con&nyng punyshement and reformacion of herytykes and lollardes and e9y provysyon therin conteyned, not being repugnaunt to this ade, shalbe and stonde in theire force strengfc and effede.

CHAPTER XV.

An Acte for prynters & bynders of bokf.

WHERE AS by the pvysyon of a statute made in the fyrst yere of the reigne of Synge Richarde the thride it was pvyded in the same a&e, that all strangers reparyng into this Realme myght lawfully bryng into the seid Realme pryntyt and wrytyn bokf to sell at theire litotie and pleasure; by force of which pvysyon there hath c5men into this Realme sithen the makyn of the same a marveylous nombre of pryntyd bokes and dayly doth ; And the cause of the makyng of the same pvysion semeth to be, for that there were but fewe bokes and fewe prynters within this Realme at that tyme which cold well exercise and occupie the seid science and crafte of pryntyng; Never the lesse sithen the makyng of the seid pvysion many of this Realme being the Kynges naturall subjedes have geven theyme soo dylygently to lerne and exercyse the seid craft of pryntyng that at this day there be within this Realme a greatt nombre conyng and expert in the seid science or craft of pryntyng as abyll to exercyse the seid craft in all poyntf as any Stranger in any other Realme or Countre; And furthermore where there be a great nombre of the Kynges subjedf within this Realme which [ leve *] by the crafte and mysfte of byndyng of bokf and that there be a great multytiide well expert in the same; yet all this not withstondyng there are dyv^se psones that bryng frome [behonde*] the See great plentie of pryntyd bokes not only in the latyn tonge but also in our matemall englishe tonge, some bounde in bourdf s5me in lether and s5me in pchement and theym sell by retayle, wherby many of the Kynges Subje&f being bynders of bokes and havyng none other facultie wherwith to gett theire lyvyng be destitute of worke and lyke to be undon, except some reformadon here in be hade *, Be it therfore enacted by the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde the Lordes spirituall and temporall and the Comons in this present parliament assembled and by audoride of the same, that the seid provyso made the furst yere of the seid Kyng Richard the thride frome the feast of the natyvytie of our Lorde [Good1] next comyng shalbe voyde and of none effect.

And further be it enacted by the auctoritie aforseid that noo person or persones recyant or inhabytaunt within this Realme, after the seid feast of Cristemas next cdmyng, shall bye to sell agayn any prynted bokes brought frome any partes out of the Kynges obeysaunce redy bounden in bourdes lether or perchement, uppon payne to lose and forfett for every boke [bounde4] out of the seid Kynges obeisaunce and brought into this Realme and bought by any person or persons within the same to sell agayne contrary to this Acte vj s. viij d.

And be it further enacted by the auctoritie aforseid that no person or persones inhabytaunte or redaunt within this Realme, after the seid feast of Cristemas, shall [ by5 ] within this Realme of any Stranger borne out of the Kynges obedyence other then of denyzens, any maner of pryntyd bokes brought frome any the parties [ behonde1 ] the See, except only by engrose and not by retayle uppon payne of forfayture of vj s. viij d. for every boke soo bought by retayle contrary to the forme and effecte of this estatute: The seid forfaytures to be alwayes levyed of the beyers of any suche bokes cont*ry to this Acte, the one half of all the seid foriaytures to be to the use of our Soveraigne Lorde the Kynge, and the other moytie to be to the partie that wyll sease or sue for the same in any of the Kynges Courtes, be it by byll playnt or informacion wherin the defendaunt shall not be admytted to wage hys lawe nor noo proteccion ne essoyne shalbe unto hym allowed.

Provided alway and be enacted by the auctoritie aforseid, that yf any of the seid prynters or sellers of prynted bokes, inhabyted within this Realme, at any tyme hereafter happen in suche wyse to enhaunce and encrease the prices of any suche prynted bokes in sale or byndyng at to high and unreasonable pryces, in stiche wyse as complaynt be made therof unto the Kynges Highnes or unto the Lorde Chaunceler Lorde Tresourer or any of the chefe Justices of the one benche or of the other, that then the seid Lord Chaunceler Lorde Tresourer and two chefe Justices or two of any of theym, shall have power and auctoritie to enquyre therof as well by the othes of twelf honest and discrett psones as otherwyse by due examynacion by theire discreacions; And after the same enhaunsyng and encresyng of the seyd pryces of the seid bokes and byndyng shalbe soo founde by the seid xij men, or other wayes by examynation of the seid Lord Chaunceler Lord Tresourer and Justices or two of theym, that then the same Lorde Chaunceler Lorde Tresourer and Justices or two of theym at the least frome tyme to tyme shall have power and auctoritie to reforme and redresse suche enhaunsyng of the pryces of prynted bokes from tyme to tyme by theire discreacions and to lymytt pryces aswell of the bokes as for the byndyng of theym j and over that the offender or offenders thereof being convicte by the examynacion of the same Lorde Chaunceler Lorde Tresourer and two Justices or two of theym or otherwyse, shall lose and forfett for every boke by theym solde wherof the pryce shalbe enhaunsed, for the boke or byndyng thereof iij s. iiij d. the one half therof shalbe to the Kynges Highness and the other half unto the parties greved that wyll complayne upon the same in maner and forme before rehersed.

CHAPTER XVU.

An Acte for shotyng in crosbowes & handgonnes.

II * THERE before this tyme dyvers and sondre good Statutes and pvysions have byn made and ordyned for the v V avoydyng and eschewyng of shotyng in crose bowes and handgonnes; which seid holsome statutes and pvysions notwithstondyng, many wylfiill and lyght disposed persones frome tyme to tyme have attempted the breche or vyolacion of the same estatutes: In consideracion wherof be it enacted ordyned and establisshed by the audoryde of this present parliament that no peon or persons of what Estate or degree he or they be, except he or they in theire owne right or in the right of hys or theire wyfes to hys or theire owne uses, or any other to the use of any suche person or persons, have landf tenementf fees annuyties or offices to the yerely value of an hundred poundes, frome the forst day of June next comyng shall shote in any [hangonne*] or crosse bowe, or use or kepe in hys or theire houses or els where any crose bowe or handgonne; upon payne to forfayte for every tyme that he or they soo offende contrary to this ade [xii.:3] And that it shalbe lefull to every person that may use and kepe any crose bowe or handgonne or that may shote in the same notwithstondyng this Ade, to sease and take every suche crosse bowe and handgonne or any of theyme frome the kepyng or possession of every suche offender, and the same to kepe or retayue to hys or theire owne use.

And be it further enacted by the audoride aforseid that noo Lordes or Owners of any Lettf beare or maynteyne any of theire ten*ntf or servantes within the precinde or jurisdicdon of ther Lettf to doo or offende cont*ry to this Ade, uppon payne to forfayte for every tyme soo offendyng [ x li.;1 ] the one moyde of all the same forfaytures to be to the Kynges Highnes hys heires or successours, and the other moyde to the parde that woll pursue for the same by byll playnt acdon of dett or informadon in any of the Kynges Courtes, in which sute no essoyne or proteccion shalbe allowed nor the defendaunt receyved to wage hys lawe.

Be it also further enacted by the audoride aforseid that it shalbe lefull to the Jusdces of Peax in theire Cessions and to all Stuardf and Baylyffes in thdre severall Lettf to enquyre here and detmyne every suche offence herafter to be comytted or don cont*ry to the fourme of this estatute; Soo that alway noo lesse fyne than [x ti.J] be assessed uppon every suche jPlsentment and convycdon accordyng to the due course of the lawe j The same fyne soo by the Jusdces of the pease uppon every presentment or covyccion made before theym, to be payd and levyed only to the Kynges use; And the moyde of every fyne to be assessed by the Stuardf or Baylyffes of every Lette uppon every psentment and convycdon before theym to be made to be payde and levyed to the use of the Owner of the same Lette by distres or acdon of dett, and the other moyde of the same fyne to be to the parde that woll pursue for the same in any of the Kynges Courtes by byll playnt informadon or acdon of dett in which noo essoyne nor proteccion shalbe allowed nor the defendaunt shalbe receyved to the wager of hys lawe.

Provided alway [yf4] any offender contrary to the forme of this estatute by any maner of pcesse or meane fyrst ayenst hym conceyved or presented, shalbe compelled or constrayned to pay or content any suche forfayture or penalitie as is aforseid for hys seid offence contrary to this Ade, that then every suche offender after payment or satisfaccion made therof shalbe clerely acquyted and discharged ayenst every other pson for the same forfayture or penaltie in ev^ey sute proces or presentment ayenst hym to be pursued for the recovery of the seid penaltie.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte restraynyng the payment of Annates, &c.

TTT7TIERE sithen the begynnyng of this present Parliament, for represse of the exaction of Annates and first Fretes V v of Archebyshopryches and Byshopryches of this Realme wrongfully taken by the Bisshop of Rome otherwyse called the Pope, and the See of Rome, It is ordyned and establisshed by an a&e amonges other thynges that the paymentf of the Annates or first frutes and all maner contributions for the same, for any suche Archebishopryche or Bisshopryche or for any bulles to be opteyned frome the See of Rome to or for the seid purpose or intent shulde utterly cesse, and no suche to be payd for any Archebishopriche or Byshopryche within this Realme otherwyse then in the same Acte is expressed; And that no maner of person or persons, to be named ele&ed presented or postulated to any Archebishopryche or Byshopryche within this Realme, shulde pay the seid Annates or first frutes nor any other maner of some or somes of money pentions or annuytes for the same or for any other lyke exaction or cause, uppon payne to forfait to our Soveraigne Lorde the Kynge hys heires and successours all maner hys goodes and catallis for ever and all the temporall landes and possessions of the seid Archebishopriche or Byshopryche duryng the tyme that he or they that shulde offende contrarye to the seid Acte shulde have possede and enyoe the seid Archebishopriche or Bishopriche; And it is further enacted that yf any person named or presented to the See of Rome by the Kynges Highnes or hys heires or successours to be Bisshop of any See or Dioces within this Realme, shuld happen to be [ lettet1 ] delayed or deferred at the See of Rome frome any suche Bishopriche wherunto he shulde be soo presented, by meane of restraynte of bulles of the seid Bysshop of Rome otherwyse called the Pope, and other thynges requysite to the same, or shulde be denyed at the See of Rome uppon convenyent sute made for any bulles requysite for any suche cause, that then every person soo presentid mought or shulde be consecrated here in Englonde by the Archibisshop in whose pvynce the seid Byshopryche shalbe, soo alwayes that the same person shulde be named and presented by the Kyng for the tyme being to the seid Archebishop; wherin the Bishop of Rome aforseid hath not byn only to be blamed for hys usurpadon in the premisses but also for hys abusyng and begylyng your subjectes, pretendyng and pswadyng to theym that he hath full power to dispence with all humayne lawes uses and customes of all Realmes in all causes which be called spirituall, which mater hath byn usurped and practised by hym and hys predycessours by many yeres in great derogadon of your imperiall crowne and au&orytie royall contrary to right and consdence; For where this your Graces Realme, recognysyng noo superior under God but only your Grace, hath byn and ys free firome subjecdon to any mannes lawes but only to suche as have bene devysed made and ordyned within this Realme for the welthe of the same, or to suche other as by sufferaunce of your Grace and your progenytours the people of this your Realme [ have6] taken at thdre free libertie by thdre owne consente to be used amonges theym, and have bounde theym selfes by longe use and custome to the observance of the same, not as to the observaunce of the lawes of any foren Prynce Potentate or Prelate, but as to the accustomed and aundent lawes of this Realme orygynally established as lawes of the same by the sdd sufferance consentes and custome and none otherwyse: It stondith therfore with naturall equytie and good reason that in all and (7) e9ey suche lawes humayne, made within this Realme or induced into this Realme by the sdd sufferaunce consentes and custome, your Royall Majestie and your Lordes Spirituall and temporal! and C5mons, representyng the holle state of your Realme in this your most high Courte of Parliament, have full power and au&oritie not only to dispence but also to au&oryse some electe person or persones to dispense

H.

Neither the King nor his Subjc&s shall sue to Rome for any Dispensation or Licence:

III.

Dispensations may be granted by the said Archbishop in all Cases usually heretofore granted at Rome; but in unusual Cases not without the Assent of the King and Council.

CHAPTER XXII.

An Acte for the establishement of the Kynges succession.

IN THEIRE mooste bumble wyse shewen unto your Majestie your mooste humble and obedyent subjedes the Lordes Erils retaking spirituall and temporall and the Comons in this present parliament assembled, that syns it is the naturall inclinadon jn the^TOe^the of every man gladely and wyllynglye to pvyde for the suertie of bothe hys title and succession all though it touche hys onlye pryvate cause; We therfore mooste rightfull and dredfull Soveraigne Lorde reken our selfes moche more bounden to beseche and instant your Highnes, all though we doubt [not4] of your pryncely harte and wysdome myxed with a naturall affeccion to the same, to forsee and provyde for the perfite suertie of both you and of your moste lawfull succession and heires, upon whiche dependeth all our joye and welth, in whome also ys unyted and knytte the only mere true inheritaunce and title of this Realme without any contradiccion: Wherfore we your seyd mooste humble and obedyent subjedes in this present parliament assembled, callyng to our remembraunce the greate dyvysions whiche in tymes paste hathe byn in this Realme by reason of severall tides pretended to the imperiall Crowne of the same, which some tymes and for the most parte ensued by occasion of ambiguyte and doubtf then not soo perfydlye declared but that men myght upon frowarde internes expounde tbeym to every mans synystre appetite and affeccion after theirc sence, contrarie to the right legalirie of the succession and posteritie of the lawfull Kynges and Emperours of this Realme, wherof hath insued great effusion and destruccion of mans blode aswell of a great noihbre of the nobles as of other the subjedf and specially inheritours in the same; And the greatest occasion therof hath byn by

In consideracion wherof your seid moste humble and obedyent subje&es the Nobles and Comons of this Realme callyng further to their remembraunce, that the good unytie pease and welthe of this Realme and the succession of the subje&ies of the same moste specially and pryncipallye above all [wordely1 ] thynges consisteth and resdth in the certende and suertie of the procreacion and posteritie of your Highnes, in whos most royall person at this present tyme is noo maner of doubt nor question, doo therfore mooste humbly beseche your Highnes that it may please your Majesrie, that it may be enacted by your Highnes with the assente of the Lordes spirituall and temporall and the Comons in this present parliament assembled and by au&oritie of the same, that the mariage hertofore solempnysed bytwene your Highnes and the Lady Katheryne, being before lawfull wyf to prynce Arthure your elder brother, which by hym was carnally knowen as doth duely appere by sufficient prove in a lawfull proces had and made before Thomas by the sufferaunce of [ Good1 ] nowe Archebisshopp of Canterbury and Metropolitane and prymate of all this Realme, shalbe by au&oritie of this present parliament diffyntyvly clerely and absolutely declared demed and adjudged to be against the lawes of Almyghty God, and also accepted reputed and taken of noo value ne effeSe, but utterlie voyde and adnychyied, and the sepacion therof made by the seid Archebisshop shalbe good and effectuall to all intentes and purposes, any licence dispensacion or any other a&e or a&es goinge afore or insuyng the same or to the contrary therof in any wyse not withstondyng; And that every suche licence dispensacion aflte or a&es thynge or thynges hertofore hade made don or to be don to the contrary therof shalbe voyde and of none effe&e; and that the seid lady Katharyne shalbe frorne hensforth called and reputed only Dowager to prynce Arthure and not Quene of this Realme. And that the lawfull matrimonye had and solemp-nyzed bytwene your Highnes and your moste dere and entyerly beloved wyf Quene Anne shalbe establisshed, and taken for undowtfull true syncere and pfe&e ever hereafter, accordyng to the juste judgement of the seid Thomas Archibisshop of Canturbury metropolitane and prymate of all this Realme, whose groundes of judgement have byn confirmed aswell by the hole Clergie of this Realme in both the Convocacions, and by both the Unyversities therof, as by the Unyversities of Bonony Padua Paris Orleance Toulouse Angiew and dyverse others. And also by the pryvate wrytyngf of many right excellente well lerned men ; whiche groundf soo confirmed and jugement of the seid Archebisshopp ensuyng the same, together with your mariage solempnysed bytwene your Highnes and your seid lawfull wyf Quene Anne, We your seid Subjectes both spirituall and temporall doo purely playnly constantly and firmely accepte approve and ratifie for good, and consonant to the lawes of Almyghty God without errour or defaute, mooste humble besechyng your Majesrie that it may be soo established for ever by your mooste gracious and royall assente.

And furthermore syns many inconvenyences hathe fallen aswell within this Realme as in others by reason of marying within degrees of mariage prohibited by Godf lawes, that is to sey, The son to marye the mother or the stepmother, the brother the sister, the father hys sonnes doughter or hys doughters doughter, or the son to mary the doughter of hys father. procreate and borne by hys stepmother, or the son to mary hys aunte being hys fathers or mothers sister, or to mary hys uncles wyfe, or the father to mary his sonnes wyff, or the Brother to mary his brothers wyfe, or any man to mary hys wyfes doughter or hys wyfes sonnes doughter or hys wyfes doughters doughter or hys wyfes sister; whiche mariages altho’ they be playnly prohybyte and detested by the lawes of God, yet never the lesse at some tymes they have proceeded under colours of dispensedons by mannes power, which is but usurped and of right ought not to be graunted admytted ne allowed, for no man of what estate degree or condidon soo ever he be hath power to dispence with Goddes lawes, as all the Clergie of this Realme in the seid Covocacions and the most parte of all the famous Universities of Christendome and we also doo affyme and thynke :

Be it therfore enacted by auftoritie aforseid that no person or persons subjeftes or reciauntes of this Realme or in any your Domynyons, of what estate degree or dignitie soo ever they be, shall firome hensforth may within the seid degrees afore rehersed, what pretence sooever shalbe made to the contrary therof; And in case any person or persons, of what estate dignitie degree or condidon soo ever they be, hath byn heretofore mariede within this Realme or in any the Kynges Domynyons within any the degrees above expressed, and by any the Archebishoppes Byshopes or Minysters of the Churche of Englonde be separate from the [boundes4] of suche unlawfull mariage, that e$y souche sepacyon, shalbe good laufull fyrme and permanent for ever, And not by any power auSoritie or meanes to be revoked or undone hereafter; And that the children procedyng & procreate under suche unlawfull mariage shall not be lawfull ne legittymate; any foren lawes licences dispensacions, or other thyng or thynges to the contrarye therof not withstondyng.

And in case ther be any person or persones within this Realme or in any the Kynges Domynyons allredy maryed within any the seid degrees above specified, and not yet separat frorne the [boundes4] of suche unlawfull mariage, that then every suche person so unlawfully maried shalbe separatt by the diffinytyve sentence and jugementf of the Archebishopes Bishoppes and other Mynysters of the Churche of Englonde, and in other your Domynyons within the lymyttes of

STATUTES MADE IN THE Session of Parliament,

HOLDEN BY PROROGATION AT WESTMINSTER, ON THE THIRD Day OF NOVEMBER,

In the TWENTY-SIXTH Year of the Reign of K. HENRY, VIII *

CHAPTER I.

An Acte con8nynge the Kynges Highnes to be supreme heed of the Churche of Englande & to have audoryte to refourme & redr esse all errours heresy es k abuses yn the same.

The King shall be reputed Supreme Head of the Church of England, and shall corre& all Heresies and Offences.

ALBEIT the Kynges Majesde justely and rightfully is k oweth to be the supreme [heed1] of the Churche of England, and so is recognysed by the Clergy of this Realme in theyr convocations ; yet neverthelesse for corroboration & confirmacion therof, and for increase of vertue in Crisis Religion within this Realme of England, and to represse k extirpe all errours heresies and other enormyties k abuses heretofore used in the same, Be it enacted by au&orite of this psent Parliament that the Kyng our Sovaign Lorde his heires and successours Kynges of this Realme shalbe takyn acceptyd & reputed the onely supreme [heed1] in erthe of the Churche of England callyd Anglicana Ecclesia, and shall have k enjoye annexed and unyted to the Ymperyall Crowne of this Realme aswell the title and style therof, as all Honours Dignyties phemynences jurisdictions privileges au&orities ymunyties profitis and comodities to the said dignytie of supreme [heed* ] of the same Churche belongyng and apperteynyng : And that our said Sovaigne Lorde his heires and successours Kynges of this Realme shall have full power & au&orite frome tyme to tyme to visite represse redresse reforme ordre corre& restrayne and amende all suche errours heresies abuses offences contemptes and enormyties what so ever they be, whiche by any maner spirituall au&oryte or jurisdicc&n ought or maie lawfullye be reformyd repressyd ordred redressyd corre&yd restrayned or amendyd, moste to the pleasure of Almyghde God the encrease of vertue yn Chrystis Religion and for the [conservacy1] of the peace unyte and tranquylyte of this Realme: any usage custome foreyne lawes foreyne au&oryte prescription or anye other thinge or thinges to the contrarie hereof notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER II.

An Acte ratyfienge the othe that everie of the Kynges Subjects hath taken and shall hereaft' be bounde to take for due obfvacyon of the a&e made for the surede of the successyon of the Kynges Highnes in the Crowne of the Realme.

Recital of the Oath of Obedience to the King and hit Heirs by Queen Anne, required by Statute *5 Hen. VlILc.22. §.9. and the Form of the Oath a&ually taken in consequence.

WHERE at the laste Sessyon of this psent pliament yn the a&e then made for the establyshment of the Successyon of the heyres of the Kynges Highnes yn the imperiall Crowne of this Realme, it ys conteyned amonges other thinges that all and singler the Kynges subje&es as well the nobles spirituall and temporall as other shulde make and take a corporall othe, whan so ever hit shulde please the Kynges Majesde or hys heires to appoynt, that they shulde truely fyrmely and constantly without fraude or gyle observe fulfille mayntayne defende and kepe to their connynge wytt and uttermoste of theyr powers the hole effe&es and contentes of the said a&e, as yn the same a&e amonge other thynges

And be yt further enacted by auctoryte aforesaid that the Commyssioners that hereafter shalbe appoynted to receyve suche othe of the Kinges subjectes, or two of theyme at the leste, shall have power and auctoryte to certifie ynto the Kinges Benche by writinge under their seales everie refusell that hereafter shalbe made afore theym of the same othe by any person or persons commynge afore theym to take the same othe; And that everie suche certificat to be made by suche Commyssyoners as is aforesaide shalbe taken as stronge & as available yn the lawe as an ynditement of xij men laufolly founden of the said refusell; So that the person and persons ayenste whome any suche Certificat shalbe made shalbe compellyd to answere there unto as yf they were endyted; and that suche pcesse judgement execusyon and everie other thinge shalbe hadde used and mynystred of and uppon everie suche certificat ayenste the offendours as yf they had ben lawfully endyted of suche offences by the due course & order of the commen lawes of this Realme.

The said Oath declared valid, and to be the Oath intended bv the said recited Ad.

Certificate of any Refusal to take the Oath before Commissioners shall be as available as an Indidment for such Refusal, and Process Arc. shall be had thereon.

CHAPTER IIL

An Acts conceminge the paiment of Firste Fruites of all dignities benefices andpmocyons spirituall; & also conceminge one annuell pencyon of the tenthe parte of all the possessions of the Churche, spirituall and temporall, graunted to the Kinges Highnes & his heires.

FOR ASMOCHE as it is & and of verie dude ought to be the natural! inclinacion of all good people lyke moste Necessity of faithfull lovynge and obedyent subjectes sincerely and willingly to desire to pvyde not onely for the publike weale of theire natife contrey, but also for the supportacion mayntenaunce and defence of the royall estate of their Crown: moste drade [benige*] and graciouse Soveraign Lorde, uppon whom and yn whom dependith all their joye and welthe, yn whom also is united and knyt so princely a harte and courage myxed wythe mercy wysdome and jusdee, and also a naturall affeccion joyned to the same, as by the greate inestimable and benevolent argumentes therof beinge moste bountefully largely and many tymes shewyd mynystred and approvyd towardes his lovynge and obedyent subje&es hathe well aperid, whiche requireth a lyke correspondcene of gratitude to be considered accordinge to their moste bounden duetyes ; Wherfore his said humble and obedyent subje&es as well the Lordes spyrituall and temporall as the commons yn this psent pliament assembled callinge to their remembraunce not onely the manyfolde and innumerable benefyttes dayly admynistred by his Highnes to them all, and to the resydue of all other his subje&es of this Realme, but also howe longe tyme his Majestie hathe moste victoriously by his high wisedome and polycye protectyd defendyd and govemyd this his Realme and mayntenyd his people and subjectes of the same yn tranquylite peace unyte quyetnes and welthe; And also consideringe what greate excessyve and inestimable Charges his Highnes hathe heretofore benne at and susteyned by the space of fyve and twenty hole yeres, and also dayly susteynethe for the maynten*nce tuyeion and defence of this his Realme and his lovynge subjectes of the same, whiche can not be susteyned and borne without some honorable provycion and remedy may be founde pvyded and ordeyned for mayntenaunce therof, do therfore desire and moste humbly praye that for the more surety e of corny nuance and augmentacion of his Highnes royall astate, beinge not onely nowe

That is to saye9 that the Kynges Highnes his heyres and successoures Kynges of this Realme shall have and enjoye frome tyme to tyme, to endure for ever, of everie suche persone and persones whiche at any tyme alter the fyrste daye of Januarye nexte comynge shalbe nomynatyd electyd prefected presentyd collated or by any other meanes appoynted to have any Archebusshopriche, Bisshopriche, Abbacye, Monasterie, Priori, College, Hospitalle Arche-deaconry, Deanry, Provestship, Prebende, Parsonage, Vicarage, Chauntrie, Frechapell, or other dignitie benyfice office or promodon spirituali within this Realme or els where within any of the Kynges domynions, of what name nature or qualytie so ever they be or to whose foundadon patronage or gyfte so ever they belonge, the fyrste firuytes revenewes and pfytes for one yere of every suche archebyshoppriche byshoppriche abbacye monasterie priori college hospitalle archedeconry deanry pvestshipp prebende psonage vicarage chauntrie frechapell or other dignitie benefice office or promodon spirituali afore namyd, wherunto any suche parson or psones shall after the saide first daie of Januarie be nomynated electyd prefoctyd presentyd collatyd or by any other meanes appoynted; and that everie suche persone and parsonnes, before any actuall or real possessyon or medlinge withe the profites of any suche archebishopriche byshoppriche abbacy monasterie college hospitall deanry provestshipp prebende parsonage vicarage chauntrie free chapell priorie or other dignytie benefice office or promodon spirituali, shall satisfie contente and paye or compownde or agree to paye to the Kinges use at reasonable dayes upon good sureties the said fyrste fruites and profytes for one yere.

And be yt also enactyd by auctoryte aforesaid that the Chauncelour of Englande and Mayster of the Rolles for the tyme beinge joyntly and severally, or suche other person and parsonnes as shall please the Kinges Highnes his heires or successoures frome tyme to tyme at his or thdr pleasure to name and depute by commyssion or commyssions under the greate seale, shall have power and auctoryte aswell to examyne and serche for the juste and true value of the said firste fruites and profites by all wayes and meanes that they canne, as to compounde and agre for the rate of the said firste fruites and profites and to stall and lymytte reasonable dayes for paiment therof, upon good and sufficient suertie or suerties by writinges obligatorie by their discredons; And yf composition or agrement be had or made for the said firste fruites before the said Lorde Chauncelour or Maister of the Rolles, that than the Writinges obligatory or money taken for the same shall reste remayne and abide yn the Hanaper of the Kinges Chauncerie there savely to be kepte to the Kinges use; and the money to be due of suche writinges obligatorie or to be receyved in hand by reason of any suche composition shalbe payed yn the said Hanaper to the clarke of the Hanaper for the tyme beynge, and that the said clarke of the Hanaper shall make a true and a juste accompte therof, like as he is bounde to do of the money receyved of the profites of the Kinges greate seale: And yf composicion or agrement be had or made for the said firste fruites afore any other parson or persones to be deputed by the Kinges Highnes his heires or successoures by Cdmyssion under his greate seale, that then the writinges oblygatory and money taken for the same shalbe delyverid to the Treasorour of the Kynges moste honerable Chaumber for the tyme beinge, or eles where to whom it shall please the Kinges Highnes his heires or successoures to gyve au&orite by cdmyssion under his greate seale to receyve the same.

And it is also ordeyned and ena&yd by auctoryte aforesaide that everie wridnge of acquitaunce subscribed withe the hande and name of the clarke of the Hanaper and Treasorer of the Chamber, or other comissioners aforesaide or any of theyme, witnessinge the receypt of the said firste fruites or any parte therof, shall be as good and effectuall agaynste the Kinges Highnes his heires and successoures to everie parson and parsones havynge the same, for so myche money as shalbe mencyoned to be receyved and conteyned yn everie suche acquitaunce, as yf suche acquitaunce were or had bynne lawfully hadde and opteyned yn the Kynges name under the Kinges greate seale and so shalbe admitted acceprid & alowid and taken yn everie of the Kinges Courtes: And that all writinges obligatory to be taken for payment of the sayd fyrste fruytes by and afore the said Lorde Chauncelour or Maister of the Rolles or by and afore any other persone or persones to be deputyd to compounde and agre for the said firste fruytes as is aforesaide, shalbe of the same strength force vertue qualite and effect to all ententes and purposes as writinges oblygatory heretofore made by any laye parsone by auctoryte of the statute of the Staple ben; and that uppon Certificat hereafter to be made yn the Kynges Chauncerie of any suche writynges obligatory to be taken for payment of suche fyrste fruytes, like processe and execusion shalbe theruppon made and had ayenste any person spirituali or temporall as hathe benne accustomyd to be made ayenst any lay parson upon Certificate of writinges obligatory of the said Statute of the Staple; And that no persone shalbe compellid to paye for any writinge obligatory to be made for the said payment of the said fyrste fruytes above viij d. nor for any acquyetaunce to be made for receipt of suche firste fruites above iiij d. And that suche parsone and persones as shalbe deputyd by the Kynges Highnes by comyssion under the greate seale to compounde and agre for the said firste fruytes shall at the ende of everie vj monthes next after the date of their cdmyssion, and so from vj monthes to yj monthes delyver or cause to be deliveryd unto the Treasorer of the Chamber for the tyme beynge, or els where to suche cdmyssioners as shalbe appoynted as is aforesaid to receyve the same, as well all suche money as all suche specialties and bondes as they shall have taken for the payment of the said firste fruytes by indenture to be made betwene them and the said Treasorour or other cdmyssioners as is aforesaide, conteyninge the certeyntie and numbre of the somes of money and specialties and bondes by them taken and receyved. And yf any persone or parsones to whom any deputacion shalbe made by cdmyssion to compound and agre for the payment of the said fyrst fruytes, their heires executours or admynistratours, concede or imbecill any of the said specialties or bondes taken for the sure payment of the said fyrste fruites and do not deliver them accordinge to the tenoure of this acte that then everie suche offendour shall forfayte that office of deputacion and over that make fyne and raunsome at the Kinges owne pleasure Sc wyll.

And it is also enactyd by audoryte aforesaid, that yf any persone or persones whiche at any tyme after the said firste day of January shalbe nomynated eleded pffe&yd ffeentyd collated, or by any other meanes appoynted, to any of the dignyties offices benefices or other promodons spirituall before mendoned, do entre yn to the actuall and reall possessions therof or medle withe the pfites therof before they shall have truly sadsfyed and payde to the Kinges use the firste firuites and profites therof for one yere, or els shall have agreed or compounded for payment of the same at reasonable dayes uppon good suerues in maner and fourme as by this ade is above especified, that than everie suche pson and parsones so doinge and offendinge and beinge therof convyde by psentment verdyt confession or wytnesse, before the said Lorde Chauncelour or suche other as shall have audoryte by comyssion to compounde for the saide firste fruites and pfites as is aforesaid, shalbe acceptyd and takyn an entruder upon the Kynges possession; And that they their executours or administratours shall paye to the use of the Kinges Highnesse for everie suche offence so moche some* of money as shall amounte to the double value of the said firste fruites and pfyttes of suche dignyties benefices or other spirituall promocions, wherin they shall so entre and entrude before the payment of the said fyrete fruites and pfittes for one yere therof, or before due agrement made for the same yn maner & fourme as is above rehersid.

ProvydEd also, that where there be dyverse Celles apparteyninge to Monasteries and Priores and that the Priours of suche Celles be namyd and removeable from tyme to tyme at the only willes and pleasures of their maysters and [ soveraynes1 ] of the Monasteries and Priories wherunto suche Celles belonge, that the Priours of suche Celles shall not be compellyd to paye any fyrste fruites by vertue or audoryte of this ade; any thinge yn this ade conteyned to the contrarie therof notwithstandinge: But that the firste fruites and profyttes of everie suche Celle shalbe payed to the Kynges Highnesse his heires and successoures, when so ever and as often as any parsone shalbe nomynated eleded prefected or collated to the Monastery or Pryory wherunto suche Celles belongyth.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte for punyshment of Perjury of Jurours yn the Lordshippes Merchers yn Wales.

WHERE for lacke of diligente & sure custodye of Jurours sworne for trialls of murderers, felons, Sc accessaries of felonyes & murders yn Wales & the merches of the same, dyvers adherentes fryndes St kynsfolkes to suche offendours have resorted to the same Jurours, and have suborned them to aquyte dyvers murderers felons & accessaries, openly and notoryously knowen cotrarie to equyte & justice \ It is therfore enacted by the Kynge oure Soveraigne Lorde and the Lordes spirituall & temporall and the Comons yn this fPsent pliament assembled and by the audoryte of the same, that forthwithe upon the charge gyven to any inqueste hereafter to be taken and sworne before any Justyciar, Stewarde, Lieutenaunt or other Officer within Wales or the Marches of the same, of for Sc upon any traverse ayenste the Kynge or the triall of any recognysaunce broken or any other forfayture forfayted to the Kynge, or of for Sc upon the triall of any murderer felon or accessarie of felonye or murder, one Officer or other person shalbe deputed and sworne yn the fPbence of the said Justiciar or other officer, for the true Sc diligente kepinge of the same Jurours; And that the same officer or other persone so sworne, without the speciall comaundment of the said Justiciar or other officer shall not do or suffre to be mynystred to the same Jurours any breade drinke or meate fyre or lyght, nor shall suffre the same Jurours to speake to any persone or persons, nor the same Officer or other psone sworne without the comaundment aforesaide shall not speake to the said Jurours but only to demaund of theym of their agrement, unto suche tyme as the same Jurours shall have gyven their verdyte; any usage or custome hertofore used to the contrarie not withstandinge s And yf the same Officer or other psone so sworne yn fourme aforesaide do not execute and accomplysshe the fPmysses yn the othe before rehersed in everie poynte Sc article, then the same officer or other person so sworne shalbe punysshed & imprisoned, and make fyne Sc raunsom to the Kynges Highnes by the dyscrecion of the said Justiciar, Stewarde, Lyeuten*nt or other Officer.

And also be it enacted by thaudoryte aforesaid that yf the same Jurours do acquyte any suche felon murderer or accessarie upon whose triall they shalbe charged, or gyve any untrue verdyte ayenste the Kynge upon the triall of any traverse recognysaunce or other forfayture, contrary to good & pregnaunt evydence mynystred to theym by persones sworne before the said Justiciar, Stewarde, Lyeuten'nt or other Officer, or that the said Jurours or any of theym do eate drinke, or speake to or with any other person or persones then to suche as be sworne with theym, or otherwyse mysdemeane them selfes, after they be sworne and before they have gyven their verdite, that then the Lorde jPrident and other of the counsell of the Marches for the tyme beynge, upon notice or complaynt therof to them made shall not only have power and audoryte by this p>sent ade to call suche Jurours before them, but also the same Justiciar, Stewarde or other Officer afore whom any suche acquitall, untrue verdite, or mysdemeanour shall happen to be made, shall have full power & audorite to compell suche Jurours and everie of theym upon peyne of imprisonment to be bounden by recognisaunce yn a certayn some of money by their discrecion to be lymytted, that the same Jurours & everie of theym shall psonally appere at a certain daye, by the same Justiciar Stewarde or other officer to be lymytted, before the Lorde President and other of the counsaill aforesaid for the tyme beinge, then & there to abide and stonde to suche direccion and ordre as the same counseill shall make ordeyn Sc decree of yn & uppon the same; CHAPTER V.

or cattels after the son going downe dll the son be up.

FOR ASMOCHE as dayle dyverse felonyes robberies & murders ben many tymes comytted & done yn the countyes of Glou£f and Somercet, yn the parties nere adjoyninge unto the Water called the Water of Seveme betwene Englande & Southwales, and after suche murders & felonyes don the said robbers felons and murderers with the said goodes so robbed & stolne make their conveyaunce withe the saide goodes so stolne by nyght at dyvers passages or feries over the said ryver or water, as the passages of Auste, Fremeland, Pyrton, Arlyngham, Nowenham, Portsedes Poynte, and all suche other lyke passages over the said ryver yn to Southwales, or ynto the forest callyd the foreste of Dene also adjoyninge to the same water, and whan they be over the saide water then the goodes so stolne be by dyvers privyleges ther kepte, all be it the Owner and Owners have true and perfe&e knowlege therof yet they so robbed and spoyled be without remedye for to obteyne their saide goodes so stolne, and so that the secrete and sodeyne conveyaunce by nyght of the saide goodes over the said feries and passages dothe not only greatly encourage dyvers persones to come out of the ptyes of Southwales, to steale robbe & murder dyverse persones yn their houses in the saide counties joyninge upon the said borders of Wales, but also causeth manye robberies and felonyes yn sondrie wayes to be commytted and don upon the said border nere adjoyninge to the same ryver, to the great damage and hurte of the Kynges Subjects inhabitinge there onlesse some remedie therefore be provyded: It maye therfore please the Kynge our Soveraigne Lorde and the Lordes spirituall & temporall and the Commons yn this present parliamente assembled and by the au&oryte of the same, to enaft that everie parsone or persones takinge upon hym or theym to have and kepe any of the said passages or any other passage upon Seveme aforesaide, [fromheseforthe *] do not convey nother carie with any maner barge boote or other vessell any person or persones with horses, mares, oxen, kye, or any other cattell, nor no other persone or persones before the tyme of the son risinge yn the mominge, and after the tyme of the son beinge gon downe at nyght; upon peyne of imprisonment and fyne to be sette on hym that shall so convey or carie over any of the said passages over the said ryver of Seveme out of Englande yn to Wales or the forest of Dene, or out of Wales or the saide forest of Dene in to Englande, oneles the saide passengers & everie of theym have good knowlege of suche person & persones and of their dwellinge places, and upon requeste to theym made by any person or persones do disclose the name and the dwellinge place of everye suche person or persones so by theym conveyed over the said water, to any suche persone or parsones requiringe the same, If sute be made for or after theym upon any outcrie, hute, or fresshe sute of or for any felonye robberie murder and manslaughter, commytted and done from henseforth: And that the Kynges Justiciars of Peace within everie the seid Countyes of Glouc? and Somercet at their Quarter Sessyons shall have full power and au&orite to call before theym all suche persones whiche hereafter shall kepe any of the saide passages, or any other ferie or passage over the saide water yn to Wales or the saide foreste, or oute of Wales or the said forest ynto Englande, and to bynde theym with sufficient sureties with theyin in recognisaunce yn suche somes of money as it shall seme to the discrecion of the said Justiciars of peace, that they and everie of theym, beinge passengers and kepars of feries and passages as is aforesaid, from hensforthe shall not after the saide tymes before lymytted and appoynted convey or carie, nor cause to be conveyed or caried, any maner of person or persones or any kynde of cattail, but suche persones as they do knowe and will answere for, and knowe where their abidingf dwellinges & habitacions be, and upon requeste made to theym or any of theym as is above saide shall from tyme to tyme disclose aswell the same persone or persones as the goodes and cattals so passinge the saide passages upon fresshe sute made or hereafter to be made upon any felonye murder or robberie, commytted & done yn the borders of the Countyes aforesaide, or yn any other place within this Realme or Southwales.

And also the Kynges lovynge subjects sholde not declare unto their Sovarayne Lorde now beynge, whiche unto theim hathe byn and is moste entierly bothe belovyd and estemyd, theyr undoughted syncerite and trouthe j Be yt therfore enacted, by the assent and consent of oure Soverayn Lorde the Kynge and the Lordes spirituall and temporall and Comens yn this present pliament assembled and by thau&oryte of the same, that yf any pson or psonnes after the fyrste daye of February nexte comynge, do malicyously wyshe will or desyre by wordes or writinge, or by crafte ymagen invent pra&yse or attempte, any bodely harme to be donne or cSmytted to the Kynges moste royall psonne, the Quenes, or their heires apparaunt, or to depryve theym or any of theym of the dignite title or name of their royall estates, or sclaunderously & malydously publishe & pnounce, by expresse writinge or wordes, that the Kynge oure Soverayn Lorde shulde be heretyke scismatike Tiraunt ynfidell or Usurper of the Crowne, or rebellyously do deteyne kepe or witholde frome oure said Soverayn Lorde his heyres or successoures any of his or their Castells Fortresses Fortilesses or Holdes, within this Realme or yn any other the Kynges Domynyons or Marches, or rebel liously deteyne kepe or witholde from the Kynges saide Highnes, his heyres or socces6ours, any of his or their Shyppes Ordinaunces Artillarye or other munycyons or fortifica&Sns of Warre, and do not humbly render and gyve up to oure saide Soverayn Lorde his heyres or successours, or to suche psonnes as shalbe deputed by theym, suche Castels Fortresses Fortilesses Holdes Shippes Ordinaunces Artillarie and other munycions and fortifica66ns of Warre rebellyously kepte or deteyned, *vithin vj dayes nexte after they shalbe edmanded by oure said Soverayn Lorde his heyres or successoures, by open pclama£6n under the greate Seale, that then everie such parsonne and psonnes so offendinge yn any the pmisses after the said fyrste day of February, theyr

And be yt further enacted by audoryte aforesaid, that everie offendour and ofiendours beynge hereafter laufully convide of any maner of High Treasons, by presentment confession verdide or procese of outelarie accordinge to the due course and custome of the comen lawes of this Realme, shall lose and forfayte to the Kynges Highnes his heires and successours all suche landes tenementis and hereditamends whiche any suche offendour or ofiendours shall have of any estate of inheretaunce yn use or possessyon, by anye right title or menes, within this Realme of Englonde or els where withyn any the Kynges Dominions at the tyme of any suche treason commytted or any tyme after. Savinge to everie psonne and psonnes thyr heyres and successours, other thenne the ofiendours yn any treasons their heyres and successours, and suche psonne and psonnes as clayme to anye theyr uses, all suche rightes titles interestes possessions leases rentes offices and other pfyttes whiche they shall have at the daye of commyttinge suche treasons or any tyme afore, yn as large and ample maner as yf this ade had never ben had nor made.

CHAPTER XV.

An Acte for takinge awaie certeyne Exadons taken within the Archedeaconrie of Richemond by Spirituall men.

FOR AS MOCHE as dyverse and manye the Kynge oure Soverayne Lordes Subjects, inhabyted within the Archedeconrie of Richemonde in the Countie of Yorke, be and of longe tyme have benne sore and grevously exa&ed and impoveryshed by the psonnes Vicars and other suche as have benefices and spirituall pmocions within the same, as by takynge of everie psonne when he dieth yn the name of a pensyon or of a porcion, sumtyme the ixlh parte of all his goodes and cattals and sumtyme the thirde parte, to the open and manyfest ympoverishinge of moste pte of all the Kynges pore subje&f inhabited and deceasing within the same; Wherfore be yt ordenyd ena&id and established by the Kynge oure Soverayne Lorde the Lordes Spirituall and Temporal! and the Comons yn this ^sent pliament assemblid and by
