CHAPTER XVI.

An Acte for makinge of Worstedes in the Citie of Norwiche and yn the Townes of Lynne and Yermouth.

WHERE at a pliament holden at London the xv. daye of Aprill yn the xiiij yere of the reigne of oure Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge that nowe is, and from thense adjomed to Westmynster the laste daye of July yn the xv. yere of oure said Soverayn Lorde and there endyd, It was ordeyned enadid and established that the craftes men callyd Worsted wevers inhabited in the towne of greate Yarmouth shulde have power and audoryte by that ade from thense forwarde to elede and chose yerely for ever on the Monday next after the feast of Penthecosre, one honest man of the my8terie and occupacyon of Worsted wevers beynge an householder within the said Towne of great Yermouth and havynge of his ppre goodes and cattells to the value of x ti. at the least, or landes and tenementis to his owne use of estate of freholde at the leaste to the clere yerely value of xx s. to be Warden of the same craft and mysterie of Worsted wevers for the yere nexte ensuynge, whiche man so electid and chosen shulde psonally appere before the Mayer of the Citie of Norwiche for the tyme beynge, the Mondaye next after the feast of Corpus Chrisd then next ensuynge, then and there to be swome and chargid by lyke othe concemynge the trewe and substaundali makinge of worsteddis sayes and stamynes within the said Towne of greate Yermouth, as the iiij Wardens of the said Citie of Norwiche by vertue of an Acte of ply ament made yn the vij yere of Kynge Edwarde the fourthe were chargid and swome for the same Citie of Norwiche; And yf the said Mayer heppenyd to be absent the said Monday next after Corpus Christi, or els then refusid to receyve or take the said othe, then the said Warden so electe within iiij dayes nexte after the same Mondaye shulde come before the bayliffes of the said towne of great Yermouth for the tyme beynge, or before one of theym the other beynge absent, and then and there receyve a corporall othe for the trewe exercysinge of the same office of Wardenshippe after the tenour of the othe acustomably used to be gyven to the said Wardens of the said Citie of Norwiche ; and then the saide Warden of the said Towne of great Yermouth for the tyme beynge so elede and sworne myght ordeyne and appoynt a seale withe this letter Y to be graven yn the same Seale and myght have full power and audoryte to vievve serch, sease and seale in ledde with the same seale so to be appoynted and engraven, and none other, all worsteddes sayes and stamyns within the said Towne of Yermouth and subberbes of the same made or to be made and not els where, yn as large and ample maner as the said Wardens of the said Citie of Norwiche and the Wardens of the Countie of Norfolke or any of theym had within the said Citie or Countie, or yn any wyse maye do yn that behalff by audorite or vertue of the afore remembrid ade made yn the saide vij yere of Kynge Edwarde the fourth, any thinge yn the same conteyned to the contrarie notwithstandynge; And that no psonne inhabited within the said Towne of greate Yermouthe or subberbs therof shulde weave any worsteddes sayes or stamyns within the same towne, except he be an Englishman borne and had byn a prentyse to the said occupation, and without he weavid [there1 ] suche ppre markes as shulde be lymyted and appoynted by the seide Warden of the said Towne for the tyme beynge elede and sworn as is aforesaide, uppon payne of forfature therof to the Kynge oure Soverayne Lorde; And that everie Warden of the said Towne shulde lymytte distinde and severall markes to everie of the said Worsted weavers of the same Towne of greate Yermouthe and the same Markes by the said Warden to be regestrid in a boke.

And also it was further enadid, that yf and when so ever the Towne of Lynne shulde be inhabited with x. sondrie householders or more nombre of householders exercysinge and usinge the said crafte or mysterie of worstede weavers, then and from thensforthe, that is to saie as longe as the same towne of Lynne shulde be inhabited with the nombre of tenne suche householders at the least, yt shulde be lefull to the same inhabitauntis of the said towne of Lynne yerely yn the Mondaye nexte after the feast of Pentecost to elede and chose of themseiffe one Warden of the said crafte and mysterie of Worstedde weavers, to be of the value yn landes and goodes as is aforesaid of the Wardens of Yermouth, whiche Warden so elede shulde yerely be swome and chaigid at the said Citie of Norwiche yn lyke maner and at like daie as is before lymyted to the Wardens of Yermouth, or yn defaute of the said Mayer of Norwiche then the said Warden so to be elede for the said towne of Lynne to take a Corporalle othe before the Maier of the said Towne within suche tyme and after suche forme as is befoic lymited unto the saide Warden of Yermouth, and that the said Warden of the said Towne of Lynne for the tyme beinge so elede and swome, by hym selfF might ordeyne and appoynt a seale withe this letter L. to be graven yn the seale, and myght have full power and audorite to viewe serche sease and seale yn leade with the same seale so to be graven and with none other, all Worsteddis saies and stamynes within the

And also that the same inhabitauntes and marchauntes and everie of theym so bringynge the said Worstedes to the same Cytie to be shorne dyed coloured and kalendred were reasonable and lawfully yntreatid, accordinge to the said a&e made yn the saide vij yere of Kynge Edwarde the fourthe and the Ordenaunce made and affirmed or there after to be made and affirmed for the said mystere, without lett or disturbaunce contrarie to the same Acte or Ordenauncf in that behalfe.

And yt was further ena&yd that no psonne or psonnes any tyme after that shulde convey or transpose ynto any of the ptyes of beyonde the See any maner of clothes of Worstedes before the same clothes were shorne dyed coloured and kalendred, upon payne of forfayture the value therof, the one halfe to the Kynge oure Soverayne Lorde and the other halfe therof to the ptie that will sue therfore by accyon [or4] playnt of dett yn any of the Kynges Courtes, yn whiche acc&n or suyte no ptexcion or essoyne shulde be alowed nor the defender admytted to wage his lawe: as by the said a&e therof made more playnlye apperithe: Whiche a&e was made to endure unto the nexte pliament, wherby yt ys nowe expired: In consideracion wherof and for as moche as the same Acte is a good and necessarie a&e for the trewe makynge of Worstedes saies and stamyns, and very commodious and pfitabie for the increase of the said Townes of Yermouth and Lynne, be yt therfore ena&yd by the Kynge oure Soverayne Lorde and the Lordes spirituall and temporal! and the Comons yn this pfeent pliament assembled that the same a&e and everie artycle sentence and provysyon theryn conteyned shall fromhensforthe be contynued and stande for ever yn full strenght and vertue.

CHAPTER XVH.

An Acte that no fermours of spirituall psonnes shalbe compellid or chargid to paye for their lessours First Fruitf or yeres pensyon of the tenth grunted [by1 ] the Kinges Highnes.

FOR certayne resonable and urgent considerations movinge the Kinges moste Highe Courte of parliament, yt is ordeyned and enactyd by auSorite of the same, that all and smgler fermoures and [lesses*] of any Manoures Lordshippes Londes Tenementis or other Hereditamends, psonages Vicareges porcyons of tithes or other what so ever pfittes or commodites, belonginge to any Archebishope Byshope or other prelate or spirituall psonne or psonnes or spirituall bodie corporate or politique, wherof any First Fruetes or yerely pension of the tenth partie is grauntid to the Kinge oure Soverayne Lorde yn this present session of the said Courte of pliament, shalbe discharged and not chargeable to paie to oure said Soverayne Lorde, of his or their ppre money coste or charge, for or yn discharge of the lessoor or lessoures owner or owners of the same, by reason of any couvenaunt bargayne bonde condidon dause of reentre or other thinge heretofore made or concluded ; but that everie of the said lessours and owners and thdr Successours shalbe chargid and chargeable to paie and satisfie the same of his or thdr ppre coste and charge to the Kinge oure Soverayne Lorde his Hdres and successours accordinge to the graunt therof; any couvenaunt bargayne contrail bonde condicyon clause of reentre or other thinge heretofore made or concluded to the contrarye therof yn any wyse not withstandinge.

CHAPTER I.

An Acte for reedyfyeng of dyPs Townes in the Realm.

FOR SO MOCHE as dyvers and many Howses Mesuages & Tenements of Habita£6ns in the Townys of Nodngham Shrewesbury Ludlowe Brydgenorth Quynborowe Northampton and Gloucester nowe are and of long tyme have bene in greate ruyne and decaye, and specially in the pryncipalle and chief stretes there beyng, in the whiche chief stretes in tymes passid have bene beautyfull dwellyng Howses there welle inhabited whyche at thys daye moche parte therof is desolate and void groundys, withe pittys sellers and vaultes lying open and uncoveryd very peryllous for people to go by in the nyght without jeopardy of lyfe, whyche decayes are to the great impoverysshyng and hynderance of the same Townys ; CHAPTER II.

An Acte conc?nyng the forgyng of the Kingf signe manuell Signet & Prevye sele.

FOR AS MOCHE as by the Lawes of this Realme small punyshment hathe byn hitherto provydid for forging and counterfeyting of the Kynges signe manuell or previe seignet, by reason wherof dyverse light and evyll disposid psones now of late have takyn the more boldenes and courage to comitte suche offences to the greate audacite and boldenes of suche lyke offenders ; For remedie wherof be it enactid by auctorite of this psent parliament. That if any psone or psones at any tyme hereafter falsely forge and counterfeite the Kyngis signe manuell prevy signet or previe seale, that than epy suche offence shalbe demed and adjudged highe treason, and the offenders therin their counsaylours procurours aydours and abettours, bang convict of any suche offence accordyng to the Lawes of this Realme, shalbe demed and adjugid Tray tours against the Kynge and the Realme; and shall suffer and have suche peynys of deathe forfeiture of Lendys Goodys and cattallf and also lose the pryvylege of all saintuaries as in casis of highe treason it is ordeynid.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte con9nyng Pyrottes & Robbers of the See.

WHERE Pyrottes Theves Robbers and Murtherers uppon the See many tymes escape unpunyshed bicause the triall of their offences hath heretofore be ordered before the Admyrall or his Lyeutenant or Comyssarie, after the course of the cyvyle Lawes, the nature wherof is that before (4) jugement of dethe can be gyven agaynste the offenders either they must playnly confesse their offends (whych they will never do without torture or paynes) or elles theyr offences be so playnlye and dyre&ly provyd by Wytnesses indyfferent suche as sawe theyr offends cornyttyd, which cannot be gottyn but by chaunce at fewe tymes, by cause suche offenders comytte theyr offences apon the See and at many tymes murder and kill suche psones beyng in the shyppe or bote where they comytt theyr offences whych shulde bere witnes ayenst them in that behalfe; And also suche as shuld bere wytnes be comonly Maryners and Shypmen, whych for the moste partie cannot be gottyn ne had always redye to testifie suche offences because of theyr often vyages and passages in the Sees, without long tarrying and protracdon of tyme and great costes and chargis as well of the Kyngf Highnes as of suche as wolde pursue such Offenders : For reformation wherof be it enactid by au&orite of this psent parlyament that all such offences done in or [apon * ] the See, or in any other havyn ryver or creke where the Admyrall or Admyralles ptende to have jurysdicdon, shalbe inquyryd tryed [harde5] and determynyd in suche Shyrys and placys in the Realme as shalbe lymytid by the Kynges comyssion to be dyre&id for the same, in lyke forme and conditiki as if suche offences had bene done upon the Lande ; CHAPTER VII.

An Acte for the Abuses in the Forestf of Wales.

WHERE dyvers and many Forestes be in Wales and the Marches of the same, aswell of the inheritaunce and possessions of oure Soveraigne Lorde the Kyng as of dyvers others being Lordes Marchers, within which forestes c?ten unresonable customes and exac£6ns have bene of long tyme unlaufally exaded and usid, cont*ri both to the Lawe of God and Man to the expsse wrong and greate impoveryshyng of divers of the Kynges true Subjects, The effede of whiche said unlawfall exaccions and customes be hereafter declarid, that is to witte; it hath bene there unlaufally usid that if it fortunyd any of the Kynges subjedes to passe go or ryde through or in any waye or pathe of any of the seid forestes, not havyng upon them that so shall fortune to (1) go or ryde a tokyn delyverid to hym or them by the chief foresters rulers walkers or fermers, the which tokyn shalbe well knowyn amongest all them that are walkers and rulers under hym or theym, or that he or they that so shall fortune to passe go or ryde in or thorough any of the said forestes be not yerelye trybuters or chensers, then he or they so goyng rydyng or travelyng in or thorough any of the seid forestes havyng no tokyn nor beyng yerely tributors or chensers as is aforesaide, have usid to paye by unlaufall exaccion unto the seid foresters rulers walkers and fermers of the seid forestes a grevous fyne or rewarde; And if any pson or psones not havyng such token or tokens and not beyng a yerely tributor or a chenser as is aforesaid, shulde happyn to be takyn founde or espyed by any of the seid foresters rulers walkers or fermers or theyr assignes by the space of xxiiij fote out of the highe waye, then he or they so being takyn founde or espyed out of the high waye within any of the seid forestes as is aforesaid, to forfayte & loose unto the seid foresters rulers walkers & fermers all such money and golde as shuld be then founde upon hym or theym so being takyn in any of the seid forestes oute of the high waye as is aforeseid ; And also the same pson or psones so being takyn or founde out of the high waye to forfaite and lose a joynte of one of his or theyr handes, or elles to make fyne therfore with the saide foresters rulers walkers and fermers at the wille and pleasure of the said rulers walkers and fermers ; And if also that it happen any [bese3 ] or quyeke catall to go come or escape into any of the seid forestes by stray or these stollen or otherwise, the said foresters rulers walkers or fermers after knowlege to hym or them gyvyn have lykewise unlawfully usid to sease and take the same [bese3] or catelle as his or their owne and marke them with the markes of their forest ther usid, and so seasid marked takyn and them reteigne as catell forfeyted unto theyr owne use; by reason wherof the owner or owners of the same catell have bene clere without remedie for the havyng ageyn of ther seid catelle, excepte onlye by way of redempeon or hying agayne of theyr owne cattail, cont*ry to all equyte and conscience: In consideracion wherof it may please the Kynges Highnes with the assent of the Lordes spyrituall & temporall and the Comons at this psent parlyamente assemblyd and by the audorite of the same, to enade ordeigne and establyshe, that from the fest of the Natyvite of Saynde John the Baptyste next comyng whiche shalbe in the yere of our Lorde a thousand fyve hundred thyrty and six, all the seid unlaufall customes to be dePmynid voide and had for nought throut all and evy of the seid forestes within Wales and the Marches of the same: And that it shalbe lawfalle frome thensforth to all and eVy of the Kynges trewe subjedes & al other pson or psones being in lege and amide with the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde his heyres and successors Kynges of Englond, frely quyetly and in peace to passe and repasse travayle and go into and [through4 ] the seid forestes and e$y of them, booth on horsbacke and on foote, as well folowing and dryvyng of catell as well carieng of Wares or otherwise aboute theyr laufall busines and afiayres, without any fyne forfayture tolle custome exaccion or other imposicion to be taken exaded or demaunded of them or of any of them by the seid fosters rulers walkers fermers or their assignes. And if it shall happyn or chaunse any of the seid fosters rulers

CHAPTER X.

An Acte conSnyng uses & wylles.

WHERE by the comon Lawes of this Realme Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes be not [divisible by Transfer of Land* V v testament, nor ought to be transferrid frome one to a nother but by solemne lyv*y and season matter of recorde ** Common Law > wryting suffycyent made bona fide without covyne or fraude, yet nePtheles dy verse and sundry ymaginacions subtile Evils resulting from invendons and pradlises have bene usid, wherby the Heredytamentf of this Realme have bene conveyed frome one to an other by fraudulent feoffementes fynes reco^yes and other assurances craftely made to secrete uses internes and trustes, and also by wylles and testamentes sumtyme made by nude polx and wordes somtyme by signes and tokens and somtyme by wrytyng, and for the moste parte made by such psones as be visited with sykenes, in theyr extreme agonyes and peynes or at such tyme as they have hadde scantlye eny good memorie or remembrance; At whiche tymes they beyng pvokid by gredye covetous psones lyeng in a wayte about them do many* tymes dyspose indiscretely and unadvisidly theyr landes and inheritances ; By reason wherof and by occasion of which fraudulent feoffementf fynes recoPeys and other lyke assurauncf to uses confydences and trustf dy9s and many heires have bene unjustlye at sundry tymes disherited, the Lordes have lost theyr wardes manages relyefes hariottes eschetes aydes pur fayre fitz chyvaler & pur file maryer, and scantlye any psone can be certaynly assurid of any landes by them p'chasid nor knowen surelye agayn whome they shal use theyr acdons or execucions for theyr rightes titles and duytes j Also men maryed have lost theyr tenancies by the courtesie. An Acte for true making of Wollen Clothes.

Clothier* shall weave their Marks in the Cloths; and put a Seal specify-ing the Length.

CHAPTER XIV.

An Acte conSiyng the custome of Lether.

WHERE great [quande 1 ] and moche habundaunce of Lether is daily conveied out of this Reaime, aswell by estraungers as also by Tanners and other the Kynges Subjects inhabited in dyvers parties of this Reaime towardes the See costez, and in especiall out of Wales Chesshire and Comewall where litell or no custome is paid for the same, whiche Lether is comonly pakked by the said Estraungers Tanners and other the Kinges Subjects in their Housez and so conveied unto the portes and havens where they entend to shipp the same, whiche packes so conveied and brought to suche portes and havens to be shipped be never there unpacked to be viewed what nombre of Lether is conteyned in any suche packe, but entered in the [Customer *] bokes by and uppon the informadon and reporte of the said Estraungers Tanners or other pson transporter of the same Lether ; And albe it that the Kinges Highnes in suche places and portes hath very litle custome paid for the same, yet for asmoche as in suche places there is no better serche nor viewe hadd for the pfe&e knowlege of the nombre and quantite of the Lether so by them packed, the Kinges Grace is moche deceyved of suche his Customes as ought therfore to accrue to his Highnesse; for where in the porte of London two psonnes be named and appoynted by the waier of the Wolles within the same porte for the tyme beyng, to tell and nombre all such Lether by the Hide accomptyng tene Hides to the diker, and also all Woll felles as within the same porte shalbe shipped from tyme to tyme, which two personns be sworne before the Customers of his greate Custome truely and duely to execute thir offices in telling and nombring all suche Lether and Woll felles in the psence of the said Customers and of the Countroller of the same Custome or of ther Deputies, who beyng fPsent and viewing the same do make entre therof in thir bokes; And after suche tale made and entre taken, an other psonne by the Maier of London for the tyme beyng constituted and appoynted, is also sworne truely to pakke the same Lether so told and entred into the Custumers bokes, ev*y of the same Teller and Packers taking suche fees for their labours as of olde tyme have ben used limyted and accustomed, e9y straungier payeng for Custome of ev*y diker iiij s. ix d. and e9y denysen foure shillinges and a penny, which like custome is also paied in the port of Hampton but not in many other portez of this Reaime and specially in Wales Chesshire and Comewall, out of the which parties by reason of suche smale customes more Lether is conveied over the See than out of other places of this Reaime, whiche is an occasion of the derth and greate prices of the same Lether : For the redresse wherof and to thentent that oon maner of Custome for e9y such dyker of Lether so conveid ov5 the See aswell by denysens as estraungiers shalbe paide throughout this Reaime Wales and other the Kinges Dominions, And also that the Kinges Highnes maye be the better assured of his Customes to be paid for all suche Lether as shalbe hereafter caried and conveid o9 the See, Be it enacted by thau&oritie of this psent parliament, that fromehensforthe no maner of Estraunger nor Denyson shall packe or cause to be packed any maner of Lether to be conveied or shipped over the See out of this Reaime Wales or other the Kinges Dominions otherwise than in this a&e is expssed, that is to saye; that all suche Lether shalbe hereafter packed by a packer 6wome in e$y suche porte where any Lether shalbe shipped to be conveid out of this Reaime Wales or other the Kingf Dominions, upon payne of forfaiture of all suche Lether as hereafter shalbe packed contrary to the purport of this a&e or of the value therof; And also that fromehensforth ev*y estraungier and denysen which shall shipp send or conveye eny Lether ov* the See out or frome any parte of this Reaime Wales Chesshire or other the Kinges Dominions, shall pay like custome for the same as is used to be paid within the porte of London, that is to saye every straungier to pay for ev*y diker of Lether for custome foure shillinges and nyne pence, and e9y denisen foure shillinges and a peny.

And be it also enacted that within ev*y porte haven and creke within this Reaime Wales and other the Kinges Domynions, where no tellers nor packers at this fPsent tyme be nor before the making of this a&e have ben, that frome hensforth the Customers and Comptrollers of e9y suche Port Haven & Creke, where suche Lether shalbe shipped to be conveid into the parties beyonde the See, shall have power by au&oritie of this a&e to name constitute and appoynt one able psone to tell and nombre all suche Lether as shalbe at any tyme there shipped, which p6one so named shalbe sworne by the Customer A Comptroller of e9y suche Porte Haven and Creke trewly and duely to execute his office in the fPsence of the Customer and Comptroller of epy suche Porte Creke or Haven where eny suche Lether shalbe shypped or of his or thir Depude or Deputies, the same teller taking of e9y estraunger for the telling of ev*y diker of Lether vj d. wherof the same teller to have for his labour two pens, and foure pence to be to the Comynalde of the same Towne and Porte, towarde the payment of their fee ferme and other thir charges, And of e9y denysen not beyng a free man of the said Porte and Haven, for e9y diker foure pence wherof the teller to have two pence, and other two

CHAPTER XIX.

An Acte lymyttyng an Order for Seyntuaries & Sayntuarie psonnes.

[Evils of Sanctuaries]

WHERE upon trust of Saintuaries and the licencious lifcties that heretofore have ben and yet dailye ben used in the same, divers psonnes have ben the more bolde to ppetrate and comitte many detestable murders [ rappes1 ] robberies theftes and other myschevous destestable and ibhdmynable dedes, for that they have ben alwayes releved ayded and succoured by the Saintuaries whan so eP and as ofte as they or any of theym have offended in any of the pmisses, to the moost grevous displeasour of Almyghde God and extreme Detriment and hurt of the Kinges Subjects; In avoiding of suche psumptuous boldnes, it is enacted ordeyned and establisshed by the King our SouPaign Lorde, with the assent of his Lordes spuall & tevnporall and the C5mons in this psent pliament assembled and by audoritie of the same, that all and singuler psonne or psons, whiche nowe be or at any tyme hereafter shalbe privileged in any Saintuarie within any of the Kinges Dominions for murder or felonny, frome the firste daye of Maye next cdmyng, shall daily, whan soeP he or they be without the House or Mansion wherin they have thir lodging, weare a badge or cognisaunce, by the Governour of evy Saynctuarie to be assigned and appoynted, openly upon theyr upper garment of the compasse in length and bredth of ten ynches; upon payne that they and evy of theym whan soeP and as often as any of theym beyng out of the said House or Mansion wherin he hath his said lodging shalbe founden and taken without the same badge or cognisaunce, clerely to [losse*] and forfaite his and their privilege and advauntage of Saintuarie; And that it shalbe laufull to all and singuler the Kinges Subjects to apprehend and take evy suche offendour and offendours, beyng without his badge or cognisaunce as aforesaid, and him to bring out of the Saintuarie into the next gaole there to remayne unto the nexte gaole delyPe, and then to be tried according to the due course and order of the Lawe as though he had never ben privyledged in any suche Saintuarie.

And also be it enacted by thaudorite aforesaid that no maner of the said privyleged persons at eny tyme herafter here occupie or were upon theym any maner of sworde knyffe or other weapon, other than thir meate knyves, and the same meate knyves but at their meales only upon payne as is above rehersed.

CHAPTER XXV.

An Acte for punysshement of sturdy vacabundes and beggers.

WHERE in an Acte made at Westmynster in the xxij. yere of the reigue of our Sovaigne Lorde Kinge Henry the viijth amonge other thinges it was ordeyned establisshed and enacted, that evy strong and valeante begger and vacabounde after he were whipped for his vacabundcy and idelnes should deperte frome the place where he was whipped dire&ely unto suche Towne Hundred and Counde where he was borne, or where he had dwelled by the space of there yeres nexte before, there to contynue and abid, And also that aged poore and impotent people shuld in likewise repayre into ev*y hundred within the said Coundes there to remayne and contynue according to the menyng and purport of the said Acte, upon peynes limited in the same a&e (*) more pleynlye appereth : And forasmoche as it was not pvided in the said a&e howe and in what wise the said pore people and sturdie vacabundes shuld be ordered at thir repaire and at theyr comyng into thir countreis, nor howe thinhabitauntes of e9y hundred shuld be charged for the reliefe of the same pore people, nor yet for the setting and keping in worke and labour of the aforesaid valiaunt vacabundes at theyr said repaire into evy hundred of this Realme, It is therefore nowe ordeyned and establisshed and enacted by the King our Sovaigne Lorde the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this Psent parliament assembled and by thau&oride of the same, that all and e$y the Maiers Aldermen Shireffes Bailiffes Constables Householders, and all other hede Officers and Ministers of e&y Citie Shire Townes and Parisshes of this Realme, at the repaire and comyng thider of suche poore creature or sturdie vacabund as is conteyned in the said a&e, shall moost charitably receyve the same and order the same in ma8 and forme followyng, that is to sey; That all the GoPnours and Ministres of evy of the same Cities Shires Townes Hundredf Wapentakes Lathes Rapes Rydinges Tythinges Hamlettes and Parisshes aswell within libties as without, shall not oonly socour fynde and kepe all and e$y of the same poore people by way of voluntarie and charitable almes, within evy of the same Cities Shires Townes Hundredf Wapentakf Lathes Rapes Tythinges Hamlettes and Parisshes as well within libties as without, to be socoured relived and holpen with such and convenient and necessarie almes as shalbe thought meete by their discretions, in suche wise as none of them of verie necesside shalbe compelled to wander idelly and go openly in begging to aske almes in any of the same Cities Shires Townes and Parisshes; but also to cause and to compell all and e9y the said sturdie vacabundf and valeant beggers to be sett and kepte to continuall labour, in suche wise as by their sod labours they and e$y of them may gette their owne livingf with the contynuall labour of their owne handes; And ev*y Maier Alderman Shireffe Bailiffe Constable and all other hed officers and Ministers of e9y Countie Gtie Towne and Parisshe within this Realme, or within any the Kinges Dominions as well within libties as without, and all other psonnes inhabitauntes within any of the same, shall endevour them selfes to order and dire&e the poor people valiaunt beggers and sturdy vacaboundes in such wise as the effe&e of this psent a&e shalbe duely observed and putt in due execudon; upon peyne that epy parysshe shall losse and forfaite twentie shillinges for e9y monethe in whiche it is omitted and undone; And that to be enquired of at ev*y Quarter Sessions and to be duely Rented and founde by the verdi&e of xij men.

Item, It is further enacted by thauctoritie aforesaid that all and e9y psonne or psonnes being whipped or sentt unto thir Countreis in fourme aforesaid, at the ende of e9y tenne myles shall repaire unto the Constable of any parisshe, beyng directly in his waye towardes the Counde and Place wherunto he is so appoynted, and upon sight of his ires gyven unto hym at the tyme of his whipping and sending of hym into the same his Countrey, ev*y of the said Constables and others the Kinges Subjects shall and may fumysshe hym with competent meate drinke and lodging for one nyght onely or for one meale, and so he shall continue his daily journey of tenne myles until suche tyme as he shall edme unto the hundred and place wherunto he is assigned to goo.

CHAPTER XXVI.

An Acte for Lawes & Justice to be ministred in Wales in like fourme as it is in this Realms.

ALBEIT the Domynyon Principalitie and Countrey of Wales justly and rightuouslye is and eP hath ben incorporated annexed united and subje&e to & under the Imperiall Crowne of this Realme, as a verrys membre and joynte of the same, [Wherfore*] the Kinges moost Roiall Magesde of mere droite and verye right is verie hedde King Lorde and Ruler, yet notwithstanding by cause that in the same Countrey Principalitie and Dominion dyvers rightes usagf lawes and customes be farre discrepant frome the Lawes and Customes of this Realme, And also by cause that the people of the same Dominion have and do daily use a speche nothing like ne consonaunt to the naturall mother tonge used within this Realme, some rude and ignorant people have made disdnccion and diPsitie betwene the Kinges Subjects of this Realme and hys Subjects of the said Dominion and Principalitie of Wales, wberby greate discorde variaunce debate dyvysion murmur and sedicion hath growen betwene his said subje&es; His Highnes therfore of a singuler zele love and favour that he beareth towardcs his Subjects of his said Dominion of Wales, mynding and entending to reduce them to the pfe&e order notice & knowlege of his lawes of this his Realme, and utterly to extirpe all and singuler the senister usages and customes differinge frome the same, and to bringe his said Subjects of this his Realme and of his said Dominion of Wales to an amicable concorde and unitie. Hath by the deliberate advise consent and agreament of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this jAsent (*) assembled and by the au&oritie of the same, ordeyned enacted and establisshed that his said Countrey or Dominion of Wales shal be stonde and contynue for eP fromehensforthe incorporated united and annexed to and with this his Realme of Englande; And that all and singuler psonne and psonnes borne and to be borne in the said Principalitie Countrey or Dominion of Wales, shall have enjoye and inherite all and singuler fredomes libdes rightes privileges and lawes within this Realme and other the Kynges Dominions as other the Kinges Subjects naturally borne within the same, have enjoye and enherite: And that all and singular psonne and psonnes inheritable to any Manours Landes Tentes Rentes RePcions Svices or other Hereditamentes, which shall discende after the feaste of all Sayntes nexte cdmyng within the said Principalitie Countrey or Dominion of Wales, or within any pdculer LordshipjS parte or parcell of the said Countrey or Dominion of Wales, shall foreP frome and after the said feaste of all Sayntes, inherite and be inheritable to the same Manours Landes Tenementes Rentes Revercions and Hereditamentes after the Englisshe tenure, without division or particion, and after the forme of the Lawes of this Realme of Englande, and not after any (3) tenure ne after the fourme of any Welshe Lawes or Customes; And that the Lawes Ordynaunces and Statutes of this Realme of Englande for eP, and none other Lawes Ordenaunces ne Statutes, frome and after the said feaste of all Seyntes nexte cdmyng shalbe had used pra&ised & executed in the said Countrey or Dominion of Wales and evy parte therof, in like man forme and order as they ben and shalbe had used pra&ised and executed in this Realme, and in such like ma9 and forme as hereafter by this a&e shalbe further establisshed and ordeyned ; any a&e statute usage custome psident libde privilege or other thing, had made used graunted or suffred to the cont"ry, in any wise notwithstanding.

And forasmoche as there be many and dyvers Lordshippes Marchers within the said Countrey or Dominion of Wales lieng betwene the Shires of Englande and the Shires of the said Countrey or Dominion of Wales, and beyng noo parcell of any other Shires where the Lawes and due correccion is used and bad, by reason wherof hath ensued and hath bene pra&ised ppetrated comitted and done, within and amonge the said Lordshipps and Countreys to them adjoynyng, manyfolde and dyvers detestable murders brennyng of Houses robberies theftes trespasses rowttes riottes unlawfoll assembles embraceries mayntenaunces receytinge of felons oppWone ruptures of the Peace and manyfolde other malefa&es cont*ry to all Lawes and Justice, And the said offenders theruppon making their refuge frome Lordeshipp to Lordeshipp were and contynued without punysshement or correccion; For due reformacion wherof, and for asmoche as dyvers and many of the said Lordeshippes Marchers be nowe in the handes and possession of our Sovaigne Lorde the Kinge, and the smallest nombre of them in the possession of other Lordes, It is therfore enacted by thau&oride aforesaid that dyvers of the said Lordeshippes Marchers shalbe united annexed & joyned to dyvers of the Shires of Englande, And dyvers of the said Lordshippes Marchers shalbe united annexed and joyned to dyvers of the Shires of the said Countrey or Dominion of Wales in maS and forme hereafter followyng; And that all the residue of the said Lordeshippes Marchars within the said Countrey or Dominion of Wales shalbe severed and devyded into Stayne pdcular Counties or Shires, that is to say; The Countie or Shire of Monimouth, the Countie or Shire of Brekenoke, the Countie or Shire of Radnore, the Countie or Shire of Montgomery, the Countie or Shire of Denbigh: And that the Lordshippes Towneshippes Parisshes Cdmotes and Cantredes of Monimouth Chepstowe Matheme Llanmyhangell Magour Goldcliffe Newporte Wenloge Llanweme Caerlion Uske Trelecke Tynterne Skynfreth Grousmonte White Castell Reglan Calicote Byston Abergevenny Penrose Grenefeld Maghen and Hochnyslade, in the said Countrey of Wales, and all and singuler Honours Lordshipps Castells Manours Landes Tenementes and Hereditamentes lieng or beyng within the compasse or P&n&e of the said Lordshipps Towneshippes Hamlettes Parisshes Comotes and Cantredes and evy of them, in whos possession so eP they be or shalbe, and evy parte therof, shall stand and be, frome and after the said feaste of all Seyntes, Gildable and shalbe reputed accepted named and taken as parte and membres of the said Shire of Monimouthe: And that the said Towne of Monimouthe shalbe named accepted reputed used had and taken [heed4] and Shire Towne of the said Countie or Shire of Monimouthe: And that the Shirefff Countie or Shire Courte of and for the said Shire and Countie of Monimouth shalbe holden and kepte

And it is further enacted by thaudoride aforesaid that all accions realles that hereafter shalbe conceyved perpetrated or sued for any landes tenementes or hereditamentes or any other thing, within the said Counde or Shire of Monimouth, and all accions psonals within the same Shire or Counde of the somme of fourde shillinges or above, and all accions myxte, shalbe sued by originall writte out of the Kinges high Courte of Chaun^y in England and herde de?myned and tried before the Kinges Jusdces in England, or by Assise or Nisi Prius within the said Counde of Monimouth, in suche like ma0 forme and wise as all other accions reals psonals and accions myxte be sued herde de?myned and tried in or for any Shire of this Realme of Englande; And that the Kinges Jusdces of his Benche or of his common Benche at Westni shall have full power and au&oride to direde all maS pcesse to die Shireffe and all other officers of the said Counde of Monimouth, And also to dire&e writtes of venire facias to the same ShirefT for the triall of evy issue joyned before them, and also to awarde Comissions of Nisi Prius into the said Counde of Monimouth for the triall of suche issues joyned before them, in like man! and fourme as they do into e9y Shire of this Realme of Englond; And all and e9y the Kinges Subjects and infcatauntes within the said Counde of Monimouth shalbe for e9, frome and after the said feaste of All Seyntes, obliged and bounden to be obedient and attendaunt to the Lorde Chauncellour of Englond the Kinges Jusdces and other of the Kinges moste honorable Counsaile, and unto all lawes customes ordenaunces and statutes of this Realme of England, in like maner fourme and wise as all other the Kinges Subjectes within evy Shire of this Realme of England be obliged and bounden; any acte statute usage custome libde privilege or any other thinge to the cont*ry in any wise notwithstanding. And that the Shereff of the said Counde, shall hold plee of Replegiare and all other suites and playntes under fourde shillingf in his Counde or Shere Courte in like mafl and forme as all other Shireffes do within this Realme of England. And that the Shireffe Eschetours and Coroners that hereafter shalbe within the said Countie or Shire of Monimouth shalbe obliged and bounden to execute all the Kinges pcesses, and to make due retornes thereof, and to use and exScise their offices according to the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme of England, in all and evy thing as the Shireffes Eschetours and Coroners be obliged and bounden to do in all and e9y other Shire of this Realme of England; and that Shireffe and Eschetours of the said Shire or Countie of Monimouth, that hereafter shalbe appoynted by our Sov^aigne Lorde the Kinge, make thir accomptes for theyr said offices in the Kinges Eschequier in Englond, in like maS and forme as other Shireffes and Eschetours do within this Realme of Englond, and upon suche like peyne and penaltie as is upon other Shireffes and Eschetours in ev*y other Shire within this Realme of Englond.

And forasmoche as the Counties or Shires of Brekenoke Radnore Mountgomerey and Denbigh be fare distaunt frome the Citie of London, where the Lawes of England be comonly used mynystred exScised and executed. And for that the inhabitauntes of the said Shires of Brekenoke Radnore Mountgomerey and Denbigh be not of substaunce power and abilide to travaile oute of their Countreis to seke the administradon of Justice, It is therfore enacted by thauctoride aforesaid that the Kinge our Sovaigne Lorde shall have one Chauncerie and Eschequier at his Castell of Brekenok and one other at his Towne and Castle of Denbigh : And that the Shireffes Eschetours and other Officers accomptauntes of the Coundes of Brekenok and Radnore Mountgomerey and Denbigh frome and after the said feaste of All Seintes shalbe yerely appoynted by our Sovaigne Lorde the King for and within e\?y of the said Shires of Brekenok Radnore Mountgomery and Denbigh: And that the Shireffes Eschetours and other officers accomptauntes of the Counties of Brekenoke and Radnore frome and after the said feaste of All Seintes shall yerely make thir accompte, before the Kingcs Auditours and suche Chambreleyne or Baron of the said Eschequier as shalbe therunto appoynted by our seid Sovaigne Lorde the King, in suche like maner and forme as Shireffes Eschetours and other officers accomptauntes do yerely make their accomptes in the Kinges Eschequier at Westmynster within this Realme of England ; And that the Shireffes Eschetours and other officers accomptauntes of the Counties of Mountgomery & Denbigh, frome and after the said feaste of All Seintes, shall yerely make their accomptes, before the Kinges Auditours and suche Chambreleyn or Baron of the said Eschequier as shalbe therunto appoynted by our said Sovaigne Lorde the Kinge, in such like ma8 and fourme as Shireffes Eschetours and other Officers accomptauntes do yerely make thir accomptes in the Kinges Eschequier at Westmjfeter within this Realme of England: And that Justice shalbe ministred used exccised and executed unto the Kinges Subjects and inhabitauntes, in evy of the said Shires of Brekenok Radnore Mountgomerie and Denbigh, according to the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme of Englande, and according to such other Customes and Lawes nowe used in Wales aforesaid, as the Kinge our Sovaigne Lorde and his moost honorable Counsaile shall alowe and thinke expedient requisite and necessarie, by suche Justiciar or Justiciars as shalbe therunto appoynted by our said Sovaigne Lorde the Kinge, and after suche fourme and fasshion as Justice is used and ministred to the Kinges Subjects within the there Shires of Northwales.

FRASMOCHE as manifest synne, vicious camali and abhomynable lyvyng, is dayly usyd & comytted amonges the lytell and smale Abbeys Pryoryes and other Relygyous Houses of Monkf Chanons & Nonnes, where the congregaf&n of suche Relygyous psonf is under the nomber of xij peons, wherby the GouOnours of suche Relygyous Houses and thir Covent spoyle dystroye consume & utterly wast, aswell ther Churches Monasteryes Pryoryes principall Houses Fermes Granges Londes Tenementes & Heredytamentf, as the ornamentes of ther Churches & ther goodes 6c cattallf, to the high dyspleasour of Almyghty God, slaunder of good Relygyon 6c to the greate Infamy of the Kynges Highnes & the Realme if redres shuld not be hadde therof; CHAPTER XXXIX.

AN ACTE concnyng the assuraunce of the Duke of Suff place in Southwerk to the Kyngs Highnes and his Heyres; and concnyng also the assuraunce of Norwiche place unto the Duke of Suff and his Heires.

[Assurance to the King of the Duke of Suffolk's Place in Southwark.]

FOR certeyne resonable consideracions moved & concluded betwene the Kyng oure Soveign Lorde, and the right noble Charles Duke of Suff, It is ordeyned & enacted by authorytie of this psent parliament, that oure saide Soveign Lord the Kyng shall have to hym & to his heires for ever ymediatly fromhensforthe, all that Manour and pryncypall House of the sayde Duke called the Duke of Suffe place sett and beyng in the parisshe of Seynt George in Southwerk in the Countie of Surrey, and all and singuler other Mesuages Howses Tente Gardeyns Landes and pastures of the same Duke or wherof any pson or psons is or ben seased to thuse of the same Duke set lyeng or beyng in the sayde parisshe of Seynt George & in the parysshes of Lamehyth and Kenyngton in the saide Countie or in any of them, together wyth all suche right intest possession & termes of yeres whiche the sayde Duke hath in or to any Londes or Tente inclosed with pales called the Parke adjoynyng to the sayde Maner and pryncypall House, and in or to any Houses Buyldynges Gardeyns or voyde Groundes lyeng or beyng nyghe unto the same pryncypall House.

His Majestye of his mooste aboundaunt and speciall grace, havyng conceyved suche hartie love and tender affeccion to the contynuance and augmentacion of all honeste and vertuouse larnyng artes and sciences, wherewith it hath pleased Almyghtye God so aboundauntely to endowe His Hignes as in Knowlege and wysdam he farre excellith any of his mooste noble progenytours, as his Grace cannot in enny wyse compare the same to annye Lawe Acte Constitucion or Statute ne tollerate or suffer any suche ordynaunce, thowgh the comoditie and benefice therof shulde never so highely redounde to his profute or pleasure, as myght by annye meane hynder thadvauncement. and settyng fourth of the lyvely Worde of God wherewith his people muste be fedd noureshid and instru&ed, or impeache the knowlege of suche other good letters as in xponed Realmes be expedyent to be lerned for the conservacion of their good poilices and the breadyng of discrete and prudent personnages to serve and administre in his comen welth, hath aswell for avoydyng of thoccasion of these inconveniences as for the revyvyng and quickcnnyng of the courage of Student? to thentent they shulde the more joyously and gladlye bende theire wittis and holye gyve theym selfes to thattaynyng of larnyng and knowledge pryncipallye, and before all other thynges in and of the holsome do&rine ot Almyghtye God, and after of the vij artes liberall, and the said thre tonges whiche be requisite and necessarie not onely for the understanding of Scripture, but also for the conservacion and mayntenaunce of pollicie and comen justice, thought convenient for ever by the au&oritie of this his Highe Courte of parliament to discharge acquyte and exonerate aswell the said Universities of Oxforde and Cambridge as the said Colleges of oure Lad ye in Eaton besides Wyndesore and Saynt Marie College of Wynchestre besydes Wynchester and everye of theym frome the payment of ennye suche firste frutes and tenth aforesaid; CHAPTER LXIII.

An Acte declaryng ?teyn Orden"ncf to be observyd in the Towne of Calis and Marches of the same.

rpOHE Kyng oure Soveraygne Lorde Henry the Eight Kyng of Englande and of Fraunce Defender of the Fay the Lorde of JL Ireland and in Erthe the Supreme Heed of the Churche of England, callyng to his mooste gracious remembraunce that his Towne of Caleis and Marches of the same with the good munycion and fortyfyeng therof which hath ben of long tyme and yet is one of the mooste pryncipall treasours belongyng to this his Realme of England as well for his defense of this his Realme and of the narowe Sees wherof his royall Majestie is, as other his noble progenytours have ben, Lorde and Kyng, as also for the spedy and sure Passage of all his subje&es havyng entercourse of Marchaundyse or other wyse travaylyng into the Dominions of Foreyne Prynces and Potentates, is nowe of late greattely enfeebled aswell through the decayes of the edifices and buyldynges therof as also through the negligent and remysse behavours of dyvers and sondry Offycers Mynisters and Souldeours there takyng his Highnes fees and wages; For fortificacion of which Towne and Marches his Grace moste prudently hath lately bestowed and employed sondry greate sumes of Money in fortifyeng of the Walles Castelles Towres Turettes Bulwarkes Dyches and Havyn of the said Towne, And hath also appoynted out of the Treasourie other great sumes of Money for the performyng of the same ; His Majestie therfore nowe intendyng the redresse and reformac&n of the enormyties negligences and abuses of the said Officers Mynysters and Souldeours, and also to provide for the better safegard and tuicion of his said Towne and Marches, hath by thadvyse of his Lordes Spuall and Temporall and the Cdmons in this his psent parliament assembled and by the au&orite of the same, ordeyned provyded enacted and establisshed suche constitucions orders and lawes, fromhensforth in the said Towne of Caleis and Marches of the same perpetually to be observed and kept, in maner and fourme as in this flsent Acte is and shalbe expressed ordeyned and declared.

The Nominacion of the Capitall Officers and Souldeours within the said Towne of Caleis and Marches of the same.

The Othe of the Deputie of the Towne of Caleis and Marches of the same.

Ye shall swere that ye shalbe feithfull and treue unto oure Soveraigne Lorde Kyng Henry the Eight by the grace of God Kyng of Englande and of Fraunce Defender of the faithe Lorde of Irelonde and in erth supreme heed of the Churche of England* and yf ye shall knowe any thyng that shalbe prejudiciall or hurtefull unto his Highnes or his heires or to his Towne of Calies or Marches of the same, Ye shall resyste the same to the uttermoste of your poure. And in case ye can not ye shall without delaye declare the same unto his Highnesse or to suche of his Counsaile as ye thynke wyll she we it unto hym. And ye shall safely kepe to the use of oure said Soveraigne Lorde and of his heires, and defende to the uttermost of youre power, this his Towne of Caleis and Marches of the same as moche as in you by reason of youre office belongith; And in all thynges to be done that toucheth the safegarde defence and good governance of the said Towne and Marches ye shall gyve as it shall nede frome tyme to tyme youre true faithfull and diligent Counseill to the other the Kynges offyeers of the same towne and Marches. And ye shall at no tyme be absent frome your said office without the Kynges speciall licence opteyned in that behalfe. Ye shall well and truely oversee the Marshall and all other officers his and their Ministers and Servauntes and their charge, and every one of them in his degTee entreate in his office as it apperteyneth, not sufferyng any of them to doo in his said office or by colour theirof, any excesse extorcion bribery or exadion. And yf any of them be founde and approved in that case culpable that without favour or delay ye procede to the punyshement of them and every of them to the example of other. Ye shall do your devours at your power to the kepyng of the peace amonge all estates and other persons of what degree or condicion so ever they be, within the said Towne dwellyng or therunto frome tyme to tyme repayrynge, not sufferyng any congregacions assembles commocions or conventicles to be made within the said Towne ageynste the said peace or ageynst the good restefull and politike govemaunce of the same Towne. And yf any psons, of what degree or condicion so ever he or they be within the said Towne, that provoketh pryvely or appertly any suche congregac5n assemble commocion sedicion or conventicle as be founde fautye therof, eyther elles that takethe uppon hym any unlawfull mayntenaunce to the perturbaunce and violacion of the said peace or ageynste right to represse by myght any persone, ye shall resyste and lett withe thadvyse of the resydewe of the Kynges Counsaile of the said Towne and do such punyshement therunto as with reason may serve, without accepcion of personne not sparyng so to do for favour love dredd or mede of any person. And that as moche as in you shall lye to youre power you shall foresee that the said Towne be sufficiently vittayled frome tyme to tyme as unto the same necessarily shall appertcyne or belonge. And ye shall oversee the rule and governaunce of the May re and Aldermen of the said Town touchyng all maner of vitaile and other thynges apperteynyng unto their charge, for the common weale profite and pollicie of the said Towne. And yf any defaulte ye fyndc therin ye shall mynyster and shewe it unto theym chargyuge theym to amende and redresse it. And if they be therin negligent or frowarde ye shall then by the said advyse purvey suche remedy by youre wysedome and discrecion as can be thought moste expedyent with reason; And yf you and the said Counsell can not provyde remedye in that behalfe, then ye shall disclose the same to the Kyngf Highnes or to suche of the Kynges Counsaile as ye thynke verily wyll enfourme the Kynges Highnes therof with spede. And ye shall administer truly rightfully and indifferent]ye justice to all maner psone & psons that shall have any cause moved or dependyng before you in the said Towne and Marches, without havyng any maner of respe&e to any psone for love mede drede or favour. And ye shall in tyme convenyable after your said discrecion visite and oversee the lockes and shyttyng of the gates and postemes of the said towne j And also the governaunce of the Watche Towre Walles and Dyches of the same, and generally all other thynges necessarye for the suertie sauvegarde and defence therof. And ye shall not appoynt ne admytte any personne or personnes into eny rowme within the retynue of the said Towne bclongyng to your admyssion, but if the same psone or ptonnes be borne within the Realme of England Wales Ireland the said Towne of Caleis or Marches of the same \ And that the said personne or personnes be none artificers except he or they eyther be a Bowyer Fletcher an Armourer Crosbowmaker or Smyth; And the same personne so by you named not to be admytted to any suche rowme nor to enjoye nor exercyse the same rowme to the tyme he be viewed examyned and enabled therunto as well by the Treasourer and Comptroller as by the resydue of the Kynges Counsell there then beyng present. And you shall not pmytte ne suffre any alyen borne out of the Kynges obeysaunce to take and inhabite any dwellyng house within the Towne of Calice and Marches of the same as moche as to you apperteyneth, Excepte the same psone be licensed so to do by the Kynges ires patentes under his great Seale, any graunte or grauntes heretofore made to the contrary notwithstondyng. And ye shall see suerly to be kept and safely and [straghtly •] cause to be observed as moche as in you lyeth all maner of Statutes Lawes and Ordenaunces made or to be made by the Kyng our Sovaign Lorde Henry the eight, or by his Counsaile au&orised for the same, for the safegarde tuyeion defence and good orders of his Towne of Calice and the Marches of the same, doyng due execucion uppon the t*nsgressours of eny of the said Statutes Lawes and Ordynaunces, havyng no regarde to the psone so transgressyng for affeccon mede drede or any other cause whatsoever: as God you helpe and the Holy Evangelistes.

The Othe of the Lieftbnaunt of Ruysbanke.

Te shall swere that you shalbe faythfull and true to oure Soveraigne Lorde Kyng Henry the eight by the grace of God Kyng of Englande and of Fraunce defender of the faith Lorde of Ireland and in Erthe supreme hed of the Churche of Englande, and to his heires; and yf ye shall knowe any thyng that shalbe prejudiciall or hurtfull unto his Highnes or his heires or unto his Towne of Calyce or Marches of the same ye shall resiste the same to the uttermoste of your power, and in case ye can not ye shall without delaye declare the same unto his Highnes or unto suche of his Counsell as ye thynke wyll shewe yt unto hym: ye shall gyve from tyme to tyme as it shall nede your true faithfull and diligent Counseill to the Kynges Deputie of his Towne and Marches of Calyce for the tyme beyng and to the Kynges Counsaile and Officers of the same Towne and Marches, and theym shall ayde and assiste to the uttermost of your power in all thynges to be don concemyng the safegarde defence and good govemaunce of the said Towne and Marches: ye shall safely kepe true Englysshe to the use and behofe of our said Soveraigne Lorde and of his heires and defende to the uttermoste of your power his Castell and Fortresse of Ruysbanke by his Highnes appoynted and assigned to your safe kepyng: ye shall be personally remaynyng and resydent uppon your said Rowme and Offyce there and at no tyme to be absent from the tame without the Kynges specyall lycence for the same opteyned; And you shall well and truly oversee that all Officers Souldiours and Ministers of the said Castell and Fortresse that shall serve the Kynges Highnes there under you, shall diligently do cause and suffie to be don all and every thyng and thynges that unto them shall apperteyne and belonge, concemyng the sure and safe kepyng of the said Castell and Fortresse, and yf any of them be founde and proved to be remysse or negligent in doyng his or their duede or dueties that then ye without favour or delaye procede to the correccion and punyshion of hym or them soo offendyng; and that you do your dutie to your power to the kepyng of the peas amonge all and every persone and persons of what degree or condicion he or they be, dwellyng within the said Castell or Fortresse or therunto from tyme to tyme repayryng, not sufferyng any unlaufull congregac6ns convencions or conventicles to be made within the said Castell and Fortresse ageynste good restfull and politike govemaunce of the same, and dulye to corre&e all and e9y persone and persones offendyng: And that aSmoche as in you shall lye you shall see that the said Castell and Fortresse be fumyshed aswell with vitayles aswith all other thynges apperteynyng to the safe custodye of the same, that to you belongeth by dutie of your said Office: And that you truly rightfully and indifferently administer justice to all and every person and persons that herafter shall have any cause or matter moved or dependyng before you in the said Castell or Fortresse without havyng any maner of respe&e to any person or persons for love drede mede malyce or affeccion. And ye shall ( 1) appoynt ne admytt any psone or persons within the said Castell and Fortresse but if the said psone or psones be borne within the Realme of England Waleis Ireland or beyng Englysshe, borne within the said Towne of Calyce or Marches of the same, and that the said psone be sworne to be true liege man unto the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde and to his heires. And fynally ye shall observe and kepe or cause to be observed and kept, asmoche as in you shalbe duryng the tyme you shalbe Lieftenant there, all maner of Statutes Lawes and Ordynaunces made or to be made by our said Soveraigne Lorde his heires or his successours or by his or their Counsell audorished for the same for the safegarde tuicion defence and good orders of the said Castell and Fortresse, doyng due ezecucion uppon the t*nsgressours offendyng any of the said Statutes Lawes and Ordynaunces havyng no regarde to the psonne so offendyng for love favour mede drede or other cause what so ever. So helpe you God, 8cc.

The Othe of the Lieftenaunt of Hammys.

The said Lyeftenaunt shall take lyke othe as is ordeyned for the Lieftenant of Ruysbanke.

The Othe of the Comptroller.

Ye shall swere that ye shall be faythfull and true to oure Soveraigne Lorde Kyng Henry the eight by the grace of God Kyng of Englande and of Fraunce defensour of the faythe Lorde of Irelande and in erthe supreme heed of the Churche of Englande, and to his heires *, And yf you shall knowe any thyng that shalbe prejudiciall or hurtefull unto his Highnes or his heires or unto his Towne of Calyce or marches of the same ye shall resiste the same to the uttermooste of your Power, And in case ye can not ye shall without delay declare the same unto his Highnes or unto suche of his Counsell as ye thynke will shewe it unto hym; Ye shall be diligent obedyent and attendaunt to the Deputie of the said Towne and Marches for the tyme beyng, in those thynges that to the servyce of the Kyng sure good poly tike govemaunce and defence of the said Towne and Marches appertayneth ; and that you shall not be absent frome your said Office without the Kynges especiall licence opteyned in that behalfe; and in all thynges to be done that toucheth the safegarde defence and good govemaunce of the said Towne of Calyce and Marches of the same, shall gyve as it shall nede from tyme to tyme your true faithfull and diligent Counsaile to the Deputie for the tyme beyng and to the Kynges Counsell and officers of the same Towne and Marches, and theym ayde and assiste to the uttermoost of your Power ; and you shall see as moche as in you is that due Musters shalbe taken of all the hole retynue at two severall tymes in the yere before the payeng of their Wages, and oftener yf yt shalbe thought by the Deputie and the Kynges Counsell of the said Town to be nedefull. And in asmoche as in you is and shalbe frome tyme to tyme ye shall see that the Deputie Souldeours and all other officers and ministers what so ever, be resydent attendant and fumisshed as to them in every degree apperteyneth, and (•) such as ye shall fynde defe&yve or fauty from tyme to tyme ye shall tefourme and doo therin as to your office belongeth; Ye shall also diligently and perdcularly oversee the provysiom made and to be made of all and every thyng and thynges necessarye and expedyent for the Kynges workes buyldyngf and reparacions within the said Towne and Marches, and diligently se that all artificers and workemen that frome tyme to tyme shalbe reteyned in the Kynges Wages shall do their dueties, in all suche thynges for the whiche they are so [receyved5 ] ; And that you from tyme to tyme as moche as in you is forsee that the Kynges Highnes be not deceyved nor defrauded of eny of his possessions rentes revenues wooddes waters customes forfaytures and other profytes, as well certeyn as casuall what soever they be which to his Highnes shall of right apperteyne. And that ye shall not appoynte nor admytte any psone or persons into the rowme of a Souldeour within your retynewe, but if the said person or * persons be borne within the Realme of England Wales Irelande the said Towne of Calyce and Marches of the same. And the said person to be sworne to be true liege man unto the Kyng our Soveraigne Lorde and to his heires and to be an able personne to serve the Kyng for defence of the said Towne and Marches; and fynally you shall observe and kepe or cause to be observed and kepte as moche as in you shalbe duryng the tyme that you shalbe in your office all maner of Statutes Lawes and Ordynaunces made or to be made, &c. ut sup*.

And ye shall not rere nor suffire to be done nor rered any newe Cuttomes whiche myght fume to prejudice or hynderance of eny persone: And fynally ye shall see suerly to be kepte and straytly cause to be observed as moche as in you lyeth all maner of Statutes Lawes and Ordynauncf made or to be made by your said Soveraigne Lorde or his heires or successours or by his Counsaile au&orised for the same for the safegarde tuicion defence and good orders of this Towne of Caleys and Marches of the same, doyng due execucion upon the transgressours of eny of the said Statutes Lawes and ordynaunce% havyng no regarde to the psone so transgressyng for affeccion mede dred or any other cause what so ever. The Othe of the Lieftenaunt of Newenham-bridge. The said Lieftenant shall take lyke Othe as is ordeyned before for the Lieftenaunt of Ruysbanke.

The Undermarshall his Othe.

Ye shall swere that you shalbe faithfull and true to our Soveraigne Lorde Kyng Henry the eight by the grace of God Kyng of England and of Fraunce Defender of the faithe Lorde of Irelande and in Erthe supreme heed of the Churche of England, and to his heires. And yf you shall knowe any thynge that shalbe prejudiciall or hurtfull unto his Highnes or his heires or unto his Towne of Calyce or Marches of the same ye shall resiste the same to the uttermooste of youre power. And in case ye can not ye shall without delaye declare the same unto his Highnesse or unto suche of his Counsayle as ye thynke wyll shewe it unto hym: ye shall be obeysaunt to the Kynges Deputie for the tyme beyng in all thynges to be done that toucheth the safegarde defence and good govemaunce of the said Towne of Calyes and Marches of the same: ye shall gyve as it shall nede from tyme to tyme your true faythfull and diligent Counsell to the Kynges Deputie for the tyme beyng and to the Kynges Counsell and Officers of the same Towne and Marches and theym aide and assiste to the uttermoste of your power : ye shall truely sett and do to be sett the stands watche nyghtlye on the Walles of the said Towne at the Castell Hyll, and shall suffire no persone or psonnes to kepe and fumyshe the said stande Watche but such personne or persons as shalbe by you appoynted and sworne accordyng to the Othe for the same dyvyaed and also take suerties of his or their good aberyng in the said Watche : And that ye neyther present ne do to be presented ne imprisoned nor cause to be imprisoned any maner person or watcheman ne other what so ever without reasonable and true cause. And yf you fynde any persones in chance medley drawyng any weapon or smytyng that you do lede or cause to be ledd hym or theym to pryson without any lett, And that ye present or do to be presented every faulte that longeth to your office to be presented dewely and trewely, And that ye take not or cause to be taken any other fees of any personne or personnes than of right and of reason have ben used and of olde tyme accustomed belongyng to your office * And also you shall not holde with no partie ageynste other, nor none susteyne, but ye shall be true Refferender of all that belongeth to your office of Undermarshall: And ye shall nyghtly be in the Market place to take the reporte of the typped staves of the fumysshyng of the Watches in the Easte and Weste Houses on the [Walles 1 ] and shall certifie the same reporte unto the Kyngf Deputie immediatly and all other thynges do that apperteyne to youre said office of Undermarshall duryng the tyme you shall contynewe in youre said Office. So helpe you God, &c.

The Othe of theym that be or shall be made of the Kynges Counsell of the Toune and Marches of Calyce.

Ye shall swere that ye shall be good true and faithfull unto our Soveraigne Lorde Kyng Henry the eight by the grace of God Kyng of Englande and of Fraunce Defender of the faythe Lorde of Irelande and in Erthe supme heed of the Churche of Englande, and to his heyres : And ye shalbe redy withe good attendance to come to the place of Counsell holden for the Kyng where it shalbe assigned and appoynted by the Deputie of his Towne and Marches of Caleys for the tyme beyng, and not to absent you therfrom without reasonable cause of excusacion *, And that in all matters causes and questions that by the said Counsell be or shalbe opened moved styred or axed, you shall say and utter youre good advyse and opynyon clerely after youre discrecion and understondyng, shewyng and gyvyng in conclusion your true and faythfull Counsayle, not lettyng for favour affeccion love affynyte hatred wrothe, had or borne to any partie, or for corrupcion of any goodes or other thyngf what so ever it be; And that all maner langages reasons conclusions, had moved or uttered in the said Counsaile, ye shall effectually kepe theym secretly and not discover them in no wise in other fourme or maner than by the same Counsayle shalbe ordeyned devysed and accordyd : And where as ye can devyse thynke or purpose, any thynge fourme or rule that myght be evydent to tourne to the honour weale and edmoditie of the Kynge our Soveraigne Lorde or to the good govemaunce of this Towne and Marches, ye shall at all tymes shewe and move it to the said Counsayle, to the entent that it may be ordeyned and executed : These thynges above seid and every of them with all their circumstances and dependences ye shall duely exercyse use kepe and do from tyme to tyme duryng your abydyng in the said Counsell with all the [sperites • ] of your good mynde. So helpe you God, and the Holydome and by this boke.

Also it is ordeyned provyded and enacted by au&orite abovesaid that if the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours at any tyme hetafter lycence the Deputie of the said Towne, or any other of the Lieftenantes or chief Officers within the said Towne and Marches or any of them for the tyme beyng, to come into the Realme of Englande, or commaunde hym or them to goo upon embasset or into any outwarde parties in message or warres, that then the same licence and commaundement and eyther of them so to be made shalbe expressed by ires signed with the hande of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours; And that the said Deputie and Lieftenaunt or other chiefe Officer or any of them shall not take any more nombre of personnes of the said retynue of the said Towne or beyng in petie wages under hym or theym, oute of the said Towne and Marches or out of any of them, then shalbe expressely declared and conteyned in the said ires of lycence or cdmaundement therof to be made, as the said Deputie Lieftenant and other cheif Officer will answere unto the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours at his or their uttermost perell, and to make unto the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours suche fyne as by the Counsayll of the Kynges Highnesse his heires or successours attendyng upon hym or theym, uppon any psonne or personnes offendyng contrary to the tenour of this $sent ordynaunce, shalbe assessed or taxed; And that no [spare ’] or speares at any tyme herafter whanne he or they or any of them shall passe into the Realme of Englande, or els where out of the said Towne and Marches or any of theym, shall take with hym any Souldeour or Souldeours beyng under hym in petye wages, excepte he or they have lycence of the said Deputie for the tyme beyng under his signe and his seale to be made, uppon payne of forfeyture of his or their rowme or rowmes.

Archers and Skewrers.

Also it is ordeyned and enacted by the au&orite abovesaid, that if it happen the rowme of any of the said fyve speares whiche ben commenly called the Lyeftenantes speares, to become voyde by dethe expulsion forisfacture or otherwyse, that then as tone as it convenyently may be the said Deputie for the tyme beyng shall cause to be assembled before hym in place convenyent all the other of the speares of the said Towne, and of theym by his discrecion shall ele&e and chose the moste personable a&yve and discrete psone of the same other Speares to be in that rowme then beyng voyde, And the same his nomynacion and elecdon shall publishe and declare at the next assemble of the same Councell there, unto the Treasourer Comptroller and other of the same Counsell there beyng psente; And yf the said personne so nomyna ted and ele&ed by the said Deputie be thoughte by the said Treasourer and Comptroller to be an able and an apte persone for the said rowme, then the said psone so inhabyled shalbe by the said Deputie admytted into the said rowme of a Spere so beyng voyde. And if any rowme of any of the said Speares beynge none of the said fyve Speares happen to become voyde, by suche advancement death forisfa&ure or otherwyse, that then the said Deputie for the tyme beyng shall ele&e and name the mooste personable sadde a&yve and discrete psone, beyng an Archer on Horsbacke yf any of them be thought apte and mete for the same, And in defaute of suche of the said Archers on Horsebacke then some other persone that he can any where fynde or have knowlege of, which shalbe moost apte and mete for that rowme, and hym shall nomynate unto the said Tresourer Comptroller, and more parte of the said Counsell at the next assemble j And yf the said psone so ele&ed and nomynated by the said Deputie be thought by the said Treasourer and Comptroller to be an able and an apte person for the said rowme then the said person so ndiated and abled shalbe admytted into the said rowme of the Speare so advanced to the rowme of one of the fyve Speares or otherwyse voyde as is above saide.

And if it happen the rowme of one of the Archers on Horsebacke to become voyde by death or other wyse, then one of the foure Skewrers, by like nomynacon of the said Deputie and ablement of the said Treasourer and Comptroller, shalbe by the said Deputie admytted into the said rowme of an Archer on Horsbacke$ and in the rowme of the said Skewrer one other psone by the said Deputie to be named and by the said Treasourer and Comptroller abled in fourme afore said shalbe admytted into the said rowme of one Skewrer.

For the resydence of the Deputie Lieftenant Officers and Souldeours within the Towne and Marches of Caleys.

And further more it is enacted by the au&orite abovesaid that the said Deputie Lieftenauntes or other Officer, Mynysters and Souldeours, of what estate degre or condicion so ever he or they be and every of them, nowe beynge or whiche hereafter shalbe takyng or whiche hereafter shall take ther wages within the said Towne and Marches or within any of them, duryng the tyme that he or they or any of theym shalbe Deputie Lieftenant Offycers or Souldeours in the said Towne and Marches or in any of them shall personally inhabyte hym or them selfes dwelle and be resydente upon his or their office and rowme or rowmes within the said Towne and Marches; that is to sey, he and they and as many of theym as nowe take or herafter shall take of fees wages or annuytes of for or in the said retynue of the said Towne of Calyce shalbe resydent and dwell within the walles of the same Towne of Calyes; and in lyke wyse every other Lyeftenant Officers and Souldeours of the Castelles of Caleis Guysnes Hammys Ruysbanke Newenhambrigge and other Fortresses within the Marches of Calyce afore said shalbe personally resydent upon his or their said Offices and rowmes, within the said Castels or Places of or for the whiche he they or eny of them be or shalbe reteyned in Wages and not els where. Provyded always that yf the said Deputie Lieftenauntes or other chief Officers be lycenced by the Kynges Highnes his Heires or successours to come into the Realme of England, or elleswhere to go for his or their causes or matters, that then the same lycence shalbe made in writing signed with the hande of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours. In whiche lycence shalbe conteyned for how longe tyme he or they so lycenced shalbe absent; And if the said Deputie Lieftenant or other Officer or Minister above said or any of them cont*ry to this a&e do absent hym or them selfes from the said Towne or Places in the whiche he or they is or be reteyned or hereafter shalbe reteyned that then he or they shall incurre the peyne and penaltie herafter ensewing *, and that no speare nor other Souldeour of the said Towne of Calies nowe beyng or whiche herafter shalbe, shalbe absent from the said Towne at eny tyme hereafter without the speciall licence of the said Deputie for the tyme beyng to be made in writyng under his signe and seale ; And that lycence in no wyse to extende or to be made for any lenger tyme to endure than for the space of fourtye dayes in one hole yere, upon payne of every speare and Souldeour so offendyng to forfayte to the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours for the first day of his absence suche sommes of Money as he or they taketh or take or shulde take for his or their wages and alowance for that day, and for the seconde day the double and for the third day of his absence the treble, and so to be doubled frome day to day as longe as he or they or any of them shalbe absent contrary to the fourme abovesaid ; and lyke order and penaltie to be taken for the deperture and absence of all and every Souldeour and Souldeours nowe beyng or that hereafter shalbe reteyned within the Castells and Marches abovesaid or within any of them, whiche hereafter shalbe absent without lycence of the Lyeftenant under whom he or they shalbe reteyned contrary to the tenour of this a£le; and lyke penalties to be taken of the said Deputie Lyeftenantes and other chief O/ficers above said and every of them frome tyme to tyme as he or they shall so be absent without lycence as is above rehersed *, the said penalties to be levyed from tyme to tyme by way of reteyner in the handes of the said Treasourer for the tyme beyng to the use of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours of the fees wages or annuyties of hym or them that so shalbe absent. Provyded always that it shalbe lefull to the said Deputie and Counsaylours in the said Towne and Marches and every of theym to goo and resorte at his or their libties and pleasure from tyme to tyme, into any parties within the said Towne and Marches and every of theym for his or their recreacion or disporte, this a&e or any artycle therin conteyned before made or provyded to the contrary notwithstandyng. Provyded also that yf any speare or other Souldeours of the said retynue at any tyme hereafter beyng absent over and above the said fourty dayes can duely and truely excuse his said absence by infirmytie or weakenes in his body, and that duely proved before the Deputie Treasourer or Comptroller for the tyme beyng, or that any suche speare or souldeour dyd come to Dovour before his fourty dayes expyred, and there abyde for lacke of his passage and that certyfyed unto the said Deputie Treasourer and Comptroller or to one of them by the Mayte of the said Towne of Dovour for the tyme beyng under his Seale of Office, or that any speare or souldeour be sente by the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours or by the due processe of the Lawes of this Realme deteyned or imprisoned without fraude or covyn, that then the said speare or souldeours shall not suffire nor in any wyse incurre the penalties nor forfeytures above said, nor otherwyse be dampnyfied by this afte. Provyded also that the said Deputie for the tyme beyng may give licence unto any Speare or Souldeour for the tyme beyng of the said retynue of Caleys by his discTecion to go into Flaunders and Fraunce, or to any of theym to bye horse or hameys or other lefull busynes, So that the same lycence extende not above the nombre of twenty dayes, and that he lycence not above the nombre of tenne persons at one tyme any article before pvyded to the contrary in any wyse not withstondyng.
