The Mousters.

And for as moche as in the Towne of Caleys and Marches of the same there has not ben taken any Mousters by the space of dyvers yeres nowe laste passed before the makyng hereof, whiche Musters ben right expedyent and necessarie in every Towne of Warre to be used had and takyn, Therfore it is ordeyned and enacted by the au&orite above said that the said Musters shalbe taken by the Comptroller of the said Towne for the tymc beyng, yf he be not sycke or have some other reasonable lctt, And yf he be sicke and have suche reasonable lett then by the Treasourer for the tyme beyng, at two severall tymes in the yere that is to say before the Souldeours of the said Towne and Marches do rcceyve any Wages; and the said Comptroller shall se and examyne that every spearc be sufficiently furnysshed with his retynue beyng able men not hyred only for that tyme, and Horse and Armure with other thynges to hym and them apperteynyngc of his or their owne, propre and not boro wed, And that every other Souldeour be an able man and be suffycyently fumyshed with Armure aud Weapon of his or their owne as to his or their rowme or rowmes apperteyneth and belongeth *, And yff the said Comptroller for the tyme beyng not beyng sicke or havyng lett as is above said do not take the said Musters at two tymes by the yere as is above said, that then the said Comptroller for every tyme that he shall be therm remysse or negligent shall forfayte xx ti. sterlyng, The one halfe therof to be payd to the said Treasourer for the tyme beyng to the use of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours, and the other halfe therof to be payde to the Deputie for the tyme beyng, the said xx ti. sterlyng to be levytd of the wages of the said Comptroller beyng or whiche shalbe in the handes of the said Treasourer for the tyme beyng, and by the said Treasourer to be payde as well to the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours as to the said Deputie for the tyme beyng, and that the said Treasourer, upon lyke payne and lykewyse to be levyed, at no tyme hereafter shall pay any wages to any person or psones beyng or whiche hereafter shalbe of the said retynue before the said Musters to be taken in fourme aforesaid. Provyded always that it shalbe laufull to the said Treasourer for the tyme beynge to make or advaunce suche Prcastes of Money unto the said Souldeours upon their wages as unto the said Treasourer for the tyme beynge by his discreckm shalbe thought convenient.

Byeng and sellyng of Rowmes and Offices.

Also j% is ordeyned and enacted by the au&orite above said, that in no wyse the said Deputie of the slid Towne for the tyme beyng nor any other Lieftenant or other Officers of the said Towne and Marches or any of theym, by hym solfe or by any other for hym or theym privately or appertely, shall take any somme or sommes of Money or other rewarde of any personne or personnes or of any other for hym or them or in his or their name or names whiche herafter shalbe admytted into any Oili:e or Rowme of the said retynue within the said Towne and Marches, upon payne of the said Deputie Lieftenant or other Officer so doyng or offendyng contrary to this Acte, after due profe therof made before the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours or suche personnes as the Kynges Highnes his heires and successours shall thereunto assigne, to forfayte tenne tymes so moche as he or they shall so take for the said admyssion, and the partie or parties so admytted to lose and forfayte his or their rowme or rowmes j The one halfe of suche forfeyture of some* of Money to be to the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours and the other halfe therof to be to hym that wyll pursue before the Kynges Highnes his heires or suscessours, or before suche persons as by the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours shalbe therunto assigned for the same, and the same some so forfayted to be levy'ul by the Treasorer of the said Towne for the tyme beyng of his or their wages so doyng or offendyng contrary to this jJsent Actc •, And yf any persone or psonnes what soever he or they be do hereafter covenaunt or bargayne with any Officer Man of armes or other Souldeour of the said retynue for his office or rowme, to die entente to be admytted into the same, that then upon due profe as is above said the same persone shall not be admytted into the said rowme or office without the speciall lycence in writyng of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours under the greate scale of England; and yf it happen for lacke of knowlege of any suche bargayne or sale hereafter to be made without such lycence the same person to be admytted to any suche rowme or offices, suche lycence therof before not [appoynted,1] that then upon due profe therof to be made as is above saide the same persone immediatly shalbe ammoved from his said office or rowme so bought, and shall repaye unto the Treasourer for the tyme beyng to the use of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours all and every suche somme and sommes of Money as he hath before receyved by force of the same rowme or office, And further to be punysshed as by the Kynges Highnes his heyres or successours or his or their Counsaile shalbe thought good ; And that the said Treasourer for the tyme beynge shall have full power and auftorite as well to distrayne the same person and personnes so offendyng by his or their goodes for all and every suche somme and sumes of money as owen to be by hym or them repayde accordyng to this j)sent a&e, as also to comytte the body or bodyes of hym or them so offendyng to pryson, there to remaync unto suche tyme as he or they hath contented the said somme or sommes of Money so to be repayde as is above said, and lyke order to be observed and kepte in the Castels of Caleys Ruysbanke Guysnes Hammys and Newenhnmbrigge, aswell concernyng the Lieftenantes of the same as Souldeours there and every of theym.

No Buhgeis or Artyfycer to be in the retynue of Calyce.

Also for the more increace of people inhabitacion and dwelling within the walles of the said Towne of Caleys, whiche at this tyme for lacke of Englishmen borne within the Realme of Englande is not onlye greatlye inhabyted with Alyens but also many Houses within the same ben vacant and not inhabyted and some in ruyn and decay, by reason that dyvers Burgeses Artificers and Handy craftymen ben Officers and Souldeours within the said Towne and retynue, by occasion whereof not only is lostc one able man of the said retynue whiche myght also be an inhabytant within the said Towne, but also the handycraftes and handycraftes men within the said Towne ben therby lytle or nothyng exercysed, Be it therfore enactcd by the audorite above said that afteT the sixte day of Apryll next commynge no Burgeis Artyficer or Handy crafty man, inhabytyng or dwellyng or whiche herafter shall inhabyte or dwell within the said Towne and Marches or any of theym, and exercysynge his or their arte or handycrafte, at any tyme or tymes after the said day shalbe receyved or admitted into any rowme office fee or wages of or in the said retynue of the said Towne of Calyce, except he or they be a Bowyer a Fletcher a Crosbowmaker an Armorer or a Smythe, any actes constitucions usages or ordynaunces heretofore made to the contrary notwithstondyng; And yf any Burgeis Artificer or handy crafty man usyngc or exercysyng the said artes of handy craftes at any tyme hereafter be receyved or admytted into any rowme office fee or wages of or within the said retynue, that then the said admy<sion to bo utterly voide and of none effefte 5 And the said Burgeis Artificer and Handy craftvman shall repaye

No Souldeour to be any Vytayler.

And yt ys further enacted ordeyned and provyded by the au&orite above said, that no souldeour or souldeours, or any other persone or persons takynge wages in the said retynuc within the said Towne of Caleys and Marches of the same, duryng the tyme that he or they or any of them shalbc in wages or retynue of the said Towne of Caleys and Marches of the same, after the feaste of the Natyvyte of Seynt John Baptyst next commyng shall use or occupie the mysterye of a baker bruer bocher pulter fisshemooger chaundeler or other vyttayller, or duryng the said tyme shall by hym selfe his mynysters servantes or other persone kepe or cause for hym to be kepte any vittailyng house taverne alehouse shoppe of clothe lynnen or wollen or any other open shoppe to or for the retaylyng of any wares merchandyses or other thyrig of what kynde or nature so ever it shall be; And yf any Souldeour or Souldeours which shall take wages as is above said what so ever he or they be at any tyme after the said fest use and occupie die said misteries or any of them or kepe suffire or cause to be kepte any suche house or houses shoppe or shoppes contrary to the tenour of this psent Acte, that then and immediatly after due profe therof made before the Deputie Treasourer and Comptroller of the said Towne for the tyme beynge the said Souldeour or Souldeours what so ever he or they be without delay favour or affeccion shall be expulsed and clerely discharged of his rowme and wages; And that the said Deputie Treasourer and Comptroller whiche after die said feaste after informacion to them gyven shall permytte and suffre any suche souldeour or souldeours to use or occupie any suche misteries or to kepe any suche House or Shop shall forfayte to the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours every of theym for every moneth that any such souldeour or souldeours so shall doo or offende contrarye to this afte x. ti. sterlyng, the same to be levyed of their wages by the High Marshall of the said Towne of Caleys for the tyme beynge to the use of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours: Provyded always that it shalbe laufull to any Souldeour or Souldeours to occupye and use to bye and selle wares and marchandyzes come grane or other vytaile of what nature and kynde so ever it be in gros or in the market by retayle, Provyded also that if any suche Souldeour shall marie the wyfe of any Burgeis or Comoner of the said Towne, which Burgeis or Commoner at the tyme of his deth kept a shoppe or a taverne, that then it shalbe laufull to any suche Souldeour or Souldeours to kepe any such shoppe or taverne duryng the lyfe natural! of his said wyfe $ Provyded also that yt shalbe laufull to every Souldeour and Souldeours that nowe is or hereafter shalbe in the wages of the said retynue within the said Towne and Marches in the herrynge tyme to bye and make herrynge, and the same to utter in grosse and not by retayle to any personne or persons at his and their pleasuret and also to selle saltc woode and coole at all and every tyme and tymes herafter to the inhabitauntes of the said Towne and Marches at their pleasure. Provyded also that this psent atte shall in no case be hurtfull or prejudiciall to any of the Souldeours takyng wages within the said retynue whiche used and occupyed the said misteries or any of them, or whiche kepte any shoppe or shoppes House or Houses as is above said the last daye of Auguste in the xxvij yere of our Soveraigne Lorde the Kynges reigne, so that every of them that so kept shoppe or shoppes House or Houses at the said daye do psent upon ther othes to the Deputie Mayre and Counsell there before the said feaste of Seynt John Baptyste their names and surnames and what misterie he and every of them there used and what House or Houses shoppe or shoppes he and every of theym kepte the said firste day of Auguste, and the same names so Rented cause to be regestred before the Counsell of the said Towne. Provyded also that [yf *] any of the Souldeours whiche nowe taketh or here after shall take the said wages fee or annuytie fortune to be owner half owner or quarter owner of any shippe or shippes fyssherbote or fyssherbootes, so the same shyppe or shippes botes or bootes be belongen to the haven of the said Towne of Caleys, shall and maye at all tymes at his or their fre libtie goo to the See in the said shippe or boote shippes or bootes to exercyse the feate of marchandyse or facultie of fysshyng. And the same marchandyse or fysshe so by hym or theym taken and brought to the said Towne shall and may selle within the said Towne and Marches as moche theirof as unto hym shall apperteyne and belonge as freely as any other dweller or inhabytaunt within the said Towne and Marches.

For gyvyng of Pety Wages,

For as moche as it is evydentely knowen that there ben at this presente tyme many more Pycardes and Flemmynges inhabytynge within the said Towne and Marches of Caleys than Englyshe men, whiche is ageynste the perfe&e weale suertie and tuycion of the said Towne and Marches, Therfore it is ordeyned enacted and established by the au&orite abovesaid that all and every personne and personnes havyng any Manours Mesuages Landes Tenementes or other Hereditamentes what so ever he or they be in use or in possession within the said Towne and Marches or within any of them, of the gyfte dymyse or Lease of the Kynges Highnes or any of his noble pgenytours, or whiche hereafter shall have any Manours Mesuages Landes Tenementes or Hereditamentes within the said Towne and Marches or any of theym of the gyfte graunte dymyse or lease of the Kynges Highnes his heires or successours, or of the gyfte graunte dymyse or lease of any other persone or personnes, at no tyme after the feast of Seynt Michaell tharchangell whiche shalbe in the yere of our Lord God M. And forasmoche as the multitude of people repayrvng unto the Towne of Caleys, aswell Englisshe as AJlyens is, and be greatly discoraged and of late desiste to bryng vitaile unto the seid Towne of Caleys aswell by water as by londe, by occasion of the ezoesse Tolies which daillie ben taken of theym by dy9s and sundry psons, by reason wherof the seid Towne is more scarsely vitailled and the vitailles theder brought solde the more deare then of olde tyme hath ben accustomed, to die great pjudice of the Kynges subjects inhabytyng wythyn the same, It is therfor ordeyned pvyded and enacted by thau&orite aboveseid, that no maS of pson nor psons at eny tyme, after the feaste of Penticoste next comyng, shall take or cause to be taken by eny maS of crafte or mesne eny mam of toll of eny ma8 of vitaill haye strawe sedge cabiges or of eny mafi of wood, nor eny money or money worth for the same or in the name or by colour of eny suche tolle, of eny pson or psons repayryng or comyng or which herafter shall repayre or come with eny mafi of vitaile haye strawe sedge cabages or wood unto the seid Towne of Caleys or Marches of the same by londe or by water; And if eny pson or psons offende cont*rie to this fluent Acte, and that duely pved before the Depude Tresorer and Comptroller for the tyme beyng or before two of theym, shall not oonly forfeyte his or their rowme or rowmes but also shall forfeyte tenne tymes the value of the thyng or thynges so taken, thoon halfe therof to be to thuse of the Kynges Highnes hys heires or successours and thother halfe to be to the partie greved or to hym that shall pursue for the same; And that the seid Depude for the tyme beyng shall have full power and au&orite by this psent a&e to comitte the bodie or bodies of hym or theym so offendyng to prison, there to remayne till he or they have payed the some or sdmes so forfeyted $ and this a&e to be put in due ezecucion by the seid Depude Treasourer and Comptroller or e9y of theym as they will aunswere unto the Kynges Highnes hys heires or successours at hys or theyr uttermoste pill or pills. Provyded always that it shalbe laufull unto the seid Lieutenaunt of Ruysbanke, the Constable there, in the heryng tyme to take of e9y shippe cdmyng or whiche herafter shall come into the Haven of Caleys with heryng xl. heryng oonly, and not above for hys Scope of heryng, for the kepyng of the light there nyghtlye in the seid heryng tyme to be kepte by tbe Lieutenaunt of the seid Castell of Ruysbanke, whiche lighte the Kynges Highnes straidie chargeth and comaundeth the seid Lieutenaunt to cause in the seid heryng tyme to be mayntened. For the Carpenters.

Also where before this tyme the Carpenters whiche be contynuallie reteyned in the wages wythin the seid Towne of Caleys, and have of the Kynges Highnes sufficient stipende for their lyvynges, ptende to have as for their fees and to their owne use all tholde tymbre takyn, aswell of eny of the Kynges Highnes Houses and other hys buyldyngf wythyn the seid Towne as of hys Highnes Sluces Wharfes Bridges Getters Gootes, as of all other hys Buyldyngf wythyn the seid Towne and Marches whych hath ben pulled dowue broken up or decayed, ptendyng the same to be olde corrupte and not mete to be buylded wythall agayn, by colour wherof they daillie not oonly use to take good pfitte and substaunciall tymbre bordes and plankes and the same converte to hys or their owne ppre use and behofe, wythoute yeldyng therof or for the same to the seid Treasourer Comptroller or eny other Officer eny thyng to thuse of oure seid Soveraigne Lorde, but also wilfully cutte and dispoyle the same, entendyng therby to have the same as for his or ther fees; It is therfor ordeyned pvyded and enacted by thau&orite aboveseid, that the seid Carpenters, or eny of theym by theym selfes or by eny other for theym or in their names, at no tyme herafter shall take suffre or cause to be taken any maner of tymbre bourdes giestes raftyers or plankes what so e9 they be of oure seid Sovaigne Lorde hys heires or successours, but oonly suche as they shall have by the dely9e and appoyntment of the Comptroller of the seid Towne for the tyme beyng, upon payne to forfeyte and paye unto the Kynges Highnes hys heires or successours after due pfe therof made the treble value of the thyng soo takyn, and further to be punysshed as by the Deputie and Counsell of the seid Towne for the tyme beyng shalbe thought convenyent; the same forfeyture of treble the value to be levyed to thuse of oure seid Sovaigne Lorde hys heires or successours by waye of reteynour of hys or their Wages in the handes of the Treasourer there for the tyme beyng, or otherwyse as by the seid Deputie and Comptroller shalbe thought expedient.

And that every persone beneficed or hereafter to be beneficed as is aboveseid within the said Towne of Caleis and Marches, upon the payne above said, by hym or by his Deputie shall every Sonday and Holyday and other festyvall dayes in the yere, tyme of hostilitie and warre within the said Marches only excepted, reherse publishe and declare the beades in the Englisshe tonge, And for asmoche as in hym or them is or shalbe, procure the Englisshe language used within this Realme of England to be spoken and used in every one of his or their said Parisshes from tyme to tyme, aswell amonge the Householders and their 3vauntes, as the chylderne of their parochians and others resortyng unto the same.

CHAPTER IV.

An Acte repelyng of the Statute lately made for the bryngyng in of Doulas and Lokerams.

WHERE at the parliamente holden at Westmynster the thirde day of Novembre in the xxj yere of the reign of our Sovaign Lorde King Henry the eight, amonges other thinges it was enacted and establisshed, that no pson nor psones Englissh nor Straunger Denysen or Alien from or after the feste of Seynt Michaell tharchaungell [than 1 ] next folowyng shulde bryng or convey or cause to be conveyid or brought by eny maSe of meanes into this Realme of Englonde any lynnen Cloth called Doulas or Lokerams, oonles e9y hole peace of Doulas conteyned in lenght fyve score ellf of assise accompted to e$y Ell oon ynce of assise, and in bredth one yarde of assise, and evy half peace fyfty Ellf in length and oon yarde in bredth of like assise, and all the hole peace, and halfe peace of oon goodnes in makyng ; CHAPTER VIII.

An Acts for contynuaunce of the Statutes ayenst the cariage of Brasse Laten and Cop oute of this Realme and for

makyng of Cables and Ropes and others.

WHERE in the laste parliament begonne and holden at London the thirde day of November in the xxfk yere of the Kynges most gracious reigne and from thens adjourned to Westmynster and there holden and contynued by dyv*s progacions untill the dissoludon therof, It was ordeyned and establisshed amonges other thinges one ade for restraynyng the cariages of brasse latten and coper out of this Realme, and also one other ade was made in this parliament for the trew makyng of Cabuls Halsars and Ropes, one other ade for the trew wyndyng of Wolles and one other to restrayne killyng of Weynelinges Bullockes Streres or Hester being under the age of two yeres. All which four seQall ades were made to contynue and endure to the next parliament as by the said ades more playnly appereth; For as moche as the said sev^all ades and e9y of them be necessarie for the c5men welth of this Realme, Be it therfore enacted by audoride of this psent parliamente that the said four sePall ades, and all clauses ardcles and pvysions therm conteyned shall from hensforth be and stande good and effeduell and to contynue and endure undll the laste day of the nexte parliament.

CHAPTER IX.

An Acte for contynuance of the Statutes of Peijurie, for makyng of Jayles, & for sowing of Flaxe and Hempe.

XT THERE in the parliamente begonne and holden at London the thirde day of Novembr and from thens adjourned V V to Westni and there holden and contynued by progacion unto the xv. day of January in the xxiij yere of the reign of our most drad Sovaign Lorde Kyng Henry the eight, It was [than *] in that Session of the said parliamente one ade made and establisshed for atteyntes to be sued for punysshement of pjury uppon ontrue verdides, which ade was then made to endure to the laste daye of the next parliamente; And where also in the said Session of the said parliamente one ade was made and establisshed for makyng of Jayles in dyv^s Shires of this Realme, which ade was then made to contynue and endure for one yere next after thende of the same parliamente; And where also in the tyme of the same parliament one other ade was made concernyng Pewterers which Ade was also made to endure to the laste day of the next parliament; And also in the tyme of the said parliament one other ade was made concernyng sowyng of flaxe and hempe, which ade was also made to contynue and endure to the laste day of the next parliamente; as by the said four sev^all ades more playnly appereth: For as moche as the said four ades be good and benefldall for the c5mon welthe of this Realme, Be it therfore enacted by audorite of this psent parliamente that the said four ades and e9y of them, and all clauses articles and pvisions therin conteyned, shall stande contynue and endure in their force and strength, and be observed and kepte to the laste day of the nexte parliamente.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte extynguysshing the audoryte of the Busshop of Rome.

FOR AS MOCHE as notwithstandyng the good and holsome Lawes Ordyn'nces and Statutes hertofore enacted made and establisshed by the Kynges Highnes our moste gracious Sovaigne Lorde, and by the hole consent of his High Court of Parliament, for the extirpacion aboludon and extinguyshment, out of this Realme and other his [Gracis Domynyons Seignories and Countreys, of the Ptended Power and usurped audorite of the Bisshop of Rome by some called the Pope, used within the same or els where concernyng the same Realme Domynions Seignoreis or Countreis, which did obfuscate and wreste Goddis holy worde and testament a long season from the spiritual! and trew meanyng therof, to his worldly and carnall affections, as pompe glory avarice ambidon and tyranny, coveryng and shadowyng the same with his humayne and polytyke dyvyses tradicions and invendons sett forth to pmote and stablissh his only Domynyon, both uppon the sowles and also the bodyes and goodes of all Cristen people, excludyng Criste out of his Kyngdome and rule of Man his sowle, as moche as he may, and all other tempo rail Kynges and Prynces out of their Domynions, which they ought to have by Goddis lawe, upon the bodies and goodes of their Subjects; wherby he did not oonly robbe the Kynges Majestie, being oonly the supme hedd of this his Realme of Englande immediatly under God, of his honour right and preemynence due unto hym by the lawe of God, but spoyled this his Realme yerely of ynnumerable treasure, and with the losse of the same deceyved the Kynges lovyng and obedient subjedes, pswadyng to them, by his lawes bulles and other his deceyvable meanes, such dreames vanyties and fantasies as by the same many of them were seduced and conveyed unto supstitious and erronyous opynions; so that the Kynges Majestie, the Lordes spirituall and temporall and the Cdmons in this Realme being overweried and fatygated with thexperience of the infynite abhomynadons and myschiefes pcedyng of his impostures, and craftily colouryng of his deceytes to the great damages of soules bodies and goodes, were forced of necessite for the publique weale of this Realme to exclude that forayne Ptended power jurisdicrion and audorite, used and usurped within this Realme, and to devise suche remedies for

An Acte for punysshement of Pyrotes and Robbers of the See.

An Acte conSnyng the assuraunce of a Pencyon unto Robt Shurbo’n late Bisshopp of Chichester.

WHERE of late, at thynstaunce & contemplacyon of the Kyngf most Royall Magestye, the Recent Father in God Robt Shurborn late Bysshop of Chichester in the Countye of Sussex resigned into the handes of oure sayd Soveign Lord his sayd Bysshopprych of Chichester, with all suche ryght tytle and interestes as he hadd in the same, and whiche the Kyngf seyd Highnes hath geven unto his ryght trustye and welbeloved Councellour Richard Sampson Clerk Deane of his most honorable Chapell, And into the whyche Bysshoppryche the sayd Richard ys consecrat and in leyfull possessyon, And for thassurance of the some of foure hundreth poundes sterlyng to be well and trewly payd unto the sayd Robt late Bysshop duryng his naturall Jyff oute of the Lordshyps Manors Landz Tentf and other Heredytamentf of the sayd Bysshoprychc, accordyng to thagrement hadd made & concluded betwene the sayd late Bisshop and the said Richard Sampson now Bisshop of the sayd Bysshoppryche, by the most Royall assent consent and agreament of the Kyngf Highnes: Be it therfore cna&ed ordeyned and establysshed by the Kyng oure Soveign Lorde the Lordf spuall and temporal) and the Comens in this present Parlyamcut assembled and by thau&oryte of the same. CHAPTER I.

An Acte for joynt Ten*ntf & Ten*ntf in comon*

FORASMUCHE as by the comen lawes of this Realme, di$se of the Kingf Subjectf being seised of Mannors landf tentes & hereditamentf as joynt ten*ntes or as ten*ntes in comen with other, of any estate of enheritaunce, in their owne rightf or ia the right of their wyffes, by purchase discent or otherwise, and e9y of them so being joynt ten*ntes or ten*ntes in comeil hathe like righte title interest and possession in the same Mannors landes tefites and hereditamentf for their partf or por£6ns joyntlye or in comen undevydedlye together withe other, and none of them by the lawe doeth or maye knowe their sevall partes or por£6ns in the same, or that that ys his or theirs by hit selfe undevyded, and cannot by the lawes of this Realme otherwise occupye or take the pfytt of the same, or make any severans division or partiftn thereof, without either of their mutuall consentes and assentf; By reason whereof di^Be and many of them, beinge so joyntly and undevidedly seised of the saide Mannors landf tehtf & hereditamentf, often tymes of their perverse covetous and malicious myndes and willes, ayens all right justice equkie and good conscience by strenghe and power, hath not onlye cutt and fallen downe all the Woodes and trees growinge uppon the same, but also hathe extirped subverted pulled downe and distroyed all the houses [edificyons1] and buyldyngf meadowes pastures comens and the hoole comodities of the same, and hath taken and converted them to their owne uses and bebooffif, to the open wronge & disherison & ayens the myndes and willes of other holdinge the same Mannors landes teStf & hereditamentf joyntlye or in comen withe them, and they have bene alwaies without assured remedy for the same; Be it therefore enacted by the Kinge our most drede Soveraigne Lorde and by thassent of his Lordes sjSuall and temporall and by the Cdmons in this Psent Parliament assembled, That all joyntten*ntf and ten*ntes in comen, that nowe be or hereafter shalbe of enny estate or estates of enheritaunce in their owne rightf or in the righte of their wyffes, of any Manners landes tehtf or hereditamentes within this Realme of Englande Wales or the Mersches of the same, shall and maye be coacted and compelled by vertue of this psent acte, to make pti£6n betwene them of all suche Mannors landes tentes and hereditamentf as they nowe holde or hereafter shall holde as joyntten*ntf or ten*ntes in c5men, by writt de [pti£6ex] faciend, in that case to be devised in the Kinge our Sovaigne Lordes Courte of Chauncerie, in like manner and forme as Coperceners by the comen lawes of this Realme have byne and are compellable to doe, and the same writt to be pursued at the comen lawe.

Provided alwaye and be it enacted, that ev*ye of the saide joyntten*ntf or ten*ntes in comen and their heires after suche parti£6n made, shall and may have ayde of the other, or of their heires, to thentent to deraigne the warrantye pamounte and to recover for the rate as is used betwene Copceners after ptic&n made by the order of the comen lawe ; any thinge in this acte conteyned to the cont*rie notwithstandinge.

CHAPTER n.

An Acte against fishingf in Pondf.

For preventing Robbeiy and Destruction of Fish Ponds;

The fishing in any private Pond by Night, and unlawful breaking down the Head of

any such FishPond, by Day or Night, declared to be Felony.

An Acte abolishing diPsity in Opynions.

WHERE the Kinges most excellent Majestie is by Gods lawe, supreme head ymediatly under him of this hole Churche and Congregac6n of Englande, intendinge the conservacon of the same Churche and Congregacbn in a true syncere and unyforme doftrine of Christf Religion, callinge also to his blissed and most gracious remembraunce aswell the great and quyett assurance psperous encrease and other innumerable comodyties whiche have ever ensued come and followed of concorde agrement and unyty in opynions, as also the manyfold pilles daungers and inconveniences w* have heretofore in many places and regions growen spronge and arysen of the di\?sityes of myndes and opynions especially of matters of Christen Religion ; And therefore desiringe that suche an unyty myght and shulde be charitablye established in all thinges touchinge and conceminge the same, as the same so beinge established myght cheifly be to the honour of Almyghtie God the verie Autor and founteyne of all true unytie and sincere concorde, and consequently redounde to the comon welth of this his Highnes most noble realme, and of all his lovinge subje&f and other resiantes and inhabitauntf of or in the same ; Hathe therfore caused and comaunded this his most highe Courte of Parliament, for sundry and many urgent causes and consideracbns to be at this tyme somoned, and also a Synode and Convocaf&n of all the Archbisshopps Bisshopps and other lerned men of the Clergie of this his Realme to be in like manner assembled; And forasmuche as in the saide parliament synode and convocacon there were certen articles matters and questions pponed and set forth touchinge Cristen Religion, that is to say; First, whether in the most blessed Sacrament of Thalter remayneth after the consecra££»n the substance of bread and [wynne1 ] or no; Secondly, Whether it be necessary by Gods lawe that all men shoulde be comunycate withe bothe kindes or noe; Thirdly, whether Preestf that is to saye Men dedycate to God by Preesthood may by the lawe of God mary after or noe; Fourthly, whether Vowe of Chasdtye or Widowehood made to God advisedly by man or woman be by the lawe of God to be observed or noe; Fiftly, whether privat masses stonde with the lawe of God and be to be used and contynued in the Churche and congregacbn of Englande as thinges wherby good cristen people may and do receyve both godly consolacon and holsome benefyttf or noe; Sixtly, whether auricular confession ys necessarie to be reteyned contynued used and frequented in the Churche or noe; The Kinges most Royal Majestie most prudently ponderinge and consideringe that by occasion of variable and sundrie opinions and judgementf of the saide articles, great discorde and variaunce hathe arrisen aswell amongest the clergie of this his Realme, as amongest a great nomber of vulgar people his lovinge subje&f of the same. And beinge in a full hope and truste that a full and perfe&e resolucon of the saide Articles shoulde make a pfe&e concorde and unyty geSally amongf all his lovinge and obedient subje&f; Of his most excellent goodne9 not only comaunded that the saide Articles shoulde delifeatly and advisedly by his saide Archbisshopps Bisshopps and other lerned men of his Clergie be debated argued and reasoned, and their opinions therin to be understond declared and knowen, but also most graciously vouchsaved in his owne princely pson to discend and come into his saide highe Courte of Parliament and Counsaile, and there like a Prince of most highe Prudence and noe lesse lemynge opened and declared many thingf of highe leming and great knowledge touchinge the said articles matters and questions, for an unytye to be had in the same; Whereupon, after a great and longe delibate and advised disputacon and consultaf&n had and made concerning the saide articles, aswell by the consent of the Kinges Highnes as by thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporal!, and other lerned men of his Clergie in their Convocactm, and by the consent of the CSmons in this fpfeent parliament assembled, it was and is fynally resolved accorded & agreed in manner and forme following, that is to say ; First, that in the most blessed Sacrament of the Aulter, by the strenghe and efficacy of Christf myghtie worde, it beinge spoken by the prest, is psent really, under the forme of bread and wyne, the naturall bodye and bloode of our Saviour Jesu Criste, conceyved of the Virgin Marie, and that after the consecracun there remayneth noe substance of bread or wyne, nor any other substance but the substance of Criste, God and man; Secondly, that Comunion in bothe kindes is not necessarie ad salutem by the lawe of God to all psons; And that it is to be beleved and not doubted of, but that in the fleshe under forme of bread is the verie blode, and withe the blode under forme of wyne is the verie fleshe, aswell aparte as thoughe they were bothe together; Thirdly, that Preestf after the order of Presthode receyved as afore may not marye by the lawe of God; Fourthlye, that vowes of Chastitye or Wydowhood by Man or Woman made to God advisedly ought to be observed by the lawe of God, and that it exempteth them from other libtyes of Cristen people, wch without that they myght enjoye; Fyftly, that it is inete and necessarie that private masses be contynued and admytted in this the Kingf English Churche and Congregation as wherby good Cristen people orderinge them selfes accordingly doe receyve bothe godly and goodly consolacbns and benefyttf, and it is agreable

An Acte howe Landf may be willed by Testament.

singulier his loving and obedient subjects, [and by1] many tymes past hath not only shewed and [imparted4] to them, generally by his many often [and greate5 ] benefidall pdons heretofore by au&orities their powers and graces by them receyved of God to rendre and geve unto his Majestie their moste humble reverence and obedient thankis and services, with thdr daily and contynuall praiers to Allmighty God for (6) codnual pservacion of his mooste Roial astate in moste kingely honour and prosperitie j Yet allwaies his Majesty being replete and endowed by God with grace goodnes and liberalide mooste tenderlie considering that his said obedient and loving Subjects cannot use or exercise themselfis according to their estatis degrees faculties and qualities, or to beare themselfis in suche wise as partes veray greate and abundaunt, but that in manner of necessitie as by daily experience is manifested and knowen they shall not be hable of their propre goodes cattallis and other moveable substaunce to discharge their detds, and after theire degrees sett furthe and avaunce their children and posterities j Wherefore our said Souveraine Ix>rde most vertuously considering the mortalitie that is to everie personne at Goddis will and pleasure moste comon and uncertaine, of his most blessid disposidon and liberalitie, being willing to releve and helpe his said subjecds in thdr said necessities and debilities is contented and pleased that it be ordeyned and enacted by au&oritie

Lymitac&n of Prescription.

FORASMUCHE as the tyme of Lymytacion appointed for sueyng of writtes of right, and other writtes of possession and season of mens auncestours or predecessours or of their awne possession or season, by the Lawes and Statutes of this Realme heretofore made lymited and appointed, extende and be of so farre and longe tyme past, that it is above the remembraunce of any lyving man truely to trye and knowe the parfett certainty of suche thinges as hath or shall come in triall or doon extend unto the tyme and tymes lymyted by the said lawes and statutes, to the greate daunger of mens consciences that have or shalbe impannelled in any Jury for the tiiall of the same; and also it is a greate occasion of much trouble vexacion and sutes to the Kinges loving subjectis at the comon lawes of this Realme; so that no man, although he and his auncestours and thos whos estate he or they have, ben in peasible possession of a longe season of and in landes tenementis and other hereditamentis, is or can be in any suertie quietnes or rest of and in the same, without a good remedy and reformacion be had made and provided for the same; Be it therfore enacted by the Kinge our Souveraine Lorde the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this present plament assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that no maner of personne or persones shall fromhensfurth sue have or mainetene any writte of right, or make any prescription title or clayme of to or for any Mannours landis tenementis rentis annuities comons pencions porcions corredies or other hereditamentis, of the possession of his or their auncestor or predecessor, and declare and allege any further season or possession of his or their auncestor or predecessor, but onely of the season or possession of his auncester or predecesser, which hath ben or nowe is or shalbe seased of the said Mannours landis tenementis rentis annuyties comons pencions porcions corrodies or other hereditamentis within threescore yeris next bifore the Teste of the same writte, or next bifore the said prescripcion title or claime so herafter to be sued commensed brought made or hadde.

And be it further enacted by thauftoritie aforesaid, that no maner of psone nor psonnes shall herafter have sue or maintain any assise of Mortauncestor Cosynage Ayle Writte of Entree uppon disseason doon to any of his auncestours or predecessours, or any other aftion possessorie, uppon the possession of any of his auncestours or predecessor, for any Mannours landis tentis or other hereditamentis, of any further season or possession of his or their auncestor or predecessor, but onely of the season or possession of his or their auncestor or predecessor whiche was or herafter shalbe seased of the same Manours landis tends or other hereditamentis within fiftie yeris next bifore the teste of the originall of the same writte herafter to be brought.

And be it further enacted by thauftoritie aforesaid, that no psonne nor psonnes shall herafter sue have or maineteyn any aftion for any Mannours landis tends or other hereditamentis of or uppon his or their owne season or possession therein, above rhirtie yens nexte bifore the teste of the originall of the same writt herafter to be brought.

CHAPTER IH. toti the cotinuaS&n of Ades.

■^TTtTHERE in the (') parlament begonne and holden at [Westfii*] the thirde day of Novembre in the xxj yere of T T the kinges most gracious reigne and from thence adjourned to Westfii and there holden and contynued by sundrie prorogations, It was enacted amongest other thinges that all foren plees triable by the Contry, which shuld be pleaded by any persone or psonnes arrayned uppon any inditement for any pety treason murdre or felony, shulde be tried bifore the same justices afore whome suche personnes shulde be arrayned and by the same Jurours of the Countie that shall trye the pety treason murdre or felony without any further respit or delay; And that no personne or personnes arrayned for any pety treason murdre or felony shuld be admitted to any pemptorie chalenge above the nombre of xxa: which afte was made to endure to thende of the next parlament, as by the said afte amongest diverse Clauses and provisions conteyned in the same more plainely is expressid: And where also in the same parlament it was enacted that no psone or psonnes whiche shuld happen to be founde gilty after the lawes of this Realme for any maner of pety treason, or for any wilful murdre of malice prepensed, or for robbing of any churches chappellis or other holy places, or for robbing of any persone or personnes in their dwelling houses or dwelling place the owner or dweller in the said house his wife his children or servands than being within and put in feare and dreade by the same, or for robbing of any personne or psonnes in or nere about the high waies, or for wilfull burning of any dwelling houses or baraes wherin any come or graine shal happen to be, nor that any personne or personnes being founde gilty of any abetement procurement helping maineteyning or counsailing of or to any suche petie treason murdres or felonyes, shulde be admitted to the benefite of their clergie, suche as be within holy orders that is to saye of the ordres of subdiacon or above all onely except, with many other clauses and provisions in the said acte as by the same ade more playnely apperith ; which a&e was made also to contynue and endure to the last day of the next plament: And wher also in the same plament it was further enacted, that everie suche personne and psonnes whiche shulde happen to be indited of any pety treason wilfull burning of houses murdre robborie or burgulary or other felony, according to the tenour and meaning of the said estatute next above rehersed, and theruppon arrayned did stand muet of malice or froward mynde, or chaleng peremptorie above the nombre of xx personnes or will not aunswere directly to the same inditement and felony wheruppon they shalbe arrayned, that then everie suche persone and personnes shuld lose the benefite and pvilege of their clergie; And it was also ordeyned by the same acte that if any persone or psonnes be indited & founde gilty for stealing of any goods and cattailles in any Countie of this Realme, or being indited stand muet of malice or chalenge pemptory above the nombre of xx** psonnes or will not aunswere directly to the lawe, shulde also lose the benefite of their clergie in like maner and fburme as they shuld have doon if they had ben indited arrayned and founde gilty in the same County where the same robberie or burgulary were doon, if it shall appear to the Justices by evidence or examinadon that the said felones or robbers arrained afore them shulde or ought to have lost their clergie biforce of the said estatute in cace they had ben founde gilty of the same felonies or burgularies in the same shire where they were comitted \ as by the said actis amongest other thinges more at large is expressid : And where also in the said plament it was further ordeyned that the detestable vice of buggery comitted with mankynde or beast shulde be felony and that the offendours therm shulde lose the privilege of their clergie; which acte was made to endur to the last day of the next plament, as by the same acte amongest other thingf it appereth more at large : And where also in the plament begonne and holden at Westfii the viij** day of June in the xxviij yere of the reigne of our said moste dradde souveraine lorde king henry theight and there contynued and kept until the dissolution therof. CHAPTER IX.

Aoenst maintenaunce and embracery byeng of titles, &c.

TIE King our Souveraine Lorde calling to his moste blissed remembraunce that there is nothing within this Realme that conserveth his loving subjectis in more quietnes rest peace and good concorde then the due and juste ministration of his lawes and the true and indifferent triall of suche titles and issues as ben to be tried according to the lawes of this realme, whiche his moste roiall Majestie pceyveth to be gretely hindered and lettid by mayneten*nce embracerie Champartie subomacion of witnesses sinistre labour buying of titles and pretensed rightes of personnes not being in possession, wheruppon greate pjury hathe ensued and muche unquietnes oppression vexacion troubles wrongis and dishenheritaunce hath folowed amongest his moste loving subjectis, to the greate displeasure of Allmighty God the discontentadon of his Majestie and to the greate hinderaunce and lett of justice within this his realme; For avoyding of all which misdemeanours and bying of titles and pretensed [ - - - -1 ] and to thintent that justice may be the more fully and indifferently ministred and the trueth in causes of contencion plainely tryed bitwene his subiectis of this realme: Be it enacted by our said souverain lorde with thassent of the lordes spuall and temporall and the cdrnons in this present plament assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that fromhensfurth all statutes heretofore made concerning maintenance champarty and embracery, or any of them nowe standing and being in their full streignth and force, shalbe put in due execution according to the tenures and effectis of the same statuds.

And over that be it further enacted by thau&oritie aforesaid that no psonne or psonnes, of what estate degree or condition soever he or they be, shall fromhensfurthe bargaine bye or sell, or by any waies or meanes obtayne get or have, any pretensed rightis or titles, or take promise graunte or covenant to have any right or title of anny psonne or psonnes in or to any mannours landis teritis or hereditamentis, but if such psonne or psonnes which shall so bargaine sell give graunte coven*nte or promise the same their antecessours or they by whome he or they dayme the same, have ben in possession of the same, or of the reversion or remaindre therof, or taken the rends or profittes therof, by the space of one hole yere next bifore the said bargaine covenant graunte or promise made; uppon payne that he thatt shall make any suche bargaine sale promise coven*nte or graunte to forfaicte the hole value of the landis tenemends or hereditamends so bargayned solde promised covenanted or graunted contraire to the fourme of this afte j And the byer or taker therof knowing the same to forfai&e also the value of the said landis tenemends or hereditamentis so by him bought or taken as is abovesaid : Thone half of the said forfai&ures to be to the King our souveraine lorde, and thother half to the parde that woll sue for the same in any of the Kingf Courtes of recorde by action of dett bill playnt or information ; In whiche action bill plainte or information none essoyne protection wager of lawe nor Injunction shalbe allowed.

CHAPTER XII.

Con&iing Sanctuaries.

THE Kinges most roiall Majesde, calling to his moost blessid remembraunce howe that many idell and evyll disposed psonnes within this his realme and other his Graces dominions, nothing regarding the feare of God nor the punyshment of the Kinges lawes, heretofore have doon and doo daily comitte and ppetrate wilfully as well great sundry & detestable murders robbories as also other greate and haynouse offences, to the greate displeasure of Allmighty God & to the subversion of all good and polidke ordre, wherunto suche malefactours are partely instigated and moved and the more bolde and willing so to offend by certaine lycendouse privilege and other liberties heretofore graundd to divers places and territories within this his realme comonly callid Sanctuaries, to whiche suche wilfull ofiendours heretofore have had refuge and tuidon of their lifes and bodyes after the said myschevous offencf ppetradd and doon, from the just and condigne punyshment of his Graces lawes, both contrary to the expressid worde of God and the comon tranquillity of this his Graces realme and the publique welth and suerty of the same: Wherefore his Grace of his accustumed goodness, neither mynding the encouraging nor contynually maynteyning of suche mischevouse and wilfull malefadtours and ofiendours, neither againe thutter abolishing and extinguishment of all sanctuaries and the privileges of the same, very expedient and convenient to be had and contynued in every comon welth by the lawe of mercy for some causes and offences ; The Kinges Highnes is contentid and pleasid that it be enadtid by his Highnes with thassent of the lordis sjSuall and temporall and the commons in this pnt plament assembled and by audtoride of the same, that all maner of sanctuaries and places privileged, which heretofore have ben used reputed or taken for any maner of sanctuary, except parrish churches and their churche yerdis Cathedrall churches hospitalles and churches collegiate and all chapels dedicated used as parrish churches and the cemytories to them and evy of them belonging, and except suche places and territorites as herafter shalbe declared appoinctid and named to be places of tuytion and privilege by this present adte, shalbe utterly exdnguished adnulled voide and of none effedt for any such liberty or privilege of sanctuaries to all purposes and intends ; Any lawes licences estatuds custumes privileges prescriptions allowaunces or any other thinge or thinges heretofore used or admitdd to the contrary notwithstanding.

CHAPTER XIV.

The Mayntenaunce of the Navye.

FORASMUCHE as it is evidently and notoriously knowen that the more parte of this our souveraine lorde the Kinges realme of Inglaund and the confynes and dominions of the same is and ben compassed and invironed by and with the grete sees, so that neither the kinges liege people and subjectis of this his said realme nor yet anny other of anny foren realmes or Countries can or may convey or transporte their Wares goodis marchaundises and commodities into and from the said realme by o9 (*) alongest the said sees but onely by shippes. And where the Navy or multitude of Shippes of this realme in tymes past hath ben and yet is verie profitable requisite necessarie and comodiouse aswell for the entercourse and concurse of marchauntis transporting and conveying their wares and marchaundises as is above said, and a greate defence and suerty of this realme in tyme of warre as well to offend as defende, and also the mayneten'nce of many maisters maryners and see men, making them expert and connyng in the arte and science of shippmen and sayling and they their wifes and children have had their lyvingf of and by the same, and also hathe ben the chief maynten*nce and supportacion of the Cities Townes villages havens and creekis nere adjoyning unto the see costes, and the Kinges subjectis bakers bruers butchers smythes ropers shipwrittes taillours [showe makers *] and other vitallers and handycraftis men inhabiting and dwelling nere unto the said coostis have also had by the same a greate parte of their lyvingf ; and the same Navy and multitude of Shippes is nowe of late fivailously appaired and decayed and by occasion therof not only a greate multitude of the Kinges liege people whiche thereby had their lyving be nowe mynyshed and empoverishid, but also the townes villages and inhabitations nere adioyning unto the see costi3 ben utterly fallen in ruyne and decay; For reformation wherof it was ordeyned and enacted by a Statute made in the fifte yere of the reigne of the right noble King Richard the second that none of the Kinges liege people shuld shipp marchandise in any other shipp than in an english shippe upon payne of forfeiture of the said Marchandise so shipped; And after that by one other estatute made in the y^ yere of the said most noble King it was enacted that for defeulte of english shippes every man might shipp their Schandises in straungiers shippes; And after that at a plament holden at Westfii the iiijth yere of the late noble King of famouse memorie King Henry the vijth it was ordeyned and enacted that no psonne shuld carrie or bringe any Wynes of Gascoigne and Guyen or Tholose Wode into Englaund Wales Irelaund Calais or the marches therof or Barwike but onely in shippes of England Wales Irelaund Calais or marches therof or Barwike, and that the maister and maryners of the same shippes or the most pte of them shuldc be of the same Countries uppon payne of forfaicture of the same wyne and Wadde; And after that at a plamEt holden at Westni the xv* day of Januarie in the xxiij yere of the moste noble Reigne of our nowe souveraine lord the Kinge Henry theight it was ordeyned and enacted that the said estatutis and epy thing in them conteyned shulde stand in their full streignth force and effect. So that from thensfurth no psonne shuld attempt to doo contrary to the tenures of any of the said estatutf uppon the paynes conteyned in the same, as in the same estatutis is more plainely expressid and declared: Yet notwithstanding divers and sondrie psonnes not regarding the mayneten'nce of the said Navy nor yet the commodities and profittes coming and growing unto this Realme by occasion of the same, for their owne singulier lucre and ad*vntage have not

Provided alwaies that this Acte ne anny thing therin conteyned or specified concerning the said rates or sommes of the fraight bifore rehersid shall not extende to bynde or charge any owners, maisters, pursers or maryners of anny Shipp or Vessill for the frayting or lading therof into or from any porte or haven within this realme of Englaund other then the said porte of London in raaner and fourme bifore specified.

Provided also and be it enacted by thau&oritie aforesaid that at whatt tyme any Warre shall happen to be moved or hadde bitwene this realme of Englaunde and any other exteriour potentatis foren princes their realmes or subjectis or bitwene any other outward Kingedomes or Dominions, by occasion and meanes wherof the said owners shalbe more charged for the furnyture of their Shippes and Vessillf aswell with vitallf more nombre of men and artillerie for the sure conducting conveyaunce and transportation of the marchandises goodes and wares laden in the same, that then it shalbe lawfull to the same owners to receyve take and have suche more and greater some or sommes of monney, o9 and above the rates aforesaid for the fraight of their Shippes and Vessailes, as the iSchantes and they shalbe agreed uppon, any thing or thinges conteyned and lymited in the said rate specified in this present Acte, or anny other thing in the same Acte conteyned to the contrarie therof in anny wise notwithstanding.

tharchebishopp or Bishopp of the Diocesse and to his Chauncelo' or Cdmissarie and to suche other psonnes as shulde be named by the Kinges Highnes or by suche other as His Majestie at his pleasure should appoinde to name the same, whiche Archebishop or Bishopp his Chaunceler or Cdmissarie and other psonnes so to be named or three of them at the leaste, wherof tharchebishop or bishop or his expedient by their discretions, and shulde have power and audoritie by vertue of [theira] said ade and their said comission as well to take information and accusation by the othis and depositions of twoo hable and lawfull psonnes at the least as to inquire by the othis of xij men, of all and singulier the heresies felonyes contemptis and other offences mentioned and dedarid in the same ade edmitted doon or perpetrated within the lymittes of their comission, as by the same ade amongest other thinges therin conteynid more at large it doth and may appere: And forsomuche that as well the diocesse of the See of YoTke as other [diocesse3] within this Realme ben very wide and large extending into divers shires and ben divided into severall riddingf wapentakis and sookis, and in e9y one CHAPTER XVI.

ConSoing Strangers.

TIE King our moste dradde Souveraine Lord calling unto his blissed remembraunce the infinite nombre of Straungs and aliens of foren countries and nations whiche daily doo increase and multiplie within his Graces Realme and Dominions in excessive nombres, to the greate detriment hinderaunce losse and empoQishment of his Graces naturall true lieges and subjectis of this his Realme and to the greate decay of the same; remembring also the manyfold good Adis and Statutis which have ben heretofore made aswell by his moste noble progenitours as by his owne most roiall Majestie for reformadon of the same, in divers and sondrie plamentis, that is to wit: First in the first yere of the reigne of King Richard the third, where it was enacted that no psonne not born under the sam Kinges obeisaunce, nor made denizen taking uppon him to be an artificer or handycraftf man, shulde take nor occupie anny house or chambre within this Realme nor abide or remaine in the same, nor sejourne with any straunge personne not being borne under obeisaunce of the same King as is aforesaid, nor exercise or occupie any crafte or manuall occupation within the sam Realme; but that suche straungiers shulde departe from this same Realme within a certaine tyme appoincted by the said estatute, onlesse they were reteyned in service to or with any subjectis or lieges of the King onely whiche were expert in ther craftis or occupations, under payne to forfaicte all their goodis ; And that no personne not being borne under the said Kinges obeisaunce nor made denizen being an artificer or handycraftis man shulde make any cloth within this Realme; And also that no suche straunger shulde selle anny wares within this Realme but onely in grosse and not by retaile, uppon payne of forfaicture of the said Wares; And moreover that no psonne not being borne under the said Kinges obeisaunce abiding in any house or chamber within this Realme occupying any handycrafte after a certaine tyme in the said acte lymited shulde take any serv*nt to worke with him except it were his sonne or doughter or ellis one of the subjectis of the said King and borne under his obeisaunce, under payne to forfaict for evy suche default xx H. as in the said a&e amongest other thinges more plainely apperith: And where also in the xiiij* & XVth yere of the reign of our said Souveraine Lord the King that nowe is, it was enacted that noo straungier borne out of his Graces obeisaunce were he denisen or not denisen using any handy crafte or occupation within this Realme shulde take anny apprentice except the same apprentice were borne within his Graces Dominions and obeisaunce uppon payne to forfaicte for everie suche apprentice so taken x K. And that also no straungier or alyen borne undre like payne using any handy crafte within this Realme after a certaine tyme lymited in the said acte shulde take or have any Joumayman or covenant servant excepte such joumayman or covenant Servaunt were borne undre his Graces obeisaunce; And that all maner of aliens borne as well being denisens as not denisens inhabiting within the Cide of London or a certaine space aboute the same shuld be under the serche and reformadon of the wardeines of the felaushipps of handycraftis within the said Cide of London; as in the said estatute amongest other thinges more plainely apperith: And also where in the plament of our said Souveraine Lord holden at West® in the xxj yere of his mooste graciouse reigne it was enacted among other thinges that no Straunger shulde keep any moo servauntf straungiers but onely twoo at one tyme, and that all denizens [than '] made or after to be made whiche wolde inhabite within the said Citde of London or within a certaine circuyte of the same and wolde there kepe any house or occupie any crafte or occupation shulde be contributorie to and with the Kinges Graces subjectis of the same crafte or occupation within the said Cittie of London, paying bearing and susteyning suche charges of the same craftismen as in the same acte is conteynid; and that they shulde also present them selfis at the Common Hall or Meting place of the said craftes in the Citie of London and there to take a corporall othe bifore the maister and wardeines of the same crafte to be true to our said SouvWe Lord the King & his heires; And also that noo straunger artificer or handicraftis man borne out of his Graces allegeaunce not being denisen shulde sett up or kepe any house shoppis or chambers wherin they shuld excercise any handy craft or mistery within this Realme, uppon like penalities as ben mencioned in the said former estatute; And that also no Straungier nor denisen not being boren within this Realme shulde assemble in any company felaushipp congregadon or conventicle but only in the c5mon hall of their craftis with his Graces- subjectis of the same craft uppon like payne as is aforesaid; as in the said actis and statutis amonge many other thinges more plainely apperith: All whiche holsome good and beneficiall actes and statutes ben in maner infringed frustrated and defrauded, chiefly by the meanes of divers letfts patentis obtayned by the craftie sutis inventions and practises of suche straungiers lately made denisens in great nombre, which letters patentis do conteyne that everie suche denisen shalbe as free as Englishemen naturally borne within the Kinges Graces Dnions and obeisaunce, any a&is or statutis made or to be made to the contrarie notwithstanding; by reason wherof the said denisens refuse to obey and pfourme suche orders and directions as in the said former estatutes were lymyted pscribed and declared, as well to and for suche straungers borne out of the Kinges obeisaunce (*) at that tyme were made denisens or that after shulde be made deinsens, to the greate hinderaunce and decay of the handy craftis men being the Kinges Graces naturall lieges and subjectis; Foe reformation wherof the Kinges moste roiall Majestie is contentid and pieasid that it be enactid by his moste graciouse Highnes the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comens in this present plament assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that all maner of straungers borne out of his Graces obeisaunce, which heretofore have ben made denisens or that herafter shalbe made denisens, from and after the first day of Septembr next coming shalbe bounde and obedient by & unto all the forsaid actf and statutis and to all the contends of the same, and to all other actf and statutes of this Realme heretofore made now being in their force and not repellid; CHAPTER XXffl.

The Subsidie of the Clergie of Canturbery.

"TY THERE the Prelates and Clergie of the Province of Caunterburye have lovingly and liberally for certaine v V considerations, geven and graunted to the Kinges Majesty a Subsidy of foure shilling^ of the pounde9 to be taken and levied of all and singuler their spuall promotions within the same Province during the terme of twoo yens nowe next ensueyng, in certaine maner and fourme with divers exceptions and provisions specified and conteynid in a certaine Instrument by them therof made and deliverid unto the Kinges Highnes under the seale of Tharchebishop of Caunterburie, as in the same Instrument exhibited in this psent plament more plainely dothe appere, the tenour wherof ensueth in thies wourdf : The Prelatis and Clergy of the pvince of Caunterburie calling to remembraunce not onely the greate libertie and freedome that they have by their deliveraunce from the yoke and bondage of the usurped power of the Bishop of Rome, whiche by the mooste gracious goodnes and divine wisedome of our moste dradde and naturall Souveraigne Lorde the Kinges Majestie, is moste laufully and rightuosly clerely [vanquished1 ] and extinguished out of this Realme; And that therefore the Bishopp of Rome cessith not daily most malidously to ymagyn howe to proyoke foren Princes to take parte with him to revenge his said moste unlaufull and wrongefull quarellis; but also the greate excessive and inestimable charges whiche the Kinges Highnes hath by reason therof been at, and is daily and must contynually be at herafter in making of Havens Blockehouses and other divers Fortresses for the defence and tuicion of this his Realme and his loving subjects in the same; Have of their owne mere lovinge tendre mynde and good will, geven and graunted and by thies presends doo geve and graunte unto the Kinges Majesty a Subsidy towardis his said charges in maner and fourme folowing, that is to say: That everie Archebishop Bishop Deane Archedeacon Pbendary Provost Maister of College Maistre of Hospitall psonne Vicar Chauntrie Preest and other GoOnours and ev*y of them, and e9y other psonne and psonnes of whatsoever name or degree he or they be, enjoying any spuall promotion or other temporall possessions to the same Spirituall promotions annexed, nowe not divided or seperate by acte of pliament or otherwise from the possession of the Clergie, shall pay to the Kinges Highnes for everie pounde that he may yerely spende by reason of the said spuall promotion the somme of foure shillinges sterling : And for the true and certaine knowlege of the yerely values of the said promotions and everie of them wherof the payment shulde be made, the rate taxacion and valuation and estimation all redy made and certified in the Estchequier for the payment of the ppetuall dysme, concerning all suche promotions as yet remaine in possession of the Clergie or any other not yet divided by Atte of plament or otherwyse as is aforesaid, shalbe folowed and observid without making any newe valuation rate taxation or estimation other [then*] in the said certificate is comprehendid: Provided alwayes that forasmuche as the tenth parte of the said valuation and taxe certified in theschequier is yerely paid to the Kinges Highnes for the ppetuall dysme, so as there remayneth onely nyne partis to the Incumbent clere, this subsidie of foure shillinges of the pound shalbe understand of the said nyne partis and no more; Provided also that no psonne paying first frutes shalbe charged with any parte of this Subsidy during the first yere of that Iiis promotion. The said p>latis and clergie alsoo graunten that this subsidie of foure shilling^ of the pounde of the yerely clere value of e9y promotion taxed as afore, shalbe paide to the Kinges Majestie within twoo yens next ensueing the date herof at the receipt of his Eschequier or within anny other place where it shall please the Kinges Highnes to appoint, that is to say, twoo shillinges of e9y pounde at suche daies and tyme of the yere as the ppepuall disme is nowe by tenour of thafte of plament ordred to be contentid and paid. CHAPTER XXIV. i he Possessions of Thospitallf of S1 Johns of Hierusalem.

THE Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this present plament assembled, having credible knowledge that divers and sundry the Kinges sobjecds called Knightes of [the1 ] Rodes otherwise callid Knightis of Sainct Johnes otherwise called Freers of the Religion of Sainct John of Jerusalem in England, and of a like House bring in Ireland, abiding in the parties of beyonde the See and having aswell out of this Realme as out of Irelaund and otfir the Kinges Dominions yerelye greate sdmes of Money for maynten'nce of their lyvingf, have unnaturally and contrarie to the duety of their allegeaunces sustayned and maynteynid the usurped powre and auctoritie of the Bishop of Rome, lately used and practised within this Realme and other the Kinges Dominions, and have not onely adhered theymselfis to the said Bishop being comon ennemye to the King our souvaine Lorde and to his Realme, untruely upholding knowleging and affirmyng maliciously and traiterously the same Bishop to be supreme and chef bed of Christes Churche by Goddis holy wourde, intending thereby to subvert and overthrowe the good and godly lawes and statutes of this Realme their naturall Contrey made and grounded by auctoritie of Holy Churche by the most excellent Wisedome polycye and goodnes of the Kinges Majesty with the hole assent and consent of the Realme for the abolishing expulsing and utter extincting of the said usurped power and auctoritie, but also have diffamed and sclaundred aswell the Kinges Majesty as the noble men prelates and other the Kinges true and loving subjectis of this Realme for their good and godly proceding in that bihalf; have therefore deepely pondered and considered that, like as it is and was a mooste godly acte of the Kingf moste roiall Majesty and the said noble men prelatis and comons of this Realme utterly to expulse and abolishe not only from this Realme but also from other the Kinges Dominions the said usurped power and auctoritie of the Bishop of Rome, and also the hipocritike & superstiouse Religions within this Realme and in other the Kinges Dominions being his membres and adherentis having their original erection and foundation by the said usurped auctoritie, by expulsing wherof Goddis holy Worde necessarie for increace of vertue and salvation of Cfcren soules is not onely purely and sincerely avaunced and set furth, but also the extorte exactions [and * ] inufiable somes of Money craftely exhausted out of this Realme and of other the Kinges Dominions by the Color of the said usurped auctoritie is removed and taken away, to the inestimable benefite and comoditie of the Kinges loving subjectis ; So like maner of wise it shulde be mooste daungerous to be suffired or pmitted within this Realme or in any other the Kinges Dominions any Religion being sparkis leaves or ympes of the said roote of iniquitie; Consideryng also that the Isle of [Rhoodes3 ] whereby the said religion toke their olde name and foundation is surprised by the Turke, and that it were and is muche better that the possessions in this Realme and in other the Kinges Dominions appertayning to the said religion shulde rather be employed and spent within this Realme and in other the Kinges Dominions for the defence and suertie of the same than conv^ted to and amongest suche unnaturall subjectis whiche have declyned not only from their naturall duetye erf obedience that they ought to beare unto the King their SouPaine Lorde, but also from the good lawes and statutis of this Realme their naturall Countrey, daily doing and attempting privily and craftely all that they can to subvert the good and godly Policye, in the whiche thanckis be to God and to our moste dradde Souv^aine Lorde this Realme and other the Kyngf Dominions nowe stande in; In Considera£6n wherof the said Lordis spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent plament assembled moste humbly besechin the Kinges moste Roiall Majesty that it may be enacted by his Highnes and by thassent of the Lordis squall and temporall and the Comons in this psent plament assembled, that the corporation of the said Religion aswell within this Realme as within the Kinges Dominions and lande of Ireland, by whatsoever name or names they be founded incorporatid or knowen, shalbe utterly dissolved & voyde to all intends and purposes ; And that Sir Wittm Weston Knyght nowe being Priour of the said Religion within this Realme of England shall not be named or callid from hensfurth Prior of Sainct Johnes of Jerhn in England but shalbe callid by his propre name of Wiitm Weston Knight without farther addition towching the said Religion; And that likewise John Rawson Knight nowe being Priour of Kilmaynam in Irelande shall not be callid or named fromhensfurth Priour of Kylmaynam in Ireland but onely by his awne propre name of John Rawson Knight without farther addition towching the said Religion ; nor that any of the bretheme or confreres of the said Religion in this Realme of England and land of Ireland shalbe callid Knightis of the [ Rhoodes3 ] nor Knightis of Sainct Johnes but shalbe callid by their awne propre cfcren names and surnames of their parentis without any other additions towching the said Religion.

CHAPTER XXV.

The dissolution of the ptensed manage w* the Lady Anne of Cleves.

THE Lordis spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent plament assembled, calling to their remembraunce the manyfolde detestable conflictes intestine batails mortalities of people and disherisons whiche heretofore have sprongen and growen in this Realme by occasion of diversifies of titles to the Crowne of the same, whiche moste chiefly grewe and insurged by dowbtis of manages and of the incertainrie of the succession of the same; Considering also that thanckis be to God almaner titles be nowe conjoyned consolidate united and vesfid allonly in the Kinges most roiall psone, so that his Majesty is and standeth presently a juste and undoubted pure and parfett King of this Realme, against whome none impediment or objection can or may be by any maS of meanes alleged, And that it apptaineth to thoffice and policye of all civile bodies of Realmes and Countries moste chiefly next to their Duefies to God to forsee and provide for the suerfie and certainty of the succession of their Kinges and chief gouvWurs forasmuche as upon the certainrie therof dependeth their hole comon welth rest peace and tranquillitie; And lately understanding that greate ambiguities doubtis and questions have been moved in the mariage solemnised betwene the Kinges Majestie and the lady Ann off Cleves, whereby greate troubles and inconveniences might herafter springe and growe in this Realme to the Iminent danger of the destruction of the subjectis therof if remedy shulde not spedily be provided for the same: The Temporall Lordis and Comons have therfore made their mooste humble in?cession and petition to the Kinges moste Roiall Majestye, That it might pleas his Highnes of his accustumable goodnes to comitte the state of his said mariage with all the circumstaunces and dependaunces therof unto the plates and Clergie of this Realme to be serched examined diffined and determined by them according to the trueth justice and equifie, in suche wise as shulde stande with Goddis pleasure the Kinges honour and the welth and tranquillitie of this Realme; CHAPTER XXVI.

Concerning Christes Religion.

"TXTHERE the Kinges roiall Majesde of his blissed and gradous disposition like as his Highnes is our Souveraine v v liege Lorde and supreme hed of the churche of England, so his Grace taketh the care and sollidtude therof moste diligently forseyng and providing all that can be to the quiet unyon concorde welthe prosperide and fortheraunce of the same; Considering also that nothing so muche troublith the comon welth and hyndereth quiet and concorde as diverside in opinions and belefe specially in thinges that conceme AUmighty God and his religion. And of his prudence and [wisedam1 ] well waying that out of sundry outward places and pties there have spronge ben sowen and set forth divers hereticall erroniouse and daungerouse opinions and doctrines in the religion of Christ, whereby some of his Graces liege people might be not only disquieted and moved to variaunces strifes commotions or seditions among them selfis to thutter obstruction and undoing of them selfis and of their hole posteritie for ever, but also enduced and assured unto unfaithefolnes misbelefe miscreaunce and contempt of God to thutter confusion and dampnation of their soules, unlesse by his Majesties providence some good remedy shulde be ordeynid for the same; Hath of his bountefoll roiall [clemence4] therefore appoincted established and ordeynid tharche bishops and sundry bishops of both provinces of Caunterbury and Torke within this his realme and also a greate nombre of the best lamed honestest and most vertuouse sorte of the Doctours of Divinytie men of discretion judgement and good disposition of this said realme, to thintent that according to the very gospell and lawe of God, without any pardall respect or affection to the papisticall sorte, or any other secte or sectes whatsoever they be, they shulde declare by writing and publish aswell the principall articles and poinctes of our fayth and belefe with the declaration true understanding and observation of suche other expedient poinctf as by them with his Graces advise counseill and consent shalbe thought nedefoll and expedient, and also for the laufoll rites ceremonies and observations of Goddis service within this his Graces Realme: And forasmuche as the true diffinition determination and declaration therof requierith ripe and mature deliberation and advise, and that so high and godly thinges may not rashely be diffinid determined and set forth nor to be astricte or restrayned to this present Session or anny other Session of this f?sent plament, but from tyme to tyme be diffined determyned concluded and published as the case shall require, and as his Majestie with thadvise of his moste honorable Counsaill, and suche as his Highnes hathe appoincted or shall from tyme to tyme appoinct to the same shall thincke moste convenient;
