CHAPTER XXVIL

Resumption at Calais, Berwik and Wales.

Certain Grants of Offices in Calais and Berwick, with unusual Fees, &c.;

and of Sheriffwicks in Wales for Life;

All such Grants declared void j

and also all Grants thereof in Reversion.

WHERE divers of the Kinges subjectis by their sinistre and subtill information and meanes have heretofore had and obteynid of the Kinges Majestie, as well by his Ires Patentis as by billf and warrantis assigned by his Graces hand divers grauntes for terme of life & lifes of divers offices fees wages and other profittes being extraordinary and not (1) the ordinary offices fees wages or profittes of the garysons within the Townes of Calais Guynes Hammes Ruysbanck and the Marches of the same, and in the towne of Barwicke; And have likewise obteynid of the Kinges Highnes divers especiall warrantis and lycences for to be absent and none resident in and uppon their ordinary offices within the said townes and marches: And where also divers of the Kinges subjectis, of their sinistre and subtill meanes have likewise obteynid of the Kinges Majestie for terme of life and lifes divers grauntis unto them made by the Kinges Graces ires patentis of divers offices of sherifwikes within the Kinges dominions of Wales, contrarie to the edmon welth of the Country there; not only to the greate unsuertie of the said townes and places above rehersid but also to the greate disquieting vexation and truble of the Kinges loving and obedient subjectis: For reformation wherof be it enactid ordeynid and establishid by thauctoritie of this pnt plament that all and singulier suche ires patentis warrantis and licences heretofore graunted or made by the Kinges Majesty to any psonne or psones as is aforesaid and everie of them shall by thauctoritie aforesaid from and after the first day of Septembre next coming be clerely void frustrate and of none effecte to all intends constructions and purposes; And also that all and singulier grauntis of the reverdon or reversions of any office or offices in the Townes aboverehersid and Marches of the same shall by thauctoritie aforesaid be likewise voide frustrate and of none effect to all intentis and purposes.

Evil of avoiding certain Leases;

Leases made by Tenants in Fee, or in Right of their Wives or Churches, declared valid against their Heirs and Successors.

CHAPTER XXIX.

Oswaldebeck Socke.

BE it enacted ordeynid and establishid by the King our Souveraigne Lorde and by thassent of the lordis spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent plament assembled and by auctoride of the same, that all meases landis tenemends and other hereditaments being gildable sett lying and being within the lordeshipp and [sooke'] of Oswaldebeck otherwise Oswaldebeck soke within the Countie of Nottingham wherof anny psonne or psonnes be nowe seasid in possession or remaindre in fee simple or fee taile, whiche be pretendid by a custume there to be partible betwene and amongest heires males, shall from hensfurth be clerely chaunged from the said custume and in nowise herafter be departed or departible by anny custume there amongest and betwene heires males, but shall remaine revert abide descende come and be after and according as meases landis tenemends and other hereditamentis doo or may discende remaine revert abide come or be according to the comon lawe of this Real me, and in like maner to discend and be discendable remaine come revert and be inheritable to the heir or heires after and according to the said comon lawe of this Realme of England; And that all and singulier the said meases landis tenemends and hereditamentis shall from hensfurth be acceptid taken inheritid demed and adjuged to be like as landis tenemends and other hereditamentis at the comon lawe of this Realme, and in suche maner and fourme as if the same measis landis tenemends and other hereditamentis had never ben departed or departible betwene and amongest heires males; any lawe usage or custume within the saide lordeship or soke heretofore had acceptid or used to the contrarie therof notwithstanding.

CHAPTER XXXIII.

Wrongfull disseasyn to be no descente.

Death of a Disseisor shall not operate as a Descent against the lawful Owner, unless after Five Years peaceable Possession.

WHERE divers psonnes of their insaciable myndes have heretofore by streignth and without title entered into mannours landis tenementis and other hereditaments, and wrongfully disseasid the rightfull owners and possessours therof, and so being seasid by disseasyn have therof dyed seasid, by reason of whiche dying seasid the disseisye or suche other psonnes as bifore suche discent might have laufully entred into the said mannours landis and tenementis were and be thereby clerely excluded of their entre into the said mannours landes and tenements, and put to their action for their remedy and reco^y therin, to their greate costis and charges; For reformation wherof be it enacted by auctoride of this psent plament that the dying seasid heraftre of any suche disseisour of or in any mannours landis tends or other hereditamentis, having no right or title therein, shall not be taken or demed from hensfurth any suche descent in the lawe, for to tolle or take away the entree of anny suche psonne or psonnes or their heirf which at the tyme of the same discent had good and laufull title of entree into the said mannours landis teiitis or hereditament^, Except that suche disseasour hath had the peasible possession of suche manours landis tends or hereditamentis, wherof he shall soo dye seasid, by the space of v yeris next aftre the disseasin therin by him comitted, without entree or contynuall clayme by or of suche psonne or psonnes as have laufull title thereunto.

CHAPTER XXXVIL For recoQing of Arreragf by £xecutors & Administrator.

FORASMUCH as by thordre of the Comon lawe thexecutours and administratours of ten*ntf in fee simple tenltf in fee taile & tenantf for terme of lifes of rends services rente charegs rente seckf and fee fermes have no remedy to recop such arrerages of the said rends or fee fermes as were due unto their testatours in their lifes, nor yet the heires of suche testatour nor anny psonne having the reversion of his estate aftre his deceace may distraine or have anny laufull action to levye anny suche arrerages of rends or fee fermes due unto him in his life as is aforesaid ; By reason wherof the ten*ntis of the [demayne '] of suche landis tenementis or hereditamends out of the whiche suche rends were due and paieable who of right [out * ] to pay their rends and fermes (3) suche daies and termes as they were due, doo many tymes kepe holde and retaine suche arrerages in their owne handis, so that thexecutours and administratours of the psonnes to whome suche rentis or fee fermes were due cannot have or cdme by the said arrerages of the same towardis the payment of the detds and pfburmaunce of the will of the said testatours;

suche psonne or psonnes unto whome any suche rent or fee ferme is or shalbe due and not paid at the tyme of his deathe shall and may have an addon of dett for all suche arrerages, against the tenant or ten*ntis that ought to have paide the said rent or fee fermes so being behinde in the life of their Testatour, or against thexecutours and administratours of the said ten*ntis: And also furthermore it shalbe laufull to ev*y suche executour and administratour of any suche psonne or psonnes, unto whome suche rent or feferme is or shalbe due and not paid at the tyme of his deathe as is aforesaid, to distraine for the arrerages of all suche rends and fee fermes upon the landis tenementis and other thereditamentis whiche were charged with the payment of suche rentis or fee fermes, and chargeable to the [distrees4] of the said testatour, so longe as the said landis tenementis or (4) hereditamends contynue remaine and be in the season or possession of the said ten*nt in [demaine1] who ought ymmediately to have paid the said rent or fee ferme so being behinde to the said testatour in his life, or in the season or possession of anny other psonne or psonnes clayming the said landis teiitis & hereditamends onely by and from the said tenant by purchace gifte or discent; in like maner and fourme as their said testatour mought or ought to have doon in his life tyme. And the said executours and administratours shall for the same distresse laufully make avowry uppon their matier afforesaid.

CHAPTER XXXVIIL Con&ung p>contractf and degrees of Consanguinity

"VTTHERAS heretofore the usurped power of the Bishop of Rome hathe alwayes entangled and troubled the V T mere jurisdiction and legal power of this Realme of England, and also unquiedd muche the subjecds of the same by his usurped power in them, as by making that unlaufull whiche by Goddis wourde is laufull bothe in manages and other thinges as heraftre shall appere at more length; and dll nowe of late in our Souveraine Lordes tyme, whiche is otherwise by laming tawght than his predecessours in tymes past of longe tyme have ben, hath so contynued the same, wherof yet some sparkis be lefte whiche heraftre might kindle a greater fyer and so remayning his power not to seme utterly extincte. Therefore it is thought mooste convenient to the Kinges Highnes his Lordis spuall and temporall with the Comons of his Realme assembled in this present plament that twoo thinges specially for this tyme be with diligence provided for, whereby many inconveniences hath ensued and many moo els mought ensue and followe: as where heretofore divers and many psonnes after longe contynuaunces togither in matrimonye, without any allegation of either of the pdes or anny other at their manage whie the same matrimony

should not be good juste and laufull, and after the same matrimony solemnised and consumate by camall knowlege,

and also some tyme fruite of children ensued of the same manage, have nevertheless by an unjuste lawe of the Bishop of Rome, whiche is that uppon pretence of a former contracte made and not consumate by camall copulation, for profe wherof twoo witnes by that lawe were onely required, ben divorsed and separate contrarie to Goddis lawe, and so the true matrimony bothe solemnised in the face of the Church and consumate with bodily knowlege and confirmed also with the fruite of children had betwene them derely frustrate and dissolved: Further also by reason of other prohibitions than Goddis lawe admitteth, for their lucre by that Courte invented, the dispensation wherof they alwaies reservid to them selfis, as in kynnerede or affinitie betwene cousyn germaynes and so to fourth and fourth degree camall knowlege of anny of the same kynne or affinitie bifore in suche outwarde degrees which elys were laufull and be not prohibited by Goddis lawe, and all bicause they wolde gett monney by it and kepe a reputation to their usurped

jurisdiction; whereby not onely muche discorde betwene laufull maried psonnes hath contrarie to Goddis orden*nce

arrisen, muche debate and sute at the lawe with the wrongefull vexation and greate damage of the innocent partie hath ben procured, and many juste mariages brought in doubte and daunger of undoyng and also many tymes undoone and laufull heires disherited, Wherof there had never els but for his vayne glorious usurpation ben moved any suche question, syns fredome in them was geven us by Goddis lawe which ought to be most sure & certein. But that notwithstanding mariages have been brought into suche an uncertainty thereby that no mariage coulde be so surely knytt and bounden but it shulde lye in either of the parties power and arbitre, casting away the feare of God, by meanes and compasses to prove a precontracte a kynnerede an alliance or a camall knowlege to defeate the same, and so undre the pretense of thise allegations afore rehersid to lyve all the daies of their lyves in detestable adultery to thutter destruction of their owne soules and the provocations of the terrible wrath of God uppon the places where suche abominations were suffred and used : Be it therefore enacted by the King our Souveraine Lorde the Lordes spuall and temporall and the C5mons in this fPsent plament assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that from the firste day of the monneth of July next [ensueyng 1 ] in the yere of our Lorde God a thousande fyve hundred and forty, all and e$y suche mariages, as within this churche of England shalbe contracted betwene lauful psonnes, as by this acte wee declare all psonnes to be laufull that be not prohibited by Goddis lawe to mary, suche mariages being contracte and solemnised in the face of the churche and consumate with bodily knowledge or frute of childeme or childe being had therm betwene the parties so maried, shalbe by auctoritie of this present plament aforesaid demed judged and taken to be lauful good juste and indissoluble, notwithstanding any precontracte or precontractis of matrimony, not consumate with bodily knowlege, whiche either of the psonnes so married or both shalhave made with anny other psonne or psonnes, bifore the tyme of contracting that mariage which is solemnised and consumate or wherof suche frute is ensued or maye ensue as afore; and notwithstanding any dispensation prescription lawe or other thinge graunted or confirmed by acte or otherwise: And that no reservation or prohibition, Goddis lawe except, shall trouble or impeche anny mariage without the Leviticall degrees; And that no pson of what estate degree or condition soever he or she be shall aftre the (*) first day of the [said3] monneth of July aforesaid be admitted in any of the spuall Courtis within this the Kinges realme or anyhis Graces other landis and dominions to any proces plea or allegation contrarie to this foresaid acte.

CHAPTER XL.

Con&ning Phisicians.

IN moste humble wise shewen unto your Majestie your true and faithefull subjectis and liege men the President of the corporation of the Comminaltie and felowship of the science and facultie of Phisicke in your Cittie of London and the Comons and fellowes of the same; That wheras divers of them, manny tymes having in cure aswell some of the lordis of youre most honorable counsaile and divers tymes many of the nobilitie of this Realme as many other of your faithfull and liege people, cannot geve their attendaunce to them and other their patientes with suche diligence as their duety were and is to doo, by reason they be many tymes compellid aswell within the Citie of London and suburbes of the same as in other townes and villages to kepe watche and warde, and be chosen to thoffice of Constable and other offices within the said Citie and suburbes of the sain as in odier places within this your Realme, to their greate fatigation and unquieting and to the pill of their patientes by reason they cannot be conveniently attended; It may therefore pleas your moste excellent Majestie with thassent of your lordis spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent plament assembled and by thauctoride of the same, to enacte ordeyne and stablish that the psident of the said commynaltie and felouship for the tyme being, and the C5mons and fellowes of the same, and e9y fellowe therof that nowe be or at any tyme herafter shalbe, their successours and the successours of e$y of them, at all tyme and tymes afire the making of this Psent acte shalbe discharged to kepe any watche or warde in your said Cittie of London or the suburbes of the same or any parte therof; And that they nor any of them shalbe chosen constable or any other officer in the said Cittie or suburbes: And that if at any tyme herafter the said psident for the tyme being or any of the said Comons or fellowes for the tyme being by any waies or meanes be appointed or ellectid to any watche or warde, office of Constable or any other office within the said Cittie or subburbes [of the same/ ] the same appoinctement or ellection to be utterly voideand of none effecte; any ordre custume or lawe to the contrarie bifore this tyme used in the said Cittie notwithstanding.

CHAPTER XU. Baking of Horsebred*

Recital of State, it R.IT. tt. i. c.8; 4 H. IV. c. at; against Innholders nuking Horsebread:

Innholders in Villages and Towns not corporate, &c. may make Horse-bread.

FRASMUCHE as by occasion that at a plament holden at Westfii in the xfij* yere of the reigne of King Richard the seconde amongest other thinges it was ordeynid and enacted that no hosteler or inholder shulde make any horsbreade within his house nor ellis where, but that the bakers shulde make suche horsebreade, and that thassise therof shulde also be made of reasonnable waight, as by the same acte it may also more plainely appere; And also sithens that at another plament holden at Westfii in the iiij01 yere of the reigne of Kinge Henry the fourth amongest other thinges it was also ordeynid and enacted that if any hosteler or inholder did make any horse breade contrarie to the fourme of the said Statute and acte of Richard the seconde, and the same duely proved against him, the same hosteler or inholder from tyme to tyme shulde forfaite the treple value of all suche horsbreade made by him in his house or ellis where, as by the said acte more plainely also it may appere; diverse and manny incommodities and mischieves haw* ensued therupon to the Kingf subjecds that have travailed and journaied with their horses within the Realme of Englaund ; Be it therefore nowe ordeynid and enacted by thauctohde of this present plament, that from hensfurth it may and shalbe laufull for e9y hosteler or inholder dwelling in any towne or village being a thorough fare or a comon passage within this Realme, and being no Cide towne corporate or fiket towne wherin any cdmon baker exercising thoccupadon of baking and hath ben prentice at the said occupation by the space of vij yeris is [dewelling,1 ] to make within his house horsbreade sufficient laufull and of due assise, according as the price of the graynes of come that nowe is and herafter shalbe from tyme to tyme; any thing or thinges mentioned in the said actes or statutes of King Richarde the seconde or Henry the iiij* to the contrarie notwithstanding.

CHAPTER XLIV.

Thi Parrishe of Royston.

FORASMUCHE as the Towne of Royston is a markett Towne situate and bilded to gither and eztendeth itself into Fyve severall parrishes, wherof never a Parrisshe Churche of them [of them * ] is within twoo myles of the said towne, and some of them be three myles distaunt from the same; by reason wherof the poore inhabitauntis and townesmen there being parrishiners of the said fyve pishe churches divers & sundry tymes thorough the absence of their psonnes and Curates in suche caces of necesside whan their Psence to the comforte and consoladon of their parrisheners is moste requisite and behouffull, cannot have the Sacramends and Sacramentalls to be ministered according to the lawdable custumes of holy church to their greate pillf and jeopardies: And also forasmuche as the said towne of Roiston is a greate and a comon thorough fare for the Kinges subjectis and liege people travayling from many and sundry partes of this Realme, and in the said Towne is also wekely a greate raket wherunco greate and frequent resorte is of all thinhabitauntis of the Countrey therunto adjoyning, and yet the said subjectis so travailing nor anny of thinhabitauntis so resorting canne have anny masse or other divine service in the said towne if their devotion shuld that require ; And over this (9) greate distaunce of the towne from the parrisshe churches aforesaid is verry discommodiouse and painefull to all and singulier thinhabitauntis there and most specially to the impotent [seekely3] and aged people, whiche be not hable to travaill to the said Churches ne anny of them to heare their divine services; All which discommodities and inconvenietf were litle pjudiciall to the saide towne at suche tyme as the late Priory there stode, The churche of which Priory the poore inhabitauntis of the said towne have bought to their greate charges to thintent to have the same their parrish churche and therm to have daily masse and other divine services to be celebrated and done: In consideration of whiche pmisses it may please the Kinges moste roiall Majestie of his moste excellent goodnes, that it may be enacted by his Highnes with thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Cdmons in this psent plament assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that the saide churche late being parcell of the said Pryory of Royston shalbe the parrish churche for all and singulier thinhabitauntis of the said towne of Roiston; And that the said churche shalbe named and called from hensfurth the parrish churche of Sainct John the Baptist in the towne of Roiston and that one pcell of grounde nigh or by the said church shalbe providid and enclosed at the costis and charges of the said inhabitauntis for a cemitory or church yerde for buriallf of Chren people in the same; CHAPTER XLV.

The Court of First firuytf and Tenth.

XYTHERE in die plament holden at Westm the thirde day of Notembre m the xxvj* yere of the reigne of* Vt our most dradde naturall and Souveraigne Liege Lorde Henry tbeight, King of England and of Fraonce defendour of the Faith lorde of Irelaunde and in erth supreme bed of the Churche of Englaund, it was enaedd ordeyntd and established, that the Kinges Highnes his Heires and Successours Kinges of this Realme shulde have and enjoye from tyme to tyme, to endure forever, of evy suche psonne and psoimes, which at any tyme aftre the first day of January than next commyng shulde be nomynated electid prefedid presenrid collated or by any other meanes appoinctid to have any archebishoprich bishopprich abbacye monastery priory college hospitall archedeaconry deanery provostship prebende psonnage vicarege chauntry free chapel, or other dignitie benefice office or promotion squall within this Realme and ellf where within anny the Kinges dominions, of what name nature or qualitie soe9 they were, or to whose foundation patronage or gifte soever they did bilonge, the firste frutes revenues and profittes for one yere of everie suche archebishopprich bishoprich abbacye monastery priory hospitall college archedeaconry deanery provoship pbend psonnage vicarage chauntry free chapell or other dignity benefice office or promotion spuall aforenamed, wherunto anny suche psonne or psonnes shuld aftre the said first day of Januarye be nominated electid prefe&d presenrid collarid or by any other meanes appoinctid; And that every suche psonne and psones, bifore any actuall or reall possession or medling with the profittes of any suche archebishoppriche bishopprich abbacy monastery hospitall deanery provostship prebend psonnage vicarege chauntry free chapell priory or other dignitie benefice office or promotion spuall, shuld satisfy content and pay or compounde or agree to pay to the Kinges use at reasonable daies uppon good suerties the said first frutes and profittes for one yere; And also by the same acte it was further enacted by thauctoritie aforesaid that the Kinges Majestye his Heires and Successours Kinges of this Realme, for more augementadon and maintenance of the roiall astate of his emperiall Crowne and Dignitie of supreme hed of the churche of England shulde yerely have take [and *] enjoye and receyve unytid and knytt to his Imperiall Crowne for ever one yerely rent or penrion amounting to the value of the tenth part of all the revenues rentes fermes tithes offeringes emolumentis, and of all other profittes aswell called spuall as temporall than appertayning or belonging, or that after the making of the said acte shulde bilong, to any archebishoppriche bishopprich abbacy monasterie priory archedeaconry deanery hospitall college house collegiate prebende cathedrall churche collegiate churche conventuall churche psonnage vicarege chauntrey free chapel or other benefice or promotion spuall, of what name nature or qualitie soever they were within any diocesse of this Realme or in Wales; The said pension or annuall rent to be paid yerely forever to our Souverain Lorde his Heires and Successours Kinges of this Realme at the feast of the Nativate of our Lorde God ; as by the same acte amongest divers other thinges therin conteynid, more playnely is shewed and may appere: And for the more suerty and establishment therof, and to thintent that the Kinges Majestie his Heires and Successours shalbe the better served m obteyning the premisses, and also from hensfurth be truely & justly aunswerid contentid and paide yerely of all that whiche to his Highnes his Heires or Successours appertayneth or bilongith, or herafter shall belonge or appertaine by vertue and according to the tenour of the said acte, Be it enacted ordeynid and established by the Kinges Majestie by thassent of his Lordis spuall and temporall and the Comons in this present plament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same in maner and fourme as herafter followith, that is to say; First the King our SouQaine Lorde by thauctoritie aforesaid maketh erectith and establishith a certaine courte cbmonly to be called forever the Court of the First Frutes and Tenth, which Courte by auctoritie aforesaid contynually and forever shalbe a Court of Recorde, and shalhave one seale to be engraven and made after such fourme fashon and maner as shalbe appoincted by the Kinges Highnes, and shall remayne and be ordred as herafter shalbe declarid.

And also be it enacted by auctoritie aforesaide that there shalbe one certaine psonne to be named and assigned by the Kinges Highnes his Heires and Successours whiche shalbe Chauncelour of the same Courte, and shalbe chief and principall officer of the same Courte and shalbe callid the Chauncelour of the first frutes and [tenthes1] and shalhave the keaping of the said seale to be assigned for the said Courte.

And also be it enacted by auctoritie aforesaid that there shalbe one psone to be named and assignid by the Kinges Highnes whiche shalbe called the Kinges Treasorer of the first frutes and tenth. And shalbe the second officer of the same Court; And that there shalbe one psonne to be larned in the lawe of this land to be named and assigned by die Kinges Highnes whiche shalbe the Kinges Attournay of the first frutes and tenth and shalbe die third officer of the same Courte; And that there shalbe twoo psonnes to be named by the Kinges Highnes which shalbe named the Kinges auditours of the first frutes and [tenthis,1] and shalbe officers of the same Court; and that there shalbe one Clerke to be named and assigned by the Kinges Highnes to be Clerke of the same Courte, whiche shall make all bondis writinges and other ordinary processe and entrees out and from the same court; And that there shalbe one other psone to be named and assigned by the Kinges Highnes whiche shalbe called the Mossanger of the said Court; And one other p6onne to be named and assigned by the Kinges Highnes whiche shalbe called the Hussher of the same Court, which messanger and hussher and either of them shalhave suche and like profittes and advantages as the messanger and hussher of the Kinges Duchie Chamber at Westfft have and pceyve. CHAPTER XLVI,

Thb Court of Wardf.

FORaSMUCHE as the Kinges Hlghnes hath ben heretofore and herafter is like to be yerely aunswerid of greate rentis revenues and profittes, which to his Majesde hath or shall growe aswell by reason of suche psonnes as have ben or herafter shalbe in warde to his Highnes, as also by meane of Ideottes and fboles naturall nowe remayning or being or that herafter shall remaine or be in his Graces custody, and also for licences to raary made and to be made to wymen being his Graces widowes and fynes made by them for marry eng without his Highnes licence, All whiche the phnisses of right apptayneth to his Majesty in the right of the Imperial Crowne of this Realme, For the more suerty and establishment wherof, and to thintent the Kinges Majestie his heires and successours shalbe the better served in thobteyning or having of the custody of the bodies of his Highnes wardes and their honours manours landis tenementis and hereditamentis into his Graces custody and govem*nce during the minoritie of suche wardes, And also shalbe yerely aswell truly contentid aunswerid and paid of and for the sales of the bodies of the wardes and the landis bargained for them during the said minoritie and of other the p^mises, as of the rentis fermes issues and profittes rising comyng and grotying or which herafter shall rise come or growe of all and singulier the castellf manors landis tenementis and other hereditamentis belonging and whiche herafter shall rise & belong to the King his heires and successours by reason of the said wardis and other die pmisses, in suche court place maner founne and condition as herafter shalbe lymited declarid and appoinctid; Be it enactid ordeynid and establishid by thassent of the Kinges Majesty his Lordes squall and temporall and the Comons in this psent plament assemblid and by auctoride of the same in maner and fourme as herafter followith in articles, that is to say: First the King our Souvain Lorde by thauctoritie aforesaid ordeynith maketh establishith and ereedth a certayne Courte comonly to be callid for ever the Courte of the Kinges Wardis, which Court by thauctoritie aforesaid contynually and for ever shalbe a Courte of Recorde, and shalhave one seale to be engraven and made after suche fourme fashon and maner as shalbe appoinedd by the Kinges Highnes, and shall remaine and be ordred as herafter shall be declarid.

[And1] also be it enaedd by thauctoritie aforesaid that there shalbe one certaine psonne to be named and assigned by the Kingf Highnes his heires and successours which shalbe Maister of the same Court, and shalbe chief and prindpall officer of the same Court and shalbe called the Maister of the Wardis and shalhave die keping of the said seall to be assigned for the said Court.

Also be it enactid by thauctoritie aforesaid, that there shalbe one psonne to be laraid in the lawes of this land to be named and assigned by the Kinges Highnes whiche shall be callid the Kinges Attoumay of the said Court, and shalbe the second officer of the same Court.

Also be it enactid by thauctoritie aforesaid, that there shalbe one psonne to be named and assignid by the Kinges Highnes whiche shalbe callid the Kinges Receyvour Generali of the landis of his wardis, and shalbe the thirde officer of the same Court.

Also be it enactid by thauctoritie aforesaid, that there shalbe twoo psonnes to be named by the Kinges Highnes which shalbe callid the Auditors of the landf of his Graces wardis, and shalbe callid the fourth officer of the same Court.

Also be it enactid by thauctoritie aforesaid, that there shalbe twoo Clerkis to be named and assignid by the Kinges Highnes to be Clerkis of the said Court, which shall make all indeniurf bargaines and leasis to be made and grauntid of the Kinges wardis landis, recorde all apparaunces, and make all ordinary processe and entrees out and from the same Court.

Also be it enactid by thauctoritie aforesaid that there shalbe one other psonne to be named and assignid by the Kinges Highnes which shalbe the Messanger of the said Court, another psonne to be named and assignid by the Kinges Highnes which shalbe callid the Hussher of the same Court, whiche said messanger and hussher and either of them shalhave suche and like profittes and advantages as the messanger and hussher of the Kinges Duchy chamber at Westfft have and pceyve: Also the said Maister of the Kinges wardis whiche shalbe appoinctid by the Kinges Highnes shall take a corporal I othe afore the Lord Chauncelour of England for the tyme being after the tenour ensueyng; Te shall swere that ye well and truely shall serve the King in thoffice of Maister of the Kinges Wardis, and shall ministre egall Justice to riche and [power1] to the best of your conning witt and power, And that ye shall diligently procure all thinges which may honestly and justely be to the Kinges advantage and profitt, and to thaugementation of the rightis and prerogatives of the Crowne and truely use the Kinges seale appoinctid to your office, and also endevoir yourself to thuttermost of your power [and 1 ] to se the King truely and justelye aunswerid yerely of all suche rentis revenues issues and profittis whiche shall or may arrise growe or be due to the King in your office, and from tyme to tyme deliver with spede suche as shalhave to doo afore you; And that ye shall not take nor receyve of anny psonne anny gifte or rewarde in any cace or matier depending bifore you or wherin the Kinges Highnes shalbe partie whereby any prejudice losse hinderaunce or disherison shall growe or be to the Kinges Highnes: So helpe you God and all Sainctes. Also the said Attoumay shall take a corporall othe bifore the said Maister of the wardis according to the tenour ensuring; Ye shall swere that ye well and truely shall serve the King as his attoumay in all Courtis for and concerning any matier or cause that shall conceme or touch the possessions and hereditamentis lymitid to the survey and governance of this Court, and procure the Kinges profitt therof. And that ye shall truely counsell the King and the Maister of this Court in all thinges concerning the same to the best of your connyng witt and power.

CHAPTER L. (’) The Bill for the Subsydy.

Motives for the proposed Subsidy;

THE Kingf most lovinge subjectf in this present Parliament assembled, lovynglye calling to their rememberaunce the innumerable benefitf and goodnes, which thei alweis have founde in the Kingf moste royall Majestie, iheir naturall and moste dradde Sovereigne Lorde, reynyng over them the space of xxxju yeres full and more, duryng the whiche they have welthilye lyved, and prosperouslye contynued undre his Majestie well defended governed and maynteyned from and ayenst all maner of enemyes, to their no lytle suretye welthe quyet and reste; Hou his Highnes also by the inestymable grace that God hath gyven him, and his onlye high prudence wysdome and studye, hath brought his said true subjectf out of all blyndnes & ignoraunce into the true and pfecte knowledge of Almyghtye God, by his moste holye worde; The abolysshing also of the Bishop of Rome and his usurped auctoritie, by whose subtyll imagina&o practyse inven£6ns and devises exceding somes of moneye have wounte daylye and yerelye to be conveyed out of this Realme, for payment of Bisshops Bulles Breves and Dispensations, and the moneye commonlye called Peterpence, with untrue and fayned pardons, by the whiche and dyverse other lyke, and the gatherers of the same, being no smalle numbre (speciallye of pdoners) the Kingf loving subjectf have bene greadye heretofore disceyved spoyled and hindered, wherof by his Pryncelye polide and wisedome thei be delyvered and lawfullye discharged; Consideryng also the exceading great costes charges and expencf that his Highnes hath susteyned in and aboute the repression of the great late rebellion in Lincolneshire, and the North partes of this Realme; what yerelye costf and chargf also his Majesde is at, and of longe time hath bene, for and aboute the stablisshing of three Presidentf and discreat severall Counsailes, as well in the Marches of Wales, and the Shires therunto adjoynyng, as in the North and Weste pries of this Realme, By reason wherof, his true subjectf poor and riche, without trade of tyme or any greate charges or expenses, have undelayed Justyce daylye admistred unto them; CHAPTER VH.

An Acts conceminge conveyaunce of Brasse Latten & Bell Mettell over the Sea.

WHERE in the Parliament holden at Westfii the third daye of November in the xxjth Yere of the Raigne of our Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge that nowe ys, amongest other thingf it was enacted, that noe pson or psons shoulde from thenceforthe carrye or convey any Brasse Copper Laten Bell Mettall Gunemettall ne Shroflfe Metal into anye parte or part? beyonde the Sea, upon payne of forfeyture of the saide mettall, as by the saide Acte more playnely appeareth : Synce the makinge of whiche Estatute d$se pson3 aswell Englishmen as Straungers have deceipte-fiillye obteyned lycences of the King? Heighnes to carrie over Belmettall and other broken mettall $ surmysinge the same mettall? not to be mete for makinge of Gunes and other Engyns of Warre, nor for ymplementf necessarie for household, whiche surmyse is pved untrue as the comon experience therof day lye declareth, so that all other Realmes and Countries be full of Artillarie and munycons, and this Realme ys lyke to lack yf more hastye remedye to stoppe the conveyaunce of the same be not further pvided then is in the same Acte; Wherefore maye it please the Kinges Highnes and the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comons in this psent parliament assembled and by thauctoritie of the same to enacte, that noe pson or psons from henceforthe shall carie or convey by Water or otherwise any Brasse Copper Latten Belmettall Pann Mettall Gunemettall nor Shroflfe metal whether it be clene or mixed, Tynne and Lead onely excepted, into any parte beyonde the Sea, or into anye outwarde Realme or I>nion whatsoever it be ; upon payne to forfeyt the double value of the same mettall so carried and conveyed, the one halfe thereof to be to the Kinge our Soveraigne Lorde and thother to the partie that will sue for the same by Writt Bill Piaynt or Information in the w* no essoyne or ptectiin shalbe allowed.

And further be it enacted by thauctoritie aforesaide, for the true meanynge of this Estatute, that the arrivale dischardge and deliverie of the saide mettall? in anye part? beyonde the Sea or in any other forren Realme or I>nion shalbe tried and determyned within this Realme, in suche Countye or Place where the saide mettall or mettall? were shipped or first carried, with like pees & determynatiOn as all other Informations or [actiOn to be'] tried & adjudged within this Realme or as the same fact had bene done within this Realme and Domynion.

An Acte for Mayntenance of Artyllarie and debarringe of unlauful Games.

An Acte for Worsted Yarae in Norffolke.

CHAPTER XVDI An Acte for true makinge of Kersies.

'TTrTHERE at [the1 ] Parliament holden at London [ in * ] the thirde day of November in the one and twentieth yere tv of our moste dread Soveraigne Lorde the Kinges most gracious raigne that nowe ys, and from thence adjourned to Westa and there contynued by sundrie proga£6ns unto the fourth daye of Februarie in the xxviju yere of his [Graces saide* ] raigne. And in case upon any suche profe to be made by any buyer of them at the water there sholde be founde lesse and smaller content in lenghe then sholde be conteyned and spified in everie of the saide seales, that then everie suche clothier makinge suche defoulte sholde lose and forfeyte unto everie suche buyer of the same the double value of so muche clothe as sholde want or lacke of his saide content in lenghe, at the onely sight and judgment of any two indifferent peons that sholde measure the saide Clothes and Karseyes: And furthermore it was enacted by the saide acte that everie kersey so to be putto sale sholde conteyne in breadeth one yarde within the liate, upon due profe thereof to be tried by the water, upon peyne to forfeyte for everie suche kersey lacking of the saide content in bredth twenty pencf, as by the same acte amongest other thingf therm conteyned more at large it exffesed and may appere: Whiche saide acte yf it sholde be putt in execution sholde not onelye growe and be to the great losses and decaye of the Kingf Highnes Customes, but also to the great hindraunce hurte and ympoverishment of the Kingei lovinge and obedient subjectf, anji specially of those inhabitinge within the" Counties of Berk Suthf Oxfordeshire Surrey Sussex and -Yorkeshire, where there are a great nomber of course kerseyes made beinge of the value of thirde shillingf the pece or thereaboutf, whiche kerseys are made of course wooll and are comonlye solde for twenty pence or xxij d. the yarde coloured, of whiche course sorte of kerseyes there are comonly made in the saide Counties fyve hundred againste one fyne kersey, by the makinge and workinge whereof a great nomber of the Kingf subjectf are sett a worke and gett their livingf, whiche course kerseyes are uttered unto the forr partf beyond the sea and fewe or none uttered in this Realme, and have not been used sithe the remembrance of man to be made of suche content in bredith as ys lymitted in the said estatute; any Acte or Actf to the confrie made notwithstandinge: And by the same Acte it was further enacted, that yf any peon or peons did send or convey, or cause to be sente or conveyed into the partes beyond the £ea, any white Wollen Clothe above the value of fewer pounde, or any coloured Clothe above the price of thre pounde, unrowed unbarbed and unshorne in other fourme than ys above meneftned, that then the pson or psons so offendinge shall ferfeyte the value of the saide Clothes so carried and conveyed into the Partf beyond the Sea, the one moytie of the same forfeiture to be to the use of our saide Soveraigne Lorde the Kinge, and thother moytie to any pson whiche will or shall sue by Bill Writ or otherwise againste any pson for the same, and the Defendaunte in any Plea upon anye suche suyte or ac£&n be not admytted to wage his lawe, nor any ptecc&n or essoyne for any suche Defendaunt be allowed in the same, as by the same Acte more playnlye appereth: Upon the inter p>ta£6n and expoundinge of certen wordes within the said Acte di^sitie of opynions [hathe1 ] risen amongest some p6ons, that if any pson or psons sende or convey or cause to be sent or conveyed towardes the partes of beyonde the Sea any white Wollen Clothe above the value of fewer pounde, or any coloured Clothe above the value of thre poundf, unrowed unbarbed or unshome, whether the same Clothe so sent or the value thereof be forfeited, before the same Clothe be carried and conveyed into the Partf of beyond the Sea; For a playne declarac&n of the pmisses, be it ordeyned and enacted by thauctoritie of this pfeent Parliament, that noe pson or psons from henceforth shall carrie or shippe, or cause to be shipped in any Shippe Bote Craye or Vessell, any white Wollen Clothe above the value of foure poundf, or anye coloured Clothe above the value of thre poundf, unrowed unbarbed or unshome, to thintent to be conveyed into the parties beyonde the Sea, upon payne of forfeyture of the same Clothe or Clothes or the value thereof, the same forfeiture to be recovered in suche manner and fourme as ys above mencioned.

CHAPTER XXIX. (’)

The Bill for to enhable psons late Religious suppressed to sue & and to be sued, &c.

WHERE in the Parliamente holden at Westm the xxviij*1 daie of Aprill in the xxxjrt Yere of the reign of o' So$augn Lorde Henry the eight by the grace of God Kynge of England Fraunce and Ireland defendo' of the faith and of the Churche of England and also of Irland in yerthe the supme hed, it was and is ordeyned and enacted by auctority of the said pliamente, that all and synguler suche religious persons aswell men as women professed, of what ordre rule or habit soever they were, which then were or aftre that tyme shulde be put at their libties from the daunger fyytude and condicbn of their religion and profession wherunto they were professed, by reason of suppression dissolving forfaiture by atteyndre rendrynge or otherwise gevyng to the handf of the Kingf Majestie theire houses monasteries and possessions, shuld by auctoritie of the said pliamente, from and after the first daie of the same pliamente and from and aftre the tyme that they were or shuld be put at suche libertie, have free libertie to purches to them and to theire heire6, in fee symple fee taile for terme of life for yeres or at Will, Manors landes tentf rentf annuyties and other hereditamentf and thinges whatsoeP they were, in like maner and forme as though they or any of them, had never ben professed nor entred into any suche religion; and that the same religious psons and e9y of them by auctoritie of the seid Acte of pliamente, shulde be able to sue and to be sued in almaner of actions pleyntes and sutes whatsoever they were, of and for any mater or cause growen sithens and aftre the tyme of their sev^all deraingmentf or dep*ynge out of theire religion, in all co'tes places and jurisdictions w*in this Realme of Englande, as other the Kinges subjectes were; and that they and every of them shulde and myght from that tyme use and exercise receyve take have and enjoie all and every lawfull thynge & thyngf, from thensforth to be growen fallen or happened unto them or any of them aftre the said deraingmente or departynge out of their Religion, in as large and ample maner forme and condicon as if they had never ben professed nor entred into Religion, the same profession or religion or any lawe custom or use w*in the said Realme of England to the contrary therof in any wise notw'stondinge; as by the said Acte amonge other Articles Clauses and Provisoes more plainely apperith: And forasmuch as dy9s ambiguyties and doubtes daily doo arise whether the said Acte extende unto suche late religious psons as were in dyvers late religious Houses and Monasteries, which by the Kingf Highnes were ymmediatly transposed and translated from theire religion and olde Corpora£6n into a newe Corporacbn, and never came and remeyned in his gracious handes neither by suppression dissolvynge forfaiture by atteyndre ne suche like accordyng to the wordes of the said forfi acte; In avoidyng of whiche said ambiguyties and doubtes, be it nowe ordeyned and enacted by the Kynge our Sovaigne Lorde and the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Comens of this presente pliamente assembled and by auctoritie of the same, that the said acte of pliamente above remembred made in the said xxxjtl yere, shall extende aswell to all suche persons whiche be livynge, that were religious psons in any of the said houses, whiche were so translated and transposed from one corporacbn into another, which at any tyme was professed or were religious psons in any of the said houses w*in this Realme of England, and that they and every of them, from the tyme of their said sePall deraigmente and discharge of their said professions and religions, shalbe in like qualitie estate condicbn and degree, and also shall take have and enjoie like benefite comoditie proffit and advauntage, and w* like provyso onely and not otherwise to every entente and in e9y thynge, as any other religious person or psons, may and shall have take and enjoie by vertue of the said former acte above remembred; the same profession or religion, or any lawe custome or use to the contrary therof in any wise notwithstondinge.

A Bill for the previlegis of Kingstowne uppon Hull.

FORASMUCHE as the Kingf towne uppon Hull is sytuate and buylded in length uppon the haven of the saide Towne of the parte of the Easte, and uppon the Water of Humbre of the parte of the Southe, and for the savegarde tffyettn & defence of the same the saide Towne is compassed and enclosed with greate walls dyches and bankes from the SfUth Easte ende of the saide havyn, aswell towardf Humbre as of the West and of the Northe unto the North end of the saide havyn; CHAPTER I.

An Acte for thadvauncement of true Religion and for thabbolisshment of the contraries

"TX THERE the Kinges moste royall Majesde our gracious and naturall Soveraigne liege Lorde supreame head of the V v Churche of Englande and allso of Irelande, and his honorable Counsaill, pceyveth the ignoraunce fonde opynions errours and blindenes of divers and soondrye his Subjectf of this his Realme, in abusing and not ob/ving nor folOwing the commaundementf preceptf and lawes of Almightie God nor the verye true and pfecte religion of Christy notwithstanding suche holesome doctrynes and documentf as his Mau hathe heretofore caused to be set fbrthe for that purpose, besydes the greate libertie graunted to them in having amonges them and in theyre handes the Newe and Olde Testament, whiche notwithstanding, many sedicious people arrogant and ignoraunt psones, wherof soome pretending to be learned and to have the pfite and true knowledge undrestanding and judgement of the sacred and holye Scriptures, and soome others of theyre pverse frowarde and malicious myndes willes and intentf intending to subverte the veraye true and pfecte exposic&n doctryne and declaracon of the saide Scripture, after theyre pvers fantasies, have taken upon them not oonelie to preache teache declare and set foorthe the same by woordf sermons disputae&ns and argumentf, but allso by printed bokes printed balades playes rymes songes and other fantasies, subtellye and craftelye instructing his Hieghnes people and speciallye the youthe of this his Realme, untruelie and otherwyse thanne the scripture ought or shoulde be taught declared or expounded, and contrarye to the veraye sincere and godlye meaning of the same, wherupon diversitie of opinions sayengf variauncf argumentf tumultf and scismes have been sprung and arisen among his saide Subjectf within this his Realme, to the greate inquietad&n of his saide people and greate displeas' of his Majesde, and contrarye to his Graces true meaning good inteneftn and moste godlie purpose: For rbforma£5n wherof his Majesde mott vertuouslye and prudentlye considered and thinketh, that it is and shalbe moste requysite expedient and necessarye not oonelie by lawes dredfull and penall to take awaie purge and dense this his Highnes Realme terrytoryes confynes domynions and Countreys, of all suche bokes wrydngf sermons disputacons argumentf balades playes rymes songes teachingf and instrucf&ns, as be pestiferous and noysoome with all the causes and instrumentf [and * ] meanes of the same, but allso to ordeyne and establisshe a certaine forme of pure and sincere teaching, agreable with Goddf woorde and the true doctryne of the catholicke and apostolical! Churche, wherunto men maye have recourse for the true decysion of soome such contraversies as have in tymes past and yet doo happen and aryse amongf them: And therfor be it enacted ordeyned and establisshed by our saide Soveraigne Lorde the King, the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Commons in this pnt parliament assembled and by thauctory tie of the same, that all maner of bokes of the Olde and Newe Testament in Englishe, being of the craftye false and untrue translac&n of Tyndale, and all other booke6 and wrydngf in the English tongue teaching or comprysing any matiers of Christen religion articles of the faithe or holye scripture, or any parte of them, contrarye to that doctryne whiche sithens the yere of our Lorde a thousande fyve hundred and fourtie is or at any tyme during the Kinges Majesties lief our saide Soveraigne Lorde that now is King Henrye theight, whiche our Lorde long preserve, shalbe set foorthe by his Hieghnes with suche supscripcon and subscripcftn as hereafter shalbe declared, shalbe by auctorytie of this pnt Acte clerelie and utterlie abolished extinguished and forbidden to be kepfe or used in this Realme or elswhere [within3 ] any the Kingf Domynions.

And where the Kinges Majestie of his moste gracious and blessed disposictiOn hathe heretofore caused to be set foorthe the Byble and New Testament in the Englishe tongue to be reade by his loving Subjectf, to thintent that they might therbye the better knowe theyre duede to Almightie God and to his Majestie, and allso. increase in vertue for the wealthe of theyre soules, albeit his Majesties saide moste godlye purpose and intent hathe taken good effecte emonges a greate multytude of his subjectf, and spedallie amonges the highest and moste honest sorte, according to his Hieghnes good expectation therof, yet forasmuche as his Hieghnes pceyveth that a greate multitude of his saide subjectf, moste spSallie of the lower sorte have so abused the same, that they have therbye growen and increased in divers naughde and erronyous opynions, and by occasion therof fallen into greate dyvision and discencon amonges themselves, to the greate unquietnes of the Realme and other his Majesties Domynions: For Remedye wherof be it enacted by thauctoryde aforesaide, that frome and after the firste daie of Julye next cooming, no woomen nor artificers prendses journeymen serving men of the degrees of yeomen or undre, husbandemen nor laborers shall reade within this Realme or in any other the Kingf Domynions, the Byble or Newe Testament in Englishe, to himselfe or (*) any other pryvatelie or openKe, upon paine of oone monethes imprysonement for every tyme [so * ] offending contrarye to this Acte and being therof convicte in suche maner and forme as is aforesaide; oonelesse the Kingf Majestie our saide Soveraigne Lorde King Henrye theight pceyving such reformacon and amendement in theyre lyeves and behavour, by the diligent and discrete reading and impryndng in theyre hartes of the moste blessed doctryne set foorthe or hereafter to be set foorthe by his saide Majestie, shall of his elemeneye thinke good, otherwyse to enlardge and give libertie for the reading of the same.

CHAPTER Vffl.

An Acte that persones being no coen Surgeons maie mynistre medicines owtwarde.

WHERE in the parliament holden at West® in the thirde yere of the Kingf moste gracious reigne, amongew other thinges for the advoyding of sorceryes witchecrafte and other inconveniences, it was enacted, that no p6ooe within the Citie of London, nor within seven myles of the same, shoulde take upon him to exercyse and occupie as Phisidan or Surgeon, except he be first examyned approved and admytted by the Bisshopp of London and other, undre and upon certaine peynes and penalties in the same Acte mentioned; Sithens the making of whiche saide Acte the Companie and Felowship of Surgeons of London, mynding oonelie theyre owne lucres, and nothing the profite or ease of the diseased or patient, have sued troubled and vexed divers honest psones aswell men as woomen, whome God bathe endued with the knowledge of the nature kinde and opera£6n of certeyne herbes rotes and waters, and the »*«ng and mynistering of them to suche as been pained with customable diseases, as Womens brestes being sore, a Pyn and the Web in the eye, uncoomes of handf scaldingf bumingf sore mouthes the stone strangurye saucelin and morfew, and suche other lyke diseases, and yet the saide psones have not takin any thing for theyre peynes and cooninng, but have mynistred the same to die poore people oonelie for neighbourhode and Goddes sake and of pitie and charytie; and it is nowe well knowen that the surgeons admytted wooll doo no cure to any psone, but where they shall knowe to be rewarded with a greater soome or rewarde than the cure extendeth unto, for in cace they wolde mynistre theyre coonning to sore people unrewarded, there shoulde not so manye rotte and perishe to deathe for lacke of helpe of Surgerye as dailie doo, but the greatest parte of Surgeons admytted been muche more to be blamed than those peooes that they trouble, for althonghe the most parte of the psones of the saide crafte of Surgeons have small cooning, yet they wooll take greate soomes of money and doo litle therfore, and by reasone therof they doo often tymes impaire and hurte theyre padentf rather thenne doo them good : In considexac&n wherof and for the ease comforte socour helpe relief and healthe of the Kingf poore Subjectf inhabytauntf of this his Realme, nowe peyned or diseased, or that hereafter shalbe peyned or diseased, Be it ordeyned establisshed and enacted by thauctorytie of this pnt parliament, that at all tymes from hensforthe, it shalbe lefull to everye psone being the Kingf Subject having knowledge and experience of the nature of herbes rotes and waters or of the operaeftn of the same by speculac&n or practyse, within any parte of the Realme of Englande, or within any other the Kingf Domynions, to practyse use and mynistre in and to any outwarde sore uncoom wounde appostemaebns outwarde swelling or disease, any herbe or herbes oyntementf bathes pultes and emplasters, according to theyre cooning experience and knowlege in any of the diseases sores and maladies aforesaide and all other lyke to the same, or drinkes for the stone strangurye or agues, without sute vexaefa trouble penaltie or losse of theyre goodf • The foresaide Statute in the foresaide thirde yere of the Kingf most gracious reigne, or any other Acte ordinance or statute to the contrarye hereof heretofore made in any wise notwithstanding.

CHAPTER X.

An Acte for the true making of Coverlettf in Yorke.

XX THE RE AS the Cide of Yorke being oone of the aundent and greatest Cities within the Realme of Englande, v v afore this tyme hathe been mainteyned and upholden by divers and sundrye handye craftes there used, and moste prindpallye by making and weaving of coverlettf and coveringf for Beddes, and therebye a greate nombre of thinhabytauntf and poore people of the saide Cide, suburbes therof, and other places within the Counde of Yorke, hare been dailie set on woorke in spynning carding dyeng weaving and otherwyse concerning the making of them, to the greate commodyde of the inhabytauntf and poore people of the saide Cide, having therebye honest lyvingf, and not made elswhere in anye parte of the same Counde, for the true substanciall and pfecte making [therof *] manye good and beneficiall ordnances and orders have been devised and made aswell for the good Stuf concerning the saide Coverlettf and coveringf, as allso for the lengthe and breadeth of them and otherwyse; of the whiche Coverlettf and coveringf the best sorte shoulde and ought by the same Ordnances to conteyne in length three Yardes, and in bredthe twoo Yardf and a quarter at the leaste. An Acte for the true making of Frises and Cottens in Wales.

FORA3MUCHE as thinhabytauntes clothemakers that [dwell1] within the Townes and Boroughes of Caermerthin Shyre Cardigan Shyre and Pembroke Shyre, have used in tymes paste to make theyre clothe called Welshe fryse, and cotton called Welshe cotton, to the greate profite of all the Kinges subjectes of this Realme, that is to saie; everye pece called a hiegh fryse rawe shulde be made of liiij pounde (J) yarne and shoulde conteyne in lengthe xlvj Yardes, and in breadethe oone Yarde oone quarter, and everye haulf pece highe fryse shoulde waie xxvij pounde and conteyne in length xxiij Yardes rawe, and in bredeth oone Yarde oone quarter and that everye pece cotton shoulde waye being rawe, lxviij pounde of haberdepoyse and [conteyne3] in lengthe xlviij Yardes, and in breadeth fyve quarters oone nael, without any strayning; and that everye haulf pece cotton shoulde waie xxxiiij pounde and conteyne in lengthe xxiiij Yardf, and in bredthe fyve quarters and oone nael; whiche true and good making of fryses and cottons hathe been of long time decayed and extinguisshed and yet is, to the greate decaie and ruyne of all the saide townes and boroughes and allso to the greate sclaunder and hinderaunce of all good true clothiers inhabydng within the same, and also to the greate hurte and prejudice of all the Kinges subjectf whiche doo bye the same; and the principal grounde and occasion therof is, that the Clothiers Tuckers Weavers and suche other that weare wonte to inhabyte within the saide townes and boroughes, and there to make true fryses and cottons bothe in lengthe and breadeth, bee nowe coome foreyners husbandemen and grasiers dwelling in the countrey, out of the saide townes of Caermerthin Cardigan and Pembroke and other boroughe townes aforesaide and there do make theyre owne wooll in fryses and cottons after the moste false and deceytefull maner that maie be, and the same doo carye from place to place to be solde to the greate disceyte and hinderaunce of all the Kinges loving Subjectf, and to the greate sclaunder of all true clothe makers within all the saide townes and boroughes: For reamedie and reformac6n wherof, be it enacted by the King our Soveraigne Lorde the Lordf sjSuall and temporall and the Commons in this pnt parliament assembled and by auctorytie of the same, that after the firste daie of June next cooming, whiche shalbe in the Yere of our Lorde God a thousande fyve hundred fourde and three, no maner of psone (4) make any rawe fryses called Welshe fryse, or any cottons called Welshe cottons, to be solde in any faire [or5] merket or elswhere in any other place, ooneles every pece fryse called ahieghe fryse rawe be made of cleane wooll without floxe or throome waying in Yarne liiij pounde of haberdepoyse at the leaste, and conteyning in lengthe xlvj yardf rawe and in breadethe oone yarde oone quarter, and that everye haulf pece fryse hieghe shall waye xxvij ti. and conteyne in lengthe xxiij yardf and in breadethe oone yarde oone quarter; and that everye pece cotton rawe shall waie lxviij pounde of Yarne at the leaste without floxe or throome and conteyne in lengthe xlviij Yardf and in breadeth oone Yarde oone quarter and oone nael; And that everye haife pece cotton shall waie xxxiiij pounde of Yarne without floxe or throome and conteyne in length xxiiij Yardf and in breadeth fyve quarters and oone nael; upon peyne to forfaicte everye pece and haulf pece fryse, and everye pece cotton and haulf pece cotton so put to sale contrarye to the true meaning intent and purpose of this pnt Acte, the oone haulf of whiche forfaicture to be to the King our Soveraigne Lorde and thother haulf to him and them that will sue for the same in any of the Kingf courtes, wherin no essoine wager of lawe nor protection shalbe allowed.

(6) Provided allwaie that this Acte shall take effecte after the feste of the Purification of our Ladye next cooming and not before.

CHAPTER XVm.

An Acte for Caunterburye concerning the Privileges of the same.

YY THERE the Citie of Caunterburie is and of auncyent tyme hathe been a Citie incorporate, and endowed with VV divers and many ample Privileges and Frauncheses, by divers and soondrie Charters and grauntf heretofore made by the Kinges noble progenitoures, aswell in the tyme of the Prince of famous memorye King Henrye the vjth as in the tyme of other his noble progenitoures, wherby the same Citie ought to have use and enjoye all the saide liberties privileges and frauncheses, according to the tenour [force *] p'porte and effecte of all suche of the saide Charters and Grauntf heretofore graunted and made unto the Mayre and Citizens of the saide Citie, as remaine and stande yet in full strengthe and force; yet divers ambiguous questions and varietie of opynions of divers psones learned in the Lawe of the Realme be of late rysen and growne of the validitie purporte and force of divers articles conteyned in the saide Charters and Grauntf, by cause that soome wcordf comprysed in the same seme to them obscure ambiguous and doutefall, where indede the true intent and meaning therof to the moste parte of men learned in the Lawes of the Realme dothe right well appeare to be plaine; by reason wherof not oonelie the good civile polide of the saide Citie is moche decaied but allso the welthye occupyeng, the populous inhabyting, and the beautifull building therof, be lyke to coome in greate ruyne depopulation and decaie, not a little to the extenua&n of that parte of this Realme aswell in the eyes of all Straungers, as in the eyes of suche greate psonages as shall happen to have repaire to the Kingf Majestie in Ambassade or otherwyse: In consideration wherof be it enacted by the Kinges Hieghnes with thassent of the Lordf spuall and temporall and the Commons in this pnt Parliament assembled and by thauctorytie of the same, that the Mayre and Aldremen or the more part of them of the saide Citie and theyre Successoures, by suche name or names as they be Incorporate, shall have use and enjoye all suche Liberties frauncheses and privileges, within the Lymites precincte and jurisdiction of the saide Citie, whiche they or theyre predecessoures Maires and Aldremen of the [saide1] Citie have had to them graunted by the Kinges Hieghnes or any of his noble progenitoures by his or theyre ires patentf undre the Greate Seall of Englande, nowe remayning in full strengthe and force, according to the true purporte and effecte of the same ires patentf and grauntf heretofore had and made unto the saide Maire and Aldremen of the saide Citie as is aforesaide, notwithstanding they have not been of late tyme used nor put in Execution accordinglie.

And be it further enacted by thauctorytie aforesaide, that it shalbe lawfull to all and everye psone and psones Citizens inhabyting within the saide Citie or liberties or the precincte therof, to take a prentyse or prentyses by Indentures entercheangeable sealed with the Seales of suche Parties for the terme of seven yeres or lesse, as bothe the parties canne agree, albeit suche Apprentyse or Apprentyses be within thage of xxjlie yeres; and that the same Indentures of Apprentysehode shall comprehende lyke Coven*ntf and be made written and enrolled in lyke maner and forme as is cdmonlie used in suche caces within the Citie of London; and the same Indentures comprysing suche couven*ntf made wryten and enrolled as is aforesaide shalbe firomhensforthe good and effectual! in the lawe, againste everye suche Apprentyse to all intentf constructions and purposes. The mynorytie of suche Apprentyses, the Statute made in the vij01 yere of (3) King Henrye the Fourthe concerning Apprentyses, or any other Statute lawe custome or usage concerning taking of Apprentyses, to the contrarye notwithstanding.

Be it allso enacted by thauctorytie aforesaide, that no psone or psones, being foreynes and not being free Citizens of the saide Citie of Canterburye, shall not firomhensforthe contrarie to the Libertie and Grauntf heretofore had and made unto the Mayre and Aldremen of the saide Citie, by or sell anye maner of Merchaundyse to or with anye maner of persone or psones foreines, and not being free Citizens of the saide Citie, nor keape anye open Shoppe nor use any Mysterye or Handycrafte within the same Citie Liberties and Precincte therof, without the special Licence of the saide Maire and Aldremen or the more pte of them, in wryting undre theyre Seall, upon peyne to forfaicte for everye suche Offence to the saide Maire and Aldremen to the use of the saide Citie vj s. viij d. of lawfull money of Englande: And that the Maire and Aldremen of the same Citie and theyre Successoures for the tyme being, froine tyme to tyme shall have power apd auctorytie to demaunde and aske againste everye suche Offendo', in the Courte Hall of the saide Citie, by ActiOn or Plainte of Dette the saide forfaicture, or at theyre liberties shall take levie and pceyve 'by Distresse the saide Penalties or Forfeitures, to the use of the saide Citie by and according to the course of the Common Lawe.

Provided allwaies that this Acte nor any thing therin conteyned, shall extende or be prejudiciall to the Kinges Majestie his heyres or successoures, but that it shalbe laufull to our saide Soveraigne Lorde his heyres and successoures, from tyme to tyme to sgise or resume any of the saide Frauncheses liberties or priviledges, heretofore graunted by any of his progenitoures and confirmed by this pnt Acte, for any sufficient cause of forfeiture by the lawe of this Realme; Any Clause or Article in this Acte conteyned to the contrary notwithstanding.

Provided allso that this Acte or any thing therin conteyned shall not in any wise extende to the palace of the most reverende father in God Thomas nowe Archebisshopp of Caunterburye, or to the Hamlet of Stablegate, or to the scyte and procincte of the Cathedrall and Metropolitane Churche of Christe in Caunterburye aforesaide, nor to any other place whatsoever immediatelie before the making of this Acte being out of the libertie of the saide Citie of Caunterburye; nor in any wise shalbe prejudiciall or hurtefull to the saide Archebisshopp or any of his Successoures, or to the Deane and Chapitre of the saide Cathedrall and Metropolitane Churche of Christe in Caunterburye or to anye of theyre Successoures; Any thing in the same Acte notwithstanding.

CHAPTER XXII.

An Acte that fynes in Townes corparate shalbe made as the same have been in tymes past.

WHERE in the parliament holden the [xxvijlh 4] yere of our moste dreade Soveraigne Lorde Kinge Henrye theight, it was enacted by auctorytie of the saide parliament, amonges other, that no fyne feoffment or other Acte or Actes hereafter to be made suffred or doone by the husbande oonelie, of manoures landf tenementf or hereditamentf being the inherytaunce or the freholde of his Wief, during the coverture betwene them, shall in any wyse be or make any discontynuaunce therof or be prejudiciall or hurtefull to the saide Wief or to her heyres, or to suche as shall have right tytle or interest [bythe same, by the deathe of suche wief or wieves, but the same wief and her heyres and suche other to whome suche right shall appteyne after her deceasse, shall and maie thenne lawfullie entre into all suche Manoures landes tenementf and hereditamentf according to theyre rightes and titles therin, Any suche fyne feoffement or other Acte to the contrarie notwithstanding (6); Sithens the making of whiche Acte, divers doubtes questions and ambiguyties have rysen. That is to saie, whether the recoveries and dedes enrolled whiche be in nature of fynes, and wherupon Woomen coverte have been used to be examyned, taken had or knowledged as well within the Citie cf London as in manye other Cities boroughes and townes within the Realme of Englande, shoulde bynde all suche woomen covert that shoulde happen to be examyned upon the same recoveries and dedes enrolled; In advoyding therfore of all suche ambiguities and doubtes. Be it enacted by the King our Soveraigne Lorde the Lordf spuall and temporall and the Commons in this pnt parliament assembled and by auctorytie of the same, that all recoveries dedes enrolled and releasses heretofore knowledged and taken, or at any tyme hereafter to be taken and knowledged, before the Maires Aldremen Recorders Chamberlaines or other Heade Officer or Officers, aswell of the Citie of London as of any other Citie boroughe or towne corporate within the Realme of Englande, having power and auctorytie to take and receyve the same, according to the laudable usages and customes of the saide Cities boroughes and townes and everye of them, shall stande and remaine of lyke force strengthe and effecte to all intentf and purposes as they or any of them weare before the making of the saide Acte in the saide xxxij* yere of our saide Soveraigne Lorde$ Any thing in the same Acte conteyned to the contrarye in any wyse notwithstanding.

An Acte for thedifica£6n of a Windemyll and a Conduct at the Kinges Majesties Town of Poole.

(')

IN moste humble wise shewen unto your most excellent Hieghnes, youre poore dailie Oratoures and true and faithefull Subjectf the Maire burgesses and inhabitauntf of youre Towne and Porte of Poole in youre Countie of Dorset; That where youre saide Oratoures and theyre predecessoures, burgesses and inhabitytauntf of youre saide Towne and Porte, allwaies heretofore tyme out of mynde have been compelled and driven, of verye necessitie, to carye and recarye all maner theyre Come provided for the sustentacon of theyre poore Householdes, unto certayne Mylles being foure myles distaunte at the leaste frome youre saide Towne and Porte, to grinde, to the greate losse trouble and unquietnes of your saide Orators: For reamedie wherof and for the more ease quietnes and commoditie of youre saide Oratoures, and the more and better safegarde of youre saide Towne and Porte, Be it enacted ordeyned and establisshed by youre Hieghnes with thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporall and the Commons in this youre pnt hieghe Courte of Parliament assembled and by thauctorytie of the same, that it shalbe lawfull to youre saide Oratoures and to theyre Successoures, at theyre libertie and pleasure, to erect make frame and set upp, at in and upon youre waste grounde and comon within the saide Towne called Baiter, in a place there moste requisite and convenient, at theyre propre costes and chardges, oone good and sufficient Windemill to serve the saide Towne and Porte and the Burgesses and Inhabytauntf of the same, and to take and have oone hundred fote of assise square of the saide waste grounde for a convenient hill to be made to sett oone Windemyll upon: And allso lyke libertie and lisence to set oone Conduicte heade at a certaine place called Totnam within the Kinges waste grounde without the saide Towne of Poole, taking and having sixtene fote of Assise square of the same grounde for the scituacftn of the same conduicte heade, for the conveying of fresshe water for the serving of the same Towne, and to have allso lyke free libertie to digge and drawe in by throughe and upon all places and waies therunto moste meate and convenient with free course and recourse into and frome the same at all tymes hereafter for ever; yelding and paying therfore yerelie unto youre Hieghnes youre heyres and successoures oone pepercorne if it be asked, for all other exaccbns fvices and demaundf: And youre saide Oratoures shall according to theyre most bounden dueties contynuallye praie to God for the prosperous prefvacbn of youre moste noble and royall Majestie long in felicitie to reigne and endure.

CHAPTER XXVI.

An Actb for certaine Ordinaunces in the Kinges Majesties Domynion and Prindpalitie of Wales.

OUR Soveraigne Lorde the Kinges Majestie of his tendre zeale and affection, that he beareth towardes his loving and obedient subjectf of his Dominion Prindpalitie and Countrie of Wales, for good rule and ordere to be from henseforthe kepte and mainteyned witliin the same, wherby his saide subjectf may growe and ryse to more weakhe and prosperytie, hath devysed and made divers soondrye good and necessarye ordinances, which his Mau of his moete habundaunte goodnes, at the humble sute (1) of his saide subjectf of Wales, is pleased and contented to be enacted by thassent of the Lordes spuall and temporall, and the Comons in this pnt Parliament assembled, and by thauthorytie of the same, in maner and forme, as hereafter ensueth. First that his Graces said Dominion Prindpalitie and Countreye of Wales be from henseforthe devided into twelve Shires, of the whiche eight have been Shyres of long and aundent time, that is to saie: the Shyres of Glamorgon Carmerthin Pembroke Cardigan Flinte Caemarvan Anglesey and Meryoneth, and foure of the saide twelve Shyres be newlie made and ordeyned to be Shyres, by an Act made at the Parliament holden at Westni, the xxvij* yere of our saide Soveraigne Lordf moste noble reigne, that is to saie, the Shyres of Radnor Brecknoke Mountgomerye and Denbighe, over and besydes the Shyre of Monmoth, and divers other Domynions Lordeshipps and Manoures unyted and annexed to the Shyres of Salopp Hereforde and Gloucestre, as by the saide late Acte more plainllie appearethe.

Item, That the lymita£ons of the Hundredf, of late made within the saide Shyres by vertue of his Graces Commission directed out of his Heighnes Courte of Chauncerye and againe returned into the same, shall stande in full strengthe force and effecte according to the saide lymita£6n, except suche of the same as sithe that tyme have been altered or [chaunced*] by vertue of any Acte or Actes of Parliament alreadye made, or that shalbe altered or chaunged by any Acte or Actes in this present Session to be made.

Item, That there shalbe and remaine a President and Counsaill in the saide Dominion and Prindpalitie of Wales and the Marches of the same, with all Officers Clerkf and Inddentf to the same, in maner and forme as hath heretofore been used and accustomed; whiche President and Counsaill shall have power and auctorytie to here and determyne by theyre wisdoomes and discreac&ns such causes and matiers as be or hereafter shalbe assigned to them by the Kings Ma", as heretofore hath been accustomed and used.

Item, That there shalbe holden and kepte Sessions twyse in everye yere in everye of the saide Shyres in the saide Domynion and Prindpalitie of Wales: that is to saie, in the Shyres of Glamorgan Breknocke Radnor Caermerthin Pembroke Cardigan Mountgomerye Denbigh Flinte Caemarvan Merioneth and Anglesey, the whiche Sessions shall be called the Kingf Greate Sessions in Wales. Item, that the Justice of Chester for die tyme being shall holde and keape Sessions twyse in every yere in the Shyres of Denbigh Flint and Mountgomerye, and have nothing but his olde fee of an hundreth poundes yeerelie for the same. Item, that the Justice of Northwales shall in lykewyse holde and kepe Sessions twyse everye yere in everye of the said Shires of Caemarvan Meryoneth and Anglesey, and shall have yerelie of the Kingf Majestie a yerelie fee of fiftie poundf for the same. Item, that one person learned in the Lawes of this Realme of Englande, by the Kingf Majestie to be named and appointed, shall be Justice of the Shyres of Radnor Breknok and Glamorgan, and shall in lykewyse holde and keape Sessions twyse in everye yere m everye of the same Shyres, and shall have yerelie of the Kingf Majestie fiftie poundes for his fee. Item, that oone other psone learned in the Lawes of this Realme, (’) shalbe Justice of the Shyres of Caermerthin Pembrok and Cardigan and shall in lykewyse holde and keape Sessions twyse in everye yere in every of the same Shyres, and shall allso have yerelie of the Kingf Ma** fiftie poundf for his fee. Item, the saide psones or justices, and everye of them nowe being or that hereafter shalbe, shall have severall Ires patentf and commissions for theyre offices under the Kingf greate Seale of Englande, to be exercysed by themselves or theyre sufficient deputies, according to the purposes and intentf in theyre ordinances spfified: Provided alwaies, that theyre Commissions to them alreadye graunted under the saide greate Seale, shall stande in force and effecte according to the tenor of the same, ooneles it shall please the Kingf Majestie hereafter to alter or chaunge them or anye of them; this present article last before expressed in any wyse notwithstanding.

Item, That everye of the saide Justices, within the lymites of their Commission and auctoryties to them appointed as is aforesaide, shall holde all maner of Plees of the Crowne at and in the saide Sessions, in as lardge and ample maner as the Kingf Chief Justice of Englande and other the Justices of the Kingf Benche there, or anye of them, maie doo in theyre places or elswhere within the Realme of Englande; And allso to holde Plees of Assises, and all other Plees and Actions reall psonall and mixt, in as large and ample maner as the Kingf Chief Justice of the Common Place in Englande, and other Justices of the same Place or any of them maie doe in the Realme of Englande; Item, that everye of the saide Justices of Wales shall have power and auctorytie to enquire of all treasone6 murthers felonies ryotes routes unlawfuD assemblees extor£6ns embraceries maintenances reteynoures concelementf contemptf and all other offences and eviD dedes of what natures names or qualtities soever theye bee, doone committed or perpetrated within the lymites ef theyre commissions and auctoryties, againste the forme of the common lawe of the Realme of Englande, or of any Statutes of the same, and to here and determyne the premisses and e$y of them; and generallye to mynistre comon justice to all and singler the Kingf subjectf, within the lymites of theyre commissions and auctoryties, according to the Lawes Statutes and Custume8 of the Realme of Englande, and according to this pnt Ordin*nce.
